[1. PURPOSE]
Korean friendship-themed 4-cut photobooth photo strip, vertical i2i composite, made to look like a real "인생네컷" session with a natural campus-friend vibe.
Designed for sharing as a polished yet candid friend memory card, with a real printed booth-strip layout, glossy paper texture, playful handwritten decoration, tiny date/location labels, and warm friend-memory details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center the full friend group across all 4 cuts, preserving the exact number of people from {참고 이미지} with no additions or removals.
- Keep the composition like a real Korean photobooth strip: four stacked panels, slim outer border, narrow gaps between cuts, consistent booth framing, slightly rounded printed-paper corners, and a faint glossy reflection on the strip surface.
- Use {컷별 흐름} as the pose progression across the four panels, increasing closeness and energy from first to last cut.
- Background should be {배경·톤}: soft pastel pink and mint booth backdrop with a warm film-like finish, subtle curtain seam, gentle booth-wall texture, faint reflection from the photobooth light panel, and natural depth.
- Place {감성 타이틀 (2~5단어)} as a handwritten-style title near the top or upper panel edge, without covering faces.
- Add {낙서·스티커} around side margins, panel corners, and frame gaps, integrating them like real marker doodles and small printed stickers on a photobooth strip.
- Frame the strip with {프레임}: thin white border, gentle drop shadow, tight spacing between panels, and a small bottom information area to mimic an actual Korean photobooth print.
- Include realistic printed details: tiny date label such as "2026.05.01", location tag "서울 캠퍼스 앞", small booth serial text "CUT NO. 0427", tiny caption text like "오늘도 같이", and a small decorative QR/barcode-style area at the bottom edge.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Panel 1 (top): show a clean front-facing opening pose based on {컷별 흐름}, with all people clearly visible and evenly spaced for a balanced booth-photo feel; add a tiny corner label "1/4 시작!" and a small hand-drawn sparkle.
2. Panel 2: shift into a more playful interaction pose from {컷별 흐름}, keeping shoulders, hands, and eye-lines natural and close enough to feel like real friends laughing together; include a small caption sticker reading "웃음 터짐" near the frame edge.
3. Panel 3: emphasize physical closeness from {컷별 흐름}, such as shoulder-to-shoulder or heads gently touching, while keeping the group centered and compact; add soft doodles such as hearts, stars, and tiny arrows pointing toward the group.
4. Panel 4 (bottom): finish with the most expressive friendship pose from {컷별 흐름}, such as hand hearts, V signs, or thumbs-up, with the strongest energy and happiest expressions; add a small bottom caption "다음에도 또 찍자".
5. Title placement: render {감성 타이틀 (2~5단어)} in a casual handwritten line, sized small enough to stay secondary to the faces, with a tiny underline or marker highlight in peach or mint.
6. Sticker layer: distribute {낙서·스티커} naturally around corners and side gaps, avoiding overlap with eyes, mouths, and main gestures.
7. Bottom print area: include small Korean microcopy such as "FRIENDS PHOTO BOOTH", "2026년 봄", "@ourday.cut", a tiny barcode/QR-like graphic, and small heart icons, all printed as part of the photo strip rather than floating UI.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: handwritten Korean marker style for the title, with a lightweight brush feel; decorative text should feel like a Polaroid caption, sticker label, or booth-print microcopy.
- Color palette: pastel pink, mint green, warm cream, soft white, and light peach; use the exact booth mood from {배경·톤} with lively but soft friend-memory colors.
- Border/shadow: thin white border with a soft drop shadow, about 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity, to simulate a printed photobooth strip lying over a warm cream background.
- Printed realism: add subtle paper grain, glossy laminate highlights, tiny ink-dot texture on Korean captions, slight print alignment imperfections, and realistic edge thickness.
- Decoration: use small marker hearts, starbursts, tape-like labels, smiley stickers, tiny arrows, date stamps, and campus-memory tags that feel naturally attached to a youth photobooth print.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Canon EOS R5 with 50mm f/1.8 or 85mm f/1.4 portrait look, close-range booth framing, shallow but not extreme depth of field.
- Lighting: even indoor photobooth lighting with soft front fill, slight top diffusion, and gentle catchlights; no harsh flash blowout, no dark side falloff.
- Color grade: warm pastel film grade with slightly lifted shadows, soft pink highlights, mint accents, and a light Fujifilm Pro 400H-inspired finish.
- Material finish: realistic glossy photobooth paper, subtle specular sheen along the white frame, warm off-white paper base, and tactile printed-strip presence.

[6. MOOD]
Real Korean photobooth friendship memory — like a youth-culture editorial snapshot from Seoul college friends after class, candid and affectionate, with believable booth-print details, handwritten captions, and small keepsake decorations.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the title must appear exactly as {감성 타이틀 (2~5단어)}.
- Render added Korean microtext cleanly where visible, such as "2026.05.01", "서울 캠퍼스 앞", "오늘도 같이", "웃음 터짐", "다음에도 또 찍자", and "2026년 봄".
- Preserve the exact number of people from {참고 이미지}; do not add, remove, merge, or duplicate anyone.
- Faces, body shapes, hairstyles, and overall identity from {참고 이미지} must remain unchanged.
- Each of the 4 panels must feel like the same friend group in the same booth, with consistent framing and a natural progression of poses.
- Decorative text, date labels, QR/barcode area, stickers, and doodles must not cover faces, eyes, mouths, or main hand gestures.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized celebrity likeness

The result should feel like a real Korean photo booth strip printed on glossy paper: warm, tactile, content-rich, and playful, with SD mini characters actively helping the couple get closer across the four cuts.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main layout: 4 vertical panels stacked evenly inside a realistic photobooth print strip, each panel showing the two people with natural pose progression from awkward distance to a gentle couple moment.
- Subject placement: the two real people should remain the visual center in every panel, with the mini-me characters placed around them as active supporting elements, reacting to the couple and guiding the mood.
- Background treatment: Korean photobooth studio background with warm film tone, subtle grain, faint paper texture, realistic booth lighting, tiny print imperfections, and soft cream-beige atmosphere matching {배경·톤}.
- Frame realism: each cut has a thin white photo frame, narrow panel gaps, subtle drop shadow, mild glossy print reflection, tiny crop marks, cut numbers, and small photobooth metadata details along the strip edge.
- Add photobooth-strip details: a small date/location label, tiny serial number, mini barcode/QR-like decorative block, booth-style icon marks, and a short caption area that feels printed rather than digitally pasted.
- Use {컷별 흐름}, {배경·톤}, {프레임}, {미니미 캐릭터}, {미니미 행동}, {낙서·스티커}, {감성 타이틀 (2~5단어)} placeholders.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Panel 1: show the two people at a slightly awkward distance, matching the first step of {컷별 흐름}; place one or two {미니미 캐릭터} near the frame edge as if pushing the mood forward, with tiny motion lines, a small arrow sticker, and a cut label like “CUT 01”.
2. Panel 2: bring the two people a little closer with small smiles; place {미니미 캐릭터} between them or at shoulder level, encouraging eye contact and a softer reaction through {미니미 행동}, with a small speech-bubble-style sticker and realistic booth shadowing.
3. Panel 3: make the two people look naturally comfortable and closer together; have the mini-me characters cheer from above, point playfully, or guide a hand gesture without covering the faces, while {낙서·스티커} adds hearts, stars, tape marks, and playful hand-drawn accents around the panel.
4. Panel 4: complete the couple feeling with a gentle natural touch limited to hand or shoulder contact; place {미니미 캐릭터} as excited supporters around the frame, forming hearts or reacting happily, with a printed final-cut caption and celebratory sticker marks.
5. Title placement: add one readable Korean line of {감성 타이틀 (2~5단어)} above the first panel or on the bottom caption strip, styled like a photobooth title stamp.
6. Detail layer: integrate {낙서·스티커} into the strip as real printed sticker/doodle elements, including tiny hearts, soft tape pieces, sparkle marks, arrows, date stamp, and small booth UI-style icons, positioned around the photos without covering faces, hands, or the title.
7. Footer area: include a believable mini footer with printed date, location, photo number, and a small barcode-like block so the image feels like a real keepsake from a Korean date-night booth.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use a handwritten Korean title style or clean rounded sans serif such as Pretendard SemiBold or Noto Sans KR Bold, sized to read like a booth caption; mix it with tiny monospaced metadata text for the serial number, date, and footer labels.
- Color palette: warm off-white, cream, soft beige, muted peach, and light brown, matching {배경·톤}; keep whites slightly warm with muted sticker accents in dusty pink, caramel, pale blue, and cocoa brown.
- Border/shadow: thin white frame, 1–2px inner edge feel, soft drop shadow with about 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity, plus subtle glossy paper highlight and tactile print texture.
- Frame design: {프레임} should feel like a real photobooth strip frame with small printed details, booth cut numbers, tiny corner marks, and a bottom receipt-like caption band.
- Mini-me integration: {미니미 캐릭터} and {미니미 행동} must interact with the people’s pose progression and panel storytelling, using believable scale, shadows, overlap, and contact with frame edges or sticker layers.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: realistic photobooth capture look, 35mm equivalent lens, straight-on framing, f/4 feel, natural booth print sharpness.
- Lighting: even frontal booth light with very slight upper-left softness and gentle fill from the front, like a real enclosed photo booth; preserve natural skin tones and soft facial detail from the references.
- Color grade: warm cream + honey beige + subtle film brown, light grain, low-contrast print finish, slightly faded highlights.
- Physical finish: glossy photo paper, faint scanner-like edge shadow, tiny dust specks, soft ink texture, subtle panel-to-panel exposure variation, and believable printed sticker layering.

[6. MOOD]
Korean couple photobooth editorial — playful K-drama date night strip with a Kinfolk-meets-life4cut feel, affectionate but natural, like a cherished keepsake printed after a fun evening together.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문구는 {감성 타이틀 (2~5단어)} only.
- Additional small printed Korean details may appear as realistic booth ephemera: “오늘의 네 컷”, “서울 연남동”, “2026.05.01”, “PHOTO NO. 0427”, “다시 가까워지는 중”, “저장 완료”.
- Keep the two real people’s face shape, body type, and expression identity unchanged from the reference photos.
- The mini-me characters must feel alive and coordinated with the couple’s distance progression; they should support the relationship, react to the couple, and visually guide each panel’s story.
- Final panel may include only natural hand or shoulder contact; no excessive touching or forced couple posing.
- Each of the 4 panels must retain the thin white frame and narrow gap style, with realistic printed-paper texture and small booth-strip details.

- Fake official seals / certifications
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized celebrity likeness

[1. PURPOSE]
Create an i2i travel poster collage in a premium magazine-editorial style, using the attached person photo as the hero subject for a foreign tourist-in-Korea concept.
Vertical 1024x1536 poster for social sharing and printable display, with a bold Korean headline, realistic travel-poster information, layered print ephemera, and a rich city-culture collage surrounding the subject.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Hero subject placement: place the original person as a centered 55–60% height cutout, slightly forward from the collage background, with crisp silhouette separation, believable paper-cut depth, and a confident travel-poster pose.
- Background treatment: warm off-white paper base with layered torn newsprint, magazine scraps, subway-map fragments, postage-stamp textures, ticket stubs, receipt strips, Korean street-sign snippets, halftone overlays, and subtle paper fibers; edges should feel hand-torn, taped, stapled, and assembled like a real editorial travel board.
- Framing direction: build a strong central focal zone for the person, while collaged city motifs orbit around the sides, top corners, and lower margin, creating a lively tourist diary layout rather than a sterile mockup.
- Keep {원본 보존 항목} strictly intact on the face, identity, hair, body type, and expression, while adding only the travel accessories from {트래블 패션 변환}.
- Surround the subject with collage elements derived from {국가 시각 모티프}, distributed as symbolic architectural, street, landmark, transport, food, sign, cultural, shopping, café, nightlife, and map fragments connected to {국가/도시}.
- Add realistic poster utility details: date/time block, venue line, ticket/QR-style information area, sponsor strip, small credit line, and decorative route markers integrated into the collage.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Hero cutout layer — preserve the person realistically, cleanly separated from the background, with crisp edge masking, subtle paper-cut shadow, slight lifted editorial cutout look, and tiny tape corners or paper tabs that make the collage physically believable.
2. Travel styling layer — add only the accessories from {트래블 패션 변환}; keep the outfit mostly original and believable, with global tourist fashion styling that contrasts clearly against the local backdrop.
3. Landmark collage ring — place fragments from {국가 시각 모티프} around the subject, mixing iconic architecture, subway signage, street food, taxis, crosswalks, cafés, convenience-store details, market textures, street lamps, and cultural details as layered cut-paper pieces.
4. Print ephemera layer — add {콜라주 요소} across the poster: torn newspaper edges, passport-stamp stickers, boarding-pass stubs, metro ticket strips, handwritten route doodles, photo contact sheets, map pins, halftone dots, tape pieces, receipt typography, and bold sans-serif/serif typography blocks.
5. Headline placement — set {헤드라인} prominently at the upper third or centered header zone, using large editorial Korean typography with strong contrast, confident hierarchy, and legible spacing.
6. Poster information system — include compact supporting text blocks in Korean such as "TRAVEL POSTER SERIES", "VOL.247", "2026년 5월호", "서울 산책 기록", "DATE 2026.05.01–05.31", "TIME 10:00–21:00", "VENUE 서울 도심 일대", "TICKET ₩7,500", "INFO @visit.seoul.diary", plus a small barcode/QR-like ticket area and a bottom sponsor strip reading "PARTNER · LOCAL GUIDE · CITY WALK".
7. Color and rhythm layer — build the entire composition around {시그니처 컬러}, balancing cream paper areas with vintage red, mustard yellow, deep navy, black ink, muted beige, and small accent stickers for rhythm and readability.
8. Contrast rule — keep the traveler figure visually distinct from the local collage environment so the “tourist vs. local city” contrast is immediately readable, while still making the poster feel dense, tactile, and culturally specific.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard Bold, Noto Sans KR SemiBold, and a condensed serif display style; headline size should feel poster-scale, with smaller supporting type in 18–36px range and tiny production credits in 8–12px.
- Korean copy blocks: mix large headline, short feature-style blurbs, ticket details, location captions, and micro credits; examples include "낯선 도시를 걷다", "오늘의 루트", "시장 · 골목 · 야경", "모델 크레딧: 여행자", and "PHOTO COLLAGE EDITION".
- Color palette: off-white #F4F0E6 base, vintage red #B24A3C, mustard yellow #D6A01D, deep navy #1E2B4A, plus black ink, muted paper beige, faded sky blue, and subtle street-photo neutrals.
- Border/shadow: torn-paper perimeter, layered collage shadow with 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 18% opacity, slight offset duplicates for print-cut depth, visible tape strips, staple marks, crease lines, and overlapping paper edges.
- Layout details: include small caption labels near landmarks, numbered route circles, arrow doodles, a lower information band, and a sponsor/ticket area without making them look like official certification marks.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial portrait look as if shot on a Canon EOS R5 with 85mm f/1.4 for the subject, then composited into a graphic collage poster layout.
- Lighting: soft diffused daylight from upper-left, gentle fill from front-right, with clean separation and no harsh flash reflections on the cutout edges.
- Color grade: warm cream paper, muted travel red, archival navy, mustard accents, slightly desaturated street-photo tones, tactile paper texture, subtle print grain, halftone ink variation, and realistic shadow interaction between layers.
- Material realism: make the poster feel physically assembled from matte paper, semi-gloss photo scraps, newsprint, sticker labels, tape, ticket stock, and ink-stamped fragments.

[6. MOOD]
Premium travel editorial poster — like a Kinfolk x Monocle city feature with a contemporary museum-shop collage aesthetic, enriched with the energy of a real tourist itinerary, street discoveries, ticket stubs, city captions, and collectible print design.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following Korean text, if rendered, must appear clean and correctly spelled: "외국인 관광객 여행 포스터 콜라주", "한국", "서울", "낯선 도시를 걷다", "오늘의 루트", "시장 · 골목 · 야경", "2026년 5월호", "서울 산책 기록", "VENUE 서울 도심 일대", "TICKET ₩7,500".
- Keep the original person's face, identity, hairstyle, body shape, and expression unchanged from the reference image.
- Maintain an i2i collage poster look; the result should feel like layered editorial print design, not a pure photo composite.
- All typography must be sharp, legible, correctly aligned, and integrated into the poster hierarchy.
- The composition must remain centered on the traveler while including believable poster details: date/time/venue, ticket info, sponsor strip, barcode/QR-style area, captions, route markers, and cultural fragments related to {국가/도시}.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness

Designed for ebook, blog, newsletter, and social-sharing use with a polished editorial layout, practical startup-guide feeling, and realistic Korean card-news details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Top section (about 24%): card-news header with {카드 번호}, {발행일}, {채널명}, and {핸들}; large {부업 종류} headline with {부제목} underneath, aligned slightly left with a small category tag such as "N잡 가이드".
- Middle section (about 46%): {시작 단계} displayed as a 1–2–3–4 process flow with small commerce/blog/video-style info icons, short micro descriptions, and a highlighted tip box for {핵심 팁}.
- Lower section (about 22%): compact dashboard area containing {예상 수익}, {소요 시간}, {난이도}, and {준비물}, using stat cards, progress dots, and tiny checklist markers.
- Footer section (about 8%): social-card footer with page indicator {페이지 표시}, hashtag line {해시태그}, save/share micro icons, and a clear CTA pill/button for {CTA}.
- Background treatment: warm off-white editorial paper surface with subtle grain texture, layered rounded cards, thin dividers, sticky-note accents, small arrows, and practical workbook-style decoration.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header band: place {카드 번호} and {발행일} in a small top utility row; place {부업 종류} as the primary category label and large headline in the upper third; include {부제목}, {채널명}, and {핸들} as realistic publisher metadata.
2. Main process block: render {시작 단계} as four evenly spaced numbered steps (1, 2, 3, 4), each step inside a neat rounded card or vertical mini-column with small line icons, tiny captions, and connector arrows.
3. Tip highlight: set {핵심 팁} in a contrasting accent box in the center area, using mustard or gold emphasis with a thin navy outline; add a small "TIP" label and checkmark icon.
4. Metrics strip: show {예상 수익}, {소요 시간}, {난이도}, and {준비물} in bold, easy-to-scan stat cards with clear labels, numeric emphasis, and small supporting labels such as "예상", "투입", "준비".
5. CTA footer: add {CTA} in a button-like footer area with a small arrow icon; include {페이지 표시}, {해시태그}, save/share/bookmark micro icons, and a tiny end-card teaser line {저장 안내}.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR, bold weights for headlines, medium weights for labels, regular for descriptions; headline size large, supporting text compact and highly legible.
- Color palette: navy #1F2A44, mustard #D8A62A, warm off-white #F6F1E8, soft gray #D9DDE3, deep charcoal #222222, muted mint #9DBFAF for checklist accents.

- Lighting: simulated studio-like even illumination with no harsh contrast, subtle top-left brightness and gentle shadow separation between cards.

[6. MOOD]
Modern Korean side-hustle editorial — practical ebook cover meets blog infographic and Instagram card-news slide, with the feeling of a realistic beginner checklist that could be saved and shared.

[7. CRITICAL]

[1. PURPOSE]
DIY hobby guide card for a craft tutorial, editorial infographic layout, portrait social-media card. Korean hobby magazine / Pinterest-friendly reference sheet for embroidery, paper craft, knitting, or hand-stitching, with a large finished-result hero, realistic tools and materials, step-by-step illustrations, slide-style guide markers, and bottom tips.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Top section (about 28%): centered title line using {활동/주제} at the very top, with a small issue label such as "CRAFT NOTE 01", "2026.05", and "저장용 가이드" near the header. Place a large finished-work hero image directly beneath it occupying most of the width.
- Middle section (about 46%): materials list panel and a 4–6 step process panel placed side by side or stacked in readable editorial blocks, depending on space. Include tiny icons, numbered badges, arrows, and short Korean micro-labels such as "준비물", "만드는 순서", "체크 포인트".
- Bottom section (about 18%): compact info strip for difficulty, time, size ratio, and tip text, visually separated by an olive divider line. Add a small CTA such as "저장하고 주말에 따라 만들기" plus tiny save/share-style micro icons.
- Background should be warm beige paper with visible fiber texture, faint pencil registration marks, small tape pieces, thread ends, stitch swatches, pressed-flower or fabric scrap accents, olive dividers, and hand-drawn annotation lines that feel natural for a craft notebook.
- Use {재료}, {단계}, {완성 모습}, {난이도/시간}, {컨셉 톤}, and {비율/사이즈} as visible content anchors throughout the layout.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header area: Place {활동/주제} as a bold Korean headline at the top. Add small magazine-card metadata around it: "VOL. 024", "2026년 5월호", "DIY 저장 카드", and a tiny page indicator "01 / 05".
2. Hero image: Render {완성 모습} as the main visual focus, centered and enlarged, presented in a neat hoop, small frame, folded card, knitted swatch, or finished craft display appropriate to the topic. Include tangible textures: cotton thread, linen weave, paper grain, yarn fuzz, needle marks, soft shadows, and a realistic tabletop feel.
3. Materials panel: Arrange {재료} as a checklist or icon-led list in the middle-left area, using small line drawings and realistic mini product-photo details for thread, needle, hoop, scissors, fabric, ruler, marker, yarn, glue, or paper as relevant. Add Korean label "준비물" and small checkbox marks.
4. Process panel: Visualize {단계} as 4–6 sequential mini-illustrations or diagram cards, each showing one craft step with arrows, numbered olive circles, hand-drawn callouts, and close-up detail crops. Add the Korean label "만드는 순서" and show motion clearly from preparation to finishing.
5. Info strip: At the bottom, present {난이도/시간} and {비율/사이즈} in compact badge-style labels, with a small craft notebook annotation area labeled "TIP" and a friendly Korean note such as "실 끝은 뒤쪽에서 두 번 고정해요" or "처음엔 천천히, 결을 맞춰 진행해요".
6. Tone integration: Make {컨셉 톤} visible through the palette, line weight, real craft props, paper layering, subtle sticker tags, and tactile editorial styling so the card feels like a polished Korean hobby guide page captured from a real handmade workbook.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for main text, medium to bold weight for headers, 20–34px for title, 12–18px for body, with crisp Korean readability. Use small handwritten-style Korean annotations only for short labels and tips.
- Color palette: warm beige #F4EBDD, olive green #7A8B63, soft moss #A8B38A, muted pink #D9A1A8, cream #FFF8EF, charcoal #2F2A24.
- Border/shadow: thin olive divider lines, soft drop shadow 0 4px 14px rgba(47,42,36,0.12), rounded corners 14px on info cards, subtle washi-tape shadows, lightly embossed paper edges.
- Decorative information details: include small page marker "01/05", tiny bookmark/save/share icons, a short hashtag line such as "#주말취미 #손으로만드는시간", and a small credit line "guide by @handmade_note".

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial product-photo feel, 50mm lens at f/5.6 for the hero craft photo, with top-down flat-lay framing for materials and steps.
- Lighting: soft window light from upper-left at roughly 45°, gentle fill from right, even exposure with natural shadows under tools, paper layers, embroidery hoop, thread spools, and small diagram cards.
- Color grade: warm cream + olive + muted rose, slightly desaturated and paper-like, inspired by Kinfolk-style craft pages, Korean hobby magazines, Pinterest DIY boards, and real craft studio worktables.
- Texture rendering: emphasize linen weave, cotton thread twist, matte paper grain, pencil sketch marks, tiny cut edges, printed ink density, and tactile handmade imperfections.

[6. MOOD]
Quiet handmade-editorial craft card — Kinfolk magazine spread meets modern Korean hobby guide aesthetic, warm enough to feel like a real saved tutorial page from a cozy weekend craft desk.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: must appear exactly as written:
  - {활동/주제}
  - {재료}
  - {단계}
  - {완성 모습}
  - {난이도/시간}
  - {컨셉 톤}
  - {비율/사이즈}
- Additional Korean labels should be short and legible: "준비물", "만드는 순서", "완성", "TIP", "저장하고 주말에 따라 만들기", "#주말취미".
- Layout invariants: top headline + large finished-work hero, middle materials and step-by-step instruction area, bottom difficulty/time/size info strip.
- Step illustrations must show a clear sequential workflow with 4–6 distinct steps, numbered in order and visually connected with arrows.
- All Korean labels must be rendered legibly with no broken characters.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[1. PURPOSE]
Public-sector citizen information poster for a city hall / district office style announcement.
Korean government-office editorial poster, vertical A4-like layout, designed for clear public communication and easy readability.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Overall layout: a formal vertical poster with a strong top header band, a structured central information block, and a compact footer CTA area; keep generous margins and clean alignment.
- Top section: place the institutional identity area at the upper-left or upper-center, followed by a large headline with strong hierarchy, occupying about 18–22% of the canvas.
- Middle section: allocate the largest space to {핵심 안내} and {주요 행사}, organized with icon-led steps, small cards, or a simple table/grid so the information scans quickly.
- Bottom section: place {참가 방법} and {CTA} in a distinct footer bar with contact emphasis, using a clear button-like treatment or highlighted strip.
- Background treatment: solid off-white or very light cool gray paper tone, with subtle flat color blocks in navy and mint; no photographic clutter, no dramatic gradients.
- Spacing: use wide breathing room, strong left alignment, consistent line spacing, and clean separators to reflect a municipal notice board aesthetic.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Header zone (top 15–20%): set {기관/주제} as the main title area with a formal government-poster hierarchy; if a logo mark is used, keep it small, simplified, and aligned to the title block rather than decorative.
- Headline block: convert the main announcement into a bold headline with large sans-serif type, followed by a smaller supporting line that clarifies the event period and audience.
- Information block (mid 45–50%): present {핵심 안내} as the primary factual line, then break {주요 행사} into 3–4 clearly separated items with simple icons (movie screen, stage, booth, drone) and short labels.
- Participation block: show {참가 방법} in a compact step-by-step format or checklist style, making free entry and reservation conditions immediately visible.
- CTA footer (bottom 15–18%): place {CTA} in a high-contrast bar with contact information styling, using concise spacing and a clear callout shape for quick recognition.
- Civic illustration accents: add small, friendly citizen illustrations or minimal pictograms near the middle or footer edges, keeping them restrained and flat so the layout remains official and trustworthy.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for all Korean text; headline 72–92px bold, subheads 28–36px semibold, body 22–28px regular, CTA 26–32px bold.
- Color palette: navy #153A63, mint #7FCDBB, white #FFFFFF, cool gray #EAF0F4, text charcoal #24303A; use mint only as an accent, not dominant.
- Border/shadow: thin 1–2px divider lines in pale gray, and very soft drop shadows only on floating info cards (e.g., 0px 6px 18px, 10–12% opacity).
- Graphic treatment: use flat vector icons, rounded rectangles, and clean infographic blocks; avoid ornamental flourishes, glossy effects, or heavy gradients.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: flat graphic poster composition, no photographic camera look; if illustration texture is needed, use crisp vector rendering with clean edges similar to a modern civic infographic.
- Lighting: even studio-like digital lighting with no hard shadows; if any depth is added, keep it extremely subtle and uniform.
- Color grade: restrained civic palette with navy + mint + white, slightly cool and clean, similar to Seoul public notice graphics and government portal UI styling.

[6. MOOD]
Trustworthy Korean municipal notice — clean government-office editorial design with the clarity of Seoul city public information graphics and Government 24 style communication.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following strings must appear verbatim and correctly rendered: "서울시 — 5월 가정의 달 시민 행사 안내", "5월 1~31일 / 한강 공원 무료 행사 / 가족 동반 환영", "야외 영화·공연·체험 부스·드론 쇼", "현장 참가 무료 / 일부 사전 예약", "서울시 홈페이지 / 다산콜 120".
- Layout invariants: top header must contain the institutional identity and main headline; center must prioritize factual event information; footer must clearly present CTA and contact details.
- Keep all typography clean, legible, and evenly spaced; no distorted characters, no overlapping text blocks, no decorative clutter that reduces readability.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Overly flashy neon effects or entertainment-poster styling
- Photorealistic crowd scenes that distract from the notice content
- Illegible small text or cramped layouts

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean plant home-gardening care guide poster, vertical editorial infographic for plant parents.
Designed like a real plant-shop care sheet that could be printed and displayed in a cozy Korean apartment or shared on social media, combining botanical illustration, practical care icons, small shop details, seasonal guide labels, and a realistic room mockup.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Overall layout: a tall poster with top title band (18%), central hero plant illustration (42%), care-info card zone (20%), and bottom interior mockup strip (20%).
- Subject placement: {식물명} appears at the top as the main title; the plant illustration dominates the upper-middle area, slightly offset with layered paper tabs, botanical annotation marks, and small specimen-label details so the page feels designed and lived-in.
- Background treatment: warm off-white paper texture (#F6F1E7) with visible recycled-paper grain, faint pressed-leaf silhouettes, soft shadowed paper-card layers, subtle tape corners, and a realistic printed poster surface.
- Spacing and framing: clear hierarchy between title, illustration, care icons, and mockup; include rounded-corner info cards, thin botanical line dividers, small note stickers, a tiny QR/barcode-style contact area, and a footer credit line without overwhelming the care information.
- Use {식물명}, {케어 정보}, {일러스트 톤}, {인테리어 mockup}, {색감}, {핵심 카피}, {비율/사이즈} placeholders naturally throughout the layout.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Top header area (upper 18%): place {식물명} in large Korean lettering, with a compact subtitle-style placement for {핵심 카피} beneath it; add small editorial metadata such as “식물집사 케어 가이드”, “VOL.024”, “2026년 봄호”, and “PLANT CARE NOTE” like a premium plant-shop label.
- Hero illustration area (mid 42%): render {식물명} as the main botanical illustration in {일러스트 톤}, with clear leaf silhouettes, delicate vein detail, subtle watercolor wash, small handwritten-style Korean annotation labels, a tiny pot-size ruler mark, and faint soil/pot texture details that keep the linework readable.
- Care information area (lower-mid 20%): convert {케어 정보} into three icon-led blocks for sunlight, watering, and temperature; each block should be aligned in a neat grid with simple pictograms and short Korean labels. Add realistic micro details such as “체크 주기”, “초보 난이도 ★★★☆☆”, “이번 주 관리 메모”, and a small watering calendar strip.
- Interior mockup area (bottom 20%): show {인테리어 mockup} as a realistic home corner with the plant placed naturally in a ceramic or terracotta pot, styled like a cozy Korean apartment interior with a wood shelf, linen curtain, warm window light, a small watering can, plant mister, gardening book, and textured rug or floor detail.
- Footer and utility details: include a small shop/contact block reading “GREEN ROOM SEOUL”, “서울 마포구 연남로 24”, “문의 @greenroom.home”, a small QR/barcode area labeled “CARE QR”, and a tiny credit line “Illustration & Care by 식물생활 연구소”.
- Visual integration: use {색감} consistently across title accents, icon outlines, plant shadows, sticky-note tags, barcode/QR area, and divider lines so the whole composition feels unified, warm, and realistic.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for the care text in medium weight 500–600, and a more elegant serif-like Korean display for the title if needed; title size should feel bold and poster-like, with slightly expanded letter spacing.
- Color palette: base off-white #F6F1E7, sage #A8B69A, beige #DCCDB7, dark green #2F4A3A, and muted accent gray #7D7D73; incorporate {색감} as the main accent for labels, stickers, and botanical highlights.
- Border/shadow: use thin 1px dark-green rules, soft drop shadows with 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity, rounded cards, paper-cut layering, subtle washi-tape shadows, and light print-registration texture.
- Graphic treatment: icons should be simple line icons with consistent stroke width; the watercolor illustration should keep edges crisp rather than painterly-blurry, while the room strip can include realistic textures such as ceramic glaze, woven fabric, plant soil, wood grain, and soft curtain folds.
- Poster content details: add short Korean callout blurbs such as “잎 끝 갈변 체크”, “흙이 마르면 듬뿍”, “빛 좋은 창가 추천”, plus a small page indicator “CARE SHEET 01 / 01” and a decorative botanical divider.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial product-poster look inspired by a Canon EOS R5 with 50mm f/1.8 standard lens for the interior strip and a flat botanical scan aesthetic for the illustration section; overall composition should feel like a professionally designed printed page with realistic paper and ink texture.
- Lighting: soft window light from upper-left with gentle fill from the right, creating faint natural shadows on the mockup area, paper cards, tape edges, pot rim, and small gardening props.
- Color grade: muted sage-beige botanical palette with deep forest green anchors, warm paper whites, natural terracotta and wood tones, and print-friendly contrast.

[6. MOOD]
A refined Korean plant-care editorial — like a Kinfolk-style houseplant spread mixed with a modern neighborhood plant-shop care poster, practical enough for beginners and visually rich enough to feel like a collectible botanical print.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문구가 정확히 보여야 함:

  - {케어 정보}

- Layout invariants: the top title, center care info, and bottom mockup must all appear in one vertically stacked poster with clear hierarchy, matching {비율/사이즈}.

[INPUT]

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean seasonal landscape photo series for a blog header, rendered as a realistic cinematic scenic image with season-specific visual identity.
A 4-season Korea landscape composition that can be adapted by {계절}, {장소}, and {핵심 카피} while staying editorial, natural, and usable as a premium travel blog hero image with tasteful Korean editorial text overlays.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main landscape occupies about 70% of the frame, with the horizon placed on the upper third for a wide, panoramic blog-header feel.
- Foreground, midground, and background must be clearly separated: foreground path or shoreline detail, midground seasonal subject mass, background mountain/sky or sea/sky depth.
- Background treatment should match {장소}: realistic Korean terrain, natural atmospheric perspective, believable mountain ridges, village edges, temple roofs, stone walls, coastal roads, or forest trails depending on the location.
- Place {주요 모티프} as the dominant visual anchor, with {핵심 카피} integrated as an editorial travel-title overlay in the upper-left or upper-right over sky, mist, distant hill, or calm water.
- Add subtle blog-series metadata: {시리즈 번호}, {촬영 날짜}, {지역 라벨}, and {날씨 태그} as small Korean labels near the main title or along a thin translucent information strip.
- Use {계절}, {시간/조명}, and {색감} as the controlling visual variables; keep the landscape, typography, and seasonal details balanced for a 1536x1024 blog header.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Wide establishing view: show the full Korean seasonal landscape first, with strong depth and a clear sense of location.
2. Primary subject zone: build the scene around {주요 모티프}, making it the most detailed and highest-contrast area.
3. Seasonal signature layer: express the season through {계절} cues — cherry blossoms, fresh green leaves, humid summer haze, autumn foliage, silver grass, frost, or snow cover — with natural density and realistic terrain.
4. Location character: embed {장소} as authentic Korean scenery, such as mountain ridges, a coastal edge, village roofs, a stone path, wooden signposts, small trail markers, tiled hanok roofs, low fences, or distant cable-car lines when appropriate.
5. Light direction: apply {시간/조명} so the highlights, shadow length, air clarity, and foliage translucency support the season and time of day.
6. Editorial overlay: include the Korean title {핵심 카피}, a smaller subtitle {서브 카피}, and compact metadata labels {시리즈 번호} · {촬영 날짜} · {지역 라벨} · {날씨 태그}, arranged like a refined travel magazine blog header.
7. Human-scale realism: optionally include tiny distant hikers, a parked bicycle, trail ribbon, café sign, or wooden viewpoint deck only if they naturally belong to {장소} and reinforce scale.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: if text is included, use Pretendard SemiBold or Noto Sans KR Bold, 42–56 px for the main line, 18–26 px for metadata labels, with clean modern spacing and accurate Korean rendering.
- Editorial text layout: {핵심 카피} should be the largest line, {서브 카피} should sit directly below or beside it, and {시리즈 번호}, {촬영 날짜}, {지역 라벨}, {날씨 태그} should appear as small travel-journal tags.
- Color palette: anchor the scene with {색감}, then support it with season-appropriate neutrals such as mist white, deep forest green, slate gray, soft sky blue, warm earth brown, hanok roof charcoal, or muted stone beige.
- Graphic treatment: allow a thin translucent label plate, small divider line, map-pin icon, weather dot, or understated editorial marker behind the text so the header feels designed rather than plain.
- Natural detail: include realistic bark texture, fallen leaves, gravel, wet stones, pine needles, wild grass, snow crystals, sea spray, or trail dust according to {계절} and {장소}.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: full-frame landscape photography look, 24mm wide-angle, f/8, crisp edge-to-edge detail, natural perspective compression kept low.
- Lighting: {시간/조명} rendered with realistic atmospheric behavior — spring diffused morning light, summer bright coastal sunlight, autumn golden-hour glow, or winter cold overcast clarity.
- Color grade: season-specific cinematic grade with clean blacks, moderate contrast, and restrained saturation; spring pink, summer teal-blue, autumn mustard and rust, winter white and cool gray.
- Surface realism: emphasize authentic Korean landscape textures such as granite steps, old roof tiles, tree trunks, mountain haze, wind-bent reeds, damp soil, or snow-laden branches.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean travel editorial — like a National Geographic travel spread with a Kinfolk-style composition discipline, tuned for seasonal blog-header storytelling, with the warmth of a personal travel diary and the polish of a curated regional photo series.

[7. CRITICAL]

[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean meme one-shot image for chat sharing, designed like a single-panel GIF-style reaction sticker captured at the funniest frozen moment.
A compact, punchy “짤” layout with a clear character beat, large readable Korean overlay text, and believable chat-share details such as tiny reaction tags, sticker marks, and a saved-meme thumbnail feel.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject takes about 55–65% of the frame, slightly off-center for reaction-comic energy; {캐릭터} should be immediately readable at thumbnail size with a strong silhouette, expressive face, and exaggerated pose.
- Reserve 20–25% of the frame for bold caption impact, with {문구} placed as a large overlay in the upper or lower third; add a tiny secondary tag such as “오늘의 짤”, “현실 반응”, or “GIF 저장됨” near the caption for meme authenticity.
- Background should be recognizable as {배경/소품}, including a few natural objects, surface textures, small props, motion marks, reaction symbols, or everyday details that support the joke and make the scene feel lived-in.
- Use {짤 컨셉} as the exact scene premise; keep the pose and facial expression exaggerated, instantly funny, and readable like a paused reaction GIF.
- Add small meme-share UI flavor around the edges: a tiny handle such as “@zzal_maker”, a short timestamp label like “오전 8:57”, small save/share icon marks, or a subtle sticker label, without turning it into a full app screenshot.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Hero character block: {캐릭터} shown in a single decisive reaction pose, with the expression built around {짤 컨셉}; make body language readable in one glance through raised shoulders, slumped posture, wide eyes, sweat drops, motion streaks, or comic emphasis lines as appropriate.
2. Background block: {배경/소품} rendered as a contextual setting with believable physical details such as desk items, bags, phone screen glow, wall notes, snack wrappers, coffee cup, transit handle, office chair, or other props that naturally match the chosen premise.
3. Caption block: {문구} set in very large Korean text with thick outline and strong contrast, positioned like a classic meme sticker overlay; add one small supporting Korean label such as “짤 저장 완료”, “오늘도 버팀”, or “반응 속도 0.1초”.
4. Tonal exaggeration block: {톤} applied through facial exaggeration, timing, motion lines, sweat icons, vibrating outline, impact burst, speed blur, or sticker-like comic marks that heighten the punchline.
5. Color emphasis block: {색감} used as the main palette accent, with warm and cool support tones plus saturated highlights that make the frame pop in chat previews.
6. Format block: {비율/사이즈} preserved exactly as a square social-share composition with strong edge-to-edge framing, thick readable caption treatment, and optional sticker stroke or rounded thumbnail-like crop for shareability.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: bold Korean sans-serif like Pretendard ExtraBold or Noto Sans KR Black for the main caption, 54–92px range; optional hand-drawn accent for smaller joke marks, sound effects, and reaction tags.
- Color palette: {색감} with concrete support tones such as cool gray #7A7A7A, warm paper beige #F4F0E6, accent yellow #F2C94C, deep ink black #111111, and soft highlight white #FFF7D6.
- Text treatment: thick black outline on {문구}, subtle 2–4px soft drop shadow at 20% opacity, and a slightly offset duplicate color layer for energetic meme readability.
- Character treatment: slight sticker-like stroke around the character, expressive webtoon-style facial marks, and small reaction symbols such as “!”, “?”, “헉”, “아…”, or “띠용” when they support the joke.
- Scene details: include realistic everyday textures in {배경/소품} such as fabric folds, screen reflections, paper edges, plastic shine, steam from coffee, floor shadows, or worn desk surfaces.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 50mm equivalent portrait framing, slightly compressed perspective, with a comic-sticker crop that feels like a paused reaction GIF rather than a staged studio mockup.
- Lighting: flat, readable front light with a slight top-left key and soft fill, keeping facial expression and silhouette crisp for meme readability while allowing natural shadows under props and around the character.
- Color grade: muted gray base with yellow accent pops, slightly boosted contrast, playful webtoon-like saturation without neon overshoot.
- Rendering: polished Korean webtoon-meets-realistic sticker style, with believable object depth, tactile props, visible texture, and crisp caption edges optimized for mobile chat preview.

[6. MOOD]
Korean internet meme reaction sticker — DCinside-style 짤 energy with a lively webtoon/comic punchline feel, like a saved image that people would instantly send in a group chat.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 표시되어야 하는 메인 문구: "{문구}"; 기본 문구가 “출근… 이렇게 또…”인 경우에도 철자와 말줄임표를 깨지지 않게 표시한다.
- Include small supporting Korean meme details such as “오늘의 짤”, “GIF 저장됨”, “오전 8:57”, “@zzal_maker”, or “짤 저장 완료” in tiny but legible text where appropriate.
- The image must feel like a single-panel Korean meme, with one clear joke beat, one dominant reaction, and supporting background details that reinforce {짤 컨셉}.
- Character expression must clearly match the premise in {짤 컨셉}, and the caption must be highly legible at thumbnail size.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536
- title: 한국 시대극·사극 컨셉아트 (조선·고려 한복 인물)

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean historical drama concept art poster featuring Joseon/Goryeo-era characters in accurate hanbok styling, designed as a vertical cinematic key visual.
Editorial concept-art composition for poster, thumbnail, cultural campaign, or museum-style promotional use, with restrained drama, period authenticity, and fully rendered poster information.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject placement: one central full-body figure occupying about 55–60% of the frame, posed as a dignified historical-drama protagonist with the upper title integrated into sky, palace eaves, hanji texture, or flowering branches.
- Background treatment: {배경} rendered with period-accurate architecture, wooden surfaces, stone paving, lattice windows, textile curtains, ceramic vessels, seasonal foliage, and lived-in historical atmosphere.
- Framing direction: vertical hero shot, slightly low angle for dignity, with layered foreground details such as scattered petals, a scroll edge, incense smoke, patterned floor shadows, or soft fabric movement.
- Poster information layer: add a cinematic title block using {포스터_제목}, {부제}, {세로_문구}, plus a lower information band containing {행사명}, {일시}, {장소}, {관람_정보}, {주최_후원}, {문의}, and {제작크레딧}.
- Styling anchors: {시대_인물}, {의상_디테일}, {자세_표정}, {색감}, {비율_사이즈}.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Hero character layer: depict {시대_인물} with realistic Korean facial proportions, calm eyes, refined posture, natural skin texture, and historically faithful fabric structure, seams, accessories, and hairstyle or headwear.
- Costume layer: apply {의상_디테일} with accurate garment layering, sleeve width, collar overlap, belt tension, hat shape, ornamental knots, fabric weave, embroidered trim, and shoe form; folds follow gravity and body movement naturally.
- Environment layer: place the figure in {배경}, including period furniture, ceramic vessels, low writing desk, brush and inkstone, folded scrolls, courtyard stonework, hanok timber grain, palace roof tiles, carved door frames, or era-appropriate decorative screens depending on the selected period.
- Pose and expression layer: interpret {자세_표정} with restrained dignity, controlled hand placement, believable weight distribution, and quiet narrative tension as if from a prestige historical drama still.
- Typography and information layer: render the main title {포스터_제목} in large Korean type or brush-inspired lettering, place {부제} beneath it, add {세로_문구} as a vertical side phrase, and place event details in a legible bottom credit area.
- Decorative poster layer: add dancheong-inspired line ornaments, cloud motifs, plum blossom petals, subtle hanji fiber texture, period-pattern dividers, small ticket-info label, and a sponsor/credit strip designed as promotional poster graphics rather than official certification.
- Final polish: blend the character, architecture, typography, and event information into a refined Korean historical-film key art look with realistic depth separation, painterly cinematic atmosphere, and period-authentic storytelling.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard, Noto Sans KR, or a refined Korean serif for informational text; main title may use elegant brush-calligraphy styling while all smaller details remain clean and readable.
- Color palette: {색감} with deep ink black, muted gold, warm ochre, teal-blue, pearl white, aged paper beige, and selective crimson accents inspired by traditional pigments.
- Poster text hierarchy: {포스터_제목} is dominant, {부제} is secondary, {세로_문구} reads as poetic side copy, and the lower band includes date, venue, ticket, sponsor, contact, and production-credit information.
- Graphic details: use soft contact shadow under the figure, 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 18% opacity; add tactile paper grain, fabric texture, roof-tile rhythm, carved wood details, and atmospheric particles in the light.
- Historical design tone: refined, premium, cinematic, and culturally respectful, combining realistic concept art with high-end Korean poster layout.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: cinematic full-frame 85mm f/1.8 portrait perspective, shallow depth of field, subject sharp and background gently softened.
- Lighting: overcast diffused daylight or soft window light from upper-left at 45°, with a faint warm bounce on the face and garment highlights.
- Color grade: Korean period-film palette with ink-black shadows, muted gold mids, teal-green accents, pearl highlights, and slightly desaturated filmic contrast.
- Rendering quality: high-resolution cinematic concept art, realistic textile weave, nuanced facial shading, detailed hanok/palace surfaces, soft atmospheric haze, and print-ready vertical poster clarity.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean historical drama key art — a refined film-poster atmosphere reminiscent of a prestige K-drama still, cultural festival poster, and museum exhibition promotional artwork, with quiet dignity, seasonal lyricism, and narrative anticipation.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: render clear Korean text such as "{포스터_제목}", "{부제}", "{세로_문구}", "{행사명}", "{일시}", "{장소}", "{관람_정보}", "{주최_후원}", "{문의}" without broken glyphs.
- Default text example must be legible if used: "조선의 봄", "왕의 뜰에 매화가 피다", "봄빛 아래, 숨겨진 약속", "궁중문화 특별전", "2026.05.14 목 19:30", "경복궁 흥례문 앞 특설무대", "전석 ₩25,000 · 예매 1544-0000", "주최 한빛문화재단 · 후원 서울문화관광", "문의 02-1234-5678".
- Anatomy/layout invariants: Korean facial proportions must remain natural; hands must be anatomically correct with exactly 5 fingers per hand; hanbok layers, collars, sleeve widths, belts, headwear, and shoe geometry must be historically plausible.
- Era authenticity: clothing, accessories, household objects, architecture, tableware, writing tools, textile patterns, and decorative motifs must match the selected period in {시대_인물}; any ticket or sponsor information should appear as poster graphics, not as physical objects inside the historical scene.
- Print-readiness: maintain vertical {비율_사이즈} composition, legible title and event details, crisp character silhouette through lighting and depth, and cohesive integration of typography with the cinematic artwork.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or real-person face copying
- Sexualized styling, gore, or sensationalized violence

[추천·추정·시즌·품종·MBTI 등 결과] 결 매번 다르게 자체 생성합니다.

- 아래 옵션 (디자인 톤·색·언어·길이 등) 만 사용자가 customize 합니다.

[INPUT]
- reference_image: {참고 이미지}
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean pet memorial illustration poster, vertical framed artwork for {용도}.
Turn the reference pet photo into a warm, gentle keepsake illustration that preserves the animal’s breed, fur color, expression, and pose while adding realistic commemorative poster details such as a nameplate, date label, short caption, decorative tags, and frame-ready print finishing.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject placement: {반려동물} occupies the center 55–60% of the frame, with the head slightly above center and the body fully visible in a polished portrait composition.
- Background treatment: soft beige textured art paper backdrop with {배경_모티프} elements surrounding the pet naturally, including small grass strokes, tiny flowers, warm sunlight flecks, and hand-painted memory-card accents.
- Header detail: place a small upper label reading “{상단라벨}” with {날짜} and {장소} nearby, styled like a delicate keepsake card annotation.
- Nameplate area: include a refined lower nameplate with “{반려동물_이름}” as the primary text, plus a smaller line for “{품종정보}”.
- Message area: place “{메시지}” near the lower 12–15% of the canvas in a readable caption block, with a small heart, paw icon, or ribbon divider integrated into the design.
- Decorative memorial details: add {장식태그} as tiny handwritten-style labels or sticker-like paper tags near the lower corners, plus a small date stamp “{기념일스탬프}”.
- If included, {프레임_액자_mockup} should appear as a natural wood frame preview with paper texture, soft shadow, and a small gallery-style label beneath the print.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Subject rendering: depict {반려동물} as the clear hero of the composition, matching the original photo’s species, coat tone, facial expression, and body posture as faithfully as possible.
2. Illustration treatment: apply {일러스트톤} with soft watercolor fills, delicate digital paint blending, and thin hand-drawn line accents that keep the image gentle and sentimental.
3. Background scene: build a calm garden-like setting using {배경_모티프}, with layered grass hints, small flowers, faint golden dust motes, paper grain, and a warm sunlit atmosphere.
4. Keepsake typography: render the name, date, location, breed info, and message as integrated poster typography, using clean Korean letterforms and carefully aligned lines.
5. Caption and micro-details: include a small note reading “{짧은캡션}”, a tiny paw-print divider, a memory ribbon, and a small gallery label such as “{액자라벨}” when the frame mockup is active.
6. Product presentation: if {용도} suggests memorial or birthday framing, make the artwork look like a finished premium print suitable for a tabletop frame, wall display, gift packaging preview, or online order sample.
7. Optional mockup: when {프레임_액자_mockup} is used, show a simple natural wood frame edge, visible mat board or paper edge, and realistic tabletop/wall shadowing while keeping the pet portrait dominant.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard SemiBold or Noto Sans KR Medium for Korean text, with the pet name around 42–56px equivalent, the main message around 28–40px equivalent, and micro labels around 16–22px equivalent; keep line breaks balanced and readable.
- Color palette: warm beige #F3E7D3, soft cream #FFF8EE, muted brown #8A6247, grass green #B9C9A0, pastel floral pink #E8C7C1, gentle sky blue #CFE1F2, soft gold #D8B46A.
- Poster finishing: use watercolor paper grain, soft ink bleed at flower edges, hand-painted paw icons, a light ribbon divider, and warm print texture.
- Frame and shadow: if a frame or print edge is shown, use a subtle 3–4px soft drop shadow with 10–15% opacity and a very light paper edge texture.
- Text hierarchy: pet name first, message second, date/location/breed info third, decorative tags fourth; all Korean text must be crisp, centered or intentionally aligned, and fully inside the poster area.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial portrait look inspired by a 85mm f/1.8 shallow-depth studio capture translated into illustration framing, with the pet centered and softly isolated from the background.
- Lighting: soft window light from upper-left at about 45°, with a faint warm fill from the right to keep the fur contours gentle and dimensional.
- Color grade: creamy beige + muted brown + soft spring green, with low saturation and slightly diffused highlights.
- Rendering finish: premium watercolor editorial print, delicate pen-line contouring, natural paper fibers, gentle vignette around the frame edge, and realistic framed-art mockup depth when requested.

[6. MOOD]
Quiet memorial editorial illustration — like a tender Kinfolk-style keepsake print blended with a handcrafted Korean pet remembrance card, warm birthday memory, soft garden light, and affectionate family-album sentiment.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문구를 정확히 렌더링해야 함:
  - {메시지}
  - {반려동물_이름}
  - {상단라벨}
  - {날짜}
  - {장소}
  - {품종정보}
  - {짧은캡션}
  - {기념일스탬프}
  - {장식태그}
  - {액자라벨}
- Preserve the pet’s breed, coat color, facial expression, and pose from the reference image as accurately as possible.
- Keep the overall tone gentle, lovable, and non-graphic; no sadness exaggeration, no dramatic contrast, no aggressive styling.
- Make every visible Korean label legible, correctly spelled, and naturally placed as part of a realistic printed keepsake poster.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications or government-like emblems
- Broken Korean characters, mojibake, or misspelled Korean text
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized human likeness swaps

[INPUT]

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean meditation quote card for social media, vertical Instagram-saveable poster layout, centered quote typography with gentle illustrative accents and realistic post-card details.
Designed as a quiet scripture / wisdom / poem card that can hold one short quote, its source, a small account identity, date label, hashtags, and save/share micro UI cues.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center stack composition: {인용} is the main hero text placed near the visual center, occupying about 32–40% of the frame height, with {출처} beneath it in small type.
- Build a real social quote-card feel: top metadata line with {계정명}, {날짜}, and {위치}; bottom caption strip with {보조문구}, {해시태그}, and small save/share micro icons.
- Background: warm paper-like beige surface with subtle grain, soft vignette at the edges, faint fiber speckles, and a gentle printed stationery texture.
- Decorative accents: {일러스트 모티프} placed off-center near the lower third, supported by small organic marks, washi-tape-like corner tabs, and a thin warm-gray hairline frame that echoes {테마}.
- Use {테마}, {일러스트 모티프}, {컬러}, {폰트 톤} as adjustable concept anchors while keeping the quote as the clearest focal point.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Top metadata zone (10–14%): add a small left-aligned handle “{계정명}”, a right-aligned date “{날짜}”, and a small location label “{위치}”; include a tiny leaf, moon, ripple, or ink-dot tag beside the handle.
- Main quote zone (center 35–42%): render {인용} in large Korean calligraphic display type, stacked naturally into 1–3 lines, with careful line breaks that preserve readability and a meditative pace.
- Source zone (below quote, 6–8%): place {출처} in a smaller clean sans-serif with modest tracking, aligned center, separated by a small decorative dot or faint ink divider.
- Illustration zone (lower third 18–24%): add {일러스트 모티프} as a soft watercolor, ink wash, or paper-cut style accent, integrated with printed paper grain and muted contours.
- Bottom social caption zone (8–12%): add “{보조문구}” in small Korean sans-serif, followed by “{해시태그}”; include tiny realistic UI marks such as ♡, 말풍선, 저장, 공유 icons and page indicator “{카드번호}”.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: main quote in a brush-calligraphy style reminiscent of hand-lettered editorial posters; source and metadata in Pretendard or Noto Sans KR, medium weight, small size, clean and restrained.
- Color palette: {컬러} with concrete tones such as #E9DDC8 beige, #A8B8A0 sage, #8D8A84 warm gray, #F6F1E8 off-white paper, and #6F776B muted olive ink.
- Add tactile stationery details: subtle paper fibers, faint ink bleed on calligraphy edges, soft printed registration texture, tiny pressed-flower or leaf fragments, and a delicate hairline frame with rounded corners.
- Decorative graphics should feel devotional and poetic rather than ceremonial: small ripples, petals, dots, thread-like lines, and translucent watercolor stains in low-saturation tones.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: flat-lay editorial poster look, simulated as a 50mm prime at f/5.6 for natural proportion and gentle depth separation.
- Lighting: soft diffused window light from upper-left at 45°, with almost no shadow density; add a faint fill from the right so the paper texture remains visible.
- Color grade: muted beige + sage + warm gray with low saturation, slightly lifted blacks, and a quiet analog-paper finish.

[6. MOOD]
Quiet devotional editorial — like a calm Korean stationery quote post, blending scripture-card sincerity, poetic meditation, and refined lifestyle magazine warmth.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 다음 문구가 정확히 보여야 함: “{인용}”, “{출처}”, “{계정명}”, “{날짜}”, “{위치}”, “{보조문구}”, “{해시태그}”, “{카드번호}”.
- The quote must be legible, correctly spaced, and line-broken in a natural Korean reading flow.
- Render the source line smaller than the quote and centered, while metadata and caption text remain readable at mobile-screen size.
- Maintain the hierarchy: quote first, source second, social-card details and illustration third.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or recognizable public figures

[1. PURPOSE]
Magazine-quality overhead flat lay food photograph, square layout for menu book, restaurant Instagram feed, and editorial food feature.
Create a realistic tabletop scene where plated dishes, serving ware, small menu-card typography, and natural dining details feel like a photographed restaurant spread rather than a sterile product shot.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center the main food arrangement across about 70% of the frame, with the primary dish slightly above center and side items distributed in a stable triangular balance.
- Use {음식 컨셉} as the focal menu set, arranged to read clearly from above with no perspective tilt.
- Build the scene on {플레이팅}, allowing the table grain, ceramic glaze, folded fabric, and small dining marks to remain visible and tactile.
- Place {보조 소품} around the dishes as natural restaurant-table details: utensils, napkin folds, herb sprigs, a small flower, wine glass reflections, tiny bread crumbs, and a few ingredient accents.
- Add a small printed menu card or receipt-style placard near the lower-right quadrant, partially tucked under a utensil or napkin, using {매장명}, {메뉴카드 제목}, dish names, prices, address, contact, and date.
- Keep all dish edges, utensils, card edges, and cloth lines aligned to {카메라 시점} so the entire frame reads as a true top-down flat lay.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Hero food area (middle 55%): present {음식 컨셉} as the main editorial spread, with the largest plate acting as the visual anchor and the side dishes forming a natural dining rhythm.
- Surface layer: apply {플레이팅} with realistic wood grain, ceramic sheen, soft linen texture, faint cutlery reflections, and warm tabletop depth.
- Prop ring: place {보조 소품} as secondary accents, using one richer cluster near the lower-left and a smaller counterbalance near the upper-right, including believable small ingredients from the dishes.
- Menu-card detail: include a cream paper card with thin divider lines, small icons, prices, and contact details; it should feel like an actual restaurant menu insert photographed on the table.
- Camera read: maintain {카메라 시점} so every dish looks flattened and evenly oriented, with no dramatic depth distortion.
- Color emphasis: render {색감} through natural ingredient tones, warm neutrals, tomato red, basil green, wine burgundy, toasted bread, and subtle contrast between food, table, props, and printed paper.
- Usage framing: compose for {용도} and {비율/사이즈}, making the scene suitable as both a menu-book top shot and a polished social media food image.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: include only realistic printed typography on the menu card/receipt placard, not a floating digital overlay; use clean Korean editorial sans-serif for headings and small serif or monospaced receipt-style text for prices.
- Menu-card content: show store name, three menu lines with prices, address, contact, date, and a short editorial label; use thin dividers and tiny decorative food icons such as a fork, leaf, or wine glass.
- Color palette: warm beige, walnut brown, ceramic ivory, tomato red, basil green, wine burgundy, muted charcoal ink, and the appetizing mid-tone food colors from {색감}.
- Decorative details: allow realistic table styling such as linen folds, herb flakes, bread crumbs, olive-oil sheen, condensation on glass, ceramic rim highlights, and small shadows from raised plates.
- Border/shadow: soft natural shadows beneath plates, utensils, card, and glass, approximately 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity, with crisp object edges and a gentle editorial contrast curve.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: full-frame camera with a 35mm lens at f/8, perfectly perpendicular overhead setup for a flat lay editorial look.
- Lighting: diffuse natural window light from upper-left at about 45°, with gentle fill from the right and soft shadow falloff under plates, glassware, cutlery, and the paper menu card.
- Color grade: warm editorial neutrals with slightly boosted food saturation, clean white balance, realistic highlights on sauces and ceramics, and a subtle filmic contrast curve.
- Material realism: pasta sauce should look creamy and dimensional, salad tomatoes glossy, basil fresh, bread crust crisp, wine translucent burgundy, and paper typography printed into the card surface.

[6. MOOD]
Korean food magazine editorial — warm restaurant tabletop styling, appetizing but refined, like a premium menu-book top shot with lived-in dining details and polished social feed appeal.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the printed menu card must contain clean, readable Korean text with no broken characters.
- Render the menu card text exactly as: "{매장명}" / "{메뉴카드 제목}" / "{메뉴1}  {가격1}" / "{메뉴2}  {가격2}" / "{메뉴3}  {가격3}" / "{주소}" / "{연락처}" / "{촬영 날짜}".
- Layout invariant: maintain a true 90-degree overhead view, with all plates, cutlery, paper card, glass, and props appearing evenly oriented and not skewed.
- Composition invariant: the food set must remain tidy, balanced, magazine-ready, and realistic, with believable shadows, natural tabletop textures, and appetizing ingredient detail.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized portrait likenesses

[1. PURPOSE]
Luxury wedding and honeymoon moodboard poster, vertical editorial collage for concept planning, location selection, styling approval, and vendor briefing. Combine miniature photo cutouts, palette swatches, fabric samples, handwritten Korean labels, date/location tags, and a small production note area into a polished magazine-style planning board.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Single-page vertical poster with an editorial planning-board structure: top title band 14%, main collage field 56%, right-side palette/checklist column 18%, bottom production caption band 12%.
- Center the most important miniature couple scene at mid-frame, with surrounding dress, location, bouquet, prop, fabric, and detail-shot tiles arranged as layered editorial cards.
- Background surface should feel like premium matte art paper in warm ivory, with subtle paper grain, vellum overlays, washi-tape tabs, pin marks, and soft shadow separation between panels.
- The layout should feel curated and realistic, like an actual wedding planner’s concept board used during a studio meeting, with readable labels, small notes, and tactile material samples.
- Use {촬영 컨셉}, {로케이션}, {드레스/한복}, {부케/소품}, {컬러 팔레트}, {핵심 카피}, {촬영일}, {촬영 시간}, {플래너명}, {스튜디오명}, {문의 연락처}, {프로젝트 번호} as user-editable content anchors throughout the composition.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header zone: place {핵심 카피} centered near the top in an elegant serif masthead style, with thin divider lines above and below, black ink on ivory paper. Add a small issue-style planning code on the upper right reading {프로젝트 번호}, and a tiny date label reading {촬영일}.
2. Main collage zone: build 6–8 small photo-style tiles showing {드레스/한복}, {로케이션}, {부케/소품}, a miniature couple shot, close-up hands with rings, table styling, and a fabric/texture detail. Use slight rotations of 1–3 degrees for an intentional editorial rhythm.
3. Concept panel: present {촬영 컨셉} as a mood label card with concise Korean text, paired with an elegant line illustration cue such as a hanok roof curve, pearl pin, or floral stem, plus a soft gold accent line.
4. Location panel: show {로케이션} as a framed destination note with a tiny architectural or landscape thumbnail, a small map-strip graphic, and a schedule tag reading “촬영 시간 {촬영 시간}”.
5. Styling panel: feature {드레스/한복} and {부케/소품} in separate mini cards, using realistic fabric folds, pearl-like highlights, dried-flower texture, ribbon edges, ceramic matte surfaces, and small handwritten annotations.
6. Color palette zone: render {컬러 팔레트} as 5 aligned swatches with clean Korean labels beneath each swatch, including ivory, beige, lavender, sage, and muted gold tones. Add tiny CMYK-like color notes for a professional planning-board feel.
7. Production note area: include a compact vendor credit block with “PLANNER {플래너명}”, “STUDIO {스튜디오명}”, and “CONTACT {문의 연락처}”. Add a small checklist with Korean items such as “의상 피팅”, “부케 픽업”, “한옥 촬영 허가”, “우천 플랜”.
8. Caption zone: repeat {핵심 카피} in a smaller subheadline style at the bottom, followed by a poetic Korean caption line and a restrained barcode-like planning mark for editorial realism.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Noto Serif KR or Nanum Myeongjo for the main title, Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for labels, bold 700 for headings and 400–500 for body text; title size large, labels compact and highly legible.
- Color palette: derive the page from {컬러 팔레트}, with ivory #F7F1E8, beige #DCC7A6, lavender #C9B7D8, sage #AEBFA5, and muted gold #C8A96A.
- Border/shadow: use thin warm-gray rules, soft drop shadows with 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity, lightly rounded corners on collage cards, translucent vellum note strips, gold foil-like divider accents, and small adhesive tape textures.
- Graphic details: add realistic planning-board elements such as numbered tile captions, tiny arrow callouts, fabric swatch pins, location route marks, and handwritten-style Korean memo tags while keeping all text readable.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial still-life look, 50mm prime for product tiles and 85mm portrait look for the couple miniature, shallow depth of field around f/2.8 to f/4 for a refined magazine feel.
- Lighting: soft diffused window light from upper-left at 45°, with a faint warm fill from lower-right to keep gold and beige tones luminous without harsh contrast.
- Color grade: ivory + beige + lavender + sage + muted gold, with gentle film-like contrast and slightly softened highlights.
- Material realism: matte art paper, semi-gloss mini photo prints, pressed-flower shadows, pearl reflections, cotton hanbok texture, organza veil translucency, ceramic prop surfaces, and warm metallic ink accents.

[6. MOOD]
Premium wedding magazine editorial — a Marie Claire Wedding and Wedding 21 inspired planning board with refined Korean luxury styling, tactile stationery details, calm romantic storytelling, and believable studio-planning information.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 표기할 문구는 “{핵심 카피}”, “{촬영 컨셉}”, “{로케이션}”, “{드레스/한복}”, “{부케/소품}”, “{컬러 팔레트}”, “{촬영일}”, “{촬영 시간}”, “{플래너명}”, “{스튜디오명}”, “{문의 연락처}”, “{프로젝트 번호}”.
- Rendered Korean labels should include: “컨셉”, “로케이션”, “의상”, “부케·소품”, “컬러 팔레트”, “촬영 일정”, “플래너 노트”, “체크리스트”, “문의”.
- Layout invariants: the canvas must contain a clear miniature collage, visible color swatches, realistic planning notes, vendor/contact block, date/location tag, and readable Korean labels; all text must be crisp and correctly spaced.
- Mini photo tiles should look like coordinated wedding editorial frames from the same shoot direction, with consistent lighting, matching color grade, and believable paper/photo material depth.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Illegible Korean typography
- Celebrity composites or recognizable real-person impersonation
