[1. PURPOSE]
Create a one-page small-business store interior concept board for a café startup or renovation briefing, formatted like a real designer moodboard / Pinterest-style presentation sheet photographed as a premium client proposal.
The board should communicate concept, palette, materials, props, lighting, zoning, and spatial direction at a glance, with realistic printed labels, sample tags, memo notes, and small presentation details that make it feel ready for an actual store planning meeting.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Vertical single-page board with a 4-part editorial grid: color swatches, material miniatures, interior sketch/photo panel, and signature prop/detail miniatures, plus a compact project-info strip.
- Main title area at the top 12–15% of the canvas, with the concept name {매장 종류·이름} centered or left-aligned depending on the grid balance.
- Background: warm off-white premium paper texture with subtle grain, faint pencil guide marks, taped sample corners, tiny registration ticks, and realistic printed presentation-board depth.
- Use {컨셉 키워드}, {컬러 팔레트}, {자재}, {소품·디테일}, {레이아웃}, {비율/사이즈} as the content anchors for all panels.
- Add authentic client-deck details such as project code, date stamp, small page number, scale note, budget memo, designer credit, and contact-style footer text, while keeping the core board readable.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header zone (top 12–15%): Set the title “{매장 종류·이름}” in a bold but refined Korean display style. Add a compact subtitle using {컨셉 키워드}, plus small metadata: “INTERIOR CONCEPT BOARD”, “VOL.01”, “2026.05”, “제안서 초안”, “Designer: 스튜디오 온도”, and a tiny project code such as “SB-168 / LOCAL SHOP RENOVATION”.
2. Project-info strip: Beneath the title or along the right edge, include small realistic labels: “매장 타입”, “컨셉 키워드”, “면적/비율”, “동선 요약”, “예상 공사 포인트”, with Korean text referencing {매장 종류·이름}, {컨셉 키워드}, {레이아웃}, and {비율/사이즈}. Include a tiny QR-like square and barcode-style reference area as design-deck details, not as official certification.
3. Color swatch panel: Place 4–6 horizontal or square swatches with visible HEX labels and Korean color names; use the tones implied by {컬러 팔레트}. Add printed chip codes and notes such as “MAIN WALL”, “COUNTER”, “POINT FABRIC”, “PLANT ACCENT”, with realistic paper shadows and slight ink texture.
4. Material panel: Show tactile material samples for {자재} as miniature photo tiles, cutout cards, or overlapping physical sample chips, including wood grain, painted wall texture, metal detail, stone or tile surface, fabric/leather option, and a light reflective surface if needed. Add tiny Korean captions such as “상판 후보”, “벽면 마감”, “가구 프레임”, “손잡이 디테일”.
5. Interior concept panel: Include a refined interior sketch or reference-image style view of the store layout, reflecting {컨셉 키워드} with furniture placement, wall finish, counter form, shelving, lighting fixtures, menu board, entrance view, plant accents, and customer circulation. Add believable callout arrows and labels such as “주문 동선”, “픽업 존”, “2인석”, “포토월”, “수납 선반”.
6. Floor-plan / zoning inset: Add a small simplified floor plan thumbnail based on {레이아웃}, with counter, seating, entrance, service path, and back-bar/storage zones. Include scale text such as “SCALE 1:80”, “동선 폭 900mm”, and “좌석 비율 {비율/사이즈}”.
7. Prop/detail panel: Display miniature lifestyle props from {소품·디테일} as arranged cutouts or small photo cards, such as plants, pendant lighting, ceramic cup, linen curtain, menu stand, vintage wall clock, framed coffee illustration, basket, signage plaque, or tray details. Add sticker-like labels and subtle handwritten memo notes in Korean.
8. Footer / proposal note: Add a slim footer line with “CLIENT REVIEW COPY”, “문의 02-000-1680”, “서울 로컬 상권 테스트”, “page 01 / concept direction”, and a short Korean CTA-style note such as “현장 실측 후 자재 사양 확정”.
9. Layout discipline: Keep all sections aligned in a polished designer grid with consistent gutters, visible hierarchy, label readability, and layered editorial realism; the board should feel like a designer’s client proposal page based on {레이아웃}, with real printed artifacts rather than a sterile mockup.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for Korean labels, Inter or Helvetica Neue for English/HEX labels; use bold 700 for title, medium 500 for section labels, and 18–28px equivalent sizing for clarity. Use smaller 9–12pt-equivalent captions for project codes, material tags, footer notes, and callouts.
- Color palette: cream #F6F1E8, wood brown #B88A5A, deep brown #5A3E2B, warm beige #D8C7B4, plant green #6F8B5B, charcoal #2E2A27.
- Border/shadow: thin 1px neutral border around tiles, soft drop shadow 0 6px 18px rgba(0,0,0,0.10), subtle paper edge contrast, gentle tile layering, realistic sample-card thickness, and soft contact shadows.
- Graphic details: add fine divider rules, corner labels, annotation arrows, tape strips, clipped material tags, tiny numbering marks, and presentation-sheet microcopy that support the interior concept without changing the subject.
- Text rendered in the image should be mostly Korean with compact English technical labels where appropriate, matching a professional Seoul-based interior studio proposal.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial product-board look, simulated 50mm lens perspective with gentle flat-lay composition, crisp print detail, high-resolution scanned presentation aesthetic.
- Lighting: soft diffused studio light from upper-left at 45°, mild fill from right, realistic paper and material shadows, readable grain on wood, fabric, tile, paint, and metal surfaces.
- Color grade: warm cream + wood + muted green + deep coffee-brown, with low saturation and clean neutral balance.
- Rendering quality: highly detailed realistic printed board, believable paper fibers, tactile material samples, crisp Korean typography, accurate grid alignment, and subtle depth between overlapping cards.

[6. MOOD]
Premium interior design proposal board — a polished café or small-shop concept presentation with the warmth of a Kinfolk-style editorial spread, the practicality of a designer client deck, and the credibility of a real renovation briefing package.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: “{매장 종류·이름}”, “{컨셉 키워드}”, “{컬러 팔레트}”, “{자재}”, “{소품·디테일}”, “{레이아웃}”, “{비율/사이즈}”.
- Include realistic Korean deck text such as “INTERIOR CONCEPT BOARD”, “제안서 초안”, “컬러 팔레트”, “자재 샘플”, “공간 스케치”, “소품 디테일”, “주문 동선”, “픽업 존”, “현장 실측 후 자재 사양 확정”.
- Each panel must remain visually separated and easy to read, with labels, callouts, material chips, and image tiles placed in a coherent hierarchy.
- HEX labels must be legible and paired with the correct Korean color name in each swatch.
- If any sketched interior view is included, the perspective must be coherent and architectural lines must remain straight and believable.
- The result should look like a real printed concept board for {매장 종류·이름}, not a blank template.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean blog and KakaoView store header visual for a salon content post, designed as a wide editorial hero image with realistic local-business information layered over a warm photographic cover.
Built for Naver Blog, KakaoView, and Tistory cover use, with a polished promotional layout that feels like an actually published neighborhood salon article header.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Hero image fills the full 1536x1024 canvas as a wide blog header: use {키 비주얼} as the main photographic layer, showing real salon context such as storefront glass, reception counter, mirror station, hair tools, product shelves, stylist hands, or a client styling moment.
- Place {매장명} as the brand anchor, with {블로그 글 제목} as the largest headline and {부제/한 줄 설명} as the supporting line; add blog-like metadata so it reads as a real Korean content cover rather than a bare ad image.
- Include a small top label strip with {카테고리}, {지역명}, and {작성일}; use it like a blog category/date marker.
- Add a lower information band or corner card containing {대표시술}, {운영시간}, {예약문의}, and {해시태그}, with small divider dots or thin rules for a realistic store-header layout.
- Add a subtle blog identity area with {블로그명} and “Editor. {에디터명}” as a spine-credit-like editorial signature along one side or near the bottom edge.
- Apply {컨셉 톤} through warm tinting, typography plates, cream paper-like overlays, faint grain, salon-inspired decorative line art, small scissors/comb icons, and layered translucent shapes that support readability.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Background layer — Render {키 비주얼} as the base image with natural salon detail preserved: warm wood, beige walls, mirror reflections, towels, styling chair texture, product bottles, soft daylight, and a lived-in premium local-shop atmosphere.
2. Top metadata strip — Place “{카테고리} · {지역명} · {작성일}” in small Korean text near the upper-left or upper-right, using a cream capsule or narrow ribbon over the photo.
3. Main headline zone — Set {블로그 글 제목} in a large Korean headline across the most readable central-left or central-right area, with strong contrast against the photo using a translucent cocoa or cream text plate if needed.
4. Supporting line zone — Place {부제/한 줄 설명} directly under the headline in a smaller size, aligned to the headline; let it feel like a blog post deck line rather than a banner slogan.
5. Brand signature zone — Add {매장명} as a small label, stamp-style badge, or editorial logo text near the headline cluster; include “BLOG HEADER” or “KAKAO VIEW” as a tiny interface-like tag if composition allows.
6. Practical info zone — Add a compact bottom band with “대표시술 {대표시술}”, “운영 {운영시간}”, “예약 {예약문의}”, plus {해시태그}; separate items with thin vertical dividers, small dots, or beige rounded tags.
7. Editorial credit zone — Place “{블로그명} / Editor. {에디터명}” as a small vertical or horizontal side credit, imitating a magazine-cover spine credit adapted for a blog header.
8. Size adaptation — Keep the headline and main store information comfortably readable at 1536x1024 and still recognizable when cropped by blog or KakaoView preview thumbnails.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard SemiBold for the headline, Pretendard Medium or Noto Sans KR for the subtitle, and Pretendard Regular for metadata, tags, and editorial credit; headline around 64–84px feel, subtitle around 28–36px feel, metadata around 18–24px feel.
- Color palette: warm beige #E8D8C6, cocoa brown #6A4E3B, soft cream #F6F0E8, muted taupe #B59B86, deep charcoal #2E2622, with occasional muted terracotta or dusty rose accents for salon warmth.
- Layout details: use semi-transparent text plates at about 55–70% opacity, rounded corners, fine divider lines, small tag capsules, subtle paper grain, and delicate salon-themed decorative graphics such as a comb outline, hair wave line, or tiny scissors icon.
- Border/shadow: use soft text shadow only where needed, 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 18% opacity; plates and tags may cast a very light editorial card shadow so the header feels layered and tactile.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: realistic commercial photography look, 50mm f/1.8 or 85mm f/2 framing, depending on whether {키 비주얼} is an exterior shot or a stylist work shot.
- Lighting: soft daylight or diffused indoor window light from the upper-left at roughly 45°, with gentle fill on the shadow side and controlled reflections on mirrors, glass doors, and product bottles.
- Color grade: warm cream + beige + light brown, with restrained saturation and natural skin-tone / wood-tone rendering for a polished Korean local-business blog aesthetic.
- Image texture: realistic store photography with visible material details such as wood grain, fabric chair texture, mirror highlights, hair-tool metal, signage vinyl, and softly blurred background depth.

[6. MOOD]
Korean local salon editorial header — warm, trustworthy, and publish-ready, combining neighborhood store realism with the refined feeling of a lifestyle magazine feature and a modern Naver Blog/KakaoView cover.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문구가 정확히 보여야 함:
  - {매장명}
  - {블로그 글 제목}
  - {부제/한 줄 설명}
  - {카테고리} · {지역명} · {작성일}
  - 대표시술 {대표시술} / 운영 {운영시간} / 예약 {예약문의}
  - {해시태그}
  - {블로그명} / Editor. {에디터명}
- Header hierarchy must be clear: one dominant headline, one subordinate description, one small brand label, and secondary metadata/info elements.
- Text must remain fully legible over the photo with no broken spacing or overlapped Korean characters.
- The visual should read like a genuine Korean blog/KakaoView store header for a salon review or promotion article, with realistic store details and useful local-business information.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or misleading endorsement photos

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean café merchandise mockup catalog image, multi-item tabletop presentation for promotional use.
Showcase a branded table mat, cup holder sleeve, and paper coaster together in one realistic retail-style composition, styled like an actual café counter scene prepared for a seasonal goods launch.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Single wide canvas with the tabletop occupying about 78% of the frame, slightly angled top-down view for a catalog look.
- Main hero zone: the table mat spreads across the lower half, with the cup holder sleeve placed on a warm coffee cup near center-right, and the paper coaster visible near the front-left or partly under the drink.
- Background treatment: {배경} with a real wooden table surface, visible grain, tiny natural scratches, warm neutral indoor ambience, and softly blurred café surroundings such as a counter edge, menu board tones, or window reflection.
- Add realistic retail context around the goods: a small folded launch card, a thin receipt strip, a menu/pricelist corner, a kraft paper tag, and {추가 소품} arranged naturally around the branded set.
- Use {매장명/BI}, {굿즈 종류}, {디자인 모티프}, {배경}, {추가 소품}, {비율/사이즈} as the customizable content anchors, but keep the overall mockup layout consistent with a premium café merchandise showcase.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Hero product arrangement: place the table mat first as the base layer, aligned with the table perspective, showing its full printed surface, trim line, paper thickness, and {비율/사이즈} proportions.
- Cup area: position a ceramic coffee cup and cup holder sleeve slightly above the mat center; the sleeve wraps naturally around the cup, with visible paper seam, slight fiber texture, and a soft contact shadow on the mat.
- Coaster detail: show one coaster near the cup or under a small dessert plate so the coaster design remains readable; include a visible rim, thickness, tiny paper texture, and printed motif matching the mat and sleeve.
- Branding application: apply the same {디자인 모티프} across all items so the table mat, sleeve, and coaster feel like one coordinated set from {매장명/BI}; include small Korean copy such as “오늘의 한 잔”, “시즌 굿즈”, “매장 한정”, and “따뜻한 하루를 담다” where appropriate.
- Retail information elements: add a small tabletop goods card that reads “굿즈 세트 ₩12,000”, “컵홀더 · 코스터 · 테이블 매트”, “2026 봄 에디션”, and a tiny contact line like “@cafe_goods” or “서울 성동구 카페거리 12”.
- Menu/pricelist detail: include a partially visible café menu slip with 3–4 Korean items and prices, for example “아메리카노 ₩4,500”, “라떼 ₩5,300”, “플랫화이트 ₩5,500”, “휘낭시에 ₩3,800”, printed small but legible.
- Supporting props: add {추가 소품} in a believable café tabletop way, such as a teaspoon, linen napkin, sugar packet, small dessert fork, flower stem, coffee beans, or pastry crumb details, all physically resting on the table.
- Scene realism: ensure the objects rest physically on the table with accurate perspective, paper thickness, slight curl on edges if needed, tiny imperfections in ink and fiber, believable contact shadows, and realistic overlap between items.
- Presentation tone: make it feel like a social-media café merchandise showcase and catalog mockup photographed during an actual shop launch, with the brand system easy to recognize through repeated typography, motif, and color.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard and Noto Sans KR, medium to semibold for the small Korean signature, 18–26px equivalent on the mat, crisp print edges, with smaller 8–12px equivalent text for menu slip, receipt, and goods card details.
- Color palette: use the {매장명/BI} palette as the main anchor, with beige, warm cream, soft green, muted brown, paper white, roasted coffee tones, and subtle accent colors derived from {디자인 모티프}.
- Border/shadow: soft drop shadow with 4px vertical offset, 14px blur, 18% opacity; no harsh cutout edges; paper surfaces should look matte, tactile, and slightly textured.
- Print finish: flat printed ink on paper goods, low gloss, visible paper grain, natural ink absorption, accurate registration, and realistic edges on the sleeve, coaster, tag, receipt, and table mat.
- Surface detail: include warm wood grain, cup ceramic glaze, coffee surface reflection, dessert texture if present, tiny paper fibers, and gentle wear on table corners to make the scene feel photographed rather than generated.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 35mm full-frame lens at f/4.5, top-down-ish angled product photography, realistic catalog framing.
- Lighting: natural window light from upper-left at about 45°, gentle fill from lower-right, soft shadows with no hard specular glare.
- Color grade: warm beige + sage green + coffee brown, lightly desaturated editorial finish, clean indoor daylight balance.

[6. MOOD]
Premium café merchandise editorial — feels like a modern Kinfolk-style tabletop product spread mixed with a real Korean café shop reveal, warm, tactile, curated, and ready for an Instagram goods announcement.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the rendered image must correctly show the small Korean signature and any brand text from {매장명/BI} without broken characters.
- Render Korean text strings clearly: “오늘의 한 잔”, “시즌 굿즈”, “매장 한정”, “굿즈 세트 ₩12,000”, “컵홀더 · 코스터 · 테이블 매트”, and the menu prices must not be garbled.
- All three goods must be clearly identifiable as separate items: table mat, cup holder sleeve, and paper coaster.
- The same design system from {디자인 모티프} must appear consistently across every item in the set.
- Any included coffee cup, dessert, receipt, menu slip, tag, plant, or {추가 소품} must look physically plausible on the tabletop with correct shadows, scale, and perspective.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

studio:prompts3:ours-165.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
네이버 플레이스·구글 비즈니스 등록용 {매장명} {업종} 매장 사진 4컷 세트. {비율/사이즈} 2x2 균등 그리드 한 캔버스 구성으로, 외관·내부·대표 메뉴·분위기를 실제 방문 전에 확인할 수 있게 보여주는 즉시 등록용 실사 톤 이미지.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Canvas layout: 2x2 equal grid, each panel with identical margins and gutters, straight vertical/horizontal dividers, balanced business-listing presentation.
- Subject hierarchy: panel 1 highlights {외관 컨셉} with the store exterior as the main subject; panel 2 shows {내부 구성} with seating, tabletop detail, and wall menu context; panel 3 presents {대표 메뉴 구성} as a close-up food hero; panel 4 captures {분위기} with staff and customer-facing warmth.
- Store identity: apply {매장명} and {업종} naturally through real storefront signage, door vinyl lettering, apron name tag, counter notice, menu board, receipt stand, or table tent where plausible.
- Real listing details: include small but readable Korean business information in-scene, such as {주소}, {연락처}, {영업시간}, {대표메뉴명}, {대표가격}, and {촬영일자}; these should feel printed on real shop materials rather than floating graphics.
- Labeling: each panel has a small Korean label placed at the top-left of the panel, readable and consistent: 외관, 내부, 대표 메뉴, 분위기.
- Background treatment: consistent real-world materials across all panels, with warm wood, charcoal trim, ivory walls, glass reflections, stainless utensils, menu paper, ceramic dishes, side-dish containers, floor texture, and practical restaurant lighting.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Panel 1 — 외관: photograph the exterior of {매장명} as a neat Korean restaurant storefront matching {외관 컨셉}; include a realistic signboard reading “{매장명}”, smaller category text “{업종}”, a door sticker reading “영업시간 {영업시간}”, a small address plaque “{주소}”, window reflections, entrance mat, potted plant, and a sidewalk edge in natural daylight.
- Panel 2 — 내부: show a compact dining interior with {내부 구성}; include two to three tables, aligned chairs, water bottle, chopsticks and spoon case, tissue box, side dishes already placed on one table, a wall menu board with Korean items and prices such as “{대표메뉴명} {대표가격}”, “김치찌개 9,000원”, “된장찌개 8,500원”, plus a small counter notice reading “예약·포장 문의 {연락처}”.
- Panel 3 — 대표 메뉴: place {대표 메뉴 구성} as the main close-up subject on a wooden table in sharp focus; show steam, glossy sauce texture, rice bowl, soup, kimchi, greens, pickled vegetables, metal spoon/chopsticks, a small printed table tent reading “대표 메뉴 {대표메뉴명} / {대표가격}”, and natural food reflections on ceramic plates.
- Panel 4 — 분위기: depict {분위기} through a staff member greeting politely near the entrance or service counter; include a customer coat or bag on a chair, warm ceiling lights, order counter, simple payment terminal, pickup shelf, and an in-scene caption card reading “{촬영일자} 촬영 · {매장명}”.
- Unification: all four panels must share the same time of day, white balance, photographic finish, and store materials so the set feels like one real location shoot for the same business.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard SemiBold for the panel labels, 20–24px on a 1024px canvas, black or near-black text with slight letter spacing for clarity.
- In-scene text: storefront sign, business hours, menu board, price tags, and contact stickers should use realistic Korean print styles, sized according to their distance from the camera.
- Color palette: warm wood brown, charcoal black, soft ivory, muted beige, stainless steel gray, ceramic white, kimchi red, leafy green, and natural daylight highlights; keep saturation moderate and consistent across all four panels.
- Divider/shadow: thin 1px divider lines in #E5E0D8 between panels; subtle soft shadow only if needed, 4px y-offset, 10px blur, 12% opacity.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: realistic commercial interior/exterior photography, full-frame DSLR or mirrorless look, 24mm for exterior and interior panels, 50mm for menu close-up, 35mm for the greeting scene; aperture around f/4 to f/5.6.
- Lighting: consistent natural daylight look with soft window light from upper-left at about 45°, gentle fill from the front, practical warm interior fixtures, believable glass reflections, no harsh flash, no dramatic rim light; keep shadows soft and believable.
- Color grade: neutral warm grade with slightly lifted shadows, ivory highlights, wood-brown mids, restrained black accents, natural food color, and realistic skin tones; avoid oversaturated reds or artificial contrast.

[6. MOOD]
Real Korean neighborhood restaurant editorial — reliable Naver Place featured-store photography with practical warmth, visible business information, appetizing menu detail, and a welcoming everyday dining atmosphere.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the panel labels must appear exactly as follows: 외관, 내부, 대표 메뉴, 분위기.
- Korean text accuracy: visible store text must match “{매장명}”, “{업종}”, “영업시간 {영업시간}”, “{주소}”, “예약·포장 문의 {연락처}”, “{대표메뉴명} {대표가격}”, and “{촬영일자} 촬영”.
- Layout invariant: all 4 panels must have equal size and consistent spacing, with no missing panel and no mismatched scene type.
- Image realism: the food, tables, storefront, printed signs, staff, and lighting must look like a real photographed Korean restaurant, not an illustration or 3D render.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications / verification badges
- Broken Korean characters or garbled menu text
- Celebrity composites or recognizable celebrity likenesses unless explicitly requested

studio:prompts3:ours-164.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean florist shop Instagram profile first-screen mockup, 3x3 grid feed design for social media planning and brand guide use.
A realistic, content-rich grid composition that shows how weekly posts can alternate product close-ups, copy cards, store moments, seasonal promotions, and interior shots while keeping one unified BI tone for {매장명/BI}.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center the 3x3 Instagram feed grid so it fills about 92% of the square canvas, with narrow gutters and a believable profile-planning board feel.
- Each cell should feel like a separate Instagram post tile, but all 9 tiles must share the same beige + sage green + soft pink brand palette from {컨셉 톤}.
- Use {매장명/BI} as the brand identity anchor across the grid, with repeated handle text, small logo marks, consistent typography, and coordinated color balance.
- Apply {레이아웃} as the structural framework; the mockup must read immediately as an Instagram first-screen preview in {비율/사이즈}.
- Background should be a warm off-white paper-like surface with subtle fiber texture, faint taped moodboard corners, soft botanical shadows, tiny pressed-petal details, and realistic print/post texture.
- Include small Instagram-card details inside selected tiles: @bomflower.garden, tiny save/share/comment-style micro icons, short hashtag lines, date labels, and campaign tags, all designed as part of the posts rather than phone UI chrome.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top-left tile: flower close-up post with ranunculus, tulips, and soft pink petals wrapped in translucent paper; add a small corner label reading “NEW ARRIVAL” and Korean caption “매일 새벽 도착”.
2. Top-middle tile: product close-up post showing stems, ribbon, water droplets, kraft wrapping paper, and a handwritten order tag; include tiny text “05. SPRING BUNCH” and hashtag line “#봄꽃 #오늘의꽃”.
3. Top-right tile: a text card tile with bold but friendly Korean copy using one phrase from {시그니처 카피 예시}; add small brand mark, date “2026.05”, and micro save/share icons at the bottom.
4. Middle-left tile: bouquet or wreath product detail tile, cropped close with premium editorial styling; include small price/info tag “5월 한정 화환 / 예약 ₩75,000~” and a tiny delivery note.
5. Middle-center tile: text-led campaign tile designed as a weekly content prompt card; include the main phrase “봄의 꽃”, subcopy “이번 주 추천 컬러: 세이지 그린”, a small slide indicator “02/09”, and a simple decorative flower-line illustration.
6. Middle-right tile: store interior tile showing shelving, counter, flower buckets, scissors, ribbon spools, order slips, ceramic vases, and warm natural daylight; add small location label “서울 성수동 플라워 스튜디오”.
7. Bottom-left tile: another flower close-up tile, different angle and bloom type for visual rhythm, with soft bokeh and a small caption strip “따뜻한 마음을 꽃에”.
8. Bottom-center tile: brand/social tile with handle-style copy from {시그니처 카피 예시}; include @bomflower.garden, “DM 예약 가능”, “월-토 10:00–19:00”, hashtag-like text, and tiny interaction icons.
9. Bottom-right tile: interior or counter-detail tile showing hands-free workspace with flower shears, twine, wrapping sheets, order notebook, ribbon rolls, and fresh flowers arranged for operational authenticity; include a small thank-you sticker “오늘도 피어나는 하루”.
10. Across all 9 tiles: maintain a unified tone, matched contrast, consistent crop style, recurring BI mark, and coherent monthly feed system based on {9컷 컨셉}.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard and Noto Sans KR, medium to bold weights, 18–44px equivalent depending on tile type; use clean sans-serif for readability and a slightly warmer handwritten accent only for labels, tags, and small captions.
- Color palette: beige #F3EBDD, sage green #B7C4A4, blush pink #E8C3C8, muted olive #8A9B7A, warm brown #6F5B4B, ivory #FAF7F0.
- Border/shadow: thin 1px separators between tiles, soft drop shadow 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 12% opacity, refined printed-card depth.
- Text layout should stay within grid-safe margins; Korean copy must be sharp, readable, and integrated with floral subjects through caption strips, stickers, labels, and cards.
- Add realistic florist-shop details such as wrapping tissue, handwritten order tags, ribbon, twine, small ceramic vases, flower buckets, delivery memo cards, and subtle paper grain where they naturally support the feed design.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: full-frame editorial photography look, 50mm f/1.8 for close-ups and 35mm f/2.8 for interior shots, crisp but soft-focus edges where appropriate.
- Lighting: soft window light from upper-left at 45°, slight fill from right using a white reflector, interior tiles with gentle ambient daylight and no harsh flash.
- Color grade: warm cream + sage + dusty pink with low-contrast tonal compression, like a Kinfolk-style florist editorial, with realistic petals, paper fibers, ceramic texture, and soft natural shadows.

[6. MOOD]
Premium boutique florist social feed — Kinfolk magazine spread meets quiet Aesop-style retail branding, warm neighborhood flower studio, seasonal May bouquet campaign, soft but commercially believable Instagram content planning board.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following verbatim Korean strings must appear correctly in the rendered image:
  - 봄꽃 화원 / 베이지+세이지 그린
  - 꽃 클로즈업 4 + 텍스트 카피 3 + 매장 인테리어 2 (균형있게)
  - 매일 새벽 도착
  - 봄의 꽃
  - 5월 한정 화환
  - 따뜻한 마음을 꽃에
  - @bomflower.garden
  - #봄꽃 #오늘의꽃
  - DM 예약 가능
  - 서울 성수동 플라워 스튜디오
- The 9 tiles must clearly read as a 3x3 Instagram grid mockup.
- All tiles must feel like one coherent BI system with the same palette and tone.
- Keep Korean typography sharp and fully legible.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

studio:prompts3:ours-163.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean store counter order/payment 안내 사인, one canvas showing both a flat printed design and a standing countertop mockup.
Print-ready BI signage for a café counter, with large Korean notice text, payment method icon row, QR code area, store information, and practical counter-use details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Left side (about 58% width): a fully 펼친 안내 사인 시안 laid out flat on a café counter tabletop, seen from a slight top-down angle, with paper grain, printed ink texture, and realistic edge shadows.
- Right side (about 42% width): the same sign standing on the counter in a clear acrylic holder, angled slightly toward camera for easy reading, with realistic paper thickness and reflection on the holder.
- Use {매장명} as the main brand name, {안내 메시지} as the dominant headline, {결제 방법} as the payment row, {QR 코드 자리} as the QR placeholder label, and {추가 안내} as the small footer note.
- Add realistic café-counter context around the mockup: a partial POS card reader, receipt roll edge, small loyalty stamp card, a ceramic cup rim, and warm wood surface details, all secondary to the sign.
- Background: calm café counter surface with beige paper texture, subtle wood grain, printed stationery feel, and {컨셉 톤} as the visual direction.
- Maintain a clear professional information hierarchy while allowing practical store details, small icons, dividers, badges, and café counter objects that naturally exist in this scene.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Top header area: place {매장명} in a compact brand mark zone, with a small caption line reading {안내 배지}; include a tiny date/store label such as {날짜 라벨} near the top corner.
- Main notice area: set {안내 메시지} as the largest text block, occupying the visual center of the sign; use bold, highly legible Korean typography with strong contrast.
- Payment information area: beneath the main notice, place {결제 방법} in a neat row with small rounded payment pictogram-style separators and a short label reading “결제 가능 수단”.
- QR zone: allocate a clearly boxed square/rectangle area labeled for {QR 코드 자리}, with a visible code-frame grid placeholder and a small instruction line reading {멤버십 안내}; position it near the lower-right or lower-center depending on balance.
- Store info band: add a slim lower information band with {영업시간}, {매장 주소}, {연락처}, and {와이파이 안내}, separated by thin dividers and tiny service icons.
- Footer note: place {추가 안내} as a smaller supporting line at the bottom with polite café guidance styling, plus a small SNS tag line {SNS 태그}.
- Mockup treatment: the standing version should show the exact same layout, same text hierarchy, same Korean wording, realistic thickness, paper edge shadow, and a transparent acrylic sign holder resting on the counter.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard ExtraBold for the main headline, Pretendard SemiBold for subtext and section labels, Noto Sans KR Regular for footer notes and store details; headline size should dominate clearly, with balanced tracking and crisp anti-aliased edges.
- Color palette: beige #F5EBDD, warm wood brown #8B6B4A, soft green accent #6F8F6A, dark charcoal #2E2E2E, off-white #FFFDF8; apply {컨셉 톤} consistently across both the flat design and mockup.
- Graphic system: thin 1px to 2px divider lines, rounded rectangle information chips, subtle green accent dots, payment icon capsules, small QR instruction arrow, and a gentle café-stationery pattern in the header or footer area.
- Border/shadow: thin printed border lines, soft drop shadow with 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 14% opacity for the standing mockup, natural contact shadows under the acrylic holder and nearby counter items.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 50mm full-frame lens, f/5.6, editorial product-display framing with the flat design and the mockup both fully visible.
- Lighting: soft diffused window light from upper-left at about 45°, gentle fill from right, subtle shadow under the standing sign for realism, mild highlight on acrylic edges.
- Color grade: warm beige and muted green with natural wood tones, slightly desaturated for a clean print-design presentation, preserving realistic paper fibers and ink edges.
- Material detail: matte coated paper, faint risograph-like ink density variation, clear acrylic holder with beveled edges, wood counter pores, small printed receipt texture, and soft reflections from the POS device.

[6. MOOD]
Warm Korean café stationery and retail signage — feels like a thoughtful studio mockup from a design portfolio, practical for a real counter, friendly, readable, and quietly premium.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문구가 이미지에 정확히 보여야 함
  - {매장명}
  - {안내 배지}
  - {날짜 라벨}
  - {안내 메시지}
  - 결제 가능 수단
  - {결제 방법}
  - {QR 코드 자리}
  - {멤버십 안내}
  - {영업시간}
  - {매장 주소}
  - {연락처}
  - {와이파이 안내}
  - {추가 안내}
  - {SNS 태그}
- The flat sign and the standing mockup must show the same layout, same text hierarchy, and same Korean wording.
- Korean characters must be crisp and correctly formed; no broken jamo, no swapped syllables, no garbled line breaks.
- The sign should remain the primary subject even with realistic counter objects and café texture around it.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters or garbled Hangul jamo
- Incorrect or mismatched wording between flat design and standing mockup
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized portrait likeness

studio:prompts3:ours-162.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean

[1. PURPOSE]
Vertical storefront event banner mockup for an X-banner / roll-up banner, designed to be readable from a distance and print-ready for a fitness gym promotion. The banner should feel like a real promotional stand placed near a gym entrance: bold headline, event details, coupon-style CTA, contact information, and a believable lower sponsor / notice area.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Full-frame vertical banner, centered in portrait orientation, occupying most of the canvas height like a real 600x1800mm X-banner or roll-up display.
- Show a realistic banner surface with slight vinyl texture, straight printed edges, subtle reflections, visible roll-up base or X-frame tension points, and a soft floor contact shadow.
- Top header zone uses {매장명} as the brand anchor, with {이벤트라벨} as a small campaign label near it.
- Main promotional zone features {메인혜택} in the largest type, using oversized numerals and bold stacked line breaks.
- Midsection includes benefit badges for {추가혜택}, a coupon tag for {쿠폰코드}, and a compact event details block for {이벤트기간}, {대상조건}, {운영시간}, and {체험수업}.
- Lower CTA zone includes {상담CTA}, {지점주소}, {연락처}, {카카오채널}, a generic QR placeholder box, and a small sponsor / partner strip using {스폰서문구}.
- Apply {컨셉톤} consistently across typography weight, contrast, accent shapes, and fitness-oriented graphic energy.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top brand zone: Place {매장명} at the very top as a strong signature mark with a simple gym-emblem style icon, then add {이벤트라벨} as a neon pill label such as an in-store campaign sticker.
2. Main promotion zone: Put {메인혜택} in the dominant headline area. Emphasize “PT”, “1회 무료”, “30%” with oversized numerals, thick Korean type, and neon yellow highlight blocks.
3. Benefit card zone: Add 2–3 compact benefit tiles with fitness icons, including {추가혜택}, a “COUPON {쿠폰코드}” ticket-shaped badge, and a short urgency cue tied to {대상조건}.
4. Event information zone: Create a clearly separated information band containing {이벤트기간}, {대상조건}, {운영시간}, and {체험수업}. Use small icons such as calendar, clock, map pin, dumbbell, and chat bubble.
5. CTA / contact zone: In the lower third, place {상담CTA} as a bold call-to-action button, followed by {연락처}, {카카오채널}, and {지점주소}. Include a square generic QR placeholder labeled “상담 예약 QR” with module-like patterning that reads as a placeholder.
6. Sponsor and notice area: At the bottom edge, add a thin partner strip with {스폰서문구} and a small fine-print line {하단고지}, styled like a real printed retail banner footer.
7. Decorative retail graphics: Add diagonal neon streaks, arrow callouts, dotted halftone accents, subtle speed lines, and small fitness pictograms to make the banner feel like a premium gym event advertisement.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard ExtraBold or Noto Sans KR Black for the main headline, Pretendard Bold for supporting lines, and Noto Sans KR Medium for small informational text; headline size should dominate the layout, with compact tracking and strong line breaks.
- Color palette: black #111111, neon yellow #F7FF3C, white #FFFFFF, dark gray #2A2A2A, cool gray #BFC3C7, and small electric-blue highlights #38BDF8 for secondary accents.
- Graphic hierarchy: use large discount numerals, bright CTA buttons, coupon-ticket shapes, calendar strips, and icon-labeled rows so the promotion can be understood quickly from a storefront distance.
- Border/shadow: thin white separators, 2–4px rule lines, bold neon panels, and a soft drop shadow with 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity to lift the banner off the floor.
- Print realism: keep the design vertically aligned, high resolution, sharp Korean text, clean ink edges, slight vinyl sheen, and believable roll-up stand hardware or X-frame support details.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: studio product mockup look, 50mm lens at f/8, straight-on front view with low perspective distortion for accurate banner presentation.
- Lighting: even studio softbox lighting from upper-left at 45°, with subtle fill from the right and a faint floor shadow to define the banner edges.
- Color grade: high-contrast black + neon yellow retail promo grade, crisp white text, slightly cool neutral balance for print clarity.
- Environment cue: polished storefront floor, faint glass-door reflection, and a premium gym entrance atmosphere in the background, kept secondary to the banner.

[6. MOOD]
Retail promotion mockup — energetic fitness chain storefront advertising aesthetic, like a premium mall gym campaign board with bold information hierarchy, coupon urgency, and real in-store event details.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following strings must appear correctly and fully legible in the rendered image:
  - "{매장명}"
  - "{이벤트라벨}"
  - "{메인혜택}"
  - "{이벤트기간}"
  - "{대상조건}"
  - "{추가혜택}"
  - "쿠폰코드 {쿠폰코드}"
  - "{상담CTA}"
  - "{연락처}"
  - "{카카오채널}"
  - "{지점주소}"
  - "{운영시간}"
  - "{체험수업}"
  - "{스폰서문구}"
  - "{하단고지}"
- The main headline must be the largest text, with “무료”, “30%”, and the coupon / CTA areas immediately noticeable.
- All Korean jamo, spacing, punctuation, dates, phone number, and @ handle must be correct; no broken characters, no missing punctuation, no garbled line breaks.
- QR area should look like a generic QR placeholder block labeled “상담 예약 QR”, not a real scannable code unless the generator explicitly supports it.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean retail POP price-tag card for an individual menu item, showing both a polished print design draft and a realistic in-store bakery/café mockup on one portrait canvas.
Print-ready small promotional menu price card with rich retail details, clear pricing hierarchy, store identity, item notes, and a believable counter-placement scene suitable for bakery display, café shelf, or dessert showcase.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Single portrait canvas split into two coordinated areas: left side for the finished POP card design draft, right side for the real-life placement scene beside a bakery display shelf, counter tray, or acrylic menu stand.
- Left design area occupies about 52% of the frame: front-facing card presentation with crisp printed edges, visible paper grain, rounded corners, subtle thickness, and a refined editorial layout.
- Right mockup area occupies about 48% of the frame: the same card placed physically on a light beige tabletop or in a small wooden/acrylic stand, shot at a slight 10–15° angle for realistic depth.
- Background surface should use warm cream paper texture, beige tabletop, cocoa-brown accents, real café counter materials, soft crumbs, bakery tray edge, linen napkin, small tongs, blurred pastries, and a distant menu board to create an authentic retail environment.
- Keep typography legible at small scale; use {메뉴명}, {가격}, {포인트 카피}, {추가 정보}, {컨셉 톤}, {레이아웃}, {비율/사이즈} exactly as configurable content.
- Add realistic price-card information around the main content: store name, category label, small item code, date label, address line, contact number, decorative divider rules, and small badge elements such as “TODAY”, “BEST”, or “추천”.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Left panel (design draft): build a polished POP price card with a small store header such as “BROWN OVEN BAKERY / 브라운오븐 베이커리” at the top, then {메뉴명} as the largest headline, {가격} directly beneath it in bold, and {포인트 카피} as the supporting line in a hand-written accent style.
- Left panel main card details: include a compact category line such as “BAKERY MENU · TODAY SPECIAL”, a small date label such as “2026.05”, a tiny item code such as “ITEM 024”, and a subtle badge reading “BEST” or “추천 메뉴”.
- Left panel sub-block: place {추가 정보} as a compact detail row or small footer line, separated with a thin decorative divider rule; add realistic micro-copy such as “매장 제조 · 당일 판매”, “알레르기 정보 매장 문의”, or “TAKE OUT 가능” in small Korean type.
- Left panel footer: include store contact and location details in tiny but readable text, for example “서울 성동구 카페거리 12 · 02-1234-5678 · @brownoven”.
- Left panel styling: create a warm BI-inspired palette using cream, beige, and brown, with balanced spacing, rounded card corners, small label-card proportions, light paper fibers, cocoa ink texture, and tasteful decorative dividers.
- Right panel (mockup): show the same card physically placed beside a bakery tray, cake dome, menu board, shelf tag rail, or tabletop stand according to {레이아웃}; include realistic paper thickness, slight perspective tilt, soft contact shadow, and tiny imperfections along the printed edge.
- Right panel environment: suggest a believable bakery or café counter area with warm pastries, a croissant or roll tray, kraft paper bag, ceramic plate, linen napkin, wooden shelf edge, small price tags in the distance, and softly blurred background objects while the main card stays visually dominant.
- Layout logic: keep the two panels visually linked through the same color palette, same typography system, consistent line weights, matching badge shapes, and repeated divider motifs, so the design draft and mockup feel like one coherent brand package.
- {레이아웃} should guide whether the card is shown as a tabletop card, shelf tag, or standing sign, while preserving the split-view composition.
- {비율/사이즈} should influence the apparent card proportions and print scale, while the overall canvas remains a 1024x1536 portrait composition.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard Bold for {메뉴명}, Pretendard SemiBold or Noto Sans KR Bold for {가격}, and a hand-drawn style or Nanum Pen Script for {포인트 카피}; size hierarchy should be strong and instantly readable.
- Supporting typography: use Pretendard Regular or Noto Sans KR Medium for store name, item code, date label, address line, contact number, and {추가 정보}; micro text should look like real printed retail stationery, not filler blocks.
- Color palette: cream #F6F0E6, beige #E8DDCF, warm brown #8A5A3C, dark cocoa #3E2A22, soft gray #B9B0A7; adapt this with {컨셉 톤} while preserving warm bakery retail identity.
- Border/shadow: use thin 1.5px brown outline, soft drop shadow 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity, with subtle paper edge texture and fine printed ink variation.
- Graphic details: add small dividers, rounded label tabs, tiny corner marks, dotted price leader lines, tasteful badge stickers, and café stationery motifs such as wheat lines, small bean icons, or bakery stamp-style shapes without making them look like official certification seals.
- Card styling should feel print-ready, premium, commercially usable, and rich with believable menu-card information.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 50mm prime lens, f/4, editorial product-photo framing for the mockup side; clean orthographic-like front view for the design side.
- Lighting: soft window light from upper-left at about 45°, with gentle fill from the right, producing warm café-counter realism, soft shadows under the stand, and natural paper highlights.
- Color grade: warm cream + beige + cocoa with slightly muted saturation, similar to a polished bakery editorial still life.
- Material realism: matte coated paper, faint fiber texture, slight corner rounding, printed ink density variation, tabletop grain, pastry surface texture, and shallow depth-of-field blur in the right-side environment.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean bakery stationery aesthetic — Kinfolk-style editorial meets a warm café brand system, with realistic retail POP details, appetizing counter atmosphere, and a handcrafted yet professional printed-card feel.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문구가 정확한 한글로 보여야 함: {메뉴명}, {가격}, {포인트 카피}, {추가 정보}
- Additional Korean text rendered in image should be clean and realistic, such as “브라운오븐 베이커리”, “추천 메뉴”, “매장 제조 · 당일 판매”, “TAKE OUT 가능”, “서울 성동구 카페거리 12”, “02-1234-5678”, “2026.05”, “오늘의 메뉴”.
- Layout invariant: both left design draft and right mockup must be visible in the same canvas.
- Typography hierarchy invariant: {메뉴명} largest, {가격} second largest, {포인트 카피} smaller accent, {추가 정보} smallest detail.
- Printability invariant: all Korean characters must be clean, properly spaced, and free of broken jamo.
- Realism invariant: the right-side card must match the left-side design exactly in menu name, price, point copy, colors, badge style, and footer details.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

studio:prompts3:ours-160.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Single-item menu illustration for Korean cafe menu books, blogs, delivery-menu thumbnails, and Instagram posts. Warm standalone food illustration with realistic menu-card information: item name, price, short description, store identity, address/contact line, and small divider details suitable for a polished Korean cafe menu page.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Place {음식명} as the centered hero subject occupying about 58–64% of the frame, with a tidy menu caption block below.
- Make {구성/재료} visually readable through layered shapes, fillings, toppings, cut edges, crumbs, gloss, steam, garnish, and color cues that feel appetizing.
- Show {플레이팅} as a compact cafe still-life arrangement that naturally supports the food: plate, board, cup, napkin, small spoon, crumbs, or garnish may appear when they fit the item.
- Use {배경} as a warm tabletop or paper-menu surface with gentle watercolor texture, subtle stains, faint grid/paper fibers, and small cafe-style details.
- Include a small menu information system: {매장명} at the top or lower corner, {메뉴번호}, {가격}, {한줄설명}, {주소}, and {연락처} arranged like a real printed cafe menu card.
- Keep {레이아웃} as the organizing principle: centered food illustration, Korean label and price beneath, thin divider line, and compact shop information in a secondary position.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Main food form: draw {음식명} first as the dominant object, with rounded, appetizing proportions, clearly defined silhouette, and hand-painted volume.
- Ingredient expression: reveal {구성/재료} through visible filling edges, soft cross-section hints, surface cracks, toasted color variation, syrup shine, seed specks, cream layers, or other natural food details.
- Serving setup: render {플레이팅} as a cafe-style presentation; supporting props should frame the food and reinforce scale, texture, and menu context.
- Background layer: fill the canvas with {배경}, using watercolor wash, paper grain, soft tabletop shadow, and small printed-menu marks such as a dotted divider or menu-code tag.
- Menu text block: beneath the food, render the exact item name “{음식명}”, the price “{가격}”, and the short line “{한줄설명}” in clean Korean typography.
- Shop information: add {매장명}, {주소}, {연락처}, and {메뉴번호} in smaller text, like a real cafe menu/pricelist entry rather than a poster or recipe diagram.
- Page feel: make the whole composition look like one illustrated item from a premium Korean cafe menu book, with handmade warmth and practical menu information.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use clean Korean sans-serif such as Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for menu information; item name 24–34 px equivalent, price 20–28 px, description and shop details 11–16 px.
- Menu hierarchy: item name and price should be the most legible Korean text; store name, address, contact, and menu number should be smaller but still readable.
- Linework: thin hand-drawn pen lines with slightly uneven pressure, approximately 1–2 px visual weight, preserving a natural illustration feel.
- Color palette: derive from {일러스트 톤}; use warm beige, cream, light brown, soft apricot, muted caramel, milk-white highlights, and natural food colors.
- Dividers and tags: add a fine dotted line, tiny menu-number pill, small price tag alignment, or light corner note to make the piece feel like a real cafe menu card.
- Border/shadow: a very soft paper-like contact shadow is allowed, such as 3–4 px y-offset, 10 px blur, 12% opacity, keeping the illustration gentle and print-friendly.
- Texture: add subtle watercolor granulation, light paper grain, small crumbs, utensil marks, and soft wash transitions without making the Korean text hard to read.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: illustrated still-life look inspired by a top-down editorial food photo, as if composed with a Canon EOS R5 and 50mm normal lens aesthetic, clean studio tabletop layout.
- Lighting: soft diffused daylight from upper-left at about 45°, with gentle fill from the right and delicate contact shadows under the food, plate, and props.
- Color grade: warm cream and beige base with muted caramel accents and soft milky highlights, keeping the native color of the food intact.
- Rendering: watercolor-and-pen menu illustration, not a fully photorealistic photo; preserve handmade brush edges, ink detail, and edible texture.

[6. MOOD]
Korean cafe menu illustration — a warm editorial food sketch with the delicate hand-drawn feel of a premium neighborhood bakery menu, cozy tabletop realism, and clear practical menu information.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: render the main label exactly as “{음식명}”.
- Render the price exactly as “{가격}”, the store name as “{매장명}”, the menu code as “{메뉴번호}”, the description as “{한줄설명}”, the address as “{주소}”, and the contact line as “{연락처}”.
- The illustration must clearly match {구성/재료}, {플레이팅}, {일러스트 톤}, {레이아웃}, and {배경} while still reading as one single menu item.
- The hero food should remain visually dominant, with props, dividers, and shop information supporting the menu-card story.
- Keep all Korean characters, spacing, numbers, and won symbol clean, correct, and legible at 1024x1024.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likenesses

studio:prompts3:ours-159.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
1-2 English lines: Staff uniform catalog poster for a Korean restaurant brand, combining a real-life worn look with a flat product layout for fundraising / catalog use.
Two-part vertical catalog sheet: model in uniform on one side, standalone apparel mockups on the other, with consistent branding, realistic restaurant context, item labels, price-style callouts, and order-guide details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main composition: a 2-part vertical layout, with the model occupying about 55% of the canvas and the flat mockup/catalog area occupying about 45%.
- The model should appear in a realistic Korean restaurant counter background, framed from thigh-up, slightly turned 3/4 toward camera, with a neat professional posture and a natural staff-service expression.
- The background may include softly focused counter details: wood counter edge, stainless tray stack, POS terminal, small menu board, order bell, ceramic bowls, condiment jars, receipt paper, and warm overhead restaurant lighting.
- The flat mockup section should sit beside or below the model depending on spatial balance, showing {아이템} laid out like a commercial apparel catalog sheet with small Korean product labels and measurement-style annotation lines.
- Keep all brand applications consistent across the uniform set, using {매장명/BI}, {로고 위치}, and {컬러} exactly as the brand system.
- Use a premium catalog presentation with editorial product information: issue label, date label, model-name credit, item code, size guide, fabric note, and a small barcode/order area.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Hero model area: place {모델} in the center-left or upper portion, wearing the full branded uniform set with realistic cloth folds, stitched seams, apron strap tension, collar shape, sleeve creases, and natural fit.
2) Catalog header: add a compact top header reading "STAFF WEAR GUIDE", "VOL.03", "2026년 5월호", and "1024x1536 세로" in a refined Korean editorial layout.
3) Background environment: render a tidy Korean restaurant counter scene behind the model with practical details such as handwritten menu cards, a warm pendant reflection, a tray return corner, and blurred kitchen tiles, giving the uniform a real workplace context.
4) Uniform consistency pass: apply {매장명/BI} branding to each item with the same placement logic and the same {컬러} treatment across all variants.
5) Flat mockup area: show {아이템} as standalone apparel pieces on a warm neutral tabletop or catalog panel, arranged in a clear row/grid with item tags such as "앞치마", "한식 셔츠", "두건·반다나", "폴로셔츠".
6) Logo placement details: place the mark according to {로고 위치}, making each item’s print or embroidery size proportional and commercially realistic, with close-up inset labels like "자수 확대", "가슴 로고", "측면 로고".
7) Material realism: emphasize fabric weave, embroidery thread texture, print edge sharpness, apron pocket seams, cap/bandana stitching, garment thickness, hem lines, buttons, and believable shadowing under each garment piece.
8) Product information block: include short Korean catalog copy such as "네이비 베이스 + 크림 자수", "골드 액센트 라인", "XS–XL 주문 가능", "세트 예상가 ₩78,000부터", "문의 @hansot_uniform".
9) Small catalog details: include a model credit near the portrait, "MODEL. 김서연 / STAFF", a small barcode/order-code box reading "ORDER CODE HS-247", and a bottom contact line "서울시 중구 한식로 24 · 02-1234-5678".
10) Layout harmony: ensure the worn outfit and the flat mockups feel like one unified product system, with matching lighting, consistent color balance, and realistic commercial catalog finish.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR in medium and semibold weights, 22–34px for main labels, 12–18px for catalog microcopy, with crisp editorial hierarchy and readable Korean text.
- Color palette: base on {컬러}, with deep navy, cream, muted gold accents, and warm neutral background tones like #F5F1E8, #22314A, #E8DDC8, #C7A86A.
- Border/shadow: use subtle editorial drop shadows, 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 16% opacity, with thin hairline separators in soft gray and warm beige product-card panels.
- Graphic details: add small size chips, item-number circles, fabric swatch blocks, measurement ticks, product-code labels, a barcode area, and quiet gold divider rules that support the apparel catalog mood.
- Korean text rendered in the image should feel printed and commercial, not placeholder-like; keep line lengths short and natural for a catalog sheet.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial product-portrait look, Canon EOS R5 style capture, 85mm f/1.8 for the model area and 50mm equivalent top-down for the flat mockups, crisp commercial sharpness.
- Lighting: soft window light from upper-left at about 45°, with gentle fill from front-right and a faint rim to separate the uniform from the restaurant background.
- Color grade: warm neutral catalog grade with navy and cream dominance, slightly desaturated background, and controlled gold accent highlights.
- Texture rendering: visible cotton-poly fabric grain, subtle apron canvas texture, embroidered cream thread, matte printed logo ink, brushed metal counter reflections, warm paper menu texture, and realistic tabletop shadows.

[6. MOOD]
Premium uniform catalog — a realistic editorial funding-page aesthetic similar to a high-end apparel lookbook photographed inside an operating Korean restaurant, with practical ordering information and polished brand presentation.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following strings must appear correctly if text is shown: "한솥집 한식당", "네이비 + 크림", "앞치마 / 한식 셔츠 / 두건·반다나 / 폴로셔츠", "앞치마 가슴 / 셔츠 가슴 + 등 / 두건 측면", "네이비 베이스 + 크림 자수, 약간의 골드 액센트", "한국 30대 한식당 직원, 단정한 미소, 매장 카운터 백그라운드", "1024x1536 세로".
- Additional Korean catalog text may include: "STAFF WEAR GUIDE", "VOL.03", "2026년 5월호", "MODEL. 김서연 / STAFF", "ORDER CODE HS-247", "XS–XL 주문 가능", "세트 예상가 ₩78,000부터", "문의 @hansot_uniform".
- The model must look like a real Korean restaurant staff member in her 30s, with natural proportions, realistic skin texture, believable hands, and practical clothing fit.
- All apparel items must share the same brand identity, logo system, embroidery/print scale, and color logic.
- Flat mockups must clearly show each item as a separate standalone product while remaining part of the same catalog system.

[1. PURPOSE]
A realistic takeout packaging mockup catalog for a dessert shop, combining multiple package types in one balanced studio composition for catalog, Instagram, brand proposal, and crowdfunding page use.
Show cups, dessert boxes, cake boxes, sleeves, stickers, and paper bags as a cohesive branded set with premium product-photo realism, including practical printed details such as flavor labels, price tags, order information, address/contact text, QR-style ordering block, and recycling marks.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main composition: a grouped product display occupying about 70% of the canvas, with the largest cake box and paper bag slightly behind the front cups to create depth and a natural retail lineup.
- Arrangement: two cup sizes in the front-left and front-center, dessert boxes staggered to the right, a cake box with side label in the mid-right, branded paper bag standing behind as the tallest element, and small accessory items such as sticker sheets, receipt card, ribbon tag, or dessert sleeve placed naturally near the products.
- Background treatment: {배경 톤}, matte surface with subtle tabletop grain or softly textured studio paper, warm daylight atmosphere, gentle shadows extending diagonally.
- Apply {매장명}, {로고 설명}, {패키지 구성}, {컬러 팔레트}, {패턴/모티프}, {시그니처 카피}, {제품 라벨 문구}, {매장 정보}, and {주문 안내} consistently across visible package surfaces.
- The overall image should feel like a real boutique dessert brand photoshoot: tactile paper texture, printed ink density, folds, lids, handles, sticker edges, and believable retail packaging details.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Hero package cluster: place the primary dessert box set in the mid-right 40% of the frame, slightly angled toward camera, with realistic cardboard thickness, lid seams, tuck tabs, side flaps, and a printed side label.
2. Front cups: position two takeaway cups in the lower-left 35% and lower-center 25%, one slightly taller than the other, with matching lids, cup sleeves, aligned logos, flavor sticker, and small printed order code.
3. Paper bag: place one paper bag behind the cups and boxes, occupying the upper-center 20% vertically, with twisted handles visible, centered logo, lower contact line, and a small decorative pattern band.
4. Secondary box variants: include smaller and larger box variants beside or behind the hero box, keeping consistent scale relationships and brand placement across small, medium, and large formats.
5. Printed retail details: add legible packaging copy such as "오늘의 조각케이크", "딸기 생크림", "₩7,500", "케이크 픽업 12:00-20:00", "보냉 포장 가능", "온라인 예약", and a compact QR-style block labeled "주문하기".
6. Surface realism: add soft contact shadows, subtle reflections on satin-coated cups, matte paper grain on boxes and bags, visible folded corners, handle creases, sticker thickness, and believable print registration.
7. Branding application: repeat {매장명}, {로고 설명}, {패턴/모티프}, and {시그니처 카피} across cups, boxes, sleeves, sticker labels, bag front, and small hang tags, respecting folds, lids, box seams, and curved cup perspective.
8. Color harmony: distribute {컬러 팔레트} across primary surfaces, secondary accents, pattern lines, label stickers, small icons, and fine gold details so the set reads as one premium collection.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for Korean copy, medium to bold weight for brand name and product labels, smaller regular weight for address/contact and order notes; allow a subtle handwritten accent for {시그니처 카피} if it fits {패턴/모티프}.
- Color palette: apply {컬러 팔레트} as the main palette, with crisp white or warm ivory base tones, rose-pink and lavender surfaces, and warm metallic-gold accents for premium lines, icons, and small divider marks.
- Packaging graphics: include repeating slice-cake motifs, tiny floral pattern elements, flavor stickers, small ingredient-style label blocks, barcode-like order strips, recycling icons, and a tasteful QR-style ordering square.
- Border/shadow: use soft drop shadows with about 4px y-offset, 12px blur, and 15% opacity; keep packaging cut lines crisp, with refined edge highlights and realistic paper thickness.
- Print finish: matte paper on boxes and bags, lightly satin-coated cups, slightly glossier stickers, realistic fold lines, seam edges, die-cut tabs, handle dents, and accurately aligned printed artwork.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: full-frame product photography look, 85mm f/2.8 for the main clustered mockup, straight-on slight three-quarter angle, sharp focus across all packaging.
- Lighting: soft window light from upper-left at about 45°, gentle fill from front-right, controlled specular highlights on satin cup coating and sticker surfaces, with smooth falloff on shadows.
- Color grade: creamy pastel base with rose-pink, lavender, and warm gold accents; clean editorial product tone with slightly softened contrast.
- Realism cues: shallow but sufficient product depth, tactile paper fibers, tiny print texture, soft tabletop reflections, slightly varied shadow density under each object, and physically plausible scale between cups, boxes, stickers, tags, and bag.

[6. MOOD]
Premium bakery packaging editorial — feels like a refined boutique café identity shoot with warm natural light, charming dessert-shop details, and a polished crowdfunding catalog presentation.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following strings must appear correctly and legibly on package surfaces: "슬라이스 디저트", "슬라이스 케이크", "오늘의 조각케이크", "딸기 생크림", "₩7,500", "주문하기", "케이크 픽업 12:00-20:00", "보냉 포장 가능".
- The printed store information must include: "서울 성동구 디저트길 12", "02-1234-1580", and "@slice_dessert" in small but readable packaging text.
- All package items must share the same logo system, color palette, pattern family, label hierarchy, and premium dessert-shop tone across cups, boxes, sleeves, stickers, and paper bag.
- Packaging must look physically plausible, with correct box folds, handle structure, cup lid shape, sticker placement, paper thickness, and perspective alignment.
- Render both Korean and English text cleanly if present; avoid broken characters, garbling, random glyphs, or mirrored text.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications or invented government approval marks
- Broken Korean characters or garbled typography
- Warped packaging geometry or impossible folds and handles
- Unreadable, mirrored, or randomly substituted package text

[INPUT]
- language: Korean

[1. PURPOSE]
Create a refined retail operating-hours sign design for a salon storefront door, suitable for print, window-sticker production, and client presentation mockup.
Show a polished flat signage proof and a realistic glass-door application mockup in one vertical canvas, with accurate Korean typography, store information, and practical visitor-facing details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Vertical 1024x1536 canvas split into two stacked presentation zones: top 52% for the flat design proof, bottom 48% for the real storefront glass-door mockup.
- Top proof area should appear as a finished signage presentation board on warm off-white stock, including two coordinated design directions: a main vertical sticker layout and a compact alternate decal layout.
- Bottom mockup area should show the same main design applied to a glass entrance door from an exterior street-facing angle, with realistic reflections, transparent sticker edges, door handle, sidewalk hints, salon interior silhouettes, and faint street reflections.
- Keep {레이아웃} as the guiding structure, rendered as a polished client proposal board with production-ready alignment, crop marks or small measurement ticks, and material notes.
- Use {매장명}, {영업시간}, {휴무}, {추가 안내}, {주소}, {전화번호}, {예약채널}, {인스타그램}, {사인하단문구} as the Korean content hierarchy.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top proof area (upper 52%): Present a clean window-sticker design sheet with the main sign centered-left and a smaller alternate variation panel on the right or below, clearly labeled in Korean as “시안 A” and “시안 B”.
2. Main title block: Place {매장명} at the top in large bold Korean sans-serif, with wide tracking, confident spacing, and a boutique salon identity feel.
3. Sign label: Include “운영시간 안내” as a clear heading beneath or beside the store name, supported by small pictogram icons for scissors, calendar, phone, and chat reservation.
4. Hours block: Place {영업시간} underneath in a prominent readable size, divided into weekday/weekend lines if visually helpful, using thin rules, dot leaders, or pill-shaped labels.
5. Closed-days block: Place {휴무} as a distinct notice line with a subtle cream/navy badge or calendar tag so visitors can identify it quickly.
6. Extra info block: Place {추가 안내} as supporting visitor guidance near the lower portion of the proof, with comfortable line spacing and clear punctuation.
7. Contact and location strip: Add {주소}, {전화번호}, {예약채널}, and {인스타그램} in a small structured footer, separated by slim dividers or icon bullets.
8. Visitor detail elements: Add a small QR-style reservation square labeled “예약 바로가기”, a production note such as “무광 투명 시트 / 내부 부착”, and a tiny date stamp “업데이트 {업데이트일}”.
9. Bottom mockup area (lower 48%): Apply the same main design onto a real glass door on a salon storefront, positioned at eye level, with realistic vinyl adhesion, slight transparency, edge highlights, glass glare, interior warm lighting, potted plant blur, waiting chair silhouette, and street reflection.
10. Alternate composition: Ensure the top proof area visibly includes the second design direction while keeping the essential information identical and consistent with the same brand system.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for the main signage, weight 700–800 for titles and 400–500 for support text; title around 72–96px equivalent, body around 28–40px equivalent, footer around 18–24px equivalent.
- Color palette: Use the brand feel of {컨셉 톤} with navy #17233D, cream #F4ECDD, muted gray #7B7F87, charcoal #222222, and a small warm beige accent #D7C6A5.
- Graphic details: Use thin 1–2px divider lines, rounded information chips, subtle calendar/phone/chat icons, small QR reservation block, production crop ticks, and a refined footer band.
- Sticker finish: For the door mockup, show matte translucent vinyl or cream opaque lettering on glass with soft drop shadow 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 12–15% opacity, plus slight specular highlights from the street.
- Composition rules: maintain a consistent alignment system, accurate Korean kerning, professional line spacing, and a clear signage hierarchy that remains readable in both the proof and the mockup.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Use a realistic 35mm full-frame street-level product shot for the storefront mockup, paired with a straight-on flat graphic presentation for the proof area.
- Lighting: Soft daylight with gentle overcast diffusion in the mockup, mild ambient reflection on glass, warm interior salon glow, and neutral studio-style lighting for the proof area.
- Color grade: Navy + cream editorial signage palette with clean neutral whites, slightly muted contrast, crisp legibility, realistic glass reflections, and tactile printed-vinyl texture.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean salon storefront signage — feels like a modern boutique beauty brand proposal board, calm and elegant but practical, with real customer-facing details such as hours, reservation channel, address, contact, and door-sticker production notes.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문구가 정확한 한글로 그대로 보여야 함.
  - {매장명}
  - {영업시간}
  - {휴무}
  - {추가 안내}
  - {주소}
  - {전화번호}
  - {예약채널}
  - {인스타그램}
  - {사인하단문구}
- 추가로 “운영시간 안내”, “시안 A”, “시안 B”, “예약 바로가기”, “무광 투명 시트 / 내부 부착”, “업데이트 {업데이트일}” 문구가 선명한 한글로 보이게 할 것.
- In the mockup and proof, keep all Korean characters clear and correctly formed, with no broken jamo, missing spacing, or garbled punctuation.
- The canvas must include both a flat design proof and a realistic glass-door mockup of the same main operating-hours sign.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters or garbled Korean spacing
- Low-resolution, blurry, or unreadable typography
- Celebrity composites or misleading endorsement imagery

[INPUT]

- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean modern cafe menu board for in-store use and Instagram sharing, portrait layout with a refined grid hierarchy, realistic cafe-branding details, and small illustrated accents.
Designed to feel like a trendy Seoul cafe menu in the Anthracite / Fritz / Mok aesthetic, with readable category organization, a highlighted signature section, and practical shop information that makes the design feel like an actual printed menu card.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Vertical poster composition with the store name occupying the top 12–15% as a centered masthead, menu body filling the middle 70%, and a practical footer note area at the bottom 8–10%.
- Background surface: warm beige paper or matte plaster texture in cream, with subtle wood-toned framing elements, soft sage accent lines, realistic paper grain, and faint print-press texture.
- Use an elegant 2-column menu grid for category blocks and price alignment, with fine dividers, small section labels, and menu metadata that resembles a real Korean cafe counter menu.
- Use {매장명}, {커피 메뉴}, {가격}, {시그니처·디저트}, {티·논커피}, {컨셉 톤}, {비율/사이즈} throughout the layout as the custom content.
- Add realistic supporting information without introducing new placeholders: address line “서울 성동구 카페거리 24”, contact “02-1234-5678”, hours “매일 10:00–21:00”, takeout note “TAKE OUT 가능”, and small seasonal note “시즌 원두는 매장에 문의해 주세요”.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header area (top 12–15%): set {매장명} as the primary title in a clean modern sans-serif, centered, with slightly expanded letter spacing. Add small English/Korean sublabels such as “SPECIALTY COFFEE · DESSERT”, “SINCE 2026”, and “오늘의 메뉴” beneath it, plus a thin horizontal divider line below.
2. Main menu grid (middle 35–55%): place {커피 메뉴} as the coffee category content and {가격} as the matching price column, aligned line-by-line with precise spacing, dot leaders, and subtle separators. Include realistic small labels around the list such as “COFFEE”, “HOT / ICE”, “ICE +500”, and “원두 선택 가능”.
3. Signature block (middle 20–30%, visually emphasized): present {시그니처·디저트} inside a soft rounded rectangle or outlined panel with a light sage tint, a very soft shadow, and a tiny illustrated coffee cup or dessert icon beside the title. Add short Korean callouts like “SIGNATURE”, “추천 메뉴”, and “매일 소량 준비” to make the block feel like a real cafe highlight.
4. Tea / non-coffee block (lower middle 15–20%): place {티·논커피} in a secondary block with slightly smaller type and a lighter line weight, maintaining the same grid rhythm as the coffee section. Add small labels such as “TEA & NON-COFFEE”, “카페인 없는 메뉴 표시”, and “우유 변경 +700”.
5. Decorative accents: add small line-art illustrations of a coffee cup, leaf, traditional Korean sweet, roasted coffee bean, and receipt-like tick marks near corners or separators. Use monochrome charcoal, muted olive, or sage so the accents support the hierarchy and feel integrated with the cafe brand.
6. Footer / style note area (bottom 8–10%): integrate a compact note strip that visually reflects {컨셉 톤}, and include practical shop details: “서울 성동구 카페거리 24”, “02-1234-5678”, “매일 10:00–21:00”, “@cafe_daily”, “영수증 리뷰 이벤트 진행 중”, and “{비율/사이즈}”. Add a tiny QR-code placeholder box and small social/share icon marks for Instagram-friendly realism.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for the main Korean text, weight 500–700 for headers and 400–500 for body, with 18–28 px for category titles and 12–18 px for menu lines; allow a restrained English mix in the same sans-serif family.
- Color palette: beige #F3EBDD, cream #FAF7F0, warm wood #B68A5A, sage #A8B89A, charcoal #2E2E2E, muted olive #7E8B72.
- Border/shadow: use thin 1–2 px charcoal or sage rules, hairline dividers, small rounded panels, and a very soft shadow (0px x-offset, 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 10–15% opacity) only on the signature panel.
- Build the graphic language as a believable premium cafe menu: print-ready hierarchy, tactile paper grain, careful price alignment, realistic service notes, small editorial details, and cafe-counter signage energy.
- Include tasteful decorative dividers, small item markers, category tabs, and subtle paper/ink imperfections that make the menu feel physically printed rather than sterile.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: flat-lay editorial design look, 50mm equivalent top-down composition feel, sharply legible poster typography rather than photographic depth.
- Lighting: soft diffused window light from upper-left, with a faint reflected fill from lower-right, producing gentle paper texture visibility and low-contrast edges.
- Color grade: warm cream + beige + sage with restrained charcoal text, inspired by contemporary Korean cafe branding and muted craft-paper printing.
- Rendering details: make the menu look like a high-quality printed board or thick paper card photographed for an Instagram post, with realistic ink density, slight paper fibers, and gentle edge shadows.

[6. MOOD]
Trend-forward Korean cafe branding — a restrained Kinfolk-meets-Aesop editorial menu card with Seoul specialty cafe sensibility, enriched with practical shop details, friendly handwritten-style micro notes, and a warm neighborhood cafe atmosphere.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following strings must appear correctly and exactly as provided:
  - {매장명}
  - {커피 메뉴}
  - {가격}
  - {시그니처·디저트}
  - {티·논커피}
  - {컨셉 톤}
  - {비율/사이즈}
- Additional Korean text should be correctly rendered and realistic, such as “오늘의 메뉴”, “추천 메뉴”, “서울 성동구 카페거리 24”, “매일 10:00–21:00”, “TAKE OUT 가능”, “ICE +500”, and “영수증 리뷰 이벤트 진행 중”.
- Preserve clear category alignment and readable line spacing.
- Signature section must remain visually emphasized above the other category blocks.
- Prices must align clearly with item names, using dot leaders or consistent right-aligned columns.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[INPUT]
