[1. PURPOSE]
Korean sashimi and seafood restaurant menu board, vertical poster layout, designed for in-store wall display, storefront print, and social media sharing.
A practical Korean seafood pricelist with blue ocean graphics, bold Hangul typography, item categories, prices, store information, contact details, and casual seaside restaurant charm.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main title {매장명} placed at the top center with strong visual weight, supported by a smaller tagline {대표문구} and small seafood icons.
- Use {컨셉 톤} as the overall palette: white menu paper base, marine blue and teal dividers, sky-blue waves, navy outlines, and small shell/fish illustrations.
- Add a realistic information strip below the header containing {주소}, {연락처}, and {영업시간}, with tiny map-pin, phone, and clock icons.
- Large featured sashimi set area in the upper-middle, then a structured sashimi grid beneath, followed by boxed sections for {찌개·식사} and {주류}.
- Include practical menu-board details: clear won prices, dotted leader lines between item names and prices, category labels, thin dividers, origin note {원산지표기}, and footer notice {안내문구}.
- Decorative ocean elements should feel naturally present in a Korean 횟집 menu: waves, bubbles, flatfish, rockfish, shrimp, crab, shells, seaweed, and small price-tag shapes around section corners.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Header zone (top 12–16%): place {매장명} in a bold, centered headline; add {대표문구} beneath it, plus small wave, fish, and shell motifs around the title. Add a subtle signboard label such as 오늘의 신선한 활어회 near the title area.
2) Store info strip (below header 5–7%): show {주소}, {연락처}, and {영업시간} in a horizontal band with small pictogram icons and fine navy divider lines.
3) Featured menu zone (upper-middle 22–30%): create a large hero panel titled 대표 메뉴 or 인기 메뉴. Showcase {회 메뉴} and {가격} with 모듬회 emphasized as the largest sashimi option, using a highlighted blue price badge and illustrated sashimi platter icon.
4) Single-item grid zone (middle 24–34%): organize the individual sashimi items from {회 메뉴} into a tidy 2–3 column menu grid. Use item names on the left, dotted leader lines, and prices from {가격} on the right; add small labels like 추천, 신선, 제철 where appropriate.
5) Soup and meal category zone (lower-middle 14–20%): present {찌개·식사} in a separate rounded or ruled box with a heading such as 찌개 · 식사류. Include steam icons, bowl illustrations, and clear price alignment.
6) Beverage zone (lower 8–12%): list {주류} in a compact strip with bottle, glass, bubbles, and wave marks. Keep the category label bold and make each drink-price pair easy to scan.
7) Footer zone (bottom 6–9%): include {원산지표기} and {안내문구}; add a small decorative divider, tiny anchor or buoy icon, and a simple contact repeat using {연락처} if space allows.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use a heavy Korean sans-serif such as Pretendard ExtraBold or Noto Sans KR Black for headings; use Pretendard SemiBold / Medium for prices and item text; keep numerals crisp, large, and aligned.
- Menu hierarchy: category headings should be navy or deep teal; representative items may use bright marine blue badges; prices should use consistent 원 formatting.
- Use a blue, teal, sky-blue, and white palette based on {컨셉 톤}, with restrained navy outlines, small silver-gray accents, and warm paper tones for a printed menu feel.
- Add subtle vintage print texture, slight paper grain, halftone seafood accents, thin divider rules, dotted leader lines, and small illustrated category icons.
- Shadow: very soft drop shadow 3px y-offset, 10px blur, 12% opacity on the main menu blocks; avoid heavy 3D effects.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: flat graphic poster look, like an overhead editorial menu design, no photographic lens distortion; if rendered as product-style composition, mimic a 50mm normal-view layout.
- Lighting: even studio-style lighting with no harsh directional shadow, as if scanned or photographed under diffuse daylight from above.
- Color grade: fresh marine blue, aqua, sky blue, white, and muted sea-glass teal with light vintage paper warmth.

[6. MOOD]
Korean seaside sashimi restaurant menu — casual coastal diner signage meets vintage print poster, with the lively realism of a neighborhood 횟집 wall menu and the graphic clarity of a modern café pricelist.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문자열이 정확히 보여야 함.
  - {매장명}
  - {대표문구}
  - {주소}
  - {연락처}
  - {영업시간}
  - {회 메뉴}
  - {가격}
  - {찌개·식사}
  - {주류}
  - {원산지표기}
  - {안내문구}
- The menu must clearly emphasize 모듬회 as the largest sashimi item and keep every price readable in Korean won formatting.
- Hangul characters must be clean and correctly formed; no broken jamo, garbled punctuation, or missing commas in prices.
- Layout must remain vertically oriented for 1024x1536 use, with seafood illustrations placed around panels and never covering menu names or prices.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Illegible prices or overlapping menu text
- Photorealistic fish images that obscure the menu structure

[INPUT]
- language: Korean

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean ramen and Japanese-style restaurant menu board, vertical wall poster for in-store display and takeout-counter reference.
Black-and-wood base with red accents, combining Korean menu clarity, Japanese-inspired signage details, item prices, shop information, and practical ordering notes in a vintage izakaya mood.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main header sits in the top 15% of the poster, centered, with {매장명} as the dominant title, {일본어부제} beneath it, and a red hanko-style decorative stamp graphic that is clearly non-official.
- Menu body fills the middle 70% in a structured 2-column restaurant menu layout: left column for ramen and donburi, right column for udon, set menu, drinks, and alcohol.
- Background uses dark charcoal black with visible warm wood-grain side panels, cream paper menu slips, small red divider tabs, brush texture, and slightly worn printed edges like an authentic Japanese eatery wall menu.
- Use {컨셉 톤} as the overall visual direction, with clear category hierarchy, readable price alignment, subtle dividers, and realistic counter-menu details.
- Footer area includes store address, contact, business hours, last order note, origin notice, and a small takeaway 안내 label.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header zone (top 15%): place {매장명} in bold brush-calligraphy style, with {일본어부제}, a small 「本日のおすすめ」 red label, and a thin red divider rule across the poster.
2. Category block 1 — 라멘 (upper-left): list {라멘 메뉴} with {가격} aligned in a neat price column; add a small 추천 badge reading {추천메뉴} next to the best item.
3. Category block 2 — 돈부리 (mid-left): place {돈부리 메뉴} as a separate cream paper section, using small bowl icons, dotted dividers, and neatly aligned won prices.
4. Category block 3 — 우동·세트 (mid-right): show {우동 메뉴} and {세트메뉴} with matching label style, red category tags, and compact explanatory subtext.
5. Category block 4 — 음료·주류 (lower-right): place {음료·주류} in smaller text, with a subtle red accent bar, bottle/cup icons, and a softer tone to distinguish beverages.
6. Decorative illustration zone: add ramen bowl line art, steam curls, chopsticks, naruto fish cake, chikuwa, nori strips, small nobori flag illustrations, and tiny wood-burned corner marks around the menu without blocking any essential text.
7. Footer strip: include a dark footer band with wood texture, small decorative separators, {주소}, {연락처}, {영업시간}, {안내문}, and {원산지표기} in fine but legible Korean text.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: title in a bold brush/calligraphy style resembling hand-painted Japanese signage; body in Pretendard or Noto Sans KR Medium 22–28px; prices in a condensed sans style for alignment; footer information in 16–18px clean Korean sans.
- Color palette: matte black #111111, dark wood brown #5A3A24, warm beige #E8DDC8, accent red #C73A2E, off-white #F6F1E7, aged ink gray #3B332B.
- Border/shadow: subtle paper-edge framing, soft drop shadow 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity; thin red rules between sections; small cream paper labels layered over dark wood panels.
- Menu realism: include won symbols or comma-formatted prices consistently, small dots or leader lines between items and prices, and category labels that feel like a real Seoul ramen shop counter menu.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: front-facing straight-on poster composition, 50mm equivalent lens look, flat-on commercial menu board framing.
- Lighting: soft even indoor lighting as if photographed inside a Japanese ramen shop, gentle top-front illumination with controlled natural paper sheen and warm shop ambience.
- Color grade: deep black + warm wood + muted cream with restrained red accents, slightly desaturated vintage restaurant print tone.

[6. MOOD]
Authentic Japanese ramen shop wall menu — a vintage izakaya signage feel with the practical clarity of a modern Seoul restaurant interior, including warm wood texture, hand-painted charm, readable Korean pricing, and lively small food illustrations.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 들어가야 하는 문구: "라멘이찌", "麺屋 라멘이찌", "시오라멘 / 미소라멘 / 츠케멘 / 까라이라멘 / 카라아게 추가", "시오 9,000 / 미소 9,500 / 츠케멘 10,500 / 까라이 10,000 / 카라아게 +3,000", "가츠동 11,000 / 규동 10,000 / 오야꼬동 9,500", "우동 8,000 / 냉우동 8,500 / 튀김우동 9,500", "콜라·사이다 2,000 / 사케 6,000 / 하이볼 7,000", "미소라멘 + 카라아게 2개 세트 12,000", "검+우드+빨강 액센트, 일본 캘리그래피 한자 + 한글 mix, 빈티지 일식점".
- Footer text must be readable and include: "서울 마포구 동교로 27길 12", "02-3144-0925", "매일 11:30–21:30 · 라스트오더 21:00", "포장 가능 · 매운맛 조절 가능", "쌀 국내산 · 돼지고기 국내산 · 닭고기 브라질산".
- Korean jamo and spacing must be rendered correctly with no broken characters; all menu categories should remain clearly separated and readable at a glance.
- Use realistic menu-board details such as red dividers, price leader dots, small food icons, and shop information while preserving the black + wood + red ramen-shop concept.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites

[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean lunchbox and side-dish shop menu board, portrait poster for in-store display, counter signage, delivery insert, and Instagram sharing.
Create a warm neighborhood banchan-store price list with a large lunchbox menu section, side-dish price grid, seasonal set promotion, store information, order guidance, and small illustrated food motifs.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Poster is vertically stacked with a top title band (14%), a main lunchbox menu zone (36%), a side-dish grid zone (22%), a bottom set/seasonal promo and store-info zone (20%), plus slim divider areas between sections.
- Center the shop name {매장명} in the header, add {상단 배지} above or beside it, and place {추천 문구} as a friendly subtitle under the title.
- Background should feel like light beige menu paper with subtle warm wood texture accents, faint rice-grain speckles, and soft olive divider lines, using small illustrated lunchbox and side-dish motifs.
- Organize the layout like a real printed shop menu: category labels, item rows, prices aligned on the right, small notes, contact line, address line, and ordering information at the bottom.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Header band: place {매장명} as the largest text, centered, with a small illustrated lunchbox icon, spoon/chopsticks icon, and a thin olive divider line below. Include the visible text {상단 배지} and {추천 문구}.
- Main lunchbox menu block: add a category heading “도시락 메뉴”, show {도시락 메뉴} in bold stacked lines, and place {가격} directly aligned to the right of each item for quick comparison. Add tiny tags such as “BEST”, “매콤”, “든든” where natural.
- Side-dish grid block: add a category heading “반찬 단품”, arrange {반찬 단품} as a 2x2 rounded-card grid, each card with a tiny line-drawn side-dish bowl illustration, item name, and price.
- Seasonal/set block: add a category heading “세트·시즌”, set {세트·시즌} inside a highlighted rounded rectangle with a slightly darker beige fill, a soft olive accent bar, and a small leaf/season motif.
- Store information footer: include {매장 주소}, {연락처}, {영업시간}, and {주문 안내} in a realistic lower information strip with small phone, map-pin, clock, and shopping-bag icons.
- Decorative menu details: add thin dividers, dotted separators between item names and prices, a small “포장 가능” label, a hand-drawn rice bowl, rolled omelet, kimchi bowl, lunchbox tray, spoon, chopsticks, and leaf graphics that support the home-style concept.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for all body text, Bold 700 for headings, Medium 500 for menu lines, and 42–64 px equivalent for the title depending on section.
- Color palette: follow {컨셉 톤}; use beige #F4EBDD, warm cream #FFF8EF, olive #7A8B5A, muted brown #8B6B4A, dark charcoal #2E2A27, soft sage #B7C6A1, and a muted red accent #B85C4A for BEST or seasonal labels.
- Border/shadow: use 1.5px olive dividers, rounded corners 18px, and a soft drop shadow with 0px x-offset, 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 12% opacity.
- Menu realism: prices should use Korean won formatting with commas, item rows should have dotted leader lines or right-aligned price columns, and footer information should resemble a real local shop menu flyer.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: front-facing graphic poster composition with an orthographic layout feel, like a clean menu board photographed with a 50mm lens at f/5.6 for minimal distortion.
- Lighting: even soft indoor light, as if lit by a large diffused window from upper-left with very mild fill on the right, no harsh highlights.
- Color grade: warm beige + olive + wood brown with slightly muted saturation, print-friendly and calm, similar to a modern Korean neighborhood deli menu.
- Material feel: matte printed paper, subtle fiber texture, gentle wood-counter warmth behind the poster edges, crisp vector-style food illustrations.

[6. MOOD]
A tidy Korean home-style lunchbox shop menu board with a gentle editorial retail feel, like a warm neighborhood banchan store that prepares fresh lunchboxes every morning, with approachable pricing and friendly in-store signage.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following strings must appear exactly as written: {매장명}, {도시락 메뉴}, {가격}, {반찬 단품}, {세트·시즌}, {매장 주소}, {연락처}, {영업시간}, {주문 안내}.
- Render these Korean labels clearly where appropriate: “도시락 메뉴”, “반찬 단품”, “세트·시즌”, “오늘의 추천”, “포장 가능”, “전화 주문”.
- Keep all Korean characters crisp and correctly formed; no broken jamo, no mixed-up spacing, and no illegible price formatting.
- Maintain a clear hierarchy: title largest, lunchbox menu next, side-dish cards smaller, seasonal set and store information clearly readable at the bottom.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Missing or malformed Korean prices
- Photographic food realism that conflicts with the illustrated home-style concept

[INPUT]

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean dessert café menu board for bingsu and sweets, vertical poster layout for in-store display.
Designed to present signature bingsu, desserts, drinks, prices, store details, and seasonal café character in a warm pastel Korean dessert shop style.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main title area at the top 14%: {매장명} centered as the café masthead, with a small subtitle line such as “KOREAN DESSERT CAFÉ MENU” and a tiny “SINCE 2026” or “TODAY’S SWEET TABLE” label.
- Central hero zone (middle 38%): large realistic signature bingsu photo/illustration cluster with bowls, shaved milk ice, red beans, rice cake cubes, mango, strawberry, black sesame powder, condensed milk drizzle, brass spoon, small ceramic side dishes, and a folded café napkin.
- Menu blocks below and around the hero zone: clearly aligned category sections for signature bingsu, desserts, and drinks, with readable item-price rows, small recommendation badges, and seasonal notes.
- Include practical café information near the bottom: “OPEN 11:00–22:00”, “LAST ORDER 21:30”, “서울 성수동 디저트길 12”, “문의 02-1234-5678”, plus a tiny QR/order pickup box and social handle line like “@sweet_bingsu_cafe”.
- Background treatment: cream paper base with soft pink and milk-white gradients, subtle dessert-watercolor texture, faint hand-drawn spoon/cup accents, small fruit illustrations, and printed-menu paper grain.
- Use {컨셉 톤} as the overall visual direction and maintain the vertical {비율/사이즈} poster feeling.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Header strip (top): place {매장명} in the largest text size, centered, with a soft rounded badge or hand-lettered accent behind it for café identity; add small Korean support text such as “수제 팥 · 우유얼음 · 제철 과일” beneath the title.
- Hero illustration/photo (upper-middle): show a premium handmade bingsu centerpiece in a shallow ceramic bowl, layered with realistic toppings, melting shaved ice edges, glossy fruit, chewy rice cake, red bean texture, condensed milk highlights, and small side props that feel natural to a café menu shoot.
- Signature bingsu section (mid-left or mid-right): list {시그니처 빙수} with {가격} in a tidy two-column menu layout, using bold category labels, aligned price text, and small tags like “BEST”, “SEASONAL”, “인기”, or “추천”.
- Dessert section (lower-left): present {디저트} as a separate block with small dessert doodles or watercolor icons beside each item line; include a divider label such as “DESSERT” and subtle notes like “매일 굽는 디저트”.
- Drink section (lower-right): present {음료} in a matching block, slightly smaller than the signature section, with tiny cup icons, hot/ice markers, and compact price alignment.
- Bottom information band: add store address, contact, opening hours, pickup/order note, and a tiny barcode/QR-style square labeled “ORDER”; keep all microtext visually integrated like a real printed café menu.
- Decorative accents: add thin dividers, rounded corner motifs, small spoon/cup doodles, hand-drawn fruit stamps, soft watercolor splashes, menu section frames, and light paper shadows to make it feel like an actual café poster.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard Bold or Noto Sans KR Bold for headings, Pretendard Medium for menu items, and a hand-drawn Korean accent font only for small decorative emphasis; title size should dominate the top area, while prices stay compact and readable.
- Color palette: cream #FFF6EE, blush pink #F7D9E2, milk white #FFFDF8, warm beige #EEDCC9, strawberry pink #F08FA7, cocoa brown #7A5A48.
- Border/shadow: soft drop shadow 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity on hero graphics; thin rounded border lines in muted beige for menu sections; subtle printed ink texture and café-paper grain.
- Layout finish: realistic menu-board print design with balanced section rhythm, visible category hierarchy, tactile paper texture, and small café-brand details such as “TAKE OUT 가능”, “1인 1메뉴 부탁드립니다”, and “시즌 과일은 변경될 수 있어요”.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial food-poster look photographed on Canon EOS R5 with a 50mm lens aesthetic, f/2.8 depth-of-field feel for the hero dessert elements, crisp but slightly soft-edged like a café menu shoot.
- Lighting: bright diffused window light from upper-left at 45°, with a gentle fill from right; soft natural shadows under bowls, spoons, fruit, and menu cards for realistic depth.
- Color grade: warm cream + blush pink + milk white with gentle strawberry and honey accents, lightly desaturated for a refined dessert-café finish.
- Material realism: ceramic bowl glaze, glossy red beans, powdery black sesame, translucent shaved ice, soft rice cake texture, fresh fruit moisture, matte paper background, and subtle ink bleed on printed text.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean dessert café editorial — feels like a warm Seoul café menu board, mixing a polished bakery poster with handcrafted watercolor dessert details and realistic food photography.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문구가 정확히 보여야 함.
  - {매장명}
  - {시그니처 빙수}
  - {가격}
  - {디저트}
  - {음료}
- Additional Korean menu/support text may appear and should be readable, such as “수제 팥빙수”, “오늘의 추천”, “매일 굽는 디저트”, “OPEN 11:00–22:00”, “서울 성수동 디저트길 12”, “문의 02-1234-5678”, “TAKE OUT 가능”.
- Menu hierarchy must clearly separate signature bingsu, desserts, and drinks.
- Korean syllables and spacing must be clean and readable; no jumbled characters.
- The hero bingsu imagery must visually support the menu and coexist naturally with the pricing and information blocks.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[INPUT]

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean pocha / hof house night menu board poster, vertical 1024x1536 layout for in-store wall display and window signage.
Create a realistic blackboard-style menu for {매장명}, using {컨셉 톤}: warm yellow bulb glow, hand-lettered Korean calligraphy, practical menu pricing, shop information, and small chalk food illustrations.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main title area at the top 14%: {매장명} placed large and centered, with a slightly hand-painted chalk or marker look and a warm tungsten halo.
- Directly below the title, add a small real-store information row: {주소}, {전화번호}, {영업시간}, separated by tiny dots or short chalk dividers.
- The center 58–62% is divided into three readable vertical menu sections for appetizers, meals, and alcohol, using handwritten category headers and price-aligned item rows.
- Background is matte black chalkboard or black paper texture with visible chalk dust, scuffed corners, tape marks, faint erased writing ghosts, and warm bulb reflections near the top edge.
- Small illustrated food icons sit around each category header and between item groups: 닭발, 곱창철판, 소주병, 맥주잔, 막걸리 사발, 라면 냄비, 김치전 조각.
- Bottom 18–22% contains a practical pocha footer: set menu strip, today event note, origin notice, Wi‑Fi / 주문 안내 micro text, and a chalk divider line.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Top header band: {매장명} in large Korean brush-calligraphy, warm yellow-white ink, slightly irregular stroke edges, centered, with tiny hand-drawn bulb icons on both sides.
- Subtitle under title: {대표문구} in smaller cream chalk lettering, slightly arched or written on a narrow brush-stroke ribbon.
- Shop info line: {주소} · {전화번호} · {영업시간}, written small but legible like an actual neighborhood pub board.
- Category block 1: “안주” section with {안주 메뉴}; each item and price should appear as a practical menu row with dot leaders, short dashes, or chalk divider marks.
- Category block 2: “식사” section with {식사 메뉴}; use slightly smaller rows but keep numbers and comma pricing clear.
- Category block 3: “주류” section with {주류 메뉴}; give drink options visual emphasis using small bottle, beer mug, and makgeolli bowl icons.
- Bottom set strip: “오늘의 세트” followed by {세트 메뉴}, styled as a yellow chalk label or taped-on black paper strip.
- Event / service note: {이벤트 문구} placed in a small amber badge or handwritten memo shape.
- Footer micro information: {원산지 안내}, plus small realistic labels such as “선불/테이블 주문”, “와이파이 문의”, and “마감 30분 전 라스트오더”.
- Overall layout should feel like an actual handwritten wall menu in a Korean night pocha, with lively asymmetry, practical dividers, realistic chalk smudges, and clear price hierarchy.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: hand-drawn Korean brush lettering or marker script for headers, Pretendard SemiBold or Noto Sans KR Bold for price alignment if any clean text is needed, size hierarchy 64–90px for title, 30–44px for categories, 22–30px for item lines, 14–18px for footer micro text.
- Color palette: matte black #101010, warm yellow #F5C542, amber glow #FFB84D, cream text highlight #F7E9B5, muted chalk gray #B8B8B8, small red-orange accent #E85D3F for event badges.
- Use chalk divider lines, dotted price leaders, small taped-paper labels, bulb doodles, hand-drawn arrows, and uneven chalk pressure to make the sign look used in a real pocha.
- Border/shadow: soft outer glow around title like tungsten bulb spill; chalk dust texture around edges; subtle worn paper or board grain; no glossy plastic finish.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: front-facing straight-on poster composition, as if photographed with a 50mm lens at f/5.6 for flat, readable signage realism.
- Lighting: warm practical bulb lighting from upper-left and upper-right, creating a gentle amber halo and slight uneven brightness typical of a night pocha interior.
- Color grade: deep black base with warm tungsten yellow and amber highlights, slightly faded vintage chalkboard contrast.

[6. MOOD]
Authentic Korean night pocha wall menu — a cozy Seoul neighborhood hof pub at night, with handwritten chalk prices, warm bulbs, snack illustrations, practical shop details, and the feeling of a real menu board behind the counter.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 다음 문구가 정확히 보여야 함: “포차하루”, “오늘도 한잔하기 좋은 밤”, “서울 마포구 와우산로 21길 7”, “02-332-0824”, “매일 18:00–02:00”, “안주”, “닭발 18,000 / 곱창 22,000 / 막창 24,000 / 황태구이 12,000 / 마른안주 8,000 / 김치전 13,000”, “식사”, “라면 5,000 / 우동 6,000 / 볶음밥 7,000”, “주류”, “소주 4,000 / 맥주 4,500 / 막걸리 5,000 / 폭탄주 6,000”.
- 추가 정보도 선명하게 보여야 함: “오늘의 세트”, “닭발+주먹밥+계란찜 26,000”, “소주 2병 주문 시 라면사리 서비스”, “국내산 김치 · 닭고기 국내산 · 쌀 국내산”.
- 한글 자모와 숫자, 쉼표, 슬래시, 원화 가격 표기를 정확하게 유지해야 함.
- Layout invariant: three category sections must remain clearly separated and readable; item names and prices must not collapse into a single paragraph.
- Food illustrations, bulbs, badges, tape marks, and chalk dust are supportive atmosphere elements; menu text remains the visual priority.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Illegible pricing
- Photorealistic food dominating the whole design

[INPUT]
- language: Korean

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean chicken restaurant menu board, vertical poster for in-store wall display, takeaway ordering, and delivery counter signage.
Friendly neighborhood franchise-style price board with bold item names, clear won pricing, store information, operating hours, delivery notices, and energetic yellow-red visual hierarchy for instant ordering decisions.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main layout: tall vertical poster with the header occupying the top 15%, a featured combo ribbon across the next 10%, the main chicken menu grid centered across 42% of the frame, side menu and beverage blocks across 17%, and store/order information in the bottom 16%.
- Background treatment: saturated warm yellow base with red accent panels, subtle paper grain, halftone dots, sauce-splash shapes, small fried-chicken crumb patterns, and clean vector poster finish.
- Retail signage details: thick dividers, rounded price boxes, coupon-like cut lines, small category labels, spicy-level icons, delivery badge row, and a practical bottom strip for address, phone, hours, and origin notice.
- Use {매장명}, {슬로건}, {대표혜택}, {메인메뉴가격표}, {세트사이드가격표}, {음료가격표}, {주문방법}, {주소}, {전화번호}, {영업시간}, {원산지안내}, {공지문구}, {컨셉톤} to customize the menu content and style emphasis.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header zone (top 15%): place {매장명} in a large centered masthead with a red outer stroke and cream highlight. Add {슬로건} directly below in a smaller ribbon. Flank the masthead with a chicken drumstick icon, beer mug icon, and tiny sparkle marks in flat cartoon style.
2. Promo ribbon zone (upper 10%): render {대표혜택} inside a bright red coupon banner with yellow dashed cut marks, a small “오늘의 추천” label, and a circular “HOT” sticker overlapping the right edge.
3. Main menu zone (middle 42%): render {메인메뉴가격표} as the primary focus in a bold 2-column menu list. Each row should have a menu name on the left, a short descriptor or spicy icon in the center, and the price aligned to the right in large readable numerals with ₩ or 원 styling.
4. Set / side / beverage zone (lower-middle 17%): place {세트사이드가격표} in a red rounded rectangle with yellow outline on the left and {음료가격표} in a cream price card on the right. Add dividers, mini icons for fries, tteokbokki, cola, pickled radish, and dipping sauce.
5. Ordering and store info zone (bottom 16%): place {주문방법}, {전화번호}, {주소}, {영업시간}, {원산지안내}, and {공지문구} in compact but legible info blocks. Include phone, pickup, delivery, map-pin, clock, and QR-placeholder micro icons, plus delivery-app style placeholder badges with generic Korean labels.
6. Tone and decoration zone (throughout): apply {컨셉톤} with playful chicken and beer illustrations in corners, small starbursts, sauce strokes, crispy crumb motifs, and energetic retail accent shapes that frame the text without covering prices.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard ExtraBold or Noto Sans KR Black for headers, Pretendard Bold for menu items, Pretendard SemiBold for prices, size hierarchy with title around 92–110 px, promo ribbon 46–60 px, menu items 40–54 px, prices 42–58 px, support text 24–34 px.
- Color palette: vivid yellow #FFD400, strong red #E53935, dark brown-black #2B1B10, warm cream #FFF6D8, white #FFFDF7, orange accent #FF8A00, and a small green accent #17A65A for fresh/pickup labels.
- Border/shadow: thick 4–6 px red outline on key boxes, 2–3 px dark brown inner stroke for price tags, subtle soft shadow 4 px y-offset, 10 px blur, 15% opacity for lifted sticker-like panels.
- Menu realism: show realistic Korean won prices, category separators, spice marks such as “맵”, “HOT”, or “반반 가능”, and small footnote typography for origin and packaging notices.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: flat poster design rendered like a commercial menu board, orthographic front-facing layout, no perspective tilt, equivalent to a 50mm normal-view product shot.
- Lighting: even studio-style diffuse illumination, crisp readability, slight top-left brightness gradient for visual energy, gentle paper texture visible in yellow areas.
- Color grade: high-chroma yellow and red with clean white and cream text balance, slight warm paper tint to avoid neon clipping, sharp vector edges for menu board readability.

[6. MOOD]
Friendly Korean chicken franchise menu board — lively K-food street shop energy, casual beer-and-chicken night atmosphere, cheerful neighborhood takeout counter design, and practical delivery-menu readability.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문구가 정확히 보여야 함.
  - {매장명}
  - {슬로건}
  - {대표혜택}
  - {메인메뉴가격표}
  - {세트사이드가격표}
  - {음료가격표}
  - {주문방법}
  - {전화번호}
  - {주소}
  - {영업시간}
  - {원산지안내}
  - {공지문구}
- Layout invariants: main chicken menu must be the most visually prominent section, prices must remain aligned with menu items, promo ribbon must be clearly separated from the main list, and the bottom store information must read like a real Korean menu board.
- All Korean characters must be clean, legible, and properly spaced; no missing spaces, broken syllables, or garbled text.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Fake government or award badges
- Unauthorized celebrity composites

[INPUT]

- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
High-end Korean restaurant menu board for a hansik omakase-style set meal, vertically composed for print-ready use and premium tabletop display.
A refined luxury Korean dining menu with structured pricing, tactile hanji texture, elegant calligraphy accents, realistic restaurant information, and polished fine-dining identity details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- The page is a vertical 1024x1536 print menu with a balanced editorial grid; top title zone occupies about 16%, main menu body 68%, and footer information zone 16%.
- Background treatment: warm hanji paper texture in off-white with visible subtle fiber grain, softly uneven handmade-paper tone, and a premium matte print surface.
- Layout should feel airy, formal, and complete, with clear separation between course set, course composition, à la carte specials, alcohol section, and venue details.
- Add refined menu-board realism: thin dividers, small section labels, price alignment, a reservation note, address/contact line, and a small seasonal phrase.
- Use {매장명}, {코스메뉴}, {코스구성}, {단품별미}, {주류목록}, {계절문구}, {주소}, {연락처}, {영업시간}, {예약안내}, {컨셉톤}, {비율사이즈} placeholders.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Header zone (top 16%): set {매장명} as the main title, centered, with strong visual hierarchy and a restrained ink-and-gold treatment.
- Subtitle line: place a thin gold divider rule beneath the title, then add {계절문구} in small elegant Korean serif type, centered under the divider.
- Add a small upper-corner menu identity detail such as “SEASONAL HANSIK COURSE” and “오늘의 차림” in fine uppercase/small Korean label styling.
- Course menu block: arrange {코스메뉴} in a neat premium boxed section with each course line stacked; align prices consistently to the right in a small sans-serif style while item names remain prominent.
- Course composition block: place {코스구성} directly below the course box as a compact formal list, using refined separators, small dots, or slash spacing that feels precise and restaurant-menu appropriate.
- À la carte block: set {단품별미} in a 2-column grid with clear item-price pairing, tidy baseline alignment, and a small section heading such as “단품과 별미”.
- Alcohol block: place {주류목록} in a separate lower section with smaller type, aligned to the same grid, using a subtle divider and label such as “전통주와 곁들임”.
- Footer area: include {주소}, {연락처}, {영업시간}, and {예약안내} as real restaurant information; add a small horizontal divider and a discreet decorative traditional pattern accent in muted gold.
- Styling cue insertion: apply {컨셉톤} throughout the layout as the visual direction for type, spacing, material feel, dividers, and small ornamental details.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use a refined Korean serif such as Noto Serif KR or Nanum Myeongjo for headers, paired with Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for prices, footer details, and small labels; title weight bold to semibold, body weight regular to medium, price size about 65-75% of item names.
- Color palette: deep ink black #111111, muted gold #B8944B, warm ivory #F6F1E7, soft stone beige #DDD4C5, subtle charcoal #2A2A2A, and a faint rice-paper gray #E8E0D2.
- Border/shadow: use thin rules in gold or charcoal, hairline section dividers, and very soft flat shadow only where paper layering is implied, like 2px y-offset, 6px blur, 10% opacity.
- Use restrained gold accents for separators, title embellishment, section labels, small geometric hanok-inspired ornaments, and the footer pattern; keep primary menu text ink-black for clear readability.
- Prices must look typeset, not handwritten; align currency-free Korean restaurant pricing consistently with commas.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: flat editorial poster look, simulated as a top-down print design captured with a 50mm normal lens aesthetic, no perspective distortion, no 3D mockup framing.
- Lighting: diffuse museum-like overhead light with even tonal distribution, no glare, no strong reflections, no dramatic shadows.
- Color grade: warm ivory + ink black + subdued antique gold, with slightly desaturated paper tones and crisp contrast for legibility.

[6. MOOD]
Luxury Korean fine-dining menu — a restrained editorial aesthetic inspired by traditional hanok hospitality, contemporary Seoul tasting-menu restaurants, premium hotel stationery, handmade paper craft, and calm ceremonial dining.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following strings must appear exactly as written: “고요한 식탁”, “기본 정식 35,000 / 정성 정식 55,000 / 한정 코스 80,000”, “죽 / 전 / 구이 / 조림 / 찌개 / 밥과 반찬 / 후식”, “갈비찜 28,000 / 보쌈 22,000 / 갓김치 8,000”, “전통주 안동소주 / 배혜 막걸리 / 백화 청주”, “계절의 결을 담은 오늘의 한상”, “서울 종로구 북촌로 12길 8”, “02-734-0521”, “매일 12:00–21:30”, “예약 권장 · 마지막 주문 20:30”, “먹·골드·세리프 폰트 단정, 한지 텍스처, 정갈한 그리드”, “세로 1024x1536”.
- Korean text rendering must preserve spacing, punctuation, slashes, middle dots, en dash, commas, and all jamo correctly without broken characters.
- All menu sections should align cleanly to the grid; prices, address, contact, and operating hours must remain legible and consistent in size across sections.
- The final image must read as a complete premium Korean restaurant menu, not a blank stationery sheet.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters or garbled menu text
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likenesses

studio:prompts3:ours-148.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean snack bar menu board for in-store display, vertical poster layout, bright hand-lettered commercial design.
Designed to feel like a lively neighborhood bunsik shop menu seen at the counter: laminated paper taped to a tiled shop wall, full of handwritten prices, small notices, food doodles, and warm local familiarity for quick ordering.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Vertical {비율/사이즈} menu poster photographed straight-on, with a large top masthead occupying about 14% of the frame, a dense main menu column in the middle 45%, a boxed set-menu recommendation panel on the right or lower-middle side, a drinks and add-on section near the bottom, and shop information along the footer.
- Background should be a cream paper menu sheet with visible laminated sheen, light paper grain, tiny marker bleed, transparent tape corners, pushpin marks, and a hint of pale shop tile behind the board.
- Use colorful sticker-like accents in saturated red, yellow, pink, and orange, plus hand-drawn arrows, price bursts, chili icons, steam doodles, stars, hearts, and tteokbokki sauce splashes.
- Use {매장명} as the main title, {메인 메뉴} and {가격대} as the main pricing list, {세트 메뉴} in a highlighted recommendation box, {음료} in a smaller lower section, and {컨셉 톤} as the overall styling direction.
- Add realistic in-store menu details: small label strips reading "포장 가능", "매운맛 조절", "인기", "오늘의 추천", an address/contact footer, operating hours, and a compact notice area, all in Korean and visually secondary to the required menu text.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Top header: Place {매장명} in the largest hand-drawn Korean calligraphy, slightly arched and playful, with small food doodles around it like steam, stars, hearts, chili peppers, fish-cake skewers, and tteokbokki sauce splashes.
- Header micro details: Add small shop-board text near the masthead such as "SINCE 1998", "동네 단골 맛집", "주문은 카운터에서", and a tiny handwritten credit line "손글씨 메뉴판".
- Main menu area: Set {메인 메뉴} in bold, highly legible handwritten list format, with each item paired clearly to {가격대}; emphasize popular items using red underlines, yellow highlight blocks, small circle stamps reading "인기", and tiny spice-level chili marks.
- Add secondary menu rows around the main list to make it feel like a real bunsik pricelist: "순대 4,500", "오뎅 1,000", "쫄면 6,500", "치즈 추가 1,000", "계란 추가 700", while keeping the required {메인 메뉴} and {가격대} text most prominent and readable.
- Set menu box: Put {세트 메뉴} inside a rounded rectangle or sticker-style box with a stronger hand-drawn border, diagonal yellow fill, red corner tape, and a tiny “추천” callout drawn like a shop sticker, not an official seal.
- Drink section: Display {음료} in a slightly smaller but clear handwritten style near the bottom, separated by a playful dashed divider line; add small illustrated cups, ice cubes, and a side note "시원하게 준비했어요".
- Footer info: Add a small but legible store-info strip at the very bottom with Korean text such as "영업시간 11:00–21:00", "브레이크타임 없음", "서울 동네분식길 12", "전화 02-123-4567", "현금·카드 가능".
- Decorative illustrations: Add marker-style icons of tteokbokki, gimbap, tempura, fish cake, sauce bowls, chopsticks, napkin packs, sauce splatters, and small receipt-like price tags around the edge and between sections.
- Overall layout rhythm: Make the page energetic, colorful, and packed like a real Korean bunsik menu behind a counter, with strong hierarchy so the title, main menu, set menu, and drinks remain instantly readable.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Use a mix of hand-lettered Korean calligraphy and rounded display fonts such as Nanum Brush Script, Cafe24 Ssurround Air, and Pretendard Bold for prices; title around 72–96 px, menu items around 34–44 px, prices around 30–38 px, footer notices around 16–22 px.
- Color palette: Use saturated red #E53935, bright yellow #FDD835, hot pink #EC407A, orange #FB8C00, and cream background #FFF6E8, with black text #1F1F1F for readability.
- Border/shadow: Use thick marker-like outlines 3–5 px, mild paper-cut sticker shadows with 4 px y-offset, 10 px blur, 18% opacity, occasional hand-drawn dashed separators, taped-corner shadows, and laminated-paper highlights.
- Pricing style: Align prices in a practical shop-menu rhythm, using red price numerals, black item names, small won-style commas, and occasional highlight tabs for best sellers.
- Texture and realism: Include marker strokes, slightly uneven hand lettering, paper curl at corners, transparent tape glints, tiny sauce-dot decorations, and a few believable handwritten correction stickers, while keeping all required Korean text crisp.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Front-facing poster capture aesthetic, as if photographed straight-on with a 50mm lens at f/5.6 for a natural printed-sign look.
- Lighting: Soft even daylight from front-left with gentle shop-interior reflections on the laminated surface and soft shadows from taped corners.
- Color grade: High-saturation retro snack-shop palette with warm cream paper, tomato red, sunflower yellow, bubblegum pink accents, and a cozy fluorescent-counter warmth.
- Material feel: Printed-and-handwritten hybrid menu board, laminated poster on a tiled wall, slightly glossy but readable, with handmade marker outlines and sticker overlays.

[6. MOOD]
Warm neighborhood bunsik counter menu — a cheerful Korean local shop signboard with the playful energy of a hand-painted street café display, packed with familiar prices, quick-order cues, and nostalgic after-school snack-shop charm.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문자열이 정확히 보여야 함: "추억의분식", "떡볶이 / 라볶이 / 치즈떡볶이 / 김밥 / 참치김밥 / 튀김", "떡볶이 4,000 / 라볶이 5,500 / 치즈떡볶이 6,000 / 김밥 3,500 / 튀김 500~1,000", "떡볶이 + 김밥 세트 7,500 / 떡라치 세트 9,000", "콜라·사이다 1,500 / 식혜 2,000".
- Additional Korean shop details may appear, such as "포장 가능", "매운맛 조절", "오늘의 추천", "영업시간 11:00–21:00", "서울 동네분식길 12", "전화 02-123-4567", but they must be smaller than the main menu information.
- Hangul must be crisp and correctly formed, with no broken syllables, garbled spacing, or misspelled prices.
- The hierarchy must clearly separate title, main menu, set menu, drinks, and footer shop information, with the set menu visibly boxed.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

studio:prompts3:ours-147.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: {비율/사이즈}

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean grilled-meat restaurant wall menu board, vertically formatted for in-store display, high legibility from a distance.
Traditional samgyeopsal house style with bold category hierarchy, strong contrast, realistic menu-pricelist details, and a menu-prioritized layout for a neighborhood barbecue restaurant.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Large vertical menu board composition: the main title and {매장명} occupy the top 15–18% of the frame, a richly divided menu grid fills the middle 65–70%, and store information, address, phone, and origin notes anchor the bottom 10–12%.
- Background treatment: deep matte black paper-like surface with subtle worn texture, faint charcoal grain, laminated menu-board sheen, and a restrained vintage patina like a real wall-mounted Korean BBQ menu.
- Use {컨셉 톤} as the overall design direction, with strong red category tabs, gold divider rules, off-white price labels, and readable spacing between meat, stew, rice, noodle, liquor, and beverage sections.
- Arrange the content as a practical restaurant price board: main meats, prices, side dishes, drinks, store notice, business hours, reservation line, address, and origin note all appear in their own clearly separated blocks.
- Add small realistic visual cues such as a charcoal grill icon, pork belly line-art, red stamp-style “대표메뉴” label, gold section dividers, tiny menu bullets, and a bottom information strip that feels printed rather than blank.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Top header zone: set {매장명} as the dominant title, centered or slightly top-centered, with thick Korean sans-serif lettering, red and gold accents, and a subtle embossed feel; include {대표문구} as a smaller slogan ribbon below the title.
2) Title accent area: place a small grilled-meat illustration, charcoal flame icon, or appetizing pork-belly photo badge above or beside the main menu block, sized to support the title and establish the BBQ theme.
3) Main menu block: present {메인 메뉴} in the largest category block under a heading such as “고기류 / 대표메뉴”, with {가격대} aligned directly beside or below each item in a clean list format for instant scanning; use red highlights for recommended items and gold price dividers.
4) Side-dish block: place {사이드·찌개} in a separate lower-middle column or band, using slightly smaller type than the main meats but still bold and clearly legible; include stew bowl and noodle icons as subtle section markers.
5) Drinks block: place {주류·음료} in a compact adjacent section with tight vertical rhythm, bottle/glass pictograms, and clearly separated liquor and beverage rows.
6) Store information strip: add {영업시간}, {예약안내}, {전화번호}, and {주소} at the bottom with condensed lettering, a thin gold separator rule above it, and small icons for clock, phone, pin, and reservation.
7) Origin and notice area: include {원산지} in a small but readable footer note with a realistic restaurant-menu disclaimer style, placed below the main price grid or inside the footer strip.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: bold Korean sans-serif such as Pretendard ExtraBold, Noto Sans KR Black, or Sandoll Gothic Heavy for primary text; optional serif or brush-style emphasis only for Chinese-character accents like 肉·味 and small stamp labels.
- Color palette: matte black #0B0B0B, deep red #B31217, warm gold #C9A24A, off-white #F3EBDD, muted brown #5A3A2A, charcoal gray #24211E, and a small amount of flame orange #D96A1F for food icons.
- Border/shadow: thin gold divider lines, red section bars, faint distressed edge wear, soft shadow around major text blocks, 3px y-offset with 10px blur at 12% opacity, and light printed-board texture around corners.
- Menu layout details: use table-like alignment for item names and prices, dotted leader lines or gold separators between names and prices, category badges, small “인기”, “추천”, “점심 가능” tags where they fit naturally, and a consistent won-price format.
- Realism details: include a small address/contact footer, business-hours line, reservation notice, origin note, and divider rules so the design reads as an actual Korean meat restaurant wall menu rather than a plain poster.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: flat graphic poster layout simulated as a print-design board, with a straight-on orthographic view, no perspective distortion, crisp edges.
- Lighting: studio-like even illumination, controlled laminated-board sheen, high contrast readability, with subtle specular highlights only on gold accents and printed red labels.
- Color grade: black, red, and antique gold with slightly desaturated warm neutrals for a classic Korean barbecue-house signboard look.
- Surface rendering: printed acrylic or laminated foam-board texture, faint scratches from daily restaurant use, slightly worn corner edges, and crisp ink boundaries on all Korean typography.

[6. MOOD]
Traditional Korean barbecue restaurant signage — a bold neighborhood meat-house menu board with a classic, no-nonsense street-front feel, appetizing charcoal-grill warmth, and the practical information density of a real samgyeopsal restaurant pricelist.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 표시될 문자열: '한우뜰 정육식당', '오늘도 숯불 위에 정직한 한 점', '삼겹살 / 항정살 / 갈비 / 차돌박이 / 양념갈비', '삼겹살 16,000 / 항정살 18,000 / 갈비 24,000 / 차돌박이 22,000', '된장찌개 7,000 / 김치찌개 7,000 / 냉면 8,000 / 공기밥 1,500', '소주 4,000 / 맥주 5,000 / 막걸리 5,000'.
- 하단 정보는 반드시 읽히게 표시: '영업시간 11:30–23:00', '예약·단체석 문의 가능', '02-784-2470', '서울 마포구 월드컵북로 18길 12', '원산지: 돼지고기 국내산 / 소고기 호주산·국내산'.
- Keep Korean consonant-vowel composition clean and readable; no broken Hangul jamo, no warped letters, and no missing comma separators in prices.
- Main meat prices must be visually paired with the correct item names, and the meat section should remain the primary focus while side dishes, drinks, and store info support it.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Illegible tiny menu text
- Celebrity composites

- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean fashion brand seasonal lookbook poster, editorial campaign layout for social media and print.
Premium designer-brand lookbook poster with cinematic hero fashion photography, clear collection information blocks, real event-style details, and polished campaign graphics for a seasonal collection launch.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center the main model hero in a full-body or half-body vertical composition, occupying about 60% of the frame, with the upper area used for branding and the lower area used for collection/event information.
- Keep {브랜드명} as the primary brand mark near the top, with {시즌컬렉션} as the headline and {컬렉션메시지} as the supporting campaign statement.
- Place {키룩컨셉} as the visual styling direction for the outfit, making the garment silhouette, fabric texture, seams, accessories, footwear, and styling details clearly readable.
- Build a realistic fashion poster grid: hero fashion image, collection title, look number label, launch date, pop-up/event information, ticket or reservation note, sponsor/partner strip, website, and hashtag line.
- Background should feel like a contemporary fashion studio or urban editorial set: matte off-white wall, charcoal floor, muted green painted panel, soft concrete texture, fabric backdrop, or subtle set pieces such as a chrome stool, garment rack edge, floor tape marks, acrylic block, or paper sweep.
- Add refined poster details that naturally appear in a seasonal collection campaign: thin divider rules, small vertical labels, lookbook code, price/reservation note, tiny barcode-like catalog mark, and subtle decorative geometric accents in the signature color palette.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top branding zone (10–15%): place {브랜드명} as a designer wordmark, centered or slightly left-aligned, with {시즌컬렉션} directly beneath it as the main campaign title. Add a small date label reading {룩북날짜} and a vertical spine-style credit such as “LOOKBOOK POSTER / {브랜드명} / SEOUL”.
2. Hero fashion zone (middle 55–65%): show a Korean model in {키룩컨셉}, either full-body or half-body, with editorial posture, strong garment silhouette, realistic clothing folds, visible signature accessories, and natural interaction with the studio or urban set.
3. Message and look label zone: place {컬렉션메시지} in a compact caption block, then add a small label such as “LOOK {룩번호} / EDITORIAL DROP” near the model or side margin.
4. Information box zone (lower 15–20%): add a structured campaign info panel containing {발매구매}, {행사시간}, {행사장소}, {티켓정보}, and {웹사이트}, aligned to the editorial grid and separated by thin rules.
5. Sponsor and decorative zone: include a small partner/sponsor area reading {후원표기}, a hashtag line {해시태그}, a tiny barcode-like catalog graphic, and abstract graphic accents such as coral corner tabs, green vertical bars, cropped circles, or thin diagonal fashion-layout marks.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for the main Korean text, weight 500–700 for headings and 300–400 for body copy; use 34–52px for the title, 16–22px for subcopy, and 12–14px for small info labels.
- Color palette: charcoal #111111, off-white #F4F1EA, deep green #1F4D3A, coral accent #FF6B5A, muted gray #8A8F98; allow {컨셉톤} to guide the accent balance.
- Border/shadow: thin 1px divider lines in #CFCBC2, soft drop shadow 0px 8px 24px 12% opacity on the hero cutout or information box, with realistic printed-poster depth and subtle paper grain.
- Layout texture: allow visible paper fibers, studio floor shadows, fabric weave, garment texture, small editorial labels, date stamps, and campaign catalog marks so the poster feels produced and physically plausible.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial fashion photo shot on a medium-format camera look, 85mm portrait lens at f/2.8 for half-body or 50mm equivalent for full-body, clean sharp garment detail and natural body proportions.
- Lighting: soft studio key light from upper-left at 45°, gentle fill from right, subtle rim light to separate the model from the background, with controlled contrast for a high-end lookbook finish.
- Color grade: muted monochrome base with signature black + green + coral accents, slightly warm neutral skin tones, and refined contrast inspired by modern fashion campaign grading.

[6. MOOD]
Korean designer-brand lookbook editorial — somewhere between W Korea fashion spread and Acne Studios campaign precision, with a premium runway-poster sensibility, Seoul pop-up launch energy, and polished seasonal campaign realism.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following strings must appear exactly as written in the rendered image:
  - {브랜드명}
  - {시즌컬렉션}
  - {키룩컨셉}
  - {컬렉션메시지}
  - {발매구매}
  - {룩북날짜}
  - {행사시간}
  - {행사장소}
  - {티켓정보}
  - {후원표기}
  - {웹사이트}
  - {해시태그}
  - {룩번호}
- The model must look like a Korean 20s fashion model with anatomically correct proportions, clean clothing folds, realistic accessory placement, and believable fashion-poster posing.
- Keep the text hierarchy clear: brand mark, season title, campaign message, look label, launch/event details, ticket/reservation information, sponsor strip, then website/hashtag microcopy.
- Render the lower info panel like a real printed launch poster, including small dividers, catalog code styling, a barcode-like mark, and readable Korean typography.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or recognizable public-figure likenesses

studio:prompts3:ours-145.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean public-interest campaign poster for environment/health/culture awareness, print-ready vertical layout and SNS-shareable editorial poster.
A credible civic communication piece with an action-focused message, enriched with real poster information such as campaign period, participation details, venue, sponsor area, contact line, QR-style participation block, and decorative campaign graphics.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main headline area: {핵심 메시지} placed in the upper-middle 30% of the poster, set as the largest text element with strong visual hierarchy.
- Supporting subject area: warm editorial illustration cluster around the headline using tumbler, reusable cup, plant, small earth motif, recycling arrows, and paper-cut leaf graphics.
- Top identity area: {기관/주최} aligned near the top, compact and official, with {포스터번호} and {캠페인 기간} shown as realistic poster metadata.
- Event information area: {행사일시}, {행사장소}, and {참여안내} presented in a clear civic-information block with small pictogram markers.
- Lower action area: {실천 방법} presented as 3 short, easy-to-scan lines with icon-like spacing.
- Footer CTA area: {CTA} anchored at the bottom with a clean call-to-action strip, QR-style square, contact line {문의}, and sponsor/cooperation text {후원/협력}.
- Background treatment: soft cream or beige paper-like surface with visible recycled-paper grain, tiny fiber speckles, muted green, sage, and soft blue accents.
- Framing direction: vertical poster with centered composition, print-safe crop guides implied by the layout, and a polished public-institution poster finish.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top header zone (top 10–15%): set {기관/주최} in a compact official style, add {포스터번호} on the opposite side, and place {캠페인 기간} beneath with a thin divider rule.
2. Campaign title zone (upper 16–28%): place {캠페인 주제} as the campaign title, large and bold, using a clean sans-serif hierarchy and comfortable line spacing.
3. Key message zone (center 30–50%): render {핵심 메시지} in the largest font size, visually emphasized with solid contrast, surrounded by editorial illustration accents that support the message.
4. Illustration and decorative graphics zone (center and side areas): add semi-flat motifs of a tumbler, leaf, reusable cup, small globe, recycling arrows, water droplet, and circular badge reading {슬로건태그}; use rounded shapes and gentle overlaps like a contemporary civic poster.
5. Event details zone (lower-middle 52–66%): show {행사일시}, {행사장소}, and {참여안내} in three stacked information rows, each with a simple calendar, map-pin, or ticket/participation icon.
6. Action list zone (lower-middle 66–78%): show {실천 방법} as concise bullet-style lines with small pictogram markers, evenly spaced and easy to read at a glance.
7. CTA and sponsor zone (bottom 80–94%): place {CTA} inside a footer band or button-like label, include a QR-code-like square labeled {QR라벨}, show {문의}, and add a sponsor/cooperation strip reading {후원/협력}.
8. Production detail zone (bottom edge): include small page/poster metadata such as {포스터번호}, recycled paper texture, tiny registration marks, and a fine divider line for a realistic printed poster impression.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for the main text, Bold 700–800 for headlines, Medium 500–600 for supporting text, with headline size roughly 72–110px and body size 26–38px.
- Color palette: forest green #4F7A5B, sage #A7B89A, beige #F3EBDD, soft blue #C7DDE8, charcoal #2F3437, with occasional warm yellow #E8C96A for small badges.
- Border/shadow: use soft civic-poster depth such as a subtle shadow 0px 4px 12px at 12% opacity for the main message card or CTA band when needed.
- Graphic style: vector-like editorial illustration with rounded shapes, thin clean outlines, low-detail symbolic icons, tactile paper grain, small sticker labels, and neat divider rules.
- Information design: event details, participation notice, sponsor strip, QR block, and contact line should feel like authentic Korean public campaign poster content rather than placeholder text.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial poster design look, equivalent to a clean flat graphic composition rather than photography; if a source-photo feel is needed, emulate an 85mm f/1.4 shallow-depth portrait crop for any human-free design references.
- Lighting: soft diffused studio lighting feel, even illumination with no harsh highlights, as if lit by a large softbox from upper-left.
- Color grade: muted natural civic palette with warm cream, sage green, soft blue, and restrained charcoal contrast.
- Print finish: matte recycled paper texture, fine ink grain, crisp Korean typography, slight risograph-like warmth in the green and beige areas.

[6. MOOD]
Institutional campaign poster — a Seoul civic design office meets a Kinfolk editorial spread, with the clarity of a modern museum public-information graphic and the approachable warmth of a neighborhood environmental festival notice.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문구가 정확히 표시되어야 함.
  - "플라스틱 줄이기, 작은 한 걸음"
  - "서울시 환경캠페인 본부"
  - "텀블러 한 개로 일년에 365개의 일회용컵을 줄입니다"
  - "텀블러 휴대 / 카페 음료 텀블러 할인 활용 / 분리 배출"
  - "seoul-eco.kr 캠페인 참여"
  - "2026.06.01–06.30"
  - "매주 토요일 11:00–17:00"
  - "서울숲 커뮤니티 광장"
  - "참가비 무료 · 현장 참여 가능"
  - "협력: 동네카페연합 · 시민자원순환센터"
  - "문의 02-120"
- Layout invariant: the main message must be the largest text and remain highly legible at poster distance.
- Illustrations and decorative graphics must stay secondary to the typography and must never cover required Korean text.
- Keep all text horizontal and properly spaced; avoid warped, broken, or decorative unreadable Korean characters.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or recognizable celebrity likenesses
- English replacement of the required Korean campaign text

studio:prompts3:ours-144.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean new product launch announcement poster for beauty skincare, print-ready and social-media-shareable vertical layout.
Premium cosmetic launch poster with a centered product hero, realistic retail/event information, tactile serum texture accents, and bold information hierarchy for both offline display and SNS promotion.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Create a vertical 1024x1536 product launch poster for {브랜드명}, built around a centered product hero occupying about 42–46% of the frame height.
- Place the main launch headline and {제품명} above or overlapping the upper part of the hero zone, with {카테고리} as a refined editorial label.
- Background treatment: {배경질감} with soft off-white or pale neutral paper tones, subtle serum glow, and 1–2 product signature accent colors from {컨셉톤}.
- Add realistic poster content: launch week label, event details, date/time/venue, reservation or ticket/QR area, sponsor/host area, contact line, and hashtag-style SNS copy.
- Surround the product with controlled decorative graphics derived from {장식모티프}: serum droplets, ingredient molecule line art, small texture swatches, thin dividers, calendar/ticket icons, and a small QR-code-like block.
- Keep the visual concept premium and editorial while making the poster feel like a real beauty product campaign displayed in a store, pop-up event, or official social channel.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top header zone: render {브랜드명} as a small brand header, followed by {카테고리}. Add launch labels such as “신제품 런칭”, “NEW ARRIVAL”, and “LAUNCH WEEK” using thin divider rules and compact editorial spacing.
2. Main title zone: render {제품명} large and bold, spanning roughly 70–80% of the poster width, with crisp Korean typography and strong contrast against the background. Add a short Korean subline: “피부에 닿는 첫 번째 광채 루틴”.
3. Main hero zone: show {제품비주얼} as a clean close-up of the product bottle/tube/jar, sharply lit and commercially polished. Include visible packaging details such as label text blocks, cap reflection, glass/plastic material highlight, and a refined signature texture miniature nearby.
4. USP zone: place {핵심혜택} inside a structured callout set with 2–3 short benefit lines, small ingredient icons, and a highlighted benefit tag such as “핵심 성분”, “임상 영감 포뮬러”, or “데일리 케어”. Do not present these as official certifications.
5. Launch info zone: render {출시정보} in a compact but prominent information block. Add “공식몰 선런칭”, “런칭 위크 한정”, and {CTA문구} as readable Korean promotional copy.
6. Event / ticket zone: include {런칭행사명}, {행사일시}, {행사장소}, and “입장/예약: {예약혜택}”. Add a small ticket-stub graphic, a QR-code-like square labeled {QR라벨}, and a short line “스캔하고 알림받기”.
7. Footer sponsor zone: add “HOST {브랜드명}”, {스폰서표기}, {문의정보}, and {해시태그}. Use small sponsor-text blocks, page-style microcopy, and thin horizontal rules so it feels like a real campaign poster.
8. Print/SNS balance: maintain a clear vertical grid, accurate text hierarchy, and enough bleed-aware spacing so every price, date, venue, CTA, and QR label remains readable in a 1024x1536 poster crop.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for the main structure, with bold weights for {제품명}, medium weights for launch labels, and regular weights for footer/event microcopy; size hierarchy should be clear and magazine-like.
- Color palette: off-white #F7F4EF, charcoal #1E1E1E, soft gray #CFCAC2, plus 1–2 accents pulled from {컨셉톤} such as sage #A9B8A5, coral #F08A7A, muted cobalt #4D6B9A, or vitamin amber #F2B35D.
- Graphic system: combine thin hairline rules, small rounded callout boxes, ingredient molecule line art, translucent serum smears, droplet icons, ticket-stub corners, calendar marks, and a compact QR-code-like block.
- Product realism: packaging label must look printed on the object, not floating; reflections should follow the product shape; shadow should anchor the object naturally on the poster surface.
- Border/shadow: subtle 4px y-offset soft drop shadow, 12px blur, 12–15% opacity under the product; use thin hairline rules for section separation and realistic printed-poster depth.
- Retail details: include price, launch date, reservation benefit, venue, contact, and sponsor area as actual poster elements rather than abstract placeholders.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: studio product photography, 85mm macro lens at f/5.6 for crisp packaging detail and controlled perspective.
- Lighting: softbox key light from upper-left at 45°, gentle fill from front-right, very light rim highlight to define the edges; clean commercial product lighting.
- Color grade: clean neutral whites with restrained accent color pop, slightly warm paper tones, premium cosmetic-ad style finish.
- Material rendering: realistic glass or coated plastic, crisp label edges, subtle cap highlights, tactile serum texture, soft paper grain in the printed background.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean beauty launch campaign — refined cosmetic editorial, polished store-poster realism, clean science-inspired skincare storytelling, and a confident new-arrival retail atmosphere.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 다음 문구를 정확히 렌더링: {브랜드명}, {제품명}, {카테고리}, {핵심혜택}, {출시정보}, {런칭행사명}, {행사일시}, {행사장소}, {예약혜택}, {CTA문구}, {문의정보}, {해시태그}.
- 포스터 안에 다음 한국어 라벨을 선명하게 포함: “신제품 런칭”, “런칭 위크”, “공식몰 선런칭”, “스캔하고 알림받기”, “입장/예약”, “문의”.
- Layout invariants: the product hero must stay centered and clearly dominant; the USP callout, launch date, price, event venue, QR label, and CTA must remain readable and not clipped.
- All Korean text must be clean, legible, and free of broken characters or spacing errors.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

- Broken Korean characters or misspelled Hangul
- Celebrity composites unless explicitly requested

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean lecture speaker introduction poster, vertical announcement layout for seminar/webinar promotion.
Premium speaker announcement poster with a portrait-led editorial composition, large name typography, detailed event information, ticket callout, and sponsor/footer blocks for social sharing, venue display, and online registration.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Canvas: tall vertical poster 1024x1536 with a disciplined keynote / insight talk / webinar announcement structure, using {컨셉 톤} as the overall design direction.
- Subject placement: {강연자 이름} portrait occupies the left 40–45% or upper 40% of the frame, while the right side or lower half holds the main typographic stack with strong hierarchy.
- Background treatment: matte cream, soft warm gray, or deep charcoal background with subtle paper grain, faint auditorium light bokeh, muted stage-shadow texture, and thin geometric accent graphics that support the lecture theme.
- Editorial framing: use a strong grid with clear zones for portrait, headline, lecture topic, date/time/venue, ticket information, sponsor strip, and registration micro-copy; add thin rules, small labels, and accent bars for a realistic event-poster finish.
- Place the main readable lines using {강연자 이름}, {직함}, {강연 주제}, {행사명}, {부제}, {날짜}, {시간}, {장소}, {티켓 정보}, {신청 안내}, {주최}, {후원}, {문의} as the exact content fields.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Portrait zone: place {강연자 이름} as a polished speaker portrait, cropped waist-up or chest-up, with realistic skin texture, confident neutral expression, natural fabric detail on clothing, and a crisp editorial cutout or photo panel.
2. Speaker identity stack: set {강연자 이름} as the largest typographic element, bold and highly legible; place {직함} directly beneath it with a small label such as SPEAKER or GUEST SPEAKER.
3. Topic headline: place {강연 주제} as the second major headline, with {부제} as a supporting description line; use accent yellow bars, bracket marks, or oversized quotation marks to make the topic feel like a keynote pull quote.
4. Event details block: show {행사명} near the top as the series label; place {날짜}, {시간}, and {장소} in a structured information grid with icons or micro labels such as DATE, TIME, VENUE.
5. Ticket and registration callout: add a visible CTA block containing {티켓 정보} and {신청 안내}; include a small QR-style registration square or URL-like line, plus a short phrase such as “선착순 마감”.
6. Sponsor/footer strip: place {주최}, {후원}, and {문의} in the bottom area with compact sponsor-area formatting, thin dividers, small logo placeholders, page-like serial text, and a spine-side credit reading “K-AI DESIGN TALK POSTER SERIES”.
7. Decorative graphics: use restrained but visible abstract AI/network line art, circular nodes, cropped quotation marks, stage-light gradients, or yellow geometric tags to make the poster feel produced for a real design-industry event.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard ExtraBold or Noto Sans KR Black for {강연자 이름}, Pretendard SemiBold or Noto Sans KR Medium for {직함}, {강연 주제}, and event labels, Pretendard Regular for sponsor and inquiry details; name size should dominate the poster, with headline scale around 48–80px equivalent and footer around 22–30px equivalent.
- Color palette: black #111111, cream #F5F0E8, warm gray #D9D2C7, accent yellow #F2C94C, optional white #FFFFFF; if using a dark version, invert to charcoal background with cream text and yellow accents.
- Layout detail: combine large editorial typography with realistic poster micro-elements: date chips, rule lines, small category labels, QR registration box, sponsor strip, venue/address line, and a small series number badge.
- Border/shadow: use a soft drop shadow 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity on the portrait cutout, registration card, or floating information blocks when needed; keep the look premium and conference-ready.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Canon EOS R5 with RF 85mm f/1.2L lens, shallow depth of field, realistic chest-up speaker portrait; alternatively Canon EOS R6 Mark II with RF 50mm f/1.8 lens for a more documentary speaker-photo look.
- Lighting: soft studio key light from upper-left at about 45°, gentle fill from front-right, subtle edge light to separate the subject from the background; add faint conference-stage ambience or blurred auditorium glow behind graphic layers.
- Color grade: controlled editorial grade with natural skin tones, slightly warm cream highlights, deep neutral blacks, restrained yellow accents, realistic paper texture, and polished conference-poster color treatment.

[6. MOOD]
Premium conference keynote poster — TEDx-style stage announcement meets modern Korean design-industry seminar editorial, with practical registration details and a credible event-production finish.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문구를 정확히 렌더링할 것.
  - {강연자 이름}
  - {직함}
  - {강연 주제}
  - {행사명}
  - {부제}
  - {날짜}
  - {시간}
  - {장소}
  - {티켓 정보}
  - {신청 안내}
  - {주최}
  - {후원}
  - {문의}
- Poster realism: 날짜/시간/장소/티켓/신청/주최/후원 정보가 실제 강연 포스터처럼 분리되어 읽혀야 하며, 하단에는 후원사 영역과 문의 정보가 작지만 선명하게 보여야 한다.
- Layout invariant: speaker portrait must be clearly visible and the name must be the strongest text element; lecture topic and event details must stay readable and aligned.
- All typography should be clean, sharp, and fully legible in Korean, with no broken syllables or missing spacing.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

[INPUT]

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean gallery / museum / art fair official exhibition poster, print-ready and social-media-shareable vertical layout.
A refined curatorial announcement poster with a central artwork reproduction, credible event information, ticket details, sponsor credits, and institutional gallery identity that feels like a real exhibition promotion.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Poster format: a vertical exhibition poster featuring {전시명} as the main title, {영문전시명} as a small bilingual subtitle, {작가큐레이터} as supporting credit lines, and complete event information for {기간}, {관람시간}, and {장소}.
- Subject placement: {키이미지} occupies the visual anchor area, centered in the upper-middle or placed slightly off-axis on a refined editorial grid, with the artwork reproduction treated like a mounted gallery plate.
- Background treatment: warm off-white or light gray paper tone (#F5F1EA / #F2F2EE) with subtle matte print texture, light ink grain, and faint gallery-paper imperfections.
- Information density: include practical poster details such as ticket price, opening reception, inquiry contact, QR-style ticket block, sponsor area, and small caption text so it reads as an actual public exhibition poster.
- Branding: {갤러리로고} appears as a small gallery identity mark in the footer, paired with {후원협찬} in a sponsor credit strip.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top title zone (upper 18–24%): set {전시명} in a refined serif or high-contrast sans-serif with strong hierarchy; place {영문전시명} beneath it in smaller type, with careful tracking and institutional spacing.
2. Credit line zone: place {작가큐레이터} beneath the title area, followed by a small curatorial note line: {큐레이터노트}.
3. Main image zone (middle 40–52%): place {키이미지} as the central visual focus, framed like a museum reproduction or mounted print; add a discreet artwork caption line beneath it, such as 작가명, 작품명, 연도, 매체.
4. Event info zone (lower 14–20%): organize {기간}, {관람시간}, {장소}, {티켓정보}, and {문의} in compact, highly legible blocks using thin divider rules and a clear grid.
5. Footer identity zone (bottom 8–12%): include {갤러리로고}, {후원협찬}, a small QR-style ticket block labeled 예매 안내, and a subtle decorative graphic motif based on {장식그래픽}.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Noto Serif KR or Nanum Myeongjo for the title at 34–52px, and Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for details at 14–22px; title weight medium to bold, body weight regular to medium.
- Color palette: off-white #F5F1EA, light gray #D9D9D6, charcoal black #1A1A1A, muted warm beige #D8CBB8, and one restrained accent color derived from the key artwork.
- Poster details: include thin divider lines, small page-like registration marks, a neat sponsor band, a QR ticket square, and understated gallery-style microtext to create a believable printed artifact.
- Border/shadow: use a fine 1px gray rule, delicate plate edge, or very soft shadow (0px x-offset, 4px y-offset, 10px blur, 10% opacity) for image separation when needed.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: if the key image is photographic, present it as a museum-quality art reproduction shot on a Phase One IQ4 with 80mm lens at f/8, straight-on perspective, minimal distortion.
- Lighting: neutral diffused gallery light from the front, with slight soft shadow falloff at the edges; avoid dramatic spotlighting unless the artwork itself demands it.
- Color grade: subdued neutral tones with accurate whites, soft beige paper cast, restrained contrast, and no oversaturation.
- Print realism: show crisp ink edges, subtle paper fiber, exact alignment, and believable offset-print texture suitable for a gallery lobby wall and Instagram announcement crop.

[6. MOOD]
Contemporary museum exhibition poster — a polished curatorial announcement with quiet authority, elegant editorial rhythm, and the practical details of a real Seoul gallery event.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following strings must appear exactly and correctly rendered in the image:
  - 고요한 풍경 — 한국 현대 회화전
  - QUIET LANDSCAPES: KOREAN CONTEMPORARY PAINTING
  - 김OO·박OO·이OO 작가 / 큐레이터: 정OO
  - 2026.05.01 금 — 06.30 화
  - 화–일 11:00–19:00 / 월요일 휴관
  - 성수동 GALLERY KIM, 서울 성동구 아차산로 17길 12
  - 관람료 ₩7,500 / 오프닝 리셉션 05.03 17:00
  - 문의 02-1234-5678 · gallerykim.kr
  - 후원: 서울문화재단 · 월간아트뷰
- Layout invariants: the poster must feel like an official exhibition announcement, with clear hierarchy, realistic event details, refined gallery typography, and cleanly rendered Korean characters.
- Add a small QR-style ticket block labeled 예매 안내 and a caption beneath the key image reading 작품 이미지 제공: GALLERY KIM Archive.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters or garbled Hangul
- Random celebrity composites unrelated to the exhibition
- Fabricated government emblems presented as real authority marks
