studio:prompts3:ours-141.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1536x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
YouTube and display ad key visual, strong first-frame composition for fast attention capture.
Dynamic motion-still editorial ad image with a bold headline, supporting subcopy, clear CTA button, and realistic platform-ad details, suitable for performance marketing placements and high-impact YouTube bumper/display campaigns.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center-left hero zone: dynamic human or product visual occupies about 55–60% of the frame, angled for immediate motion impact, with authentic contextual details around the subject that make {제품/서비스} feel real, desirable, and in use.
- Background treatment: deep high-contrast commercial backdrop with subtle motion blur streaks, light trails, expansion effects, realistic reflections, atmospheric haze, and environment cues matching {컨셉 톤}; keep headline readability strong while allowing rich visual texture.
- Text hierarchy: large headline at the upper or mid-right area, sub-message directly below, CTA button anchored lower-right or lower-center, plus small ad metadata such as “AD”, “15초 혜택”, “@brand_official”, and a short Korean hook badge like “지금 주목 ⚡”.
- Add YouTube/display-ad flavor: include an accent emoji or graphic burst, small channel/brand handle, compact view-bait style sticker such as “오늘의 추천”, a tiny progress-bar motif, and subtle UI-inspired micro icons that do not overpower the main message.
- Use {제품/서비스}, {후킹 헤드라인}, {핵심 메시지}, {CTA}, {컨셉 톤}, {비율/사이즈} as editable Korean placeholders.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Hero subject area: present {제품/서비스} as the visual focal point, either as a sharply lit product shot or a dynamic person-in-motion frame, with crisp separation from the background, realistic surface detail, and a slight freeze-frame campaign feel.
2. Motion effect layer: add directional blur, glow streaks, speed expansion, flying accent shapes, and light particles around the hero edges only, keeping the face/product core sharp and readable.
3. Headline block: place {후킹 헤드라인} in very large Korean type, stacked for instant scanability, with tight leading, strong contrast, and a subtle depth effect for mobile thumbnail impact.
4. Supporting copy block: place {핵심 메시지} beneath the headline in smaller but still legible Korean type, using a concise two-line or single-line arrangement.
5. CTA block: render {CTA} as a button-like element with clear padding, rounded rectangle or hard-edge ad button style, visually separated from surrounding text; add small nearby microcopy such as “지금 바로 확인” or “클릭하고 혜택 보기”.
6. Platform detail layer: add small realistic ad elements such as “AD”, “Sponsored”, “@brand_official”, “조회수 12만+”, “NEW 캠페인”, a tiny play icon, progress bar, or swipe arrow, all in Korean-friendly layout proportions.
7. Tone integration: interpret {컨셉 톤} through a performance-ad aesthetic with punchy composition, high energy, polished commercial finish, and believable real-world staging rather than a sterile template.
8. Canvas fit: format everything for {비율/사이즈}, keeping the ad instantly legible across desktop, mobile, and display placements while allowing layered graphics, product context, and promotional details.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for headline and body, headline in ExtraBold 900 at very large size, subcopy in SemiBold 600, CTA in Bold 700 with slightly widened letter spacing; use smaller Medium 500 text for handle, AD label, badge captions, and UI microcopy.
- Color palette: use a high-contrast base such as charcoal black #111111, pure white #FFFFFF, and 1–2 accent colors like electric blue #2D6BFF and neon lime #B9FF3D, or vivid red #FF3B30 if needed for CTA emphasis.
- Border/shadow: CTA button with soft drop shadow, 0px x-offset, 6px y-offset, 18px blur, 20% opacity; headline may use a thin dark shadow, subtle outline, or luminous rim for readability.
- Layout discipline: maintain a strong advertising grid with clear hierarchy between hero, headline, subcopy, CTA, badge, and handle; layer secondary details like arrows, stickers, UI icons, and light streaks to enrich the image without obscuring the Korean text.
- Realistic detail: include tactile materials, product reflections, clothing texture, natural skin detail if a person appears, believable background depth, and campaign-production lighting so the image feels like a finished commercial key visual.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Canon EOS R5 with 85mm f/1.4 portrait look for a person-led key visual, or Sony A7R V with 50mm f/1.8 product-commercial look for an object-led key visual, both with shallow depth of field and crisp subject focus.
- Lighting: studio key light from upper-left at about 45° with a controlled rim light from the right, plus a small fill to preserve facial or product detail; add luminous edge highlights, practical light reflections, and colored accent glows for motion energy.
- Color grade: high-contrast commercial grade with deep blacks, bright whites, and saturated accent colors; slight teal-blue highlights or warm red punch depending on the chosen accent, with realistic skin/product tones and glossy digital-ad finish.

[6. MOOD]
Premium performance-ad key visual — Think Apple-style clarity meets Nike campaign energy, with a polished digital billboard, YouTube thumbnail urgency, and real campaign-shoot richness.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문구를 정확한 한글로 렌더링해야 함.
  - {제품/서비스}
  - {후킹 헤드라인}
  - {핵심 메시지}
  - {CTA}
- Additional Korean text details may appear as realistic ad elements: “AD”, “15초 혜택”, “@brand_official”, “지금 주목 ⚡”, “오늘의 추천”, “조회수 12만+”, “NEW 캠페인”, “지금 바로 확인”.
- Typography must render Korean Jamo correctly, with no broken characters, no spacing glitches, and no illegible overlap.
- If a person is used, facial proportions and hands must be anatomically correct, with natural posture and no extra fingers.
- The layout must remain ad-like and instantly legible within a 5-second glance while feeling like a real premium YouTube/display campaign asset.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Unauthorized celebrity likeness or celebrity composite

[1. PURPOSE]
Luxury Korean magazine advertisement poster for a premium watch brand, editorial fashion-ad layout with cinematic product emphasis.
Designed to feel like a Vogue Korea / Esquire / Harper’s Bazaar print advertisement: refined, high-end, tactile, and realistic for premium brand marketing use, including authentic magazine-page details such as issue information, page folio, campaign caption, product specifications, and discreet purchase/contact information.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Vertical luxury advertisement poster in {비율/사이즈}, using {레이아웃} as the main composition logic with a polished editorial grid and premium print-ad hierarchy.
- The key visual should feature {키 비주얼}; when full-screen, the model occupies about 55–65% of the frame, and when split-layout, the model occupies about 40–45% with a product/copy zone beside it.
- Background treatment: deep matte black or charcoal with subtle velvet-like texture, faint studio-floor reflection, thin gold rule lines, champagne cream typography panels, and small editorial page details.
- Brand name, tagline, campaign copy, and product details should be placed with luxury magazine-ad hierarchy: primary logo/brand line near {브랜드 로고 위치}, supporting copy aligned to the grid, and fine-print information placed as realistic lower-margin advertising text.
- Add believable print-ad elements: {발행 정보}, a small page number, a discreet barcode or QR-like product inquiry block, {스파인 크레딧}, and an editorial caption so the piece reads as a real luxury magazine advertisement rather than a blank product mockup.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Main hero area: Place {키 비주얼} as a sharply lit luxury portrait, with the watch visibly emphasized either on the wrist, near the cuff, or as a detail crop with realistic skin contact and fabric texture.
2. Product emphasis zone: Add a refined watch close-up with crisp metal reflections, polished bevels, sapphire-glass highlights, visible crown detail, bracelet links, and a premium highlight on the gold signature surface.
3. Main copy block: Set {브랜드/제품} as the primary brand line, followed by {태그라인} in a smaller editorial hierarchy; include {캠페인 문구} as a short Korean campaign sentence beneath it.
4. Product information block: Include {제품 스펙}, {가격 표기}, {문의 정보}, and {웹사이트} as small but readable luxury retail information, separated by thin gold dividers or subtle cream text panels.
5. Magazine authenticity layer: Add {발행 정보}, page indicator, small advertising label, {에디토리얼 캡션}, and {스파인 크레딧} along one edge or lower margin, matching the overall black-gold editorial direction.
6. Layout variation handling: If using the left-model/right-product option, keep the model on the left 60% and the product + copy on the right 40%; if using full-screen portrait, anchor the copy in the lower third with strong editorial alignment and a premium magazine rhythm.
7. Logo placement: Place the logo at {브랜드 로고 위치} in a discreet, premium manner while ensuring the brand line remains readable and central to the advertisement.
8. Finish: Use a luxury retail atmosphere with tactile suit fabric, polished metal, realistic shadows, magazine-print micro typography, and cinematic black-and-gold contrast.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use a refined editorial serif like Playfair Display or Cormorant Garamond for the main brand line, paired with a clean sans-serif like Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for supporting Korean copy; weight range 400–700; headline around 72–96px, body around 24–36px, fine print around 14–18px.
- Color palette: matte black #0B0B0D, gold #C8A24A, champagne cream #F4EBDD, charcoal #1C1C1F, optional silver highlight #BFC3C9, with warm skin tones and controlled metallic shine.
- Border/shadow: ultra-soft drop shadow, 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 18% opacity; thin gold rule lines at 1–2px where used; soft reflection under the product close-up for a premium tabletop/studio feel.
- Keep typography crisp and editorial, with careful kerning, wide tracking for the luxury headline, and readable Korean microcopy.
- Use realistic magazine print details: page number, issue/date line, small barcode/QR-like inquiry marker, product code, caption line, and fine-print retail information integrated into the design.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: high-end fashion editorial photography, Phase One IQ4 look with a 85mm f/1.4 portrait lens for the model and a 100mm macro-style crop for the watch details.
- Lighting: dramatic studio setup with a soft key light from upper-left at 45°, subtle rim light from the right, and controlled specular highlights on the gold watch; background falls into rich shadow.
- Color grade: black + gold + cream luxury grade, with deep contrast, polished highlights, and slightly warm metallic reflections.
- Texture realism: visible suit weave, brushed and polished gold metal, sapphire-glass reflection, subtle paper-grain impression in typography areas, and soft contact shadows for believable print-ad depth.

[6. MOOD]
Premium luxury editorial — Vogue Korea fashion ad meets Esquire watch campaign, with a cinematic high-end retail finish, quiet confidence, mature elegance, and a realistic Seoul luxury-magazine advertising atmosphere.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 렌더되어야 하는 문구:

  - {태그라인}

  - {제품 스펙}

  - {에디토리얼 캡션}
  - {문의 정보}

  - {스파인 크레딧}
- Additional small Korean page details may include: “광고”, “PAGE 024”, “VOL.247”, “2026년 5월호”, “서울 에디션”, “QR 문의”, “시그니처 컬렉션”.
- Layout invariants: the image must clearly communicate a premium watch advertisement, with the model and product both readable; if split layout is used, keep the composition balanced and editorial, not symmetrical like a brochure.
- The watch must look anatomically and physically plausible on the wrist or in close-up, with realistic reflections, bracelet articulation, crown placement, dial depth, and polished metal edges.

[INPUT]

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean brand message campaign poster for social, OOH, and print use.
Large-format vertical ad with a bold headline, cinematic key visual, campaign metadata, venue/date information, sponsor strip, QR-style participation block, and premium editorial brand presence.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject occupies about 62% of the frame, either as a large realistic photo of a running Korean 20s person or a single dominant message block, depending on {키 비주얼}.
- Build a strict premium poster hierarchy with cinematic image depth, bold message placement, tactile paper texture, accent graphic lines, and readable campaign information.
- Place {브랜드명} as a compact brand lockup in the upper-right corner or as a single-line footer, using {브랜드 로고 위치}.
- Set {캠페인 메시지} as the main statement and {부제 카피} as the secondary line, both readable at a distance.
- Add realistic poster details: {캠페인 일자}, {캠페인 시간}, {캠페인 장소}, {참여 안내}, {캠페인 코드}, sponsor area, and a small QR-style participation box.
- Use the exact visual tone described in {컨셉 톤}, with a monochrome base and one sharp accent color.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Hero zone (center 60%): Build the composition around {키 비주얼} as the dominant visual, with cinematic contrast, crisp subject separation, motion energy, and a believable urban running atmosphere.
2. Message zone (upper third or center-left): Render {캠페인 메시지} in a bold sans-serif headline, oversized and highly legible, so it becomes the primary campaign statement.
3. Sub-copy zone (beneath headline or near hero edge): Place {부제 카피} in smaller text with tight tracking, functioning as a refined supporting campaign line.
4. Campaign detail zone (lower third): Add a structured information block containing {캠페인 일자}, {캠페인 시간}, {캠페인 장소}, and {참여 안내}; use thin dividers, small labels, and a practical poster information rhythm.
5. Brand zone (top-right or bottom line): Place {브랜드명} according to {브랜드 로고 위치}, styled like a premium campaign signature with a compact wordmark treatment.
6. Sponsor and CTA zone (bottom strip): Include {후원 문구}, a small QR-style square labeled {QR 라벨}, and the campaign code {캠페인 코드}; make it feel like an actual street poster or launch campaign print.
7. Graphic system: Apply {컨셉 톤} across the full poster, using monochrome blacks, whites, and grays plus a single accent color for arrows, route lines, date markers, underlines, or small geometric graphics.
8. Print-readability pass: Maintain strong contrast, sharp typographic hierarchy, and clear separation between headline, image, details, sponsors, and participation CTA for Instagram feed, OOH, and A1/A0 print.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Use Pretendard ExtraBold or Inter Tight Black for the main headline, Noto Sans KR SemiBold for Korean supporting copy, and a clean condensed sans-serif for metadata; headline size should feel 88–120 px equivalent, subtitle 28–38 px equivalent, metadata 18–26 px equivalent.
- Color palette: Follow {컨셉 톤} with black #0B0B0B, charcoal #2A2A2A, off-white #F5F5F2, and one accent color matching the brand signature.
- Graphic details: Add accent route lines, small coordinate marks, subtle halftone grain, poster-fold texture, thin dividers, and a QR-style participation box that supports the campaign concept.
- Text layout: Combine large Korean headline blocks with compact metadata rows; align details precisely so the poster feels designed for a real brand launch.
- Shadow and contrast: Use a subtle soft drop shadow only if needed for headline separation, about 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 12% opacity.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Realistic editorial sports portrait photographed on a 85mm f/1.8 lens or 70–200mm at 135mm, shallow depth of field, clean subject isolation, magazine-ad sharpness.
- Lighting: Cinematic directional light from upper-left with a controlled rim light from the right, as if shot during blue hour or in a studio with a hard key + soft fill.
- Color grade: High-contrast monochrome with one accent color preserved at full saturation; deep blacks, cool grays, and crisp highlight roll-off.
- Surface realism: Printed campaign poster feel with slight paper grain, ink density variation, very subtle scuffing near edges, and realistic overlay of typography on the photographic key visual.

[6. MOOD]
Premium global brand campaign editorial with cinematic sports-commercial energy, confident Korean copywriting, urban night-running atmosphere, and polished launch-poster realism.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문구를 정확히 렌더링할 것.
  - {브랜드명}
  - {캠페인 메시지}
  - {부제 카피}
  - {캠페인 일자}
  - {캠페인 시간}
  - {캠페인 장소}
  - {참여 안내}
  - {후원 문구}
  - {QR 라벨}
  - {캠페인 코드}
- Layout must feel like a major brand campaign poster: bold, premium, information-rich, realistic as a printed campaign asset, and highly legible at a distance.
- If the hero includes a person, the running pose must be anatomically correct and natural.
- All Korean typography must be clean, readable, and free of distorted syllables.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized celebrity likenesses

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean seasonal sale and Black Friday poster for retail promotion, optimized for Instagram, display ads, in-store display, and print.
Large-number discount poster with strong purchase motivation, clear hierarchy, event details, coupon information, and a believable retail campaign finish.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Vertical poster with the discount rate as the dominant hero, occupying 55–65% of the frame in oversized typography.
- Top area presents {스토어명} and {세일 종류} as a campaign masthead, with {배지 문구} as a small urgency sticker or corner tag.
- Mid area centers {할인율} in the largest size, followed by {기간}, {대상 / 카테고리}, and {프로모션 코드} in stacked support lines.
- Lower area presents {추가 혜택} as a bold benefit strip, then adds practical retail details: {지점 / 채널}, {영업시간}, {주소}, {문의}.
- Add a compact sponsor / partner row using {제휴사} and a small coupon or QR-style block labeled {QR 안내 문구}.
- Include decorative sale graphics that naturally belong in a retail poster: diagonal price-tag shapes, lightning accents, coupon perforation marks, small shopping-bag icons, percent symbols, and barcode-like retail marks.
- Use {컨셉 톤} to guide contrast, typography scale, accent treatments, and the balance between bold sale energy and readable campaign information.
- Background should feel bold and retail-driven: deep black base with yellow and red accent shapes, subtle paper-grain or screen-print texture, glossy highlight streaks, and strong separation between headline, offer, and information blocks.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header zone (top 15–18%): Place {스토어명} as a small brand line, then {세일 종류} in a compact masthead style, centered or slightly upper-left, with strong sans-serif type, separator rules, and a small {배지 문구} sticker.
2. Hero discount zone (center 48–58%): Render {할인율} as massive typographic artwork, filling most of the frame; use layered shadow, slight 3D depth, offset outline, or torn-paper highlight so the numerals remain dominant from a distance.
3. Event detail zone (below hero, 12–16%): Set {기간}, {대상 / 카테고리}, and {프로모션 코드} in three clear lines, aligned to the discount block like a real retail campaign poster.
4. Benefit band (lower 10–12%): Place {추가 혜택} inside a ribbon, coupon strip, or high-contrast ticket band; add small percent icons and arrow markers to reinforce urgency.
5. Store information footer (bottom 10–13%): Add {지점 / 채널}, {영업시간}, {주소}, and {문의} in a structured footer with dividers, small icons, and a readable hierarchy.
6. Partner and QR area: Include a compact row for {제휴사} plus a QR-style square or barcode-like element labeled {QR 안내 문구}; it should feel like a plausible coupon/download guide rather than an official certification.
7. Legal note: Place {유의사항} in a small but legible line near the footer, using warm gray or white text over a dark panel.
8. Accent graphics: Use diagonal blocks, burst elements, price tags, coupon edges, shopping-bag silhouettes, and red/yellow motion lines to increase tension and directional flow toward the discount number.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Use Pretendard ExtraBold or Noto Sans KR Black for main headlines, Pretendard Bold for support copy, and slightly condensed spacing for the discount numerals; size hierarchy should be extreme and immediately readable.
- Color palette: Black #0B0B0D, yellow #FFD400, red #E53935, white #F5F5F5, optional warm gray #B7B7B7 for secondary lines.
- Border/shadow: Use sharp high-contrast drop shadows, 6px y-offset, 14px blur, 20% opacity; add thin white or yellow outline for numerals, coupon strips, and price-tag badges when needed for readability.
- Layout character: Energetic retail poster composition with layered sticker shapes, coupon bands, barcode graphics, and footer information; all details should support the central discount offer.
- Texture and finish: Add subtle ink texture, halftone dots, glossy sale-card reflections, or paper fold details to make the poster feel printed and campaign-ready.
- Information hierarchy: The viewer should read in this order: {할인율}, {세일 종류}, {기간}, {추가 혜택}, then store and coupon details.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Graphic poster design, no photographic subject required; if using product imagery, frame it like an 85mm product-ad crop with shallow depth cues and crisp edges.
- Lighting: High-contrast studio-inspired lighting logic, with hard-edged highlight accents and deep shadow separation, like an Adobe MAX retail poster or sports-sale key visual.
- Color grade: Punchy black-yellow-red retail grade with strong saturation, controlled highlights, crisp white text contrast, and saturated yellow highlight shapes.

[6. MOOD]
High-impact retail campaign poster — Japanese department-store sale graphics meets modern D2C performance ad design, with coupon energy, loud discount typography, and practical in-store promotion details.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 렌더할 문자열
  - {스토어명}
  - {세일 종류}
  - {배지 문구}
  - {할인율}
  - {기간}
  - {대상 / 카테고리}
  - {프로모션 코드}
  - {추가 혜택}
  - {지점 / 채널}
  - {영업시간}
  - {주소}
  - {문의}
  - {제휴사}
  - {QR 안내 문구}
  - {유의사항}
- The discount rate must be the largest element and occupy more than half of the visual emphasis.
- Maintain a believable promotional tone; any benefit, code, partner row, coupon block, or footer detail must look like ordinary retail campaign information.
- Korean character shapes, numerals, punctuation, and spacing must be clean and correctly formed.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites unless explicitly requested
- Misleading legal, government, or award-style markings

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean influencer collaboration announcement poster, vertical 2:3 promotional layout for social media launch campaigns, store display, and event reposts.
Clean beauty product collab reveal with a premium retail-poster feel, designed to highlight a limited edition launch, influencer appearance details, purchase call-to-action, and shareable campaign information.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject placement: top announcement header occupies about 16% of the frame, center hero area about 50%, event and purchase details about 24%, footer sponsor and hashtag strip about 10%.
- Background treatment: warm cream-beige base with subtle paper grain, soft cosmetic powder texture, pastel pink and sage accent blocks, translucent sticker shapes, small sparkle marks, ribbon labels, and product-swatch graphics inspired by {컨셉톤}.
- Spacing and framing: editorial grid with layered cards, soft shadows, thin divider rules, rounded CTA modules, and a polished retail campaign composition suitable for mobile reading.
- Include {브랜드_인플루언서}, {제품_이벤트}, {기간}, {구매방법}, {행사일시}, {장소}, {티켓혜택}, {협찬파트너}, {캠페인슬로건}, {CTA문구}, and {해시태그} as the main readable text blocks.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top header strip: place a large collaboration headline such as “X 콜라보” or “한정판 런칭” in bold display type, with {브랜드_인플루언서} directly below in a smaller line; add a tiny poster-code label such as “COLLAB POSTER 05” and a vertical spine credit reading “LAUNCH CAMPAIGN / INFLUENCER EDITION”.
2. Hero zone: show a polished beauty product arrangement with ampoule, toner, cream jar, outer box, ribbon wrap, and a framed influencer portrait card or photo cutout; position {제품_이벤트} as the focal caption beside the hero using a premium editorial frame.
3. Decorative campaign layer: add cosmetic texture smears, soft oval color chips, hand-drawn sparkle icons, mini heart stickers, and a ribbon badge containing {캠페인슬로건}; keep all decorative elements aligned with the pink/beige/sage beauty palette.
4. Event detail module: create a structured information card with labels “LIVE EVENT”, “DATE/TIME”, and “VENUE”; render {행사일시} and {장소} clearly, with a small map-pin icon and calendar icon.
5. Purchase and ticket module: stack {기간}, {구매방법}, and {티켓혜택} in a retail-style info band; include a rounded CTA button labeled {CTA문구}, plus a small QR-style square labeled “구매 바로가기”.
6. Sponsor and footer area: add a compact sponsor strip reading “PARTNER” with {협찬파트너}, small divider lines, campaign contact-style microcopy, and {해시태그} as a social sharing line.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard ExtraBold for the main headline, Pretendard SemiBold for subheads and module labels, Pretendard Regular for supporting copy; headline large and condensed, info labels crisp, body copy medium and highly legible.
- Color palette: soft pink #F4C6CF, warm beige #F3E8DD, muted sage #B9C8B1, ivory #FAF7F2, charcoal #2F2F2F, warm gray #B8AEA4, muted rose #D98D9A.
- Border/shadow: use very soft drop shadow, 0px x-offset, 6px y-offset, 18px blur, 14% opacity, with thin 1px divider lines in warm gray; rounded cards may use 18px corner radius and subtle paper-edge highlights.
- Graphic details: include layered product cards, small label stickers, a dotted ticket stub edge, subtle QR block, circular “LIMITED DROP” mark, and pastel color chips without using fake official certification seals.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: studio product-poster look, equivalent to Canon EOS R5 with 85mm f/1.4 for a portrait-style hero, or 50mm f/2.0 for a centered product flat-lay composition.
- Lighting: soft diffused key light from upper-left at 45°, gentle fill from front-right, faint rim light to separate the hero from the background.
- Color grade: clean beauty editorial grade with warm cream highlights, soft blush midtones, and muted sage accents, slightly desaturated for a premium launch-poster feel.
- Material realism: glossy cosmetic bottles, satin-finish carton box, paper-grain poster surface, soft translucent sticker overlays, and realistic printed ink texture on small labels.

[6. MOOD]
Premium clean-beauty launch poster — like a glossy Olive Young campaign visual mixed with a soft lifestyle editorial layout, influencer fan-event energy, and polished retail promotion design.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 렌더링할 문구:
  - {브랜드_인플루언서}
  - {제품_이벤트}
  - {캠페인슬로건}
  - {기간}
  - {구매방법}
  - {행사일시}
  - {장소}
  - {티켓혜택}
  - {협찬파트너}
  - {CTA문구}
  - {해시태그}
  - “X 콜라보” 또는 “한정판 런칭”
  - “LIVE EVENT”, “DATE/TIME”, “VENUE”, “PARTNER”, “구매 바로가기”
- Layout invariants: headline must be at the top, hero product and influencer visual must remain centered and dominant, event information must sit below the hero, and the CTA purchase band must be clearly visible near the bottom.
- Text must be clean Korean with no broken characters, no garbled spacing, and no mixed-language corruption in the rendered Korean strings.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Illegible small text blocks
- Unauthorized celebrity composites

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean expo and fair booth announcement poster, vertical print-ready promotional layout for a real trade-show booth wall and online pre-event notice. The poster should feel like an actual exhibitor poster: bold headline, brand mark area, booth location, product hero visual, benefit promotion, date/time/venue details, sponsor/support strip, ticket/QR-style info area, and small decorative expo graphics.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main poster uses a tall vertical hierarchy: headline and event identity at the top 18%, brand and booth wayfinding at 18%, central product/brand visual at 34%, benefits and visit CTA at 18%, footer event details and sponsor/contact strip at 12%.
- Build a strong expo-signage composition that reads from 3–5 meters away while still containing realistic printed-poster details for close viewing.
- Background should be a warm off-white premium paper surface with visible fine paper grain, soft pastel gradient patches, subtle botanical skincare motifs, small dotted expo-map accents, and translucent geometric panels using {컨셉 톤} as the visual direction.
- Use {박람회명}, {회사·브랜드}, {부스 번호·위치}, {제품/서비스 한 줄}, {혜택} as the primary copy blocks.
- Include a believable company wordmark area near the headline plus small supporting labels such as “NEW LAUNCH”, “BOOTH EVENT”, “LIMITED SAMPLE”, and Korean wayfinding notes.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Top header zone: Render {박람회명} in a very large, bold Korean headline spanning most of the width, with a compact English subtitle line beneath it: “EXPO BOOTH ANNOUNCEMENT”. Add a small issue/event tag such as “2026 EXHIBITOR POSTER” and a date label “2026.05.14–05.17”.
- Brand zone (upper-middle): Place {회사·브랜드} as a refined logo-like wordmark with a small Korean descriptor line, a tiny “VEGAN SKINCARE” label, and a short credit line such as “Brand presentation by LAIRA Team”.
- Booth info block: Set {부스 번호·위치} in a high-contrast rounded label box or directional sign panel, making the booth number especially legible. Add small wayfinding details: “입구에서 오른쪽 2번째 라인”, “BEAUTY ZONE MAP”, and a simplified mini map strip with arrows and booth-grid marks.
- Product zone (center): Show a polished skincare product hero visual representing the brand concept: serum bottle, cream jar, refill pouch, sample sachets, soft shadows, translucent botanical leaves, water-droplet highlights, and a premium catalog-style product arrangement. The visual should feel like photographed products integrated into an infographic poster.
- Message strip: Place {제품/서비스 한 줄} directly under the product visual as a concise supporting line. Add two tiny icon labels such as “민감 피부 테스트 컨셉”, “데일리 루틴 추천”, and “클린 포뮬러”.
- Benefits box (lower-middle): Create a framed highlight box for {혜택} with a distinct pastel accent background, thin border, coupon-ticket edge detail, small gift/sample icons, and a clear CTA: “현장 방문 혜택”, “오늘 부스에서 받기”, “수량 소진 시 종료”.
- Event detail band: Add realistic poster details in Korean: “운영시간 10:00–18:00”, “장소 코엑스 3관”, “입장 등록 QR”, “문의 @laira.official”, and “무료 상담 / 피부 타입별 추천”. Include a small QR-code-like square and a ticket-info pill reading “사전등록 권장”.
- Sponsor/footer zone: Add a compact Korean/English info band with visual separators: “SEOUL BEAUTY WEEK 2026”, “SUPPORTED BY EXPO PARTNERS”, “HALL 3 · BEAUTY ZONE · H-08”, plus small sponsor placeholder wordmarks and micro contact text.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Use Pretendard ExtraBold or Noto Sans KR Black for the main headline, Pretendard SemiBold for labels, and Pretendard Medium for supporting copy; headline size should feel poster-scale, not brochure-scale.
- Color palette: Follow the BI tone implied by {컨셉 톤}, anchored by soft pink, sage green, warm white, and charcoal black, with accent use of muted beige, dusty rose, pale mint, and warm gray.
- Border/shadow: Use thin 1–2px rules, rounded rectangles, coupon-ticket perforation details, tiny map-line dividers, and a soft drop shadow of 0px x-offset, 6px y-offset, 16px blur, 12% opacity for boxed elements.
- Add layered editorial poster details: small numbered labels, pictogram icons, subtle flower/leaf line art, booth-map arrows, QR-code block, sponsor strip, and ticket-style CTA panel. Maintain crisp alignment and print-clean legibility.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Studio poster composition with a 50mm standard lens look, straight-on front view, sharp infographic clarity, no perspective distortion.
- Lighting: Even softbox-style lighting with bright white illumination from the front-left and subtle fill from the right; allow gentle realistic product shadows and soft paper texture visibility.
- Color grade: Clean editorial white balance with pastel pink and sage accents, slightly warm-neutral print tone, high contrast for text clarity, realistic ink-on-paper finish.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean trade-show branding poster — polished beauty expo signage with editorial skincare catalog richness, approachable booth-event energy, and clear Apple-style information hierarchy.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 렌더링할 문구: "서울 뷰티 위크 2026", "라이라 (LAIRA) — 비건 스킨케어 브랜드", "부스 H-08 / 코엑스 3관 뷰티존", "100% 비건, 민감 피부에 안전한 데일리 케어", "무료 샘플 1500개 한정 + 부스 방문자 30% 쿠폰".
- Additional Korean poster details should be readable and realistic: "2026.05.14–05.17", "운영시간 10:00–18:00", "사전등록 권장", "현장 방문 혜택", "문의 @laira.official", "수량 소진 시 종료".
- English/Korean mix must be clean and intentional, with all major text sharp, aligned, and fully readable like an actual printed expo poster.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness

studio:prompts3:ours-135.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean store opening announcement poster, vertical print-ready + SNS-shareable layout.
Promote a new store or pop-up with a large event headline, brand wordmark area, signature illustration, practical visit details, ticket/reservation info, benefit callout, sponsor area, and realistic retail campaign footer.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Overall layout: tall 1024x1536 poster with a strong top event header occupying about 18–22%, a centered brand and visit-information block occupying about 50–55%, a benefit/ticket strip below it, and a practical footer with sponsor/contact/map cues.
- Main subject: {매장명} presented as the brand focus, with {이벤트 종류} as the primary headline language and {슬로건} as a short campaign phrase.
- Background treatment: soft pastel shop-inspired backdrop with tactile paper grain, cream base, counter-like curved panels, receipt-sticker accents, and {컨셉 톤} color details.
- Composition details: use layered rounded cards, a small illustrated storefront arch, dessert/product motifs, ribbon labels, dotted dividers, map-pin icon, calendar icon, ticket stub shape, and tiny social-media micro icons to make the poster feel like a real opening campaign.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top header area: place a large bold headline reading {이벤트 종류} across the upper band, add a compact brand wordmark area for {매장명}, and include a small line reading {슬로건}. Add decorative sparkles, pastry/product icons, and a soft ribbon behind the headline.
2. Brand block: set {매장명} prominently in the upper-middle section with a refined display style, paired with a signature illustration matching the shop concept such as a pastel storefront, dessert tray, gift box, or pop-up booth.
3. Key info block: place {기간/날짜} and {장소} in a stacked schedule/location card with clear Korean labels like “일정” and “장소”, plus mini icons for calendar, clock, and map pin.
4. Benefit block: highlight {이벤트/혜택} in a coupon-like box or bright ribbon area, with supporting microcopy such as “오픈 기념”, “선착순 혜택”, and “현장 안내”.
5. Ticket and visit info: add a ticket-stub panel reading {티켓/입장정보}, a QR/reservation cue labeled “예약 확인”, and a small wayfinding note reading {지도안내}.
6. Sponsor/contact footer: include {인스타그램}, {연락처}, {후원/협찬}, and a small address/contact strip with divider lines, sponsor logos as generic text badges, social save/share micro icons, and a compact page-like production credit.
7. Decorative graphics: use pastel confetti, sticker tags, ribbon folds, receipt-paper texture, illustrated product thumbnails, and subtle shadows so the poster feels like a real Seoul café/pop-up retail announcement.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard ExtraBold for the headline, Pretendard SemiBold for labels, and Noto Sans KR Regular for details; headline around 72–96px, brand name around 54–72px, body around 28–36px, footer around 18–22px.
- Color palette: use the tones in {컨셉 톤}, anchored by soft pink #F7C6D0, cream #FFF6EA, lavender #CDB9F6, butter yellow #FFE7A8, and warm gray #6E6A67.
- Border/shadow: rounded cards, coupon perforation details, small dotted dividers, soft drop shadows with 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 12–15% opacity, and warm pastel outlines where helpful.
- Text hierarchy: headline and store name must be dominant, schedule/location must be immediately readable, benefits should appear as the strongest callout after the headline, and footer details should feel practical but still legible.
- Print realism: include tiny production marks such as “OPENING WEEK”, “MAP INFO”, “SAVE THE DATE”, a compact barcode-like retail graphic, and small sponsor badges without implying official certification.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: studio product-poster look, equivalent to a 50mm standard lens with a clean front-facing composition and minimal distortion.
- Lighting: soft diffused studio light from upper-left, gentle fill from right, even exposure with mild highlight control.
- Color grade: pastel editorial grade with cream, pink, and lavender balance, slightly warm whites and clean neutral shadows.
- Material feeling: matte coated poster paper, soft paper grain, printed ink texture, layered sticker/coupon elements, and gentle tactile shadows between panels.

[6. MOOD]
Elegant boutique opening poster — polished retail campaign feel like a Kinfolk-inspired brand launch with a contemporary Seoul café/pop-up aesthetic, playful enough for SNS sharing and detailed enough for a real storefront announcement.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문구가 정확히 렌더되어야 함:
  - {매장명}
  - {이벤트 종류}
  - {슬로건}
  - {기간/날짜}
  - {장소}
  - {이벤트/혜택}
  - {티켓/입장정보}
  - {지도안내}
  - {인스타그램}
  - {연락처}
  - {후원/협찬}
- Poster must clearly show these Korean labels as readable rendered text: “일정”, “장소”, “혜택”, “입장 안내”, “예약 확인”, “오픈 기념”, “선착순 혜택”.
- Layout invariant: headline, brand name, schedule, location, benefit, ticket/reservation cue, and contact/footer information must all be clearly legible and not overlap.
- Keep the design vertical, print-poster-like, and suitable for 1024x1536 SNS sharing.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Fake government or institutional approval marks

studio:prompts3:ours-134.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean music festival lineup poster for print and social sharing, official event announcement layout.
Grid-structured concert poster with a realistic full-event information system: festival name, date/time, venue, headliners, lineup tiers, ticket CTA, sponsor strip, and social channel details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Vertical 1024x1536 poster with a strong editorial grid: top title/header block, center hero lineup block, lower event detail/ticket/footer block.
- Main title area occupies about 18% of the frame at the top; 헤드라이너 block takes the visual center at 35–45%; 라인업 is arranged beneath in tiered rows with a realistic multi-artist festival roster density.
- Background is a dark stage-like surface with neon gradient haze, halftone grain, laser-beam streaks, waveform graphics, speaker silhouettes, ticket-stub corners, and sharp punk-inspired geometric accents.
- Use {페스티벌명}, {부제}, {일시}, {장소}, {헤드라이너}, {라인업}, {티켓정보}, {CTA}, {스폰서}, {SNS}, {컨셉톤} with clean grid alignment, clear hierarchy, and convincing official-poster details.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top header band: Place {페스티벌명} centered in a bold condensed masthead style, with {부제} as a small uppercase-style Korean tagline nearby; include thin divider rules, VOL-style micro text, and a small stage icon to make the poster feel like a finished event announcement.
2. Event info block: Set {일시} and {장소} directly under the title in smaller sans-serif type, aligned to the grid with precise tracking; add small labels such as “DATE”, “VENUE”, “OPEN” and a compact map-pin symbol.
3. Main headline block: Render {헤드라이너} as the largest text element in the middle of the poster, stacked or slash-separated as provided, with a neon glow edge, crisp white fill, and subtle cyan/pink offset shadows for stage-light depth.
4. Lineup tier block: Arrange {라인업} in 2–4 tier groups using descending font sizes; separate tiers with thin rules, dot separators, bracket marks, and small day labels such as “DAY 1” and “DAY 2” so the roster feels authentic and information-rich.
5. Event detail strip: Add a lower information zone containing {티켓정보}, age/entry guidance, gate-open note, and weather notice in tiny but readable Korean microcopy; use boxed callouts and small icons for ticket, clock, and location.
6. Style accent layer: Apply {컨셉톤} through abstract neon gradients, punk-inspired angular shards, waveform lines, sticker-like labels, diagonal caution-tape graphics, and stage-light bloom behind the text without hiding the lettering.
7. Sponsor and CTA footer: Place {CTA} in the bottom zone as a clear ticketing callout, boxed or underlined for emphasis; include {스폰서} as a sponsor/partner strip and {SNS} as an official channel line with small social-style icons.
8. Final polish: Keep all text aligned to the poster grid, with no overlap, no warped letters, and consistent spacing across Korean and English typography; the result should look like a realistic printed festival lineup poster photographed flat-on.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Use Pretendard ExtraBold for title blocks, Noto Sans KR Medium/SemiBold for event info and lineup tiers, and a condensed sans style for festival branding; title size should dominate, headliners should feel monumental, and lineup tiers should step down by hierarchy.
- Color palette: Use {컨셉톤} as the base direction, with black #050505, neon pink #FF3EB5, cyan #20E5FF, electric purple #8B5CF6, warm white #F5F5F5, and small lime accents #B6FF3B for ticket and sponsor highlights.
- Border/shadow: Add subtle 4px y-offset soft shadows with 12px blur at 18% opacity; use thin neon outline strokes, divider lines, boxed information modules, diagonal corner ticks, and glowing typographic emphasis for structure.
- Realistic print details: Include slight paper grain, faint ink misregistration, halftone dots, micro scratches, and layered poster texture while keeping the rendered Korean text sharp and readable.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Graphic poster composition, simulated 50mm editorial framing with no photographic distortion; crisp vector-like text rendering and layered print texture.
- Lighting: Stage-inspired neon illumination with a faint top-left glow, secondary cyan rim from the right, magenta bloom behind the headliner names, and diffused light around major text.
- Color grade: High-contrast black base with neon pink/cyan/purple gradient accents, slight halftone grain, modern festival print saturation, and punchy nighttime concert atmosphere.

[6. MOOD]
Official Korean festival lineup poster — Pentaport / DMZ / Have a Nice Trip poster energy with contemporary neon-punk editorial design, realistic ticketing information, sponsor footer, and energetic Seoul summer-night festival atmosphere.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 다음 문자열이 정확히 보여야 함: "웨이브 페스티벌 2026", "도시의 밤을 흔드는 이틀간의 사운드", "2026.06.22(토)~06.23(일) 14:00 OPEN", "한강 노들섬 라이브파크", "네온라인 / 김성 / 글로우", "오아시스 블루 / 팔팔런즈 / 슬로우 번 / 늦은밤 / 비너스 / 달빛소년 / 윤하린 / 로컬웨이브 / 시티노이즈 / 모노드림 / 라임스톤 / 구름합창 / 나이트버스 / 스파클키즈 / 블루파도 / 사운드마켓 / 피크닉클럽 / 새벽라디오", "얼리버드 89,000원 · 1일권 119,000원 · 양일권 179,000원", "ticket.wavefest.kr 예매", "후원: 서울문화재단 · 노들섬 · 사운드랩", "@wavefestival.kr  #웨이브페스티벌".
- Layout invariants: title, subtitle, date/time, venue, headliner, lineup tiers, ticket information, sponsor strip, SNS line, and CTA must all be present; lineup text must remain tiered and grid-aligned.
- Poster realism: include event-detail microcopy, icon labels, decorative neon graphics, stage-light texture, footer partner area, and ticket-style callout while preserving legibility.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized likeness mashups

studio:prompts3:ours-133.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536
- target_format: vertical event poster for print, mobile sharing, and venue signage

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean conference / seminar / lecture official poster, print-ready and SNS-shareable vertical layout.
Create a polished event promotion poster with a realistic conference identity system: strong title, practical registration information, speaker lineup, program highlights, sponsor area, and a clear CTA for online pre-registration.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main title area occupies the top 22% of the poster, with {행사명} as the primary focal point and {부제_태그라인} directly beneath it in smaller type.
- Add a small editorial event label near the header: {행사라벨}, set like a premium forum series marker or session code.
- Middle section uses a structured grid: left-side event facts panel for {일자}, {시간}, {장소}, {주소}; right-side speaker portrait cards or editorial avatar illustrations for {주요연사}.
- Center-lower section includes a program highlight band showing {프로그램}, with time blocks, small divider lines, and conference-session icons such as keynote, panel talk, workshop, and networking.
- Bottom section contains ticket and registration information: {티켓정보}, sponsor/host line {주최후원}, contact line {문의}, and a high-contrast CTA strip for {CTA}.
- Include realistic poster details: QR-style registration box, small ticket badge, venue floor label, sponsor footer, subtle geometric stage-light arcs, grid coordinates, and thin gold divider rules that reinforce the conference theme.
- Background treatment: deep navy, black, or charcoal surface with premium paper grain, faint architectural grid, soft spotlight gradients, and restrained metallic gold accents.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Header block (top 22%): Place {행사라벨} above the title in small caps or compact Korean/English mixed styling; place {행사명} in large bold sans-serif with strong visual weight and tight line spacing.
- Tagline line: Place {부제_태그라인} immediately below the title in smaller medium-weight type, using warm off-white or pale gold for hierarchy and readability.
- Event facts panel (mid-left 28–32%): Stack {일자}, {시간}, {장소}, and {주소} with icon-like labels such as DATE, TIME, VENUE, ADDRESS; use thin rules, small numerals, and structured spacing like a real conference poster.
- Speaker block (mid-right 28–32%): Display {주요연사} as 3–5 labeled speaker cards, paired with circular or rounded-rectangle portrait crops, monochrome silhouette portraits, or refined vector avatar illustrations. Add small role tags like KEYNOTE, CTO TALK, CREATOR SESSION.
- Program band (lower-middle 16–20%): Render {프로그램} as a compact schedule strip with time chips, session separators, and small decorative timeline dots.
- Ticket / registration area (bottom 14–16%): Place {티켓정보} next to a QR-style registration square; place {CTA} inside a solid highlight bar or bordered band sized for quick recognition on mobile.
- Sponsor footer: Place {주최후원} and {문의} in a formal footer area with small logo-like wordmarks, sponsor tiers, and publication-style microtext.
- Decorative graphics: Add thin gold rules, abstract conference stage lines, modular grid coordinates, subtle spotlight beams, and small directional arrows to create an official event-system feel.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for Korean + Inter or Helvetica Neue for English, bold weights for {행사명}, medium weights for {부제_태그라인}, regular/semibold for details; title size should dominate the poster while supporting text stays compact and legible.
- Color palette: use {컨셉톤} as the governing palette, with specific tones such as navy #0B1F3A, black #111111, gold #C8A96A, warm off-white #F5F1E8, muted gray #A7B0BC, and a controlled accent blue #2F6BFF if needed for registration highlights.
- Layout language: premium corporate editorial design with modular panels, session labels, sponsor footer, and QR/ticket elements; all text blocks should feel intentionally typeset for a real conference.
- Border/shadow: thin gold separators, 1–2px rules, soft panel shadows, and subtle metallic linework may be used for depth; avoid turning the poster into a party flyer.
- Information hierarchy: {행사명} first, {일자}/{시간}/{장소} second, {CTA} third, with speaker and program details readable after a quick glance.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: if using speaker photos, treat them like editorial portrait cutouts shot on an 85mm f/1.4 lens with shallow depth of field; if no photos, use clean vector-style profile placeholders with consistent framing.
- Lighting: studio softbox key light from upper-left at 45° with a faint fill from right; for portrait imagery, keep skin tones even and conference-portrait neutral.
- Color grade: deep navy + black base with restrained gold accents, crisp neutral whites, and slight cool contrast for a premium corporate-event look.
- Print finish impression: matte coated paper texture, crisp ink edges, subtle foil-like gold line accents, and high-resolution typography suitable for a 1024x1536 vertical poster.

[6. MOOD]
Institutional keynote poster — similar to a TEDx / conference identity system with a polished editorial layout, practical registration details, sponsor credibility, and premium corporate clarity.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문자열이 정확히 보여야 함:
  - K-AI 디자인 컨퍼런스 2026
  - AI 시대, 디자이너의 역할을 다시 정의하다
  - 공식 포럼 06 · 2026 여름 세션
  - 2026년 6월 15일 (토)
  - 14:00–18:30
  - 코엑스 그랜드볼룸
  - 서울 강남구 영동대로 513
  - 김디자이너 · 박CTO · 이크리에이터 · 정프로덕트리드
  - 14:00 오프닝 키노트 / 15:20 패널토크 / 17:00 네트워킹
  - 얼리버드 ₩79,000 · 현장등록 ₩99,000
  - 주최 K-AI Lab · 후원 서울디자인재단 · 미디어 파트너 Design Weekly
  - 문의 hello@conf.example.kr · 02-1234-5678
  - conf.example.kr 사전등록
- Layout invariants: event title must be the largest text; date, time, venue, ticket info, and CTA must remain clearly legible; speaker names must not overlap with other blocks.
- If profile photos are used, faces must be cleanly cropped and consistently sized; no distorted facial features.
- QR-style box, sponsor footer, and program strip should look like part of a real event poster, not random ornaments.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications that imply government or institutional approval
- Broken Korean characters or unreadable Hangul
- Celebrity composites or recognizable public figures used as speakers without explicit request

[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536
- ratio_size: {비율/사이즈}

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean startup and enterprise-style recruitment poster, vertical hiring announcement for social media, campus boards, office elevators, and careers landing pages.
Create a realistic content-rich hiring poster with a polished corporate design system: company branding, large role title, practical hiring details, benefit cards, application timeline, QR-style apply area, contact line, and clear CTA.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Centered vertical poster with a strong top-to-bottom reading flow: company and campaign header at top 12%, role title hero at 22%, keyword and benefits grid in the middle 38%, application details and CTA block at bottom 18%.
- Background treatment: matte off-white base with subtle warm gray paper texture, fine printed grain, faint geometric grid accents, soft color panels, and a few tasteful recruitment-themed graphic marks such as arrows, rounded stickers, timeline dots, and small check icons.
- Layout should feel like a real Korean hiring poster: scannable, editorial, information-rich, with believable HR details and printed poster depth.
- Use {회사명}, {채용 직무}, {인재상 키워드}, {주요 복지}, {컨셉 톤}, {CTA} placeholders.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Header zone (top 12%): place a compact company wordmark or logo placeholder for {회사명} in a clean rounded rectangle or wordmark area. Add a small campaign label: "2026 상반기 공개채용" and a tiny issue-style tag such as "RECRUIT POSTER 01".
- Hero zone (upper-middle 22%): render {채용 직무} in very large bold sans-serif Korean type, using the highest contrast on the page; this is the primary focal point. Add a short supportive hiring line below: "함께 만들 다음 성장의 자리".
- Sub-hero line: place {컨셉 톤} as a small direction label or tone badge, paired with realistic details like "정규직 · 신입/경력 · 하이브리드 가능".
- Keyword strip (middle-left or middle row): show {인재상 키워드} as 3 spaced key tags or chips with small icons; make each chip feel like a real applicant-fit badge, such as checkmark, spark, graph, or team icon.
- Benefits area (middle 38%): present {주요 복지} as 3 concise icon-text rows or cards. Add realistic supporting labels around them: "복지 하이라이트", "성장 지원", "업무 환경".
- Hiring details module: include a compact schedule card with "모집 기간 2026.05.01–05.31", "전형 절차 서류 → 인터뷰 → 최종합격", and "근무지 서울 · 판교 · 원격 협업".
- Info footer module: add an application guide area with a small QR-code style square, a short URL label "careers.company.kr/apply", contact line "문의 recruit@company.kr", and a tiny map-pin or link icon.
- Sponsor / partner area: create a small footer strip with subtle labels like "People Team", "Tech Hiring", "Career Talk 05.18 19:00"; keep it like a real HR poster footer rather than an official certificate.
- CTA zone (bottom 12%): place {CTA} inside a prominent button-like pill or outlined box with high readability, paired with a small arrow, QR cue, or "지원서 작성하기" label.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for all Korean text; title weight 800~900 at very large size, section labels 600~700, body 400~500, tight but readable line spacing. Use realistic hierarchy like a premium recruitment campaign page.
- Color palette: off-white #F6F3EE base, charcoal #1F2328 text, accent blue #3B82F6, accent lime #A3E635 or coral #FF6B6B for key chips, timeline dots, and CTA highlights; maintain a corporate-clean palette with richer printed detail.
- Border/shadow: thin 1px dividers in cool gray #D7DCE2, soft card shadows around benefit and schedule modules, gentle paper-edge shading, and subtle depth for the CTA card.
- Add believable micro-layout elements: small section numbers, divider labels, application deadline badge, tiny navigation dots, and footer metadata, while keeping all important text legible.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: front-facing graphic poster composition, equivalent to a 50mm normal-perspective editorial layout, straight-on orthographic presentation with no distortion.
- Lighting: studio-flat, evenly lit paper-poster look with subtle top-left highlight, natural printed-paper texture, soft ambient shadow at the poster edges, and crisp digital-print clarity.
- Color grade: crisp cool-neutral corporate grade with off-white, graphite, blue accent, and a small fresh secondary accent; refined Korean tech-company recruitment aesthetic.

[6. MOOD]
Modern Korean startup and enterprise recruiting poster — feels like a polished careers campaign from a fast-growing tech company or large corporate innovation team, informative enough to be real and stylish enough for social media sharing.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following verbatim strings must appear correctly in the rendered image:
  - {회사명}
  - {채용 직무}
  - {인재상 키워드}
  - {주요 복지}
  - {CTA}
  - "2026 상반기 공개채용"
  - "함께 만들 다음 성장의 자리"
  - "정규직 · 신입/경력 · 하이브리드 가능"
  - "모집 기간 2026.05.01–05.31"
  - "전형 절차 서류 → 인터뷰 → 최종합격"
  - "문의 recruit@company.kr"
- Korean text must be clean, fully legible, and rendered with correct Hangul syllables and spacing.
- All text should look like a real hiring poster, with clear hierarchy, readable details, and no decorative distortion.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

studio:prompts3:ours-131.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1536x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Premium typography hero banner for an AI prompt archive website, designed like a contemporary editorial brand identity poster with realistic web-launch details.
Large, clean, content-rich landing hero with a bold wordmark, Korean subtitle, floating circular prompt-preview thumbnails, small navigation labels, metadata chips, and editorial microcopy that makes the page feel like a real service launch screen.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center the huge wordmark across the upper-middle 55% of the frame, spanning nearly the full width, with the subtitle placed directly beneath it in a smaller line.
- Use a smooth {배경 톤} premium background with subtle warm paper grain, soft ink texture, and very faint printed-poster surface variation.
- Arrange {원형 썸네일 컨셉} as 6–8 floating circular mini-scenes around the wordmark, mostly along the left edge, upper-right corner, and lower-right quadrant; each preview should feel like a real saved prompt thumbnail with tiny caption labels.
- Add a refined top navigation strip with small Korean labels: "프롬프트", "컬렉션", "매거진", "가이드", plus a tiny handle-like label "@prompt.archive" and an update chip "2026.05 업데이트".
- Add editorial metadata around the hero: "VOL.131", "AI PROMPT INDEX", "2,600+ CURATED", "NEW 128", and a small bottom-right barcode-style catalog block labeled "ARCHIVE CODE 1536×1024".
- Add 2–3 short Korean feature blurbs in small type near the lower portion, such as "오늘의 큐레이션", "상업용 이미지 레퍼런스", "한국어 프롬프트 최적화", using tidy column alignment.
- Keep the overall design balanced and poster-like, with strong typographic hierarchy, realistic spacing, and rich secondary details that support the main wordmark.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Main wordmark zone (upper-middle 55%): render {사이트/서비스 이름} in a huge ultra-bold modern sans-serif, centered, using {워드마크 색상}, with tight tracking, clean edges, and premium editorial weight.
2. Subtitle zone (directly below wordmark): render {한국어 부제} in smaller Korean sans-serif text, centered, with medium weight, slightly increased letter spacing, and exact punctuation.
3. Floating thumbnail system: place {원형 썸네일 컨셉} as 6–8 circular mini-scenes, each with a different visual theme such as portrait, product shot, food styling, magazine cover, interior mood, travel poster, profile card, and cinematic still; each circle evenly clipped with clean edges, realistic image detail, subtle depth, and a tiny Korean label tag nearby.
4. Navigation and metadata layer: add small header text, update/date labels, volume number, archive index text, micro dividers, and a barcode-style catalog block without turning it into a full dashboard.
5. Feature blurb layer: include 2–3 short Korean blurbs in compact editorial columns near the bottom or side margin, set in light sans-serif with small accent dots or rule lines.
6. Background field: fill the canvas with {배경 톤} as a tactile premium backdrop with subtle paper fiber, soft tonal noise, and faint print-like texture.
7. Accent balance: make the wordmark dominate the composition while the thumbnails, metadata, and feature blurbs act as colorful secondary accents that make the hero feel like a real published web identity.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Inter for the English wordmark, ultra-bold 900 weight, very large display size; use Noto Sans KR or Pretendard for the Korean subtitle, navigation, metadata, and feature blurbs.
- Color palette: {배경 톤}, {워드마크 색상}, plus restrained accent colors inside the thumbnails such as coral, teal, mustard, sky blue, olive, soft pink, warm gray, and muted cobalt.
- Detail typography: top navigation and metadata should be small but legible, with realistic editorial spacing, tiny separators, short Korean labels, and catalog-style numbering.
- Thumbnail styling: thumbnails should have a subtle soft drop shadow, about 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity, crisp circular clipping, and realistic mini-image content rather than flat icons.
- Decorative system: use tiny accent dots, hairline dividers, small caption tags, barcode-like vertical lines, and catalog labels to enrich the composition while keeping the wordmark visually dominant.
- Surface finish: add a slight printed-paper texture and soft ink softness around dark typography, as if the website hero were photographed from a premium brand poster proof.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Canon EOS R5 with RF 50mm f/1.2L studio product-shot mindset, front-facing flat composition, orthographic poster feel, no perspective distortion.
- Lighting: soft diffused studio light from upper-left, very even fill, gentle contact shadows under floating circular thumbnails and small printed elements.
- Color grade: clean cream + deep wordmark color + muted colorful thumbnail accents, with a premium editorial web-brand finish.
- Rendering quality: sharp vector-like typography, realistic paper grain, crisp circular image clipping, high-resolution Korean text, and refined print-design realism.

[6. MOOD]
Premium AI startup landing page hero — contemporary Korean editorial archive, independent magazine index, refined brand poster, and curated creative-tool launch page atmosphere.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 렌더링할 문자열: "이미지 프롬프트 아카이브 · 2,600+ 프롬프트"
- Korean text accuracy: if any Korean subtitle typography is shown, keep the exact punctuation and spacing clean and unbroken.
- Korean text accuracy: render short supporting labels clearly, for example "프롬프트", "컬렉션", "매거진", "가이드", "오늘의 큐레이션", "상업용 이미지 레퍼런스", "한국어 프롬프트 최적화", "2026.05 업데이트".
- Composition invariant: the main wordmark must occupy more than half of the visual impact, and the circular thumbnails, metadata, navigation, and feature blurbs must remain secondary.
- Circular thumbnails must look like distinct mini image previews, not generic dots or icons.
- Keep {사이트/서비스 이름}, {한국어 부제}, {원형 썸네일 컨셉}, {배경 톤}, {워드마크 색상}, and {비율/사이즈} exactly as usable input concepts.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness

studio:prompts3:ours-130.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1536x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Punk zine-style collage hero banner for an AI prompt site, designed like a real scanned magazine moodboard advertisement for a creator-focused landing page.
Horizontal website hero with bold typographic branding, cutout imagery, issue-label details, editorial cover blurbs, and high-contrast creator-culture energy.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center composition: a large sans-serif wordmark for {사이트/서비스 이름} occupies the middle 28–32% of the frame, with a smaller Korean subtitle directly beneath it and a compact brand quote tucked near the lower-right of the title block.
- Surrounding layout: collage elements radiate around the title in an asymmetric ring, with torn-paper edges, clipped magazine scraps, BW portrait fragments, doodles, paint splashes, sticker labels, tape strips, and scanned note fragments filling the left, right, and top corners.
- Background treatment: gritty off-white paper texture with visible fold marks, scuffed print noise, staple impressions, coffee-ring stains, layered halftone ink, photocopy streaks, and small registration marks so the piece feels physically assembled and scanned.
- Editorial realism: add a tiny issue marker such as “VOL.247”, a date label such as “2026년 5월호”, a small barcode area in one lower corner, a compact price line “₩7,500”, small spine/credit text, and 2–3 short Korean feature blurbs around the collage.
- Framing: keep the central typography highly readable while the pasted collage, captions, and zine artifacts build density toward the outer edges for a lively magazine spread look.
- Use {사이트/서비스 이름}, {브랜드 quote}, {액센트 컬러}, {콜라주 요소}, {텍스트 카피}, {비율/사이즈} as the customizable content anchors.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Main title block — Set {사이트/서비스 이름} in a heavy, wide sans-serif wordmark, centered and spanning roughly 40% of the banner width, with crisp black fill, slightly imperfect ink edges, and neon edge accents that feel like screen-printed ink.
2. Subtitle and quote — Place a small Korean subtitle directly under the wordmark using a phrase from {텍스트 카피}; add {브랜드 quote} as a compact supporting line near the title’s lower edge, using tight tracking and a utilitarian editorial layout.
3. Magazine-zine metadata — Add realistic publication details: “VOL.247”, “2026년 5월호”, “PROMPT ZINE / CREATOR ISSUE”, a small barcode block, tiny page code “P.01 HERO”, vertical spine text “AI PROMPT ARCHIVE”, and a model/creator credit line such as “MODEL: 생성형 크리에이터 / PHOTO: 스캔 아카이브”.
4. Feature headline blurbs — Around the title block, include 2–3 short Korean cover-line blurbs in different pasted-label styles: “프롬프트가 결과를 바꾼다”, “아이디어를 붙여라”, “오늘의 생성 실험”, plus smaller stamped fragments derived from {텍스트 카피}.
5. Hero collage field — Arrange {콜라주 요소} across the perimeter as layered cutouts: creator portrait crop shots, café table snapshots with notebooks and laptops, neon alley scenes, BW portrait slices, keyboard close-ups, chat-window printouts, hand-drawn doodles, ticket stubs, sticky notes, ripped arrows, and paint splashes, each overlapping like a physical pasted-up zine page.
6. Accent system — Apply {액센트 컬러} as the dominant highlight language, with 1–2 colors used aggressively on stickers, underline marks, taped corners, rough border strokes, starbursts, arrows, and highlight blocks; keep the remaining tones mostly black, white, paper beige, muted skin tones, and café browns.
7. Copy integration — Embed {텍스트 카피} as scattered slogan fragments in varying sizes, with one phrase acting as a secondary header and the others appearing as stamped cut lines, handwritten labels, caption strips, or tiny sidebar notes.
8. Finish and texture — Add torn paper seams, photocopy grain, staple holes, uneven glue shadows, slight misregistration, rough halftone shadows, ink bleed, scan dust, and curled paper corners so the whole banner feels like a high-end pasted collage from a punk design magazine.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use bold grotesk sans-serif for the main brand mark, e.g. Helvetica Neue, Neue Haas Grotesk, or Pretendard ExtraBold; subtitle in Pretendard Medium or Noto Sans KR Medium; keep the wordmark around 88–120 px equivalent on a 1536x1024 canvas.
- Editorial text hierarchy: use tiny condensed sans-serif for issue/date/barcode captions, bold Korean cover lines for feature blurbs, and marker-like handwritten Korean for doodled annotations; make small text look printed or stamped rather than like a clean app UI.
- Color palette: primarily off-white paper, deep black, and the neon spectrum from {액센트 컬러}; let the accent colors appear in sharp blocks, sticker shapes, underlines, paint swipes, doodle strokes, and torn label backgrounds rather than soft gradients.
- Border/shadow: use torn-paper irregular edges, rough taped labels, subtle photocopy shadowing, and 8–14 px offset cast shadows at 18% opacity for pasted elements; favor handmade zine construction with visible overlaps and physical layering.
- Realistic artifacts: include barcode lines, crop marks, tiny edition numbers, caption arrows, sticker residue, creases, thumbprint smudges, and slight paper warping to make the digital banner feel like a scanned physical collage.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: simulated graphic design composition rather than direct photography, but with editorial cutout realism inspired by a 35mm documentary flash look, scanned magazine clippings, and close-up photocopied print textures.
- Lighting: flat studio scan aesthetic with hard contrast, slight flash glare on clipped photos, faint paper sheen on high-ink areas, and small specular highlights on glossy magazine fragments.
- Color grade: aggressive punk zine palette with black, paper white, hot neon pink, cyan, and yellow, plus occasional muted skin tones, café browns, gray newsprint, and saturated {액센트 컬러} overlays from the collage fragments.
- Material feel: combine matte copier paper, glossy magazine scraps, masking tape, risograph-like ink, marker strokes, printed labels, and gritty halftone photo grain.

[6. MOOD]
Patagonia and Off-White advertisement energy fused with a late-1990s punk zine spread and a Korean creator magazine cover — rebellious, tactile, graphic, noisy, and creator-culture forward.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 렌더링되어야 하는 문자열 — “프롬프트가 결과를 바꾼다”, “아이디어를 붙여라”, “오늘의 생성 실험”, “메인 사이트 이름”이 아니라 {사이트/서비스 이름}의 실제 값, 그리고 한글 부제는 {텍스트 카피} 안에서 사용되는 한국어 문구를 그대로 정확히.
- Required editorial details: include “VOL.247”, “2026년 5월호”, “₩7,500”, “P.01 HERO”, a barcode area, a small credit line, and at least two short Korean feature blurbs.
- Layout invariant: the main wordmark stays centered and dominant, with collage elements orbiting the title rather than covering it.
- Text rendering must preserve mixed Korean and English exactly as provided, with no broken characters or scrambled glyphs.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness

studio:prompts3:ours-129.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1536x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
AI prompt archive site hero illustration for a landing page, 3:2 horizontal banner.
A modern flat editorial illustration that communicates creativity, inspiration, and a professional prompt-library service through a believable creator workspace, rich UI details, and Korean-first content.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center the Korean creator character in the mid-right 40% of the frame, seated at a desk and gazing thoughtfully toward floating thumbnail cards.
- Place the main site wordmark in the upper-left zone as a strong landing-page brand anchor, with the subtitle just below it in a softer calligraphic Korean tone.
- Build the scene around {배경 / 장면} with the desk as the visual anchor, the laptop screen as a live prompt editor, and the floating cards as the secondary focal cluster.
- Use {사이트/서비스 이름}, {한국어 부제 또는 카피}, {캐릭터}, {떠있는 카드 종류}, {컬러 팔레트} as the core content elements.
- Add realistic service-page details: a small top navigation row, search pill, category chips, prompt-count badge, bookmark icons, and a subtle CTA button in Korean, all integrated into the hero illustration.
- Create a layered left-to-right reading flow: brand and copy first, then workspace details, then character expression, then floating prompt-category cards.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header zone (upper-left 20%): place {사이트/서비스 이름} as the primary wordmark in bold English sans-serif, with {한국어 부제 또는 카피} directly beneath it in a lighter handwritten/calligraphy-inspired Korean tone. Add small supporting UI text nearby: "PROMPT ARCHIVE", "VOL.129", "2026.05 업데이트", and a compact pill button reading "프롬프트 둘러보기".
2. Navigation / service layer (upper-left to upper-middle): include a slim landing-page navigation strip with short Korean menu labels such as "홈", "카테고리", "인기 프롬프트", "저장함", plus a search bar containing "무드보드 프롬프트 검색" and a tiny count label "오늘의 추천 24개".
3. Character zone (center-right 40%): draw {캐릭터} seated at the desk, body angled slightly toward the cards, with a reflective, curious expression and relaxed posture. Add believable details such as soft hair strands, a cardigan or casual work shirt, warm skin-tone shading, small glasses or earrings if fitting the character, and one hand near a stylus or keyboard.
4. Desk zone (lower-middle 35%): render {배경 / 장면} with a laptop open, desk lamp, small plant, stacked books, notebook, pen cup, sticky notes, coffee mug, phone, and a small calendar card. On the laptop screen, show a prompt editor interface with readable Korean snippets like "캐릭터 비주얼", "톤: 따뜻한 크림", "저장됨" and tiny UI buttons.
5. Floating card cluster (upper-middle to right 30%): show {떠있는 카드 종류} as 4–5 small rounded thumbnails hovering with subtle tilt, each with a tiny Korean label and different concept illustration inside. Suggested labels: "상세 묘사", "표지 디자인", "제품컷", "캐릭터", "카드뉴스". Include micro-icons for bookmark, copy, sparkle, and rating stars so the cards feel like usable prompt-library items.
6. Background field: use a soft cream base with gentle beige gradients, olive accents in props, coral highlights on cards or UI accents, faint grid-paper texture, translucent interface panels, tiny floating cursor marks, and decorative sparkles that support the creative-tech theme.
7. Information hierarchy: ensure the wordmark reads first, then the subtitle, then the CTA/search details, then the character, then the floating cards; all elements should feel integrated as a polished site hero rather than isolated assets.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use a bold geometric sans-serif for the main wordmark, such as Pretendard ExtraBold or Noto Sans KR Bold; subtitle in a lighter calligraphy or hand-drawn Korean style, medium size, with slightly relaxed tracking. UI labels should use small clean Korean sans-serif text with strong legibility.
- Color palette: {컬러 팔레트}; include cream #F5EFE3, beige #DCCDB8, olive #8A9B6E, and coral #F08A7B as accent touches.
- Border/shadow: use soft vector-style shading with a 2–4px offset shadow, 10–14px blur, and about 15% opacity; cards should have crisp rounded corners and a subtle paper-like edge.
- Surface detail: add tactile but refined textures such as paper grain, matte desk finish, soft fabric folds, translucent UI glass layers, and warm lamp gradients while keeping the illustration web-hero friendly.
- Icon and UI treatment: use consistent rounded icons, small copy/bookmark/save symbols, category chips, tiny progress bars, and Korean labels that make the service look active and content-rich.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: isometric editorial illustration feel, digitally painted flat-vector composition with a 35mm documentary framing logic and a slightly elevated top-front viewpoint.
- Lighting: soft window light from upper-left at 45°, gentle fill from the right, balanced shadow contrast, with a warm desk-lamp glow near the laptop and subtle highlights along the floating cards.
- Color grade: warm cream + beige + olive + coral with a soft pastel saturation curve, clean web-friendly contrast, and no harsh neon tones.
- Rendering approach: modern flat illustration with layered editorial detail, believable workspace proportions, soft painterly gradients, crisp vector edges, and readable Korean UI microcopy.

[6. MOOD]
Premium creative tech landing page — the friendly clarity of Notion meets the editorial polish of a Behance showcase, with the warm lived-in feel of a Korean creator’s desk during an inspired late-afternoon work session.

- Card labels: each floating thumbnail must include a small, legible Korean label rendered clearly without broken characters.

- All cards should feel like slightly different prompt-category thumbnails, not duplicated copies.
- Keep {사이트/서비스 이름}, {한국어 부제 또는 카피}, {캐릭터}, {배경 / 장면}, {떠있는 카드 종류}, {컬러 팔레트}, {비율/사이즈} conceptually intact and visibly represented where applicable.

studio:prompts3:ours-128.content:
[INPUT]
