[1. PURPOSE]
AI 프롬프트 사이트/아카이브 메인 hero banner, mosaic showcase header image for a curated prompt library.
Premium editorial website visual that communicates variety, curation, creative range, and real product depth at a glance, like a polished creative-tech landing page captured as a high-end digital catalog spread.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center hero wordmark occupies about 22% of width and sits slightly above center; subtitle is directly below with tight vertical spacing.
- Surrounding mosaic wall fills the rest of the frame with dozens of floating thumbnail tiles, arranged in a loose isometric arc around the center, with realistic UI card details and small Korean category labels.
- Background is a warm beige-to-cream paper-like field with subtle gold glow near the upper-left and lower-right edges, fine tactile grain, and a faint editorial vignette.
- Add a believable website-header layer: small top navigation labels, a rounded search field, category chips, tiny bookmark/share icons, prompt-count metadata, and a few floating prompt cards that make the hero feel like an actual AI prompt archive service.
- Keep the central wordmark instantly readable while allowing the surrounding thumbnails to feel content-rich, layered, and curated.
- Apply {사이트/서비스 이름}, {한국어 부제}, {썸네일 컨셉}, {배경 톤}, {레이아웃}, {비율/사이즈}, {금지} as content and styling constraints.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Background layer — build a soft editorial backdrop in warm beige, cream, and muted gold, with fine paper texture, subtle fiber speckles, faint vignette, and soft gold atmospheric glow to anchor the layout.
2. Central typography block — place {사이트/서비스 이름} as the largest element in the center, set in a bold modern sans-serif, then place {한국어 부제} beneath it in smaller Korean text with clear hierarchy. Add a tiny metadata line below the subtitle such as 업데이트 2026.05 · VOL.128 · 큐레이션 247개, set much smaller so it supports but does not compete.
3. Website UI accents — add a slim top navigation bar with short Korean labels such as 추천, 카테고리, 인기 프롬프트, 새 컬렉션; include a small rounded search box reading 프롬프트 검색 and tiny micro icons for 저장 and 공유 at the far right.
4. Thumbnail mosaic field — surround the center with dozens of small tiles showing varied AI-generated visuals such as Korean cafe scenes, K-pop poster art, webtoon panels, editorial portrait cards, magazine-cover layouts, food photography, product mockups, architecture interiors, fashion crops, menu boards, Instagram cards, and cinematic landscape prompts; each tile should differ in style, framing, color treatment, and apparent use case.
5. Tile details — several thumbnails include realistic Korean micro text such as 카페 무드, 웹툰 컷, 포스터, 메뉴판, 룩북, 썸네일, 카드뉴스, 제품컷, plus tiny slide numbers like 03/12, prompt badges like Midjourney and SDXL, small heart/bookmark icons, and thumbnail captions; all text should be small but legible where visible.
6. Depth and floating effect — offset thumbnail tiles with slight rotations, shallow perspective, soft lifted shadows, thin neutral borders, occasional overlapping corners, and layered z-depth so the wall feels like a floating curated collage rather than a flat grid.
7. Curation rhythm — alternate bright and muted thumbnails, mixing portrait, square, and landscape mini-cards while maintaining premium editorial cohesion; distribute warm cafe browns, vivid poster reds, muted webtoon pastels, food yellows, and fashion blacks evenly around the center.
8. Main readability — maintain a soft luminous halo around the central wordmark, with thumbnails subtly scaling down and fading in contrast near the exact center so the title and subtitle stay crisp.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: {사이트/서비스 이름} uses a bold modern sans-serif such as Inter, Helvetica Neue, or Pretendard ExtraBold, large headline scale; {한국어 부제} uses Noto Sans KR or Pretendard Medium at a much smaller size.
- Supporting Korean UI labels use Pretendard, Noto Sans KR, or a similar clean interface font; keep labels short, realistic, and aligned like a polished SaaS landing page.
- Color palette: warm beige #EADCC8, cream #F6F1E7, soft gold #D8B66A, muted cocoa #7A5E45, charcoal #2A2522, with small thumbnail accents in dusty coral, sage, muted blue, soft black, and warm ivory.
- Border/shadow: each thumbnail has a soft drop shadow with 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 16% opacity; slight rounded corners and thin neutral borders only where needed.
- Add realistic tactile and digital details: subtle paper grain in the background, faint glassy highlight on select UI cards, small cursor-like dot accents, tiny prompt chips, and soft shadow contact points under overlapping cards.
- Keep all extra text secondary to the main identity; microcopy should make the archive look useful and inhabited, not like filler.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 35mm editorial product-style composition, front-facing with subtle isometric depth; if thumbnail imagery appears photographic, treat them like mixed-media mini prints rather than a single camera capture.
- Lighting: soft diffused window light from upper-left at 45°, gentle fill from lower-right, faint gold rim glow around the mosaic edges.
- Color grade: warm cream + beige + antique gold with restrained saturation, premium catalog-editorial finish, no neon spill.
- Rendering quality: crisp high-resolution UI typography, believable anti-aliased edges, realistic layered shadows, clean perspective alignment, and rich thumbnail variety without looking randomly generated.

[6. MOOD]
Premium creative-tech editorial — like a curated Notion, Aesop, and Kinfolk-inspired landing page collage with a high-end magazine spread feel, upgraded with the density and usefulness of a real Korean AI prompt archive dashboard.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the subtitle must appear exactly as 이미지 프롬프트 아카이브.
- Korean text accuracy: no broken Korean characters, no missing spacing, no garbled syllables.
- Layout invariant: {사이트/서비스 이름} must be the dominant central wordmark, with {한국어 부제} directly underneath.
- Layout invariant: thumbnail mosaic must include many distinct prompt-image genres and must look curated, not repetitive.
- Required Korean microcopy examples to render where appropriate: 추천, 카테고리, 인기 프롬프트, 새 컬렉션, 프롬프트 검색, 카페 무드, 웹툰 컷, 포스터, 메뉴판, 룩북, 썸네일, 카드뉴스, 제품컷.
- Include small archive metadata such as VOL.128, 2026.05, 큐레이션 247개, and 03/12 on selected cards, while keeping the main wordmark hierarchy intact.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

studio:prompts3:ours-127.content:
[INPUT]
- reference_image: {참고 이미지}
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean body-analysis motivation report infographic based on a full-body or upper-body reference photo. Social-media-friendly vertical editorial report for Instagram/card-news use, combining realistic body reference, practical health guidance, progress tracking, and uplifting self-care framing.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Top header area (about 18%): create a magazine-report style title block with {리포트 유형}, {리포트 번호}, {발행일}, {작성자}, and a small page indicator “01 / 05”. Add a subtle date stamp and a thin olive divider.
- Main comparison area (about 28%): place the current-person photo on the left and the expected-change illustration on the right in a balanced comparison panel. Use labels “현재 기록” and “{예상 변화 기간} 예상 변화”, plus a small location/date label reading “{기록 라벨}”.
- Center analysis area (about 34%): arrange multiple analysis cards with {중앙 분석 항목} as the main content. Each card should include a small wellness icon, a bold Korean label, a short one-line explanation, and one compact metric chip such as “균형”, “루틴”, “식단”, “목표”.
- Progress and stats strip (about 10%): include three small dashboard widgets: “목표: {현재 목표}”, “루틴: {주간 루틴}”, “배지: {건강 배지}”. Add a friendly 5-star motivation score nearby.
- Bottom CTA area (about 10%): feature {하단 동기부여 메시지} as the main closing line, followed by “저장하고 1주 뒤 다시 체크하기” and {CTA 문구}. Include tiny save/share micro icons and a page footer “다음 장: 맞춤 루틴 가이드 →”.
- Background treatment: soft beige paper-like surface with visible subtle texture, gentle olive accent shapes, soft coral highlights, rounded report cards, checkmarks, tiny graph ticks, and warm editorial sticker tags.
- Spacing and framing: use clear card margins, rounded rectangles, column-aligned report modules, section dividers, caption labels, and a polished Korean health magazine grid suitable for a 1024x1536 vertical card.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header zone: introduce the report with {리포트 유형} in a bold title block, then place a smaller supportive tone line using {리포트 톤}. Add “REPORT ID {리포트 번호}”, “발행일 {발행일}”, “작성 {작성자}”, and “for {대상 닉네임}”.
2. Top comparison zone: show the current body photo cleanly cut out on one side with a soft shadow, and place the expected {예상 변화 기간} change illustration on the other side; the change should look natural, realistic, and non-exaggerated. Add small captions: “오늘의 기록”, “8주 후 예측”, “건강한 변화 기준”.
3. Analysis grid: build 4 compact boxes for {중앙 분석 항목}, each box containing a simple line icon, a short Korean heading, a one-line explanation, and a soft coral mini tag such as “START”, “MOVE”, “MEAL”, “GOAL”.
4. Motivation strip: add a warm encouragement sentence using {하단 동기부여 메시지}, followed by a 5-star score graphic that feels friendly, editorial, and self-care oriented.
5. Progress widgets: include small realistic report details: weekly checklist, hydration dot tracker, sleep/meal/routine mini bars, and a badge area using {건강 배지}. Keep all numbers framed as motivational examples rather than medical diagnosis.
6. Footer note area: add a small lifestyle-health editorial disclaimer style line: “본 리포트는 참고용 웰니스 가이드이며, 개인 컨디션에 맞춰 조절하세요.” Add a card-news page indicator, save/share icons, and the end-card CTA {CTA 문구}.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for all body text, with Bold 700 for headings and Medium 500 for descriptions; title large, subheads clear, captions compact but legible.
- Color palette: {주요 색상}, warm ivory, muted charcoal; use exact tones such as #F3EBDD, #8A9B6E, #F2A7A0, #FFF9F1, #3B3B3B.
- Border/shadow: rounded cards with soft drop shadows, 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 12% opacity; use thin divider lines in muted olive and small coral status chips.
- Graphic treatment: modern wellness infographic shapes, tiny icons for dumbbell/leaf/bowl/flag/star, soft editorial stickers, mini progress charts, and certificate-style corner flourishes without implying official certification.
- Layout personality: {디자인 스타일} with warm lifestyle magazine detail, realistic social-media report density, readable Korean captions, and subtle paper texture.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: realistic portrait cutout based on a 50mm full-frame portrait look, natural proportions, sharp but flattering detail.
- Lighting: soft diffused window light from upper-left with gentle fill from front-right, minimal shadow hardness, realistic skin tones.
- Color grade: warm editorial neutral grade with beige and olive dominance, soft coral accents, slightly desaturated health-magazine finish.
- Rendering quality: crisp infographic text, clean vector icons, realistic photo integration, tactile paper texture, and soft shadows that separate each report module.

[6. MOOD]
Korean wellness editorial report — calm, encouraging, magazine-like lifestyle guidance with a Kinfolk x health infographic feel, practical card-news energy, warm self-care tone, and realistic motivation-tracker details.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 렌더링할 문구: "체형 분석 및 건강 동기부여 종합 리포트", "긍정적·응원·자기긍정 톤 (자기 비하 X)", "8주 후", "체형 타입 분석, 추천 운동, 추천 식단, 목표 설정 가이드", "오늘의 작은 한 걸음이 미래의 나를 만듭니다".
- 반드시 포함할 추가 한국어 요소: "REPORT ID RPT-0526", "2026.05.01", "for 오늘의 나", "01 / 05", "현재 기록", "8주 후 예상 변화", "목표: 건강한 체지방 감량과 근력 향상", "루틴: 주 4회 30분", "배지: 꾸준함 레벨 3", "저장하고 1주 뒤 다시 체크하기".
- The current-person photo and the expected-change illustration must remain realistic and respectful; no exaggerated body transformation.
- All four analysis items must be shown clearly and evenly balanced, with icons, short explanations, and small metric chips.
- Include a visible 5-star motivation score and a small lifestyle-health disclaimer line.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Humiliating, body-shaming, or overly negative wording
- Exaggerated transformation, unrealistic anatomy, or misleading fitness claims

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean tarot card analysis report poster for a person using the attached portrait as the reference image. A premium three-card mystical reading laid out like a polished social-media horoscope feature, with realistic printed-card texture, editorial labels, date stamps, fortune ratings, and shareable poster details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: {참고 이미지} is placed as a small cutout portrait panel on the left-middle side, integrated like a client profile card with a gold nameplate-style caption and a tiny date/location label.
- Card arrangement: {카드 배열} should be rendered as three vertically aligned luxury tarot cards with equal spacing, each card framed in gold and presented as real printed cards resting above the poster surface with slight shadow depth.
- Background treatment: deep navy to plum gradient backdrop with subtle star-dot texture, faint Korean minhwa pattern overlays, soft smoky vignette around edges, and layered paper-like grain so the image feels like a real premium fortune poster.
- Text zones: right side contains layered Korean analysis text blocks, small dividers, mini tag labels, and a compact “오늘의 리딩 노트” area; bottom band contains five star-rating items for {운세 항목} with readable alignment.
- Editorial poster details: include a small top-right issue/date label such as “TODAY TAROT VOL.126”, “2026년 5월 1일”, a tiny barcode/QR-style area near the lower corner, a small social handle such as “@today_tarot.kr”, and micro footer text like “저장하고 다시 보기”.
- Typography balance: title and card labels should feel mystical and editorial, while analysis text remains highly readable in {텍스트 폰트}.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Top header area: elegant title banner with a gold filigree frame, subtle glow, decorative stars, and a premium magazine-like label; title reads “오늘의 타로 카드 사진 분석” with a smaller subtitle “오늘의 카드 · 나를 위한 3장 리딩”.
- Center hero area (middle 55%): three tarot cards arranged in a neat row with slight perspective depth, gold rim decorations, corner ornaments, and each card showing Roman numerals at the top plus Korean/English card names at the bottom.
- Card artwork layer: each card uses {카드 그림체} illustration style, with refined linework, muted jewel tones, antique cream highlights, and a tactile premium printed-card texture with tiny paper fibers.
- Card labels and notes: add compact Korean labels beside or below the three cards: “과거”, “현재”, “미래”; each card has a one-line keyword tag such as “흐름”, “선택”, “기회” and a concise Korean meaning sentence.
- Left portrait inset: a small cropped portrait panel of {참고 이미지} placed beside the cards, bordered in thin gold with a soft shadow, visually linked to the analysis text; include a small caption plate reading “오늘의 질문자” and a subtle sticker tag “PHOTO READING”.
- Analysis text area: adjacent to each card, place one concise Korean meaning line in the style of a tarot note, followed by one short overall interpretation block using {분석 톤}; include realistic section labels like “카드 해석”, “핵심 키워드”, and “오늘의 조언”.
- Summary block: a composite message at mid-lower section written as a warm reading that connects the three cards into one narrative; match {종합 메시지 분량} and make it feel like a personal tarot report rather than generic filler.
- Rating strip: bottom section shows five fortune categories from {운세 항목}, each with a 5-point star rating row, small gold star icons, and short Korean micro-comments such as “차분히 상승”, “기회 포착”, “균형 유지”.
- Footer details: add a refined lower footer with “연애 · 재물 · 직업 · 건강 · 인덕”, a tiny barcode/QR-style graphic block, page-like marker “CARD 01 / DAILY READING”, and a small credit line “Tarot styling by Luna Archive”.
- Decorative finish: scattered gold sparkles, crescent moon icons, fine line ornaments, tiny constellation marks, and subtle minhwa cloud motifs should frame the content and make the poster feel handcrafted and premium.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use {텍스트 폰트} for the main Korean typography; headers/card titles may combine a refined serif such as Cormorant Garamond or Noto Serif KR with Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for body text; title around 44-56px, body around 24-30px, rating labels 22-26px, micro footer text 12-16px.
- Color palette: deep navy #0B1230, plum #4A234B, gold #D8B15A, antique cream #F4E9D6, soft violet #8E72B6, star white #F7F6F2, with accent tones drawn from {전체 디자인 테마}.
- Borders/shadows: thin gold border lines, soft drop shadow with 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 18% opacity, plus faint outer glow around cards and portrait panel.
- Text styling: Roman numerals crisp and centered at card tops; Korean and English card names must be stacked neatly at the bottom in high-contrast light cream; use small gold divider rules and pill-shaped tags for realistic editorial hierarchy.
- Realistic print details: include subtle paper grain, slight ink texture on the tarot illustrations, tiny registration-like footer marks, and layered sticker/card shadows to avoid a flat digital mockup.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: front-facing editorial composition, 50mm lens look with slight top-down angle, crisp card edges and controlled depth layering.
- Lighting: studio softbox key from upper-left at 45° with a gentle rim light from upper-right, plus low-intensity ambient glow behind the cards.
- Color grade: luxury nocturne grade with navy, plum, gold, and cream; subtle bloom on highlights, no neon saturation.
- Material realism: cards should look like satin-coated paper with embossed gold foil edges; portrait inset should look like a small glossy photo print mounted onto the design.

[6. MOOD]
Premium mystical fortune editorial — a luxury tarot spread with the refined atmosphere of a high-end magazine horoscope feature, enriched with believable social-poster details, warm personal guidance, and elegant Korean fortune-report styling.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 표시되어야 하는 문구: “오늘의 카드”, “과거”, “미래”, “연애”, “재물”, “직업”, “건강”, “인덕”.
- 추가로 선명하게 보이면 좋은 문구: “오늘의 타로 카드 사진 분석”, “현재”, “오늘의 리딩 노트”, “핵심 키워드”, “오늘의 조언”, “저장하고 다시 보기”, “2026년 5월 1일”, “TODAY TAROT VOL.126”, “@today_tarot.kr”.
- 카드 상단의 로마 숫자, 카드 하단의 한글·영문 카드명, 그리고 분석 문장은 모두 깨끗하고 선명하게 읽혀야 함.
- {참고 이미지} 인물 사진은 실제 인물의 얼굴 비율이 자연스럽고 왜곡 없이 유지되어야 함.
- 각 카드의 레이아웃은 3장 모두 통일감 있게 유지하고, 별점은 모두 5점 만점 형식으로 표시해야 함.
- 전체 분석 문체는 {분석 톤}에 맞추고, 종합 메시지는 {종합 메시지 분량}에 맞는 분량으로 구성해야 함.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean cosmetic consultation infographic, before/after comparison report with multiple facial-area simulation cells, editorial medical-aesthetic layout.
Designed for clear side-by-side review of subtle facial refinement concepts, suitable for beauty consultation presentation and social-media sharing, with realistic report metadata, clinic-document details, annotations, and readable Korean microcopy.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Top hero zone (about 26%): the original face photo stays natural and unchanged as the Before reference, framed with a thin report-style border, small label area, date stamp, report number, and consultation metadata.
- Main grid zone (about 54%): multiple simulation cells for {시뮬레이션 부위} arranged in a precise 2-column or 3-column grid, each cell with a Korean label, arrow indicator, one-line change note, tiny measurement guide marks, and a small confidence-style visual bar labeled as 참고용.
- Bottom summary zone (about 20%): a boxed headline for {종합 메시지}, followed by compact checklist notes, a small QR/barcode-style appointment block, and a clear disclaimer line for {면책 문구}.
- Overall spacing should feel like a premium clinic report: balanced margins, crisp alignment, layered panels, realistic document density, and no crowded overlaps.
- Use {분석 톤}, keeping the layout objective and calm rather than promotional.
- Use {디자인 색상} across background, panels, dividers, accent details, small icons, tag labels, and chart lines.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header area: set a compact title block with a clinic-report feel, using a subtle gold rule and restrained typography above the hero image. Include Korean title text “성형 전후 비교 리포트”, “REPORT No. A-0526”, “상담일 2026.05.01”, “PRIVATE PREVIEW”, and a small page marker “PAGE 01 / 01”.
2. Before reference area: place the original face photo at the top in a clean rectangular frame, with a small “Before” tag, a tiny crop/angle note “정면 기준”, and no heavy filters or beauty retouching. Add light facial guide lines or semi-transparent landmark dots around nose bridge, jawline, cheekbone, eye line, and lip center so it reads as a real consultation analysis sheet.
3. Simulation grid: create separate cells for 코, 눈, 턱, 이마, 입, 광대; each cell should contain a tiny left-to-right arrow, a labeled Korean 부위명, and a short natural-change description. Example cell notes: “라인 정돈”, “또렷한 인상”, “부드러운 윤곽”, “비율 균형”, “입매 정리”, “광대 볼륨 완화”.
4. Per-cell visual treatment: show each simulated result as a refined, slightly altered concept, with the face geometry staying realistic and the changes staying within a subtle range. Add miniature before/after thumbnails inside each cell, small corner labels “B” and “A”, and fine dotted guides that align with the relevant facial area.
5. Comparison logic: keep all cells visually consistent in size, padding, and label placement so the report reads like a systematic consultation sheet. Add small sublabels such as “변화 강도: {변화 강도}”, “분석 톤: {분석 톤}”, and “시뮬레이션 부위: {시뮬레이션 부위}” where appropriate.
6. Summary box: place {종합 메시지} in a prominent rounded rectangle or clean bordered panel, using slightly larger type and a soft gold accent line. Surround it with three compact supporting notes: “자연스러운 비율 우선”, “과한 변화 지양”, “개인 얼굴형 기준”.
7. Disclaimer strip: place {면책 문구} in small text at the bottom edge or side strip, clearly readable but secondary to the main content. Include the exact line “재미용 시뮬레이션, 실제 시술 전 전문의 상담 필수” and a small footer with “상담 예약 02-0000-0000”, “@clinic_preview”, and a simple barcode/QR-like graphic block without claiming certification.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for body and labels, Medium to SemiBold for section titles, Regular for notes; title size around 36–44px, body around 20–26px, disclaimer around 14–16px, micro metadata around 11–13px.
- Color palette: {디자인 색상} with off-white #FAFAF7, warm beige #EFE5D6, soft gray #D9D9D9, muted gold #C8A96A, charcoal #2E2E2E for readable text.
- Border/shadow: thin 1px–2px dividers, soft drop shadow 0px 6px 18px at 12% opacity, rounded corners with a restrained clinic-document look.
- Graphic details: use fine gold rules, soft beige section tabs, pale gray measurement ticks, tiny dot markers, discreet iconography for calendar / memo / camera angle, and a realistic report footer.
- Text hierarchy: title, report metadata, panel labels, per-cell notes, and disclaimer should all be legible in Korean, with visual emphasis on the comparison grid and summary message.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: clean front-facing portrait capture, 85mm f/1.8 look for the face reference, and crisp infographic framing for the comparison cells; keep perspective natural and undistorted.
- Lighting: soft studio light from upper-left at about 45°, gentle fill from front-right, low-contrast and even across all panels to preserve medical-consultation clarity.
- Color grade: neutral cream and beige base with controlled gold accents, slightly desaturated skin-tone presentation, no oversaturated makeup look.
- Material realism: make the report look like a premium printed consultation sheet or high-resolution tablet document, with subtle paper grain, soft panel shadows, and realistic photographic texture in every portrait thumbnail.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean aesthetic-clinic consultation report — a restrained editorial medical infographic with the calm clarity of a high-end dermatology brochure and magazine-style layout discipline. The image should feel like a real client-facing preview sheet prepared after a consultation, polished, informative, and content-rich without becoming chaotic.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 렌더링되어야 하는 문구: "코", "눈", "턱", "이마", "입", "광대", "본연의 매력을 살린 변화", "재미용 시뮬레이션, 실제 시술 전 전문의 상담 필수", "Before".
- Additional Korean text should be clean and readable: "성형 전후 비교 리포트", "REPORT No. A-0526", "상담일 2026.05.01", "정면 기준", "변화 강도: {변화 강도}", "분석 톤: {분석 톤}", "자연스러운 비율 우선", "과한 변화 지양", "개인 얼굴형 기준".
- All comparison cells must keep a consistent layout and subtle-change scale; no exaggerated facial distortion, no duplicate anatomy errors, and no mismatched labels.
- The original face photo must remain natural in the Before area and should not be beautified beyond a clean report presentation.
- Keep {종합 메시지}, {면책 문구}, {시뮬레이션 부위}, {분석 톤}, {변화 강도}, and {디자인 색상} visibly integrated as report content or styling references.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean aging-process comparison simulation poster, 4x2 grid layout, family-friendly self-awareness and health-motivation content.
Single-canvas comparison chart showing the same face across multiple life stages with clear age progression, realistic editorial portrait detail, and an informational campaign-style message panel.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Overall layout: {그리드 레이아웃} arranged as a 4x2 comparison grid on a vertical poster canvas, using seven portrait cells plus one information/message cell that feels like part of a real printed health-awareness poster.
- Subject placement: each portrait cell contains the same person’s face and upper torso, aligned consistently to keep bone structure, eye shape, nose bridge, jawline, and expression identity stable across ages.
- Background treatment: {배경 스타일} in a soft off-white or pale warm gray poster surface with warm paper grain, subtle studio backdrop gradients inside the portrait cells, and faint editorial layout marks that support the comparison-chart feeling.
- Spacing and framing: equal gutters between cells, thin separators, softly rounded cell corners, small caption bars beneath portraits, and an eighth information panel containing the message, date, venue, and campaign details.
- Add realistic poster details: small top date label, campaign subtitle, page-like reference text, sponsor strip, QR-code placeholder box, and tiny credit line such as “Aging Simulation Editorial Study / Model: Same Identity Composite”.
- Use {연령별 변화 강조}, {인물 의상 스타일}, {셀 라벨}, {메시지 문구}, {전체적인 분위기} as controllable placeholders.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Header area (top 10-12%): create a premium health-campaign title area with Korean headline “노화 과정 비교 시뮬레이션”, small issue-style label “LIFE AWARENESS POSTER 2026”, date tag “2026.05”, and a short subtitle “같은 얼굴, 다른 시간의 기록”.
2) Grid cells: place the same face in seven age stages from 20s through 80s, each cell preserving identity while changing skin elasticity, hair color, wrinkle depth, facial fullness, eyelid heaviness, neck texture, posture nuance, and expression maturity according to age.
3) Age progression detail: 20대 should look smooth and bright; 30대 natural and healthy; 40대 with subtle expression lines and calmness; 50대 with visible eye and forehead lines; 60대 with early silver-gray hair and a warm expression; 70대 with white hair, gentle smile, and deeper wrinkles; 80대 with white hair, serene calm, and a life-worn depth.
4) Clothing treatment: keep {인물 의상 스타일} consistent with each age, updating cut, fabric texture, collar shape, knitwear weight, and styling subtly per life stage so the series feels realistic rather than costume-like.
5) Label area: place {셀 라벨} as small Korean text beneath every cell, aligned centrally, with a readable hierarchy; include secondary micro-captions such as “피부 탄력”, “표정선”, “생활습관 기록” in tiny Korean text where appropriate.
6) Information/message cell: use the remaining grid cell as a campaign card containing {메시지 문구}, plus realistic poster copy: “무료 상담 데이”, “2026.05.18 SAT 14:00”, “서울 라이프케어 홀”, “문의 02-1234-2026”, and a small QR-code placeholder with label “참여 신청”.
7) Footer area: add a slim sponsor/credit strip with invented organizer text such as “주최 라이프케어 스튜디오”, “후원 헬스루틴 매거진”, small barcode-like registration block, and fine-print educational disclaimer in Korean: “본 이미지는 건강 인식 캠페인을 위한 시뮬레이션입니다.”

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR, medium to semibold weight for labels, bold for the main title and message box, compact microtext for credits and event details, size hierarchy tuned for mobile viewing.
- Color palette: soft cream #F7F3EB, warm gray #D9D4CC, muted beige #CBBBA3, charcoal #2F2F2F, gentle sage #A9B8A8 for accent only if needed.
- Border/shadow: thin 1px separators in light gray, subtle drop shadow 3px y-offset, 10px blur, 12% opacity for the message box, soft rounded portrait cards, gentle inner shadows for a premium printed-poster feel.
- Graphic accents: use small sage dots, thin timeline arrows, age markers, light beige caption ribbons, and discreet registration/barcode/QR blocks to make the poster feel authentic and content-rich.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial portrait consistency using an 85mm f/1.8 look for facial realism, with each age stage framed as a controlled head-and-shoulders crop.
- Lighting: soft diffused studio light from upper-left at about 45°, gentle fill from front-right, even exposure across all cells so age differences read clearly without dramatic mood shifts.
- Color grade: warm neutral editorial grade, slightly desaturated creams and beiges with natural skin tones, avoiding harsh contrast.
- Realism detail: visible natural skin pores, age-appropriate fine lines, hair texture, fabric weave, subtle catchlights in the eyes, and slight variations in facial softness while preserving the same underlying identity.

[6. MOOD]
Positive lifestyle editorial — similar to a thoughtful health-awareness infographic in a premium magazine like Kinfolk or Monocle, with a calm, compassionate, realistic family-content tone and a gentle motivation toward long-term self-care.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문자열: “20대”, “30대”, “40대”, “50대”, “60대”, “70대”, “80대”, “오늘 우리가 가꿔야 할 것은 미래의 나”.
- Additional Korean poster text should be legible and natural: “노화 과정 비교 시뮬레이션”, “같은 얼굴, 다른 시간의 기록”, “무료 상담 데이”, “2026.05.18 SAT 14:00”, “서울 라이프케어 홀”, “참여 신청”, “본 이미지는 건강 인식 캠페인을 위한 시뮬레이션입니다.”
- Identity consistency: the same person must remain recognizable across all age stages, with preserved facial structure, eye placement, nose shape, jawline, and expression essence.
- Grid integrity: all 7 age stages must be shown within one coherent comparison layout, with clear age ordering and no duplicated labels.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean traditional face-reading report infographic, portrait editorial layout, social-shareable vertical card.
Blend folk-fortune booklet cues with modern data-viz framing for a light, trend-friendly reading sheet.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center the isolated face photo as the main hero, occupying about 52% of the canvas height, with generous margins so the annotations remain readable.
- Place a clean, calm background behind the face: warm paper-beige base with subtle hanji fiber texture and no busy patterns.
- Use {분석 톤} to guide the wording style of all callouts and summary notes.
- Use {리포트 종류} as the main report framing language.
- Mark the facial regions with fine arrow lines and compact Korean labels, arranged evenly around the face to avoid overlap.
- Build the lower or side summary area as a structured results box with star ratings, short comments, and a neat grid hierarchy.
- Use {핵심 분석 부위} as the labeled regions to annotate around the face.
- Use {종합 운세 항목} as the summary categories in the rating box.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Hero face area (mid 52%): {참고 이미지} isolated cleanly and centered, with soft realistic cutout edges and a subtle paper-shadow on the beige background, no gradient bleed.
- Annotation ring: thin gold and dark-ink arrows radiate from the face toward each key region, with small rounded label capsules placed in balanced positions around the portrait.
- Region labels: each of {핵심 분석 부위} should appear as paired Korean + Hanja text, followed by a one-line interpretive note in compact infographic style.
- Main title block: place {리포트 종류} at the top in a prominent headline treatment, with a small subtitle line in a restrained traditional-card style.
- Summary score box: dedicate the lower third to {종합 운세 항목} as a 5-row rating panel, each row including a short comment and five-star maximum indicator.
- Tone layer: keep every insight aligned with {분석 톤}, using supportive, neutral-positive phrasing rather than sharp or negative wording.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard Bold for headers, Noto Sans KR Medium for labels, and Nanum Myeongjo or a traditional serif Korean/Hanja font for accent lines; title around 42-56 px, labels 20-24 px, body notes 16-18 px.
- Color palette: warm beige #F3E8D7, ink black #1B1B1B, muted gold #B8924C, deep ink-red #7A2E2A, soft parchment #FBF6EE.
- Border/shadow: use thin 1.5px ink lines, rounded card corners, and a soft drop shadow with 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity.
- Hanji texture should be subtle and even, never overpowering the face or the text blocks.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial portrait look with an 85mm f/1.4 aesthetic, shallow depth of field feel for the face cutout, but keep all infographic text crisp and flat.
- Lighting: soft window light from upper-left at roughly 45°, gentle fill from right, with a faint rim separation to keep the isolated face distinct from the background.
- Color grade: warm cream, muted gold, and ink-black with a slight dried-red accent; preserve natural skin tones while keeping the overall card refined and traditional.

[6. MOOD]
A premium Korean fortune-book editorial with modern infographic clarity — like a Kinfolk-style paper spread mixed with a contemporary K-culture tarot card.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 표기할 문구 — "한국 전통 관상학 분석 리포트", "이마", "관록궁", "눈", "인덕", "코", "재백궁", "입", "식복", "턱", "지각", "광대", "권위", "직업", "재물", "연애", "건강", "인덕".
- Every facial region label must pair Korean and Hanja consistently and remain legible.
- The face must stay anatomically natural, with the original photo preserved as the base subject.
- All star ratings in the summary box must use a 5-star maximum scale.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals or certification marks
- Broken Korean characters
- Negative, scary, or humiliating fortune language
- Overlapping arrows or unreadable label collisions
- Extra facial features, warped anatomy, or exaggerated stylization that obscures the source face

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean palmistry analysis report infographic, vertical fortune-card layout, social-media-friendly editorial poster.
Combine a realistic hand-scan presentation with playful fortune-analysis panels, date-stamped report details, and shareable card-news styling for casual reading and posting.
Apply {메인 디자인 컨셉} as the main design direction while keeping the image polished, warm, and content-rich.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center the {참고 이미지} palm photo as the main hero, occupying about 52% of the frame height, naturally masked with a soft shadow and thin highlight edge so the palm texture feels tangible.
- Surround the palm with labeled line callouts, arrow pointers, tiny measurement ticks, and analysis notes, keeping the composition balanced and readable at a glance.
- Use {주요 색상 팔레트} as the overall palette, with warm paper-like background texture, subtle paper fibers, faint astrological marks, dotted guide lines, and small lucky-symbol accents.
- Place the summary analysis boxes along the lower third and right-side margin in a neat card-grid arrangement, with realistic printed-card layering and soft shadows.
- Include editorial metadata: top issue label “VOL.122”, date label “2026.05.01”, small category tag “PALM READING REPORT”, model-name credit “HAND MODEL: @lucky_hand”, and a small barcode-style area near the footer.
- Add subtle social-card UI details such as tiny save/share icons, a page indicator “01 / 05”, and a short CTA chip “저장하고 다시 보기”.
- Apply {분석 톤}, {내용 톤 제약}, and {텍스트 스타일} to all caption text, rating labels, and short Korean report copy.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Main header area (top 14%): title “손금 분석 리포트” set in a fortune-card masthead style, with elegant handwritten accent on key words, thin decorative divider lines, issue number “VOL.122”, date “2026년 5월호”, and a small subtitle “오늘의 손바닥이 말해주는 흐름”.
2) Palm hero area (center 52%): {참고 이미지} isolated as a realistic scanned-photo hero, centered on a cream-beige paper surface with soft shadow, visible palm texture, faint scan guide marks, and small decorative celestial symbols around the outer edges.
3) Line annotation layer: draw five distinct colored line overlays with small arrow pointers and compact tags for 생명선, 감정선, 두뇌선, 운명선, 태양선; each label should include Korean and English names, e.g. “생명선 Life Line”.
4) Analysis note layer: next to each line tag, add a short positive interpretive sentence using {분석 톤}, with concise handwritten or rounded sans-serif callouts; include tiny icons such as heart, coin, star, compass, and leaf where appropriate.
5) Summary fortune cards (bottom 24%): create five mini boxes for {종합 분석 항목}, each with a one-line comment, a 5-star rating row, and a small numeric score such as “4.5 / 5”; align consistently for easy comparison.
6) Side report strip: add a narrow right-side vertical strip with three quick stats — “집중도 87%”, “직감 지수 92%”, “행운 컬러 골드” — plus small badge labels “GOOD FLOW” and “NEW CHANCE”.
7) Footer microcopy: add a small disclaimer-style line in subdued gray indicating the content is for entertainment use, plus barcode-style graphic, creator credit “Editor. 별빛 리포트”, and page indicator “01 / 05”.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard Bold for headers, Pretendard Medium for body, and a hand-drawn calligraphy font for emphasis; title around 54-64px, labels 20-24px, notes 16-18px, metadata 11-14px.
- Color palette: warm beige #F4E9D8, gold #C9A24A, blush pink #E9B7C6, soft gray #CFCFD4, deep charcoal #3A3A3A, plus line colors from {표시할 손금 라인}.
- Border/shadow: soft drop shadow 0 6px 18px rgba(0,0,0,0.10), thin gold borders on cards, rounded corners 18px, subtle paper grain overlay, fine dotted dividers, and tiny sticker-like badges.
- Print details: add realistic microtext blocks, small caption strips, light crease texture, faint ink variation, and delicate ornamental corner marks without overpowering the palm.
- Text density should feel like a real Korean lifestyle report card: readable main labels, short blurbs, compact metadata, and layered editorial elements.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: top-lit scanned-photo editorial look, simulated with a 50mm lens feel at f/5.6, sharp detail on palm texture and precise graphic overlays.
- Lighting: soft diffused window light from upper-left with gentle fill from right, low-contrast and evenly readable across the entire poster.
- Color grade: creamy beige, muted gold, soft pink, and cool gray with restrained saturation, like a modern Korean fortune-card infographic printed on premium stationery.
- Rendering quality: realistic paper grain, natural skin texture from the reference palm, crisp vector-like labels, clean print registration, and subtle depth between stickers, cards, and the hand image.

[6. MOOD]
Playful Korean fortune report — trendy card-news infographic mixed with a gentle lifestyle editorial feel, similar to a warm magazine advice spread with collectible fortune-card details.
The overall impression should feel friendly, optimistic, personalized, and share-worthy rather than clinical.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 표시할 문구 — “손금 분석 리포트”, “생명선”, “감정선”, “두뇌선”, “운명선”, “태양선”, “오늘의 운세”, “연애운”, “재물운”, “직업운”, “건강운”.
- Additional Korean text to render clearly: “VOL.122”, “2026년 5월호”, “오늘의 손바닥이 말해주는 흐름”, “저장하고 다시 보기”, “집중도 87%”, “직감 지수 92%”, “행운 컬러 골드”, “Editor. 별빛 리포트”, “HAND MODEL: @lucky_hand”, “01 / 05”.
- Each palm line must have the correct arrow direction and matching label color from {표시할 손금 라인}.
- Keep all five summary boxes visible, evenly spaced, and clearly readable with one-line comments and star ratings.
- All analysis wording should follow {분석 톤} and {내용 톤 제약}, staying light, casual, and non-alarming.
- All Korean characters must render cleanly without distortion, clipping, or broken spacing.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

- 아래 옵션 (디자인 톤·색·언어·길이 등) 만 사용자가 customize 합니다.

[INPUT]
- reference_image: {참고 이미지}
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Create a professional hairstyle simulation comparison sheet for a Korean salon catalog, showing 10 hairstyle variations in a 5x2 grid on one vertical canvas.
Designed for hair consultation, trend lookbook presentation, and before/after-style hairstyle preview using the same face and outfit across all panels, with realistic salon catalog information such as issue date, salon name, consultation number, and contact block.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- A single model based on {인물 컨셉} is repeated across all 10 cells with identical face, expression, pose angle, skin tone, and clothing; only the hair changes.
- Use a {컷 종류} framing in every panel so the head, shoulders, and upper chest stay consistently visible, like a salon consultation portrait board.
- Arrange the 10 images in a strict {그리드 레이아웃} with thin white or light-gray divider lines between cells and consistent gutters.
- Add a refined catalog header at the top: main title “{카탈로그 제목}”, small season label “{시즌 라벨}”, salon name “{살롱명}”, consultation number “{상담 번호}”, and date/location label “{촬영 날짜} · {촬영 지점}”.
- Use a realistic salon lookbook background treatment: warm white studio backdrop, subtle paper texture, faint beige label strips, and small hair-tone swatch chips beside selected labels where appropriate.
- Bottom label area in each cell must display the hairstyle name from {헤어스타일 목록} in a compact, readable Korean caption, with a tiny numbered tag from 01 to 10.
- Add a slim footer band with “{상담 안내 문구}”, “{연락처}”, “{주소}”, and a small QR-style reservation placeholder labeled “예약 QR”.
- Maintain full visual consistency according to {인물 일관성} so each variation feels like the same person in a hairstyle matrix.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Overall canvas: build a vertical premium comparison board with a 90–120 px catalog header, 10 equal portrait cells, and a 70–90 px footer information band.
2. Identity lock: keep facial structure, skin tone, expression, pose angle, makeup intensity, and outfit unchanged across all panels; only the hair changes per style.
3. Hairstyle application: render each cell to match one item from {헤어스타일 목록}, with clear differentiation in length, curl pattern, hair color, bangs, volume, texture, parting, and face-framing layers.
4. Grid separation: use thin divider lines, consistent gutters, subtle label strips, and small numbered tags so the layout reads like a real salon portfolio sheet.
5. Label strip: place the exact Korean hairstyle name under each cell, centered or left-aligned within the label area, separated from the image area by a thin rule.
6. Header details: include the visible text “{카탈로그 제목}”, “{시즌 라벨}”, “{살롱명}”, “{상담 번호}”, “{촬영 날짜}”, and “{촬영 지점}” with clean editorial spacing.
7. Footer details: include contact and booking information using “{상담 안내 문구}”, “{연락처}”, “{주소}”, and “예약 QR”, designed like a practical salon handout.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR, medium weight for hairstyle labels, 22–28 px equivalent; header title 36–48 px equivalent; small metadata 14–18 px equivalent; clean Korean sans-serif with excellent legibility.
- Color palette: pure white #FFFFFF, warm off-white #FAF7F1, soft gray #E7E7E7, charcoal #222222, muted beige #D8C8B4, salon brown #8A6A4F, pale rose-beige #EFE4DD for label accents.
- Graphic details: thin divider lines, small rounded numbered tags, subtle hair-color swatch chips, discreet footer icons for phone/location/booking, and a small QR-style square that looks like a reservation code without claiming official certification.
- Border/shadow: ultra-thin divider lines and a soft editorial card shadow may be used, around 2px y-offset, 8px blur, 10% opacity.
- The entire board should feel like a premium Korean salon lookbook and consultation handout, polished enough for print or social media sharing.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Canon EOS R5 studio portrait simulation with an 85mm f/2.0 look, natural face compression, realistic head-and-shoulders proportions, and consistent camera distance across all cells.
- Lighting: soft diffused studio light from upper-left at 45°, gentle fill from front-right, controlled highlights on hair strands, natural catchlights, and soft shadow transition under the jawline.
- Color grade: neutral-cool whites with accurate Korean skin tones, slightly polished editorial finish, subtle contrast for hair texture clarity, realistic shine on straight hair, curls, highlights, and dyed sections.
- Rendering quality: realistic hair fiber detail, natural scalp line and parting, believable bangs, flyaways, layered ends, perm volume, and color transitions while keeping the same facial identity.

[6. MOOD]
Professional Korean salon catalog — clean yet realistic hair trend lookbook aesthetic, similar to a premium beauty consultation board for a high-end Seoul salon, with practical printed-catalog details and soft editorial warmth.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 한글 텍스트가 정확히 렌더링되어야 함:
  - {카탈로그 제목}
  - {시즌 라벨}
  - {살롱명}
  - {상담 번호}
  - {촬영 날짜} · {촬영 지점}
  - 단발
  - 롱 스트레이트
  - 레이어드 롱
  - 시스루 뱅 + 미디엄
  - 픽시 컷
  - 한국 펌
  - 바일렛/와인 컬러 염색 + 미디엄
  - 밝은 갈색 하이라이트 + 롱
  - 옆가르마 + 길게 흘러내린 굵은 웨이브
  - 자연 컬리 + 짧은 단발
  - {상담 안내 문구}
  - {연락처}
  - {주소}
  - 예약 QR
- All 10 panels must show the same face, same expression, same outfit, same crop, same lighting direction, and same makeup intensity.
- Hair must be the only changing element between panels; each style must visibly match its label in length, color, curl, bangs, and parting.
- The grid must contain exactly 10 styles, no duplicates, no missing panel, ordered left-to-right and top-to-bottom from 01 to 10.
- All Korean characters, numbers, punctuation, plus signs, slashes, and spacing in labels must be crisp and not garbled.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized celebrity likeness
- False medical, legal, or government-style endorsement marks

[1. PURPOSE]
K-pop comeback poster collage for idol group branding, designed as a fandom zine x trading-card x album-booklet hybrid.
Vertical 1024x1536 promotional poster for social sharing, street-poster printing, fan reposts, and comeback announcement use, with a cinematic center hero, layered collage typography, real album-release information blocks, and collectible fan-culture details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject placement: {포스터 메인 인물} takes the central 42–48% of the frame as the hero cut, with the surrounding collage elements wrapping in a loose oval rhythm.
- Background treatment: textured off-white paper base with visible grain, taped magazine scraps, torn edges, photocopy noise, scanned stickers, folded ticket stubs, translucent memo labels, and layered sticker-like fragments in black and neon pink.
- Spacing and framing: keep a strong vertical hierarchy; top area for group title and issue-style release label, middle for hero and collage cluster, lower third for tracklist, comeback date, showcase details, ticket / streaming CTA, and credits.
- Match the energy of {컨셉} while keeping the layout dense, editorial, readable, and realistically printed like a premium K-pop comeback poster pasted into a fan zine.
- Add tangible poster artifacts: tape overlaps, paper fibers, staple marks, small registration crop marks, tiny barcode / QR-style block, serial text such as “POSTER NO. 120”, and a narrow side spine line reading “COMEBACK ARCHIVE / FAN ZINE EDITION”.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top header band: set {그룹 이름} as the largest masthead, with bold condensed sans-serif lettering, slightly distressed print texture, and tight alignment to the top margin; add small issue text around it such as “VOL.247”, “2026 SPECIAL COMEBACK”, “FANDOM EDITION”, and a tiny date label “2026.05”.
2. Secondary title block: place {앨범명} beneath the group name in a smaller serif or italic accent style, like a magazine issue subtitle, with clear hierarchy and strong spacing; add a short Korean cover line: “새로운 장면, 가장 선명한 우리”.
3. Center hero zone: show {포스터 메인 인물} as a realistic cinematic color cutout, sharply separated from the background, with trendy Korean 20s styling, expressive pose, polished idol hair / makeup, fashion-editorial accessories, and a soft realistic shadow on the pasted-paper layer.
4. Collage ring: surround the hero with torn-paper strips, clipping edges, pasted tape corners, hand-cut ticket shapes, photocopied texture fragments, mini lyrics, rehearsal-photo snippets, handwritten memo stickers, and folded paper tabs that create a punk zine wall composition.
5. Member card cluster: add 3–4 small photocard-style panels for the other members, mixing black-and-white and color, each with a tiny Korean name label such as “멤버 A”, “멤버 B”, “멤버 C”, varied crop scale, card numbering, tiny heart stickers, and a footer note “총 {그룹 멤버 수}명”.
6. Tracklist and countdown area: place a compact album tracklist with Korean and English song titles, a title-track marker, and a bold comeback countdown using {컴백일 정보} or a “D-7” style treatment; include realistic track text: “01 INTRO : SIGNAL”, “02 타이틀곡 ★”, “03 밤의 속도”, “04 Replay Heart”, “05 우리만의 장면”.
7. Event and fan info block: include comeback showcase details in Korean, e.g. “COMEBACK SHOWCASE”, “날짜 {컴백일 정보}”, “시간 PM 8:00 KST”, “장소 SEOUL LIVE HALL”, “티켓 예매 OPEN PM 2:00”, “온라인 스트리밍 동시 공개”, plus a small QR/barcode-style area labeled “SCAN FOR TEASER”.
8. Doodle and logo details: add hand-drawn crowns, hearts, stars, arrows, lightning bolts, signature marks, scribbles, lipstick-like marker strokes, sticker labels reading “NEW ERA”, “TITLE TRACK”, “ON AIR”, and a group logo lockup that feels like a fan-decorated zine page.
9. Footer strip: include a small lyric excerpt block “한 번 더 크게 외쳐, 지금이 우리의 시작”, credit-like microtext “PHOTO BY STUDIO 247 / STYLED BY COMEBACK TEAM / ART DIRECTION FAN ZINE LAB”, a model-name credit “COVER: {포스터 메인 인물}”, sponsor-style area with fictional partner text “WITH STAGE MAG / RADIO K / FAN CLUB DESK”, and a tiny legal-style album line without using fake official certification marks.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard Black or Montserrat ExtraBold for the headline, Noto Sans KR Bold for supporting Korean text, and a small serif like Cormorant Garamond for accent lines; mix in hand-drawn marker lettering for doodles and rough stamped text for ticket / barcode labels.
- Color palette: anchor the design in {시그니처 컬러}, then support with matte black, neon pink #FF4FD8, warm paper cream #F4F0E6, gray photocopy tones, silver-gray tape, and tiny red registration marks.
- Border/shadow: use cut-paper edges, subtle halftone prints, 3–5px taped shadow, soft drop shadow with 12px blur at 18% opacity, folded corners, layered sticker thickness, and printed ink misregistration for a tactile real-poster finish.
- Layout rhythm: combine oversized masthead text, rotated sticker labels, diagonal ticket strips, vertical spine text, and clean rectangular information boxes so the poster feels crowded with real comeback content but still readable at social-feed size.
- Realistic print details: add paper grain, dust specks, scan streaks, slight toner noise, glossy photocard reflections, transparent tape glare, and different paper stocks between the hero cutout, member cards, and photocopied scraps.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial fashion look shot like a Sony A7R IV with 85mm f/1.4 portrait framing for the hero, plus flat photocopy-style inserts for the card pieces.
- Lighting: soft studio key light from upper-left at 45°, light fill from front-right, with crisp but controlled contrast on the hero cutout and flatter scan-like lighting for the collage pieces.
- Color grade: black + neon pink + muted cream with slight magenta lift, punchy contrast, and magazine-print saturation.
- Finish: realistic mixed-media poster photographed or scanned after assembly, with believable shadows between paper layers and crisp high-resolution Korean typography.

[6. MOOD]
High-energy punk zine comeback poster — a Dazed Korea x i-D fashion editorial feel with K-pop fan-collage density, real album-release excitement, collectible photocard culture, and late-night Seoul street-poster energy.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: must render exactly these strings where used: {그룹 이름}, {앨범명}, {컴백일 정보}, {컨셉}, {그룹 멤버 수}명, {포스터 메인 인물}, {시그니처 컬러}.
- Include short, legible Korean poster text such as “새로운 장면, 가장 선명한 우리”, “컴백 쇼케이스”, “티켓 예매”, “온라인 스트리밍”, “타이틀곡”, and “총 {그룹 멤버 수}명”.
- The poster must remain a vertical layered collage, with one dominant hero, 3–4 smaller member cards, a top masthead, a tracklist, comeback date, showcase / ticket info, barcode or QR-style block, sponsor-style footer, and clearly separated text zones.
- Keep all Korean and English typography crisp, correctly spaced, and fully legible, especially {그룹 이름}, {앨범명}, {컴백일 정보}, tracklist items, and event details.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized real-person likeness

studio:prompts3:ours-119.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Streetwear brand poster in punk zine / moodboard collage style, designed as a realistic editorial collection announcement for social sharing, in-store campaign display, and a drop-event flyer.
Korean fashion poster with a central hero model, layered street-documentary collage fragments, event details, sponsor strip, ticket information, barcode labels, and bold neon-accent typography.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: {모델 특징} as the central hero cut, occupying about 55% of the vertical frame, standing slightly low-angle for attitude with a restrained, believable editorial expression.
- Outfit focus: {의상 종류} layered in a streetwear stack, with oversized silhouettes, fabric weight, seams, zippers, patches, sneakers, and accessories clearly readable from head to hem.
- Background treatment: {배경 장소} rendered as a gritty nighttime street scene with wet pavement reflections, neon signage glow, shutter doors, posted flyers, haze, smoke texture, and partial paper-collage interruption.
- Layout: header and brand blocks at the top, hero image centered, collage inserts orbiting around the subject, event and ticket information placed in the lower third, sponsor strip near the bottom edge, and dense zine-style pacing like a real street campaign poster.
- Text placeholders: {브랜드명}, {컬렉션명}, {컬렉션 컨셉}, and {주요 색상} must appear as integrated poster elements, printed as masthead, collection label, slogan, and color-chip annotation.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top header band: place {브랜드명} in a bold oversized masthead, with {컬렉션명} directly beneath it in smaller condensed type, aligned left or slightly off-center like a pasted magazine title. Add small issue/drop text such as DROP 01, STREET EDITION, and 2026 S/S CAMPAIGN in tiny technical type.
2. Hero area (center 55%): show {모델 특징} wearing {의상 종류}, standing in front of the neon street setting from {배경 장소}, with a slight low-angle camera feel, crisp pasted cutout edges, realistic garment folds, reflective highlights, and a faint rim light separating the figure from the smoke.
3. Signature campaign text: place {컬렉션 컨셉} as a strong slogan block near the hero image, using hand-drawn marker or stamped type, with rough edges and a screen-printed look. Add a Korean support line: 거리에서 완성되는 태도.
4. Event information block: add a pasted flyer panel reading 신상품 공개 / 2026.05.17 SAT 19:00 / 장소: {배경 장소} / 입장: 선착순 100명, styled like an authentic club-night poster insert with stamped numerals.
5. Ticket and barcode details: include a vertical barcode strip, serial label such as NO. 119-SEOUL-247, a torn ticket stub reading TICKET ₩15,000 / 현장 ₩20,000, and a small QR-like graphic block used as a design element.
6. Collage fragments: surround the hero with torn newspaper and magazine edges, 1–2 small black-and-white model snapshots, cropped sneaker detail, close-up fabric texture, photocopied street signs, serial-number labels, safety-pin graphics, sticker residue, and small patch-like brand inserts arranged asymmetrically to mimic an authentic 90s punk zine page.
7. Graffiti layer: add hand-drawn doodles such as crowns, smiley faces, arrows, hearts, lightning bolts, X marks, stars, and underline strokes around the composition, with quick marker strokes, spray-paint overspray, and slight overprint misalignment.
8. Typography boxes: include two hand-drawn text boxes containing short bilingual copy: WEAR YOUR FREEDOM, 오늘 입는 반항, and AFTER DARK STREET CLUB, rendered like marker annotations taped onto the poster.
9. Sponsor and credit strip: at the bottom, add a realistic sponsor area with small text such as SUPPORTED BY STREET RADIO / NIGHT MARKET CREW / PHOTO BY KIM STUDIO / STYLING TEAM 247, plus a tiny contact line @streetdrop.kr and 서울 기반 스트리트웨어 캠페인.
10. Color emphasis: push {주요 색상} as the main accent lights and ink pops against a black-and-white base, with selective neon highlights on edges, signs, stickers, barcode labels, ticket numbers, and handwritten arrows. Add a small color-chip label reading ACCENT: {주요 색상}.
11. Final poster balance: keep the overall feel raw, layered, tactile, and editorial, with visible paper grain, pasted seams, staple marks, tape strips, scuffed ink, spray texture, folded corners, photocopy streaks, and print noise across the whole frame.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: mix heavy sans-serif display type, handwritten marker script, condensed gothic, dot-matrix numerals, and classic serif accents; use bold condensed grotesk for title blocks, 24–72 pt visual hierarchy, with rough cut-and-paste alignment and intentionally varied baseline shifts.
- Color palette: black #0B0B0D, white #F4F4F2, and {주요 색상} as neon accents, with small secondary pops of cyan, red, safety orange, and metallic gray.
- Border/shadow: use torn-paper edges, photocopy noise, tape shadows, staple impressions, sticker layers, and slight offset shadowing like layered magazine clippings; combine hard-edged clipping shadows with soft airbrush haze and neon bloom.
- Print realism: include halftone dots, risograph-style ink overlap, paper wrinkles, scuffed corners, registration marks, crop marks, handwritten price labels, and small production notes to make it feel physically printed and pasted outdoors.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial fashion photography feel, shot on a full-frame camera with an 85mm f/1.4 lens for the hero, plus a few 50mm documentary-style inserts for the collage snapshots.
- Lighting: nighttime urban neon practicals with mixed sources, including signboard glow from the side, soft fill from the front, smoky backlight for rim separation, wet-street reflections, and small colored bounce light from nearby signage.
- Color grade: black-and-white base with neon pink, cyan, yellow, and red accent grading, slightly crushed blacks, high contrast, and printed-zine grain.
- Material detail: emphasize paper fiber, ripped fibers, glossy tape, matte photocopy patches, spray-painted texture, denim/cotton/nylon fabric grain, metallic zipper catches, and realistic skin texture on the model.

[6. MOOD]
90s punk fashion ad meets Japanese street-zine editorial — like a Clash magazine collage spread crossed with a raw campaign poster for an underground Seoul streetwear drop. Energetic, rebellious, tactile, nocturnal, and commercially believable.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 렌더링할 문자열: {브랜드명}, {컬렉션명}, {컬렉션 컨셉}, {주요 색상}.
- Korean event text must be clean and legible: 신상품 공개, 거리에서 완성되는 태도, 오늘 입는 반항, 장소: {배경 장소}, 입장: 선착순 100명.
- Korean/English mixed typography must be clean and legible, with no broken Hangul characters.
- Keep the central model anatomically correct, with natural proportions, realistic hands, believable clothing fit, and a convincing low-angle stance.
- Include 1–2 small black-and-white auxiliary snapshots plus product/fabric detail fragments, integrated as pasted collage pieces.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Unauthorized celebrity likeness or celebrity composite

studio:prompts3:ours-118.content:
[목적]
한국 16:9 TV 속보 뉴스 중계화면·하단 자막·방송 그래픽 패키지.

[장면]
딥 네이비 톤의 대형 뉴스룸 배경 위에 실제 방송 캡처처럼 정교한 UI를 구성한다. 화면 왼쪽 58%에는 {메인 화면 비주얼}을 라이브 피드 패널로 배치하고, 상단에 LIVE 태그와 “서울 강남” 위치 라벨, 미세한 스캔라인과 영상 압축 질감을 넣는다. 하단 22%에는 {뉴스 종류}, {메인 헤드라인}, {하단 자막 내용}이 이어지는 강한 속보형 로어서드를 가로로 배치하며, 오른쪽에는 {인포 박스 내용} 데이터 패널과 강수량 차트, 기상청 발표 정보를 정리한다. 전체 그래픽 시스템은 {그래픽 스타일}을 따른다.

[스타일]
실사형 방송 그래픽 mockup, 정면 직교 레이아웃, Pretendard 또는 Noto Sans KR 기반의 선명한 한국어 UI.  
네이비 #0B1E3A, 블루블랙 #07111F, 속보 레드 #D62828, 흰색과 쿨그레이를 사용하고 스튜디오 조명, LCD 픽셀 질감, 은은한 화면 글로우를 더한다.

[텍스트]
"NEWS 24", "08:00", "2024.07.26", "LIVE", "서울 강남", "날씨특보", "현장 연결", "제보 영상", "기상 레이더", "긴급 재난 문자 확인 중", "{뉴스 종류}", "{메인 헤드라인}", "{하단 자막 내용}", "{인포 박스 내용}", "우회도로 안내 · 지하차도 진입 통제 · 기상청 호우경보 유지", "시간당 강수량", "누적 강수량", "기상청 발표"

[🚫 중요]
한국어 텍스트 정확히 / 한글 깨짐 X
실제 식음료·소매·전자제품 브랜드 로고 스타벅스·맥도날드·삼성전자·LG 등 X
단 다음은 실제 그대로 OK: KBO 야구팀 삼성·SSG·LG·롯데·두산·KIA·NC·키움·한화·KT / K리그·KBL 등 한국 스포츠팀 / KBS·MBC·SBS·JTBC·tvN·MBN·YTN 같은 한국 방송사 UI·로고·자막
로어서드, 속보 캡슐, 헤드라인, 보조 자막, 티커, 우측 정보 박스는 분리되고 읽기 쉽게 유지할 것

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean magazine/newspaper interview portrait illustration, vertical 2:3 editorial feature image with a warm, approachable tone.
Designed as a realistic article opener for a culture magazine profile, combining a softly stylized portrait with believable publication metadata, pull quote, caption, and interview layout elements.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: {인물 정보} placed slightly off-center, occupying about 55% of the frame height, with a gentle 3/4 angle, relaxed posture, and direct but soft eye contact.
- Composition type: {컷 종류} crop, head, shoulders, torso, and natural hand gesture readable as an interview portrait; include posture details that suggest the person is mid-conversation.
- Background treatment: {배경} arranged as a lived-in writer’s workspace with books, manuscript pages, laptop, coffee cup, sticky notes, desk lamp, ceramic pen cup, and soft window shapes that support the interview theme.
- Editorial layout: place {매체명}, {호수}, {발행일}, {섹션명}, {인터뷰 제목}, {부제}, {기자명}, {크레딧}, {페이지 번호}, and {짧은 캡션} as believable magazine/newspaper design elements around the portrait.
- Quote placement: {인용구} set as a prominent pull quote in a clean side column or lower-right feature box, paired with a small decorative quote mark, thin column rule, and warm accent color.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Portrait block (center-left 55%): depict {인물 정보} with realistic facial structure, soft smile, natural skin undertones, glasses reflections, short bob hair texture, and calm eye contact; use {일러스트 스타일} to preserve likeness while keeping a warm editorial illustration feel.
2. Outfit and pose layer: dress the subject in interview-appropriate attire with subtle fabric folds, a cardigan, blouse, linen jacket, or scarf detail; show one hand resting near a notebook or mug if it helps the scene feel candid and conversational.
3. Workspace layer: build {배경} with a desk surface, stacked books with Korean spine text, open notebook, laptop displaying vague document lines, coffee cup, pencil marks, small plant, pinned memo cards, and soft paper textures that make the space feel real and inhabited.
4. Publication header: at the top, render {매체명} as the main masthead, followed by {호수} and {발행일}; add a small section label {섹션명} and a thin editorial divider line.
5. Article text system: set {인터뷰 제목} as the primary Korean headline, {부제} as a smaller subhead, {기자명} and {크레딧} as byline/credit text, {페이지 번호} near the bottom edge, and {짧은 캡션} close to the portrait or desk detail.
6. Quote area: render {인용구} as the main pull quote in quotation marks, large enough to be readable, with balanced line breaks and a refined Korean editorial font.
7. Final polish: add soft paper grain, watercolor wash transitions, gentle vignette warmth, small layout ornaments such as a column rule, page folio, and caption marker so the image feels like a finished magazine interview spread rather than a plain portrait.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use clean Korean editorial sans-serif such as Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for metadata and caption, with a softer serif-style Korean display treatment for the main quote if suitable; maintain clear hierarchy between masthead, headline, quote, byline, and page number.
- Color palette: build the scene from {색감}, anchored by warm beige #D8C6A8, mustard #C8A04A, sage #A8B49A, creamy off-white #F5F0E6, muted ink brown #4B3F35, and natural skin tones with soft rosy undertones.
- Line and shading: use refined, slightly softened contour lines, muted shadow edges, smooth watercolor-like fills, subtle hatching on books and paper, and gentle tonal variation in hair, glasses, fabric, and desk objects.
- Editorial decoration: include a thin vertical rule, small page folio, issue/date line, caption marker, and understated quote-mark graphic; keep all decoration integrated with the magazine interview concept.
- Print realism: allow paper grain, slight ink texture, soft registration-like color overlap, and tactile illustration texture while keeping facial features and Korean text clean.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial portrait framing inspired by an 85mm f/1.8 portrait lens with a shallow depth-of-field feel, even though the final result is an illustration.
- Lighting: soft window light from upper-left at roughly 45°, with a faint bounce fill from lower-right to keep the face bright and approachable.
- Color grade: warm cream + beige + sage with muted mustard accents, slightly lifted shadows, and gentle contrast similar to a Kinfolk-style print spread.

[6. MOOD]
Premium interview feature illustration — calm, thoughtful, intimate, and magazine-polished, with the restrained warmth of a Korean culture magazine profile and the lived-in sincerity of a writer’s studio.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the pull quote must appear exactly as {인용구}, including the surrounding quotation marks.
- Required rendered Korean editorial text: show {매체명}, {호수}, {발행일}, {섹션명}, {인터뷰 제목}, {부제}, {기자명}, {크레딧}, {페이지 번호}, and {짧은 캡션} clearly enough to read.
- Portrait accuracy: keep the subject clearly readable as {인물 정보}, with glasses, short bob hair, and a warm smile matching the provided description.
- Layout invariant: preserve a vertical Korean interview-article structure where the portrait is the emotional focus and the pull quote, headline, byline, caption, issue/date, and page folio feel like authentic publication elements.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized famous-person likeness blending

studio:prompts3:ours-116.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean Gen Z trend summary card, single-page editorial infographic for Instagram-style card news sharing.
A modern vertical card that explains one trend keyword with a memorable visual, micro-data, slide indicator, account metadata, and save-worthy CTA.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Vertical social card composition based on {이미지 비율}, optimized for 1024x1536 display while retaining the feel of a 1080x1350 Instagram card.
- Top utility strip occupies about 8–10% of the frame: include {계정 핸들}, {날짜 라벨}, {카테고리 태그}, and a small page marker {페이지 표시}.
- Main header occupies about 18% of the frame, with {트렌드 키워드} set as the largest typographic element and treated like a strong Gen Z trend headline.
- Subtitle sits directly below the header in a compact editorial line block, using {한 줄 설명} with readable spacing and a warm social-card tone.
- Central visual zone takes 42–48% of the frame and features an editorial illustration based on {시각화 내용}, supported by sticker-like labels, tiny arrows, reaction bubbles, and a hashtag accent.
- Data emphasis area appears near the central visual as a rounded callout containing {미니 데이터}, plus a small label that reinforces the key insight.
- Bottom information zone occupies 14–18% of the frame: include {푸터 정보}, {해시태그}, tiny save/share micro icons, and the CTA text {CTA 문구}.
- Background uses {색상 팔레트} with subtle paper grain, soft geometric shapes, thin dividers, and card-news editorial texture that fits {디자인 스타일}.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Utility header: place {계정 핸들} at the upper-left, {날짜 라벨} near it, {카테고리 태그} as a small rounded pill, and {페이지 표시} at the upper-right so the card feels like part of a swipeable card-news series.
2. Headline block: place {트렌드 키워드} in oversized bold Korean type, centered or slightly left-aligned, with {한 줄 설명} directly beneath it in a shorter paragraph width.
3. Main visual block: render {시각화 내용} as a friendly editorial infographic illustration in the center, adding 2–3 natural card-news accents such as a coral sticker, a small arrow, a speech bubble reading “요즘 포인트”, and a tiny hashtag badge.
4. Data callout: add a rounded rectangle or ticket-shaped label near the illustration containing {미니 데이터}; make it visually prominent enough to be saved or shared.
5. Footer and CTA: place {푸터 정보} along the lower-left or lower-center, add {해시태그}, then place {CTA 문구} near the bottom with small save/share/bookmark micro icons.
6. Slide identity: integrate {슬라이드 번호} subtly near the footer or side edge, while {페이지 표시} remains visible in the top utility strip.
7. Layout integrity: maintain crisp hierarchy, readable Korean spacing, consistent baseline alignment, and clear separation between headline, illustration, callout, and footer metadata.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for all Korean text; headline weight 800–900 at large display size, subtitle weight 500–600, metadata weight 500, footer weight 400–500.
- Color palette: use {색상 팔레트} as the base, interpreted as beige #EDE3D1, soft gray #D8D8D8, coral #F38B7C, plus off-white #FAF7F2 and deep charcoal #2B2B2B for readability.
- Border/shadow: rounded card container with a soft editorial drop shadow, 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 12% opacity; use thin muted-gray dividers and small coral highlight strokes.
- Graphic treatment: flat editorial illustration with smooth curves, friendly icon language, tactile paper-grain texture, sticker tags, tiny UI-like icons, and restrained accent shapes.
- Social-card details: include micro elements common to Korean Instagram card news, such as a bookmark icon, share arrow, carousel dot indicator, small handle line, and hashtag-style typography.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: top-down flat lay editorial framing, equivalent to a 35mm full-frame look with crisp composition and minimal distortion.
- Lighting: soft diffused studio light from upper-left at about 45°, with a very faint fill from lower-right to keep the card evenly legible.
- Color grade: warm beige and coral accent palette with soft gray neutrals, low contrast, clean social-media infographic finish.
- Surface detail: subtle matte paper texture, faint printed ink feel, and soft contact shadows around sticker-like graphics and callout cards.

[6. MOOD]
Kinfolk-meets-Carrot Market editorial card — calm, smart, save-worthy, and realistic as a Korean Gen Z trend briefing on social media.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following strings must appear exactly as rendered text where placed:
  - {트렌드 키워드}
  - {한 줄 설명}
  - {계정 핸들}
  - {날짜 라벨}
  - {카테고리 태그}
  - {페이지 표시}
  - {슬라이드 번호}
  - {미니 데이터}
  - {해시태그}
  - {CTA 문구}
  - {푸터 정보}
- Keep all Korean typography clean and correctly spaced; no broken Hangul, no garbled punctuation, no mixed-up line breaks.
- The central illustration must clearly communicate the trend as a card-news infographic, with social UI details that make it feel ready to post.
- Render the save/share/bookmark micro icons as tiny interface symbols, not as large decorative objects.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters or garbled Hangul
- Celebrity composites or recognizable real-person likenesses unless explicitly requested

studio:prompts3:ours-115.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean newspaper and magazine column main illustration, editorial-style vertical cover art for a printed opinion feature.
Softly conveys an abstract opinion column topic through one simplified figure, symbolic surroundings, and realistic column-page details such as section labels, date marks, caption lines, and small editorial credits.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: a simplified single silhouette occupying the lower-middle 45% of the frame, with surrounding symbolic elements arranged like an editorial vignette inside a real printed column page.
- Background treatment: off-white newspaper/magazine paper surface with visible fiber grain, faint ink speckles, light fold impressions, and soft print-registration texture.
- Page framing: compose as a full vertical opinion-page illustration with a top section strip, small issue/date label, page number, columnist credit, caption line, and a narrow side note area for {화면 라벨}.
- Add believable editorial furniture around the illustration: tiny column rules, short Korean teaser blurbs, small body-text fragments, photo-caption style notes, and a subtle section marker such as “오피니언”, “칼럼”, “3면”, “VOL.115”, “2026.05.01 금요일”.
- Use {칼럼 주제} as the conceptual anchor, {인물 표현} for the figure and environment relationship, {라인 스타일} for contour rendering, {채색 톤} for overall palette, {그림자 및 명암} for depth treatment, and {전반적인 분위기} for the emotional tone.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top editorial header area: create a slim newspaper/magazine section band with Korean microcopy such as “오피니언”, “시사 칼럼”, “VOL.115”, “2026년 5월호”, and a small page mark “p.03”. Keep it refined and print-like rather than poster-sized.
2. Central figure area (mid-lower 45%): render {인물 표현} as a restrained editorial illustration, with the figure looking inward or slightly downward to suggest reflection rather than action.
3. Symbolic environment: place smartphone shapes, soft city blocks, small window rectangles, speech-bubble fragments, document sheets, clock marks, transit-map lines, and quiet surrounding forms around the figure so they imply {칼럼 주제} through layered editorial metaphor.
4. Column-page details: add 2–3 short Korean feature blurbs near the sides, for example “오늘의 쟁점”, “거리에서 읽은 변화”, “느린 질문의 힘”, plus tiny gray body-text rows that look like real newspaper columns without overpowering the illustration.
5. Linework layer: draw all contours with {라인 스타일}, keeping strokes elegant, consistent, and slightly varied in pressure for a hand-inked magazine feel.
6. Color block layer: fill the silhouette and symbols with {채색 톤}, using harmonized muted hues with nuanced ink density, slight overprint effects, and natural paper absorption.
7. Shadow layer: add {그림자 및 명암} beneath the figure and selected environment shapes, using broad soft-edged patches and printed halftone-like tonal areas.
8. Label and credit area: reserve one side of the image for {화면 라벨}, with a small columnist credit line such as “글 김하린 · 일러스트 편집부” and a caption-style note beneath it.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for {화면 라벨}, section labels, credits, and microcopy; medium weight for the label, regular weight for caption text, with modest letter spacing and sharp anti-aliased edges.
- Korean editorial text: include short readable strings such as “오피니언”, “시사 칼럼”, “오늘의 쟁점”, “2026.05.01 금요일”, “3면”, “글 김하린”, and “나다운 선택이 가장 좋은 답” where appropriate to the layout.
- Color palette: use muted beige, sage green, light blue, warm gray, and off-white; keep the palette aligned to {채색 톤}, with subtle ink variation and no neon accents.
- Printed realism: show paper grain, slight ink bleed, faint halftone dots, marginal crop marks, tiny registration imperfections, and delicate column dividers to make the image feel like a real published editorial page.
- Border/shadow: subtle paper-edge framing is acceptable; add a soft drop shadow with 4px y-offset, 10px blur, and about 12% opacity under the main figure and a few layered paper-like graphic elements.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: flat editorial illustration look, as if composed for a magazine spread, with a clean orthographic presentation and no perspective distortion.
- Lighting: diffuse studio-like illumination from upper-left, with gentle contrast and soft highlights on the paper texture, similar to a calm printed feature illustration photographed or scanned for publication.
- Color grade: desaturated cream + sage + pale blue grading, with restrained warm-gray balancing to preserve the reflective mood.
- Rendering finish: refined Korean editorial illustration with realistic print production details, balanced between hand-drawn symbolic art and a finished newspaper/magazine column page.

[6. MOOD]
Editorial illustration with a New Yorker essay cover sensibility, mixed with a calm Korean magazine column aesthetic, thoughtful newsroom atmosphere, and {전반적인 분위기}. The result should feel published, tactile, intelligent, and quietly observant.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: "{화면 라벨}" must appear as clean, correctly rendered Korean text, with no broken characters.
- Include additional small Korean print text accurately, such as “오피니언”, “시사 칼럼”, “VOL.115”, “2026.05.01 금요일”, “글 김하린”, “오늘의 쟁점”, and “3면”.
- The image must remain a single-column main illustration: one simplified figure, symbolic environment, and real editorial page context.
- The subject should express {칼럼 주제} indirectly and poetically, using page design, symbolic surroundings, and atmosphere rather than literal infographic explanation.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness
