[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1536x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean economic news infographic header, realistic data-driven editorial chart layout for a newspaper, newsletter hero, or financial article lead image.
Designed to summarize {경제 분야} market movement with a headline, chart, big number, issue/date metadata, source line, compact article snippets, and publication-style micro details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Wide 16:9 composition with the top editorial header occupying about 18% of the frame, central chart area about 52%, and bottom insight/news brief block about 20%.
- Place a small publication masthead strip at the very top with Korean newspaper-style metadata such as “경제 데일리”, “VOL.247”, “2026년 5월호”, “서울판”, and page marker “BIZ 03”.
- Place the main headline at the upper-left, the English subheadline directly beneath it, and a source/date label aligned to the upper-right or just below the subheadline using {시간/기간}.
- Keep the chart as the visual anchor in the middle, with the large key figure layered near the chart’s right side or lower center for strong hierarchy.
- Use {경제 분야}, {핵심 데이터}, {시간/기간}, {차트 유형}, {디자인 팔레트}, {화면 비율} placeholders naturally in the headline, chart labels, annotation text, and footer notes.
- Background should feel like a premium financial editorial page: deep matte dark base, subtle grid texture, scanned-paper grain, soft data glow accents, thin dividers, tiny ticker labels, and realistic publication metadata.
- Maintain sharp editorial alignment with enough surrounding article texture, chart labels, captions, and microcopy so the image feels like a real Korean financial news graphic rather than a sterile template.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Publication masthead strip (very top): Add small but legible Korean metadata such as “경제 데일리”, “MARKET BRIEF”, “VOL.247”, “2026년 5월호”, “서울판”, and “BIZ 03”; include a tiny barcode-like area or issue code on the far right.
2. Header zone (top 18%): Set a bold Korean headline referencing {경제 분야}, for example “{경제 분야}, {시간/기간} 흐름과 {핵심 데이터}”; add an English subheadline in smaller uppercase text underneath such as “KOREA MARKET DATA WATCH”; add a tiny source line reading “자료: 한국은행·통계청·거래소 / 기준: {시간/기간}”.
3. Title support line: Insert a concise one-line explanation of the trend directly below the headline, using a clean sans-serif and tighter tracking, such as “주요 지표 변화와 투자 심리를 한눈에 정리한 {차트 유형} 분석”.
4. Main chart zone (center 50%): Render the {차트 유형} as the primary data visualization, with crisp axes, date ticks, value labels, highlighted peak/trough markers, a small legend, and a subtle caption label “단위: %, 지수, 조원”. The chart should reflect {핵심 데이터} and connect visually to the headline.
5. Key number callout: Place a large numeric emphasis panel beside or partially overlapping the chart, showing the most important percentage or value from {핵심 데이터} in oversized type, with a short Korean descriptor below such as “전월 대비 변화”, “시장 반응”, or “핵심 지표”.
6. Secondary data cards: Add two or three compact mini-stat cards near the chart edge, each with short Korean labels like “전일 대비”, “3개월 평균”, “변동성”, “전망치”, and tiny arrow indicators in gold or blue.
7. Insight block (bottom 20%): Add two to three short supporting insight bullets or micro-statements, each no more than one line, summarizing market implications for {경제 분야}; include realistic Korean snippets such as “소비 심리 회복 여부가 다음 분기 관건”, “금리 경로에 따라 변동성 확대 가능”, “외국인 수급은 제한적 개선”.
8. Article texture and captions: Add a small right-side or lower-left column of short Korean article-style body text lines, not dominant, with a caption such as “시장 해설” or “데이터 코멘트”; include a tiny photo-caption-like label even if no photo is present, for example “그래픽=경제데일리 데이터팀”.
9. Data annotations: Include small tooltip-style notes, trend arrows, comparison tags, and marker labels near the chart lines/bars, such as “고점”, “저점”, “예상 상회”, “전년 동기 대비”, making them editorial rather than dashboard-like.
10. Footer microtext: Place a tiny disclaimer or source note at the very bottom edge in low-contrast text, such as “본 그래픽은 공개 자료와 자체 집계를 바탕으로 작성되었습니다. 투자 판단의 책임은 독자에게 있습니다.”

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for Korean body text, Pretendard ExtraBold or Noto Sans KR Bold for the headline, and Inter or Helvetica Neue for English subheads; headline around 42–56px, support text 18–24px, microtext 11–13px.
- Color palette: Follow {디자인 팔레트} with deep navy #0B1F3A, black #0A0A0A, gold #C8A24A, and blue accent #4A90E2; use off-white #F4F6FA for small text contrast when needed.
- Border/shadow: Use thin gold divider lines, soft 4px y-offset shadows with 12px blur at 15% opacity, faint inner glow around key numerals, and subtle chart panel depth to make the editorial graphic feel printed and layered.
- Layout discipline: sharp alignment, consistent gutters, professional newspaper hierarchy, readable chart labeling, and publication-grade spacing with realistic micro-elements such as issue code, page number, source note, legend, and ticker strip.
- Decorative graphic elements: Use fine gridlines, faint candlestick or sparkline fragments, small arrow badges, thin rule lines, and editorial section labels to enrich the financial-news atmosphere while keeping the data story dominant.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Clean vector editorial infographic style with subtle photoreal depth cues, as if composited in a Bloomberg / Financial Times style motion-graphics still; if textures appear, keep them as scanned-paper grain at 5–8% opacity rather than photographic distortion.
- Lighting: Simulated studio-grade top-left softbox look with gentle contrast falloff and a faint right-side rim glow to separate chart elements from the background.
- Color grade: Cool financial editorial grade with navy base, muted gold highlights, and restrained electric-blue accents; avoid saturated rainbow colors.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean financial newspaper infographic — Bloomberg terminal clarity mixed with Financial Times editorial restraint, with the density and authenticity of a real market briefing page.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 표시되어야 하는 문구: "{경제 분야}", "{핵심 데이터}", "{시간/기간}", "{차트 유형}".
- Additional Korean text rendered in the image should be short and realistic, such as “경제 데일리”, “2026년 5월호”, “서울판”, “시장 해설”, “전월 대비 변화”, “자료: 한국은행·통계청·거래소”, “그래픽=경제데일리 데이터팀”.
- The chart, headline, numeric emphasis, mini-stat cards, and insight bullets must all be internally consistent with the same economic story.
- All Korean text must be cleanly rendered with no broken characters, no garbled spacing, and no mixed-up Hangul glyphs.
- Keep the big number visually dominant and readable within a split second.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1536x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean newspaper and online media main headline illustration for a social issue article. Create one editorial newspaper feature layout that combines a symbolic illustration with realistic newspaper-page elements, suitable for a Sunday feature section or digital main article hero image.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: simplified young adult figure as a universal representative, placed slightly off-center inside a compact studio-room vignette.
- Composition: the {이슈 주제} is communicated through {구체적 상황/장면} with {주요 시각 요소} arranged as everyday objects around the figure, forming a readable editorial scene.
- Newspaper layout: place the illustration as the dominant visual on a Korean newspaper page with a masthead, date, edition line, page number, captions, and multiple article columns wrapping around the artwork.
- Text hierarchy: use a large Korean headline area containing {메인헤드라인}, a smaller deck line containing {서브헤드라인}, and a short summary block containing {기사요약}.
- Label placement: render {한글 라벨 내용} as a small Korean annotation tag attached naturally to the room vignette, like an infographic callout.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Newspaper page base: a horizontal broadsheet-style editorial page with slightly warm off-white newsprint paper texture, faint fold line, narrow column guides, and realistic ink density variation.
- Masthead zone: top band includes {신문명}, {발행일}, {판정보}, {가격정보}, and a compact section label such as “사회면 특집”.
- Central figure: a simplified youth figure with clean silhouette, relaxed but tired posture, and subtle facial marks that suggest everyday pressure without resembling a real person.
- Symbolic objects: place a laptop, ramen bowl, potted plant, phone charger, folded blanket, utility bill envelope, small calendar, and delivery receipt around the figure to make the one-person household setting feel lived-in.
- Article structure: include 3–4 narrow Korean article columns with visible paragraph blocks, pull quote box, small subheading, byline {기자명}, and caption {캡션문구} below the illustration.
- Spatial cues: compress the living space into a tight, slightly asymmetrical studio-room arrangement, using shelves, floor mat, window edge, and wall outlet to reinforce small-room scale.
- Navigation details: add page marker {면번호}, small continuation note “관련 기사 3면”, and a tiny infographic strip showing “월세·식비·고립감” as three labeled indicators.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR, newspaper-like hierarchy with bold headline, medium subhead, regular body columns, compact captions, and clearly legible Korean text.
- Color palette: {주요 색상 팔레트} with neutral support tones like off-white #F4F1EA, charcoal #2A2F36, faded ink gray #77736B, and muted paper beige #E7DDCC.
- Linework and paint: {일러스트 스타일}, clean editorial line art, soft flat color fills, slight gradient transitions, restrained shadow edges, and subtle halftone/newsprint grain.
- Newspaper realism: show column dividers, small paragraph rhythm, caption rule lines, masthead spacing, edition metadata, and slight ink misregistration for authentic printed-media texture.
- Border/shadow: subtle paper-edge softness and a light 8px blur shadow at 12% opacity to separate layered illustration objects from the newspaper background.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: editorial illustration look, top-down-to-slightly-oblique composition akin a 35mm documentary layout translated into vector-like art.
- Lighting: diffused studio-style light from upper-left with a soft fill from the right, gentle contrast, natural paper shadows, and readable object silhouettes.
- Color grade: muted navy + mustard + olive + sage + light gray, with a slightly cool newsroom tint, gentle desaturation, and warm paper undertone.
- Rendering: hybrid newspaper illustration and editorial page design, crisp Korean typography, tactile paper surface, soft grain, clean icon-like objects, and believable printed-page proportions.

[6. MOOD]
Korean newspaper feature illustration — calm, socially observant, information-rich editorial mood with a lived-in everyday realism and a thoughtful Sunday-paper opener aesthetic.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following strings must appear exactly as written: "1인 가구", "{메인헤드라인}", "{서브헤드라인}", "{신문명}", "{발행일}", "{판정보}", "{면번호}"
- Render realistic Korean newspaper text elements including masthead, date, edition, byline, captions, page marker, and article columns; body paragraph text may be small but must look like coherent Korean newsprint.
- Human figure: simplified and universally readable, no identifiable real person, no political likeness.
- Composition intent: the issue should be conveyed symbolically through ordinary objects and newspaper context, with the compact room scene clearly supporting the social-issue headline.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or identifiable real-person likenesses
- Party-specific propaganda imagery

studio:prompts3:ours-112.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1536x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean interior concept visual for {공간 종류 및 크기}, rendered as a realistic lifestyle/editorial interior photograph for a designer portfolio, blog hero image, and Pinterest-style inspiration board.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main room composition: frame {공간 종류 및 크기} from {시점 및 구도}, with believable room depth extending from foreground left to back right and visible Korean apartment or small-shop architectural details such as baseboards, window frame, curtain rail, wall outlet, door trim, and ceiling light wiring.
- Subject placement: the seating/rest or customer-facing zone occupies about 45% of the frame, while the desk/storage/display zone, plants, lighting, and daily objects balance the opposite side.
- Background treatment: Korean interior with matte white or cream walls, light wood flooring, subtle wall texture, fabric curtains, realistic floor joints, and small lived-in details that support {인테리어 스타일}.
- Spacing and framing: compose the room like an interior magazine feature with clear sightlines, natural furniture spacing, and a small editorial Korean label area integrated into the image as a caption card, sticky note, or translucent magazine-style text block.
- Use {공간 종류 및 크기}, {인테리어 스타일}, {핵심 요소 및 분위기}, {주요 색상 팔레트}, {시점 및 구도}, {조명 및 시간대} as the concrete design directions.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Foreground zone: show a soft-textured rug, a low sofa, floor cushion, dining bench, or compact lounge chair; include a small side table with stacked Korean magazines, a ceramic mug, phone, remote, small tray, or linen coaster to establish domestic scale.
- Main living zone: arrange the primary furniture according to {인테리어 스타일}, with warm wood surfaces, practical Korean storage, open shelving, baskets, hooks, framed prints, folded textiles, and everyday items placed naturally rather than symmetrically.
- Functional detail layer: add realistic objects suited to {공간 종류 및 크기}, such as slippers near the entrance, a tiny kitchen cart, laptop on a desk, wall calendar, fabric tote bag, diffuser, bookends, table lamp, price/menu card for a store concept, or neatly displayed product samples.
- Accent layer: express {핵심 요소 및 분위기} through natural lifestyle details — healthy green plants in ceramic pots, books with Korean spines, a throw blanket, cushion texture, glass vase, candle warmer, small speaker, or handmade ceramic cup.
- Color application: build the palette from {주요 색상 팔레트}, with warm oak brown on furniture, cream on textiles, soft gray in metal or structural elements, off-white wall surfaces, and one muted accent color repeated in small objects such as a cushion, poster, lamp shade, or flower.
- View and light: render the room from {시점 및 구도} with {조명 및 시간대} so window light, pendant light, and bounce reflections create realistic shadow falloff, highlights on wood grain, gentle fabric texture, and depth across the room.
- Text overlay area: include a small Korean editorial caption in one corner or on a paper label, such as "공간 기록", "오늘의 무드", "서울 작은집 스타일링", plus tiny metadata lines like "VOL.112", "2026.05", "@home_note.kr"; the label should feel like an interior magazine caption rather than a poster headline.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR, medium to bold weight for the short Korean title label, regular weight for metadata, with crisp anti-aliased Korean characters and realistic printed or screen-rendered texture.
- Color palette: warm oak brown, cream #F4EFE6, soft gray #CFCBC4, off-white #FAFAF7, and one muted accent from {주요 색상 팔레트}.
- Surface detail: emphasize tactile realism — woven rug fibers, linen curtains, matte ceramic, wood grain, paper edges, book covers, plant leaves, soft cushion seams, and subtle wall imperfections.
- Graphic treatment: if an editorial label is present, place it on a small translucent panel, paper tag, or magazine-caption block with a fine hairline rule and soft natural shadow that matches the room lighting.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: full-frame interior photography look, 24mm wide-angle lens at f/8, angled corner composition with corrected verticals.
- Lighting: late-afternoon natural light entering from one side, combined with a warm pendant lamp overhead; soft directional shadows and gentle bounce fill.
- Color grade: warm cream and wood tones with slightly desaturated gray balance, clean editorial contrast, realistic texture response, and a touch of muted Seoul apartment realism.
- Rendering quality: photorealistic interior photography with believable scale, accurate perspective, visible material grain, natural object placement, and magazine-quality composition for a 1536x1024 horizontal image.

[6. MOOD]
Korean lifestyle magazine interior spread — between Dezeen apartment reportage, a calm Kinfolk home feature, and a realistic Seoul small-space styling shoot with warm lived-in details.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following Korean strings must appear correctly in the rendered image if label text is included: "공간 종류 및 크기", "인테리어 스타일", "핵심 요소 및 분위기", "주요 색상 팔레트", "시점 및 구도", "조명 및 시간대".
- Additional Korean text may appear as realistic editorial details, for example "공간 기록", "서울 작은집 스타일링", "오늘의 무드", "VOL.112", "2026.05", "@home_note.kr"; all Korean characters must be sharp and correctly formed.
- Layout invariants: the space must remain clearly a small Korean interior concept for {공간 종류 및 크기}; preserve believable proportions for furniture, lighting, plants, shelving, textiles, and architectural elements.
- The final image should read as an actual photographed room or store corner, not a flat layout mockup.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean watercolor food illustration for a recipe book, cafe menu, and printed menu-board editorial page, featuring one main dish with side dishes, menu labels, store information, and small decorative food-note graphics.
Soft, refined culinary illustration that presents {일러스트 용도} with a balanced, ready-to-print vertical composition and realistic Korean menu details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: {메인 음식} placed slightly below center and sized to occupy about 42% of the frame width, with the side dishes arranged around it in a gentle semicircle.
- Supporting dishes: {곁들임 음식} positioned as complementary components, visually separated but close enough to read as one meal set.
- Tableware: {식기 재질} arranged asymmetrically so the main dish sits in the visual anchor area while the smaller dishes create rhythm around it.
- Background treatment: {배경 및 소품} on an off-white or pale beige watercolor paper field with visible paper grain, warm pigment stains, and light tabletop hints.
- Menu information: include a neat header with {매장명}, a category label {메뉴 카테고리}, the main label {한글 라벨 내용}, and a small pricelist area showing {추가 메뉴 목록}.
- Store details: place {주소}, {연락처}, and {운영 시간} near the lower portion like a real cafe or cookbook menu footer, separated by fine hand-drawn dividers.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Hero dish area (center-lower 42%): {메인 음식} rendered with realistic ingredient color variation, soft watercolor blooms, fine pen outlines, visible toppings, sauce highlights, steam hints, and edible texture.
- Side-dish cluster (around hero): {곁들임 음식} painted in smaller scale with distinct shapes and colors so each item remains identifiable in a balanced meal layout.
- Tableware layer: {식기 재질} shown with subtle reflective highlights, gentle contour shading, rim thickness, and believable contact shadows integrated naturally under and beside the food.
- Prop layer: {배경 및 소품} include a spoon, chopsticks, a folded napkin corner, tiny flower stems, sesame seeds, chili flakes, and a few watercolor ingredient sketches that support the food story.
- Text layer: {한글 라벨 내용} set as a crisp menu label panel, paired with {매장명}, {메뉴 카테고리}, {추가 메뉴 목록}, {주소}, {연락처}, and {운영 시간} in readable Korean typography.
- Divider and note layer: add thin hand-drawn rule lines, small dot separators, a tiny “추천” tag, and a short caption {짧은 메뉴 설명} to make the page feel like a realistic printed cafe menu.
- Overall finish: preserve visible paper texture, watercolor diffusion at the edges, controlled pigment pooling, delicate ink definition, and a warm artisanal hand-painted look.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: clean sans-serif Korean font such as Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for menu text, medium weight for prices, slightly larger header for {매장명}, precise spacing and sharp anti-aliased edges.
- Color palette: warm natural hues with off-white #F7F3EB, beige #E9DDC9, muted red #C95A4A, soft green #8FA57A, earthy brown #8B6A4A, gentle gold #B08A57, and ink gray #3F3A34.
- Menu graphics: use fine divider lines, small watercolor dots, tiny ingredient icons, and light beige label blocks; shadows may appear softly under plates and paper elements, 4px y-offset, 10px blur, 12% opacity.
- Layout hierarchy: store name at top, illustrated meal as the hero, price and menu notes near the food, additional menu items and store details toward the bottom with consistent alignment.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: top-down editorial food composition, as if photographed with a 50mm lens on a high-resolution studio setup, then translated into watercolor illustration with controlled perspective.
- Lighting: soft diffused daylight from upper-left at about 45°, with very mild fill from the lower-right to maintain ingredient visibility and avoid harsh contrast.
- Color grade: warm cream, soft terracotta, muted herb green, and gentle beige with low saturation and natural pigment variation.

[6. MOOD]
{전체 분위기} — calm cookbook illustration with the charm of a small Korean cafe menu, hand-painted food notes, and a warm printed-paper editorial finish.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following strings must appear exactly as written: "햇살분식", "떡볶이", "₩6,000", "김치볶음밥 ₩7,500", "인절미 와플 ₩5,800", "유자에이드 ₩4,500".
- Store detail text must appear legibly: "서울 종로구 익선동 12-4", "02-1234-5678", "매일 11:00–20:30", "추천", "쫄깃한 떡과 달큰한 고추장 소스".
- The label, menu list, address, phone number, and operating hours must be fully readable, correctly spaced, and rendered without broken Korean characters.
- Food anatomy and tableware proportions must remain believable; no distorted bowls, no floating utensils, and no overlapping text over the main dish.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or real-person likeness misuse
- Text that is blurry, misspelled, or partially cut off

studio:prompts3:ours-110.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1536x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Postcard-style Korean cityscape illustration for exhibition graphics, travel-blog visuals, and souvenir print goods, rendered as a refined pen-and-ink drawing with restrained watercolor accents.
Specific: detailed urban landscape art of {주요 장소}, balancing architectural accuracy, hand-drawn atmosphere, and print-friendly caption readability with authentic postcard metadata.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main scene: {주요 장소} fills the full width with a layered street view; foreground alley and building edges occupy about 35% of the frame, midground rooftops 40%, and distant landmark 25%.
- Subject framing: the composition should feel like an editorial postcard, with a stable horizon line, slightly elevated viewpoint, and a clear left-to-right visual path through the alley.
- Background treatment: warm off-white paper surface with visible fiber grain, faint sky wash, soft cloud traces, subtle ink bleed, and postcard-stock printing texture.
- Use {장소의 핵심 요소} as the primary visual anchor, enriched with everyday street details such as small signboards, potted plants, utility lines, steps, stone paving, and quiet pedestrian silhouettes.
- Bottom caption band: integrate a tasteful exhibition-postcard label zone containing {도시명}, {장소명}, {전시명}, {작가명}, {제작 날짜}, {엽서 코드}, {좌표 라벨}, {하단 캡션}, and {보조 문구}.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Foreground: draw the nearest alley edges, low walls, roof eaves, paving stones, doorway thresholds, planters, and a few small human silhouettes as scale references within the street scene.
2. Midground: render the main cluster of houses and roofs in {그림 기법}, with {세부 묘사 요소} articulated in crisp linework and controlled cross-hatching.
3. Landmark layer: place the distant landmark subtly above the roofline so it is recognizable and integrated into the city silhouette, with atmospheric line fading toward the horizon.
4. Color wash: apply {색상 팔레트} selectively across roof planes, foliage, plaster walls, wooden doors, paper lantern hints, and stone surfaces while keeping the ink drawing dominant.
5. Texture pass: overlay {질감 및 분위기}, light paper fiber, faint vintage print impression, tiny registration specks, and gentle uneven ink density as if printed on archival postcard stock.
6. Caption and postcard details: create a curated label area with a hairline charcoal frame, small crop marks, postcard serial text, exhibition credit, date, coordinate-style location line, and a tiny non-official stamp-like travel mark.
7. Printed text placement: set the largest Korean label as {도시명} / {장소명}; place {전시명} and {작가명} as gallery-credit text; use {제작 날짜}, {엽서 코드}, and {좌표 라벨} as small metadata; add {하단 캡션} and {보조 문구} as short travel-note copy.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Korean label set in Noto Sans KR or Pretendard, regular to medium weight, 16–28 px equivalent, with neat spacing; postcard metadata can use smaller 11–14 px equivalent text.
- Color palette: black ink, off-white paper #F4F0E6, beige wash #D8C7A7, sage wash #A7B8A0, muted warm gray #8C857D, faded brick #A77D67, dusty blue-gray #8795A1.
- Linework: combine thin architectural outlines, hatch shading, stippled shadow patches, and delicate ink pooling at roof tile edges, window frames, tree branches, and stone joints.
- Decorative print system: use a 1px charcoal hairline frame, faint shadow with 4px y-offset and 10px blur at 12% opacity, small corner ticks, and understated postcard crop marks that support the exhibition-print feeling.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: simulated architectural illustration look inspired by a 35mm documentary frame with a slightly elevated perspective, as if referenced from a Canon TS-E 24mm f/3.5L II tilt-shift composition.
- Lighting: soft overcast daylight with even contrast, gentle tonal separation between roof tiles, walls, foliage, stone paving, and distant skyline.
- Color grade: monochrome ink base with muted beige, sage, faded brick, and dusty blue-gray watercolor accents, warm paper-white highlights, and low-saturation vintage editorial tonality.

[6. MOOD]
Exhibition postcard illustration — a refined Monocle travel feature meets museum catalog print aesthetic, with quiet Korean street life, archival paper warmth, and collectible souvenir realism.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 렌더링할 한글은 {도시명}, {장소명}, {전시명}, {작가명}, {제작 날짜}, {엽서 코드}, {좌표 라벨}, {하단 캡션}, {보조 문구}이다.
- The illustration must keep architecture lines crisp, perspective stable, and the caption band readable over the textured paper surface.
- Small silhouettes should be anatomically plausible and secondary to the architecture, matching the quiet scale of the street.
- All postcard metadata must look like printed editorial text, not a government certificate or official seal.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters or misspelled Korean text
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized portrait likenesses

studio:prompts3:ours-109.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
1-2 English lines: one-page brand identity guide poster for a handmade bakery owner, showing business card mockups, logo lockups, color palette, typography samples, and practical store-contact details.
Realistic Korean one-person business BI kit page, designed as a polished editorial brand board that feels printed, handled, and ready for a local bakery launch.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main canvas: vertical A4-style brand guide layout with a structured editorial grid and four clearly separated zones for Card / Logo / Color / Type, plus a compact header and footer information strip.
- Primary subject: {인물 이름} as the brand owner context, with the page focusing on the visual system while including owner credit, role label, and practical bakery contact information.
- Background treatment: warm off-white paper stock with visible fine grain, cream base, subtle printed ink texture, faint shadowed panel borders, and a realistic tabletop setting.
- Surrounding context: add natural bakery-brand-board details such as a kraft paper sleeve corner, small receipt slip, pencil, cotton twine, tiny pastry crumb, linen edge, or translucent tracing-paper overlay, integrated around the printed guide.
- Spacing and framing: left-aligned labels, organized information hierarchy, editorial section dividers, visible print registration details, and enough tactile detail to feel like a photographed real BI kit sheet.
- Use {브랜드/매장명}, {브랜드 키워드}, {디자인 컨셉}, {컬러 팔레트}, {폰트 스타일} placeholders as the content anchors.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Top header band: set the brand title area for {브랜드/매장명} with subtitle text “명함·BI 키트 1페이지 가이드”, small guide metadata “BRAND IDENTITY KIT / VER.01 / 2026.05”, and owner line “Owner: {인물 이름} · {직업/역할}”, aligned cleanly to the upper-left with a refined editorial layout.
2) Card section: show front and back business card mockups in a realistic tabletop presentation, one card slightly overlapping the other, with soft paper edges, visible thickness, rounded corners, print grain, and natural shadow on a light wood table; include section label text “Card / 명함”. The front card should show {브랜드/매장명} logo, {브랜드 키워드}, and a small tagline such as “오늘 구운 따뜻한 한 조각”. The back card should include {인물 이름}, {직업/역할}, phone “010-0000-0000”, email “hello@bakery.kr”, Instagram “@daily_bread”, and address line “서울시 성동구 베이커리길 12”.
3) Logo section: display exactly two logo versions for {브랜드/매장명} — one square mark and one horizontal wordmark — each placed inside its own framed sample tile with fine grid ticks, lockup spacing marks, and small captions “Square Mark” and “Horizontal Wordmark”; include section label text “Logo / 로고”.
4) Color section: present 3–4 swatches derived from {컬러 팔레트}, each with a small HEX tag and Korean color name beneath it, arranged in a compact brand palette grid; include section label text “Color / 컬러”. Suggested labels: “크림 베이지 #F7F1E8”, “라떼 브라운 #B58A67”, “코코아 #8B6A4E”, “버터 옐로 #E8D8C4”.
5) Type section: show typography samples using {폰트 스타일}, with one Korean sample and one English sample, aligned on separate lines, sized like a brand board specimen; include section label text “Type / 타입”. Korean sample: “매일 아침, 손으로 빚은 빵”. English sample: “Freshly baked with quiet care.” Include small weight notes like “KR 600 / EN 400”.
6) Supporting notes: add tiny Korean annotations around the board that reinforce {브랜드 키워드} and {디자인 컨셉}, such as “따뜻한 첫인상”, “수제 베이커리 톤”, “포장 스티커 적용 가능”, “매장 사인 확장용”, plus a footer note “Print guide for {브랜드/매장명} · brand board sample”.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for labels and captions, medium weight 500–600, 18–24px for section labels, 12–16px for supporting notes; handwritten Korean sample can use a clean hand-drawn style, English sample a simple sans serif such as Inter or Helvetica Neue.
- Color palette: warm beige, soft brown, cream, and muted latte tones from {컬러 팔레트}; suggested tones like #E8D8C4, #B58A67, #F7F1E8, #8B6A4E, with ink behaving like matte print on textured paper.
- Border/shadow: thin 1px separators in light taupe, soft drop shadow 0 8px 24px at 14% opacity, paper card edges slightly rounded with realistic print texture, tiny paper fibers, and gentle corner wear.
- Printed details: include small crop marks, guide numbers, micro caption lines, footer credits, and realistic alignment labels without making the sheet look like an empty template.
- Bakery identity detail: let the design hint at handmade bread through subtle icon shapes, kraft-label accents, stamp-like logo usage, and warm packaging-inspired graphic dividers.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: top-down flat lay look with a 50mm lens aesthetic, slight perspective correction, realistic print mockup detail, crisp but not overly sharp.
- Lighting: soft window light from upper-left at 45°, gentle fill from lower-right, subtle natural shadow falloff, no harsh reflections.
- Color grade: warm cream + beige + latte + cocoa, slightly desaturated editorial tone, clean neutral white balance.

[6. MOOD]
Premium handmade bakery brand board — Kinfolk-style editorial layout with Aesop-like restraint and a calm Korean lifestyle magazine feel, tactile paper warmth, local-shop sincerity, and ready-to-print professional detail.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문자열: “Card”, “Logo”, “Color”, “Type”, “명함”, “로고”, “컬러”, “타입”.
- 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 추가 문자열: “명함·BI 키트 1페이지 가이드”, “BRAND IDENTITY KIT”, “VER.01”, “2026.05”, “오늘 구운 따뜻한 한 조각”, “매일 아침, 손으로 빚은 빵”.
- {브랜드/매장명} 표기는 BI 제목과 로고/명함 내용에서 일관되게 유지할 것.
- Card mockup must show two sides, logo section must contain exactly two versions, color section must show 3–4 swatches, and type section must show both Korean and English samples.
- Include owner credit using {인물 이름} and role using {직업/역할}; include brand context using {브랜드 키워드}, {디자인 컨셉}, {컬러 팔레트}, {폰트 스타일}.
- All Korean typography must be rendered cleanly without broken syllables or missing jamo.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

studio:prompts3:ours-108.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
1-2 English lines: Korean 1-person brand merchandise lineup mockup catalog, multi-product grid, social-media shop announcement and crowdfunding-page ready.
Showcase one signature mascot or emblem applied consistently across apparel, mugs, keychains, bags, stickers, pin badges, packaging cards, and small printed inserts in a polished editorial catalog page.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main composition: a tall realistic catalog page organized by {굿즈 배치 방식}, filling the central product field with layered merchandise, product labels, price tags, and small catalog annotations while preserving clear product recognition.
- Product hierarchy: the most visually important item occupies the upper-middle 22% as a hero product, with the rest of {굿즈 종류} arranged around it in a shop-ready lineup with believable scale differences.
- Brand identity: every product must feature {시그니처 디자인} with identical visual language across all items, unified by {브랜드 컬러}; repeat the motif on hang tags, sticker backing cards, enamel pin cards, and packaging sleeves.
- Optional lifestyle element: if {모델 포함 여부} is included, place the model in one lower-side panel wearing the apparel, cropped from mid-thigh upward, styled like a small lookbook photo with natural hands, fabric folds, and visible print placement.
- Background treatment: {배경 스타일} with warm off-white paper, subtle grain, realistic tabletop depth, kraft paper backing cards, folded fabric swatches, washi tape pieces, shipping label scraps, and a few small dried-flower or plant props that make the scene feel photographed.
- Framing: keep the layout vertically structured like a boutique merch catalog spread, with crisp product separation, realistic shadows, layered paper details, and enough surrounding context to feel like an actual product shoot for Instagram and a funding page.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header zone (top 12%): create a branded catalog masthead using {브랜드 이름}; include Korean micro text such as "굿즈 라인업", "VOL.247", "2026년 5월호", "신상품 프리오더", a thin divider line, small credit text "design by {브랜드 이름}", and a tiny issue/date label.
2. Hero product zone (upper-center 22%): show the most representative item from {굿즈 종류} larger than the others, featuring {시그니처 디자인} sharply printed; add a small callout sticker reading "BEST ITEM" and Korean label "대표 굿즈" with a realistic product tag and price such as "₩28,000".
3. Merchandise grid zone (middle 46%): arrange the remaining {굿즈 종류} in a tidy editorial grid with product name captions, short Korean descriptors, SKU-style labels like "ITEM 01", "ITEM 02", and prices such as "₩7,500", "₩12,000", "₩18,000"; include a mug, tote or pouch, keychain, sticker pack, badge card, and apparel item if relevant.
4. Apparel presentation zone (lower-left or lower-right, only when {모델 포함 여부} is used): place a model wearing the branded shirt or hoodie, styled like a Korean indie lookbook insert photo, with natural pose, correct fabric drape, and the same {시그니처 디자인} visible on chest, sleeve, or back; add a small caption "착용컷 / free size" and date-location label "서울 성수 · 2026.05".
5. Small accessory zone (lower-middle 14%): cluster keychains, pin badges, sticker flakes, backing cards, tiny zip pouch, and postcard-size inserts; render realistic enamel shine, metal rings, sticker paper edges, transparent packaging reflections, stitching, and printed barcode-style product labels.
6. Footer zone (bottom 8%): include a shop information strip with Korean text "온라인 스토어 오픈", "예약 판매 5.10–5.24", "문의 hello@brand.kr", "@brand_goods", a small barcode area, simple QR-like square graphic, address line "서울시 마포구 독립상점 2F", and tiny production credit text.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard SemiBold for the brand title and main product labels, Pretendard Regular for supporting micro text, around 28–42 px for the title, 16–24 px for item names, and 10–14 px for barcode, SKU, credit, handle, and caption details.
- Color palette: derive all accents from {브랜드 컬러}, with cream #F6F0E6, beige #D8C7B0, dark brown #4A3327 as the core set, plus warm gray #E9E4DB for paper fields, tags, caption boxes, and subtle dividers.
- Border/shadow: use soft drop shadows with 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 14% opacity; add thin 1px neutral borders, rounded backing-card corners, taped paper edges, and small printed dividers where they help the catalog feel real.
- Surface treatment: matte paper-like background with subtle grain, gentle edge vignetting, realistic product cutout boundaries, tactile cotton weave, ceramic glaze, brushed metal, enamel coating, sticker-paper fibers, and transparent plastic sleeve reflections.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: studio product-catalog setup, full-frame camera with 85mm f/1.8 for apparel/model cutouts and 50mm f/2.8 for flat mockups, straight-on orthographic feel.
- Lighting: softbox key light from upper-left at 45° with a weak fill from right, producing even shadows and crisp material definition; controlled specular highlights on mug glaze, metal keychain rings, enamel pins, and glossy sticker sheets.
- Color grade: warm cream and cocoa-toned grade with restrained contrast, slightly desaturated beige highlights, clean neutral whites, and natural print-shop color density.

[6. MOOD]
Indie Korean boutique merch lookbook — a small creator brand catalog photographed on a warm studio tabletop, mixing crowdfunding-ready product clarity with charming handmade shop details.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 렌더링되어야 하는 문자열: "{브랜드 이름}", "{시그니처 디자인}", "{브랜드 컬러}", "{굿즈 종류}", "{굿즈 배치 방식}", "{모델 포함 여부}", "{배경 스타일}"
- Additional Korean text in the image should be short and legible, including examples such as "굿즈 라인업", "신상품 프리오더", "대표 굿즈", "온라인 스토어 오픈", "예약 판매 5.10–5.24", "서울 성수 · 2026.05", "문의 hello@brand.kr".
- All merchandise items must share the same signature visual identity and feel like a coherent brand lineup, including the same {시그니처 디자인} on products, tags, packaging cards, and printed inserts.
- If a model is present, hands and body proportions must be anatomically correct, with natural fabric folds, believable pose, and clean product visibility.
- Keep all product materials realistic: cotton weave for apparel, glossy ceramic for mugs, anodized metal for keychains, enamel-like finish for pin badges, kraft card stock for backing cards, transparent sleeve reflections, and paper texture for stickers.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized likeness

studio:prompts3:ours-107.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1536x1024
- format: landscape Korean children’s picture-book page, 3:2 ratio, print-ready single page

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean children’s picture-book page illustration, single-page story scene. Warm, gentle read-aloud page with a cozy forest cabin setting, an integrated story text panel, page folio, running title, and small decorative narrative details that make the page feel like a real published picture book.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject placement: {주인공} centered slightly right, occupying about 45% of the frame, with both characters seated at a small table near the cabin window.
- Scene framing: {장면} fills the midground; the cabin interior, window view, table props, and story panel should all read clearly as one complete picture-book page.
- Background treatment: {배경소품과디테일} with layered trees outside, warm window light, wood grain, small household objects, and soft forest shapes that support the story atmosphere.
- Story text area: place {동화본문} inside a warm paper-like lower-left story panel with hand-painted edges, tiny leaf and acorn motifs, and readable contrast against the illustration.
- Header and folio: add a small running header near the top-left or top-center reading “{책제목} · {장면소제목}”, and a small page number “{페이지번호}” near the lower-right corner.
- Character design: {캐릭터디자인} with expressive faces, small hands/paws, rounded silhouettes, cute proportional heads, and soft body shapes.
- Color direction: use {그림스타일} with warm beige, olive, mustard, light pink, muted cream, honey gold, and gentle forest green tones.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Foreground (bottom 20%): small wooden table, steaming teacups, a teapot, an open book, acorn cookies, a patchwork cloth napkin, and a tiny bookmark or teapot tag reading “{작은소품문구}”; arrange props to guide the eye toward the characters and story text.
- Main character cluster (center-right 45%): {주인공} sitting closely together, one holding a cup of tea and the other looking at the book, showing calm friendship and shared attention.
- Cabin interior (midground): simple wooden wall, window frame, small shelf with jars, dried flowers, a knitted blanket, a candle lantern, children’s picture cards, and gentle paper textures that make the cabin feel lived-in.
- Outdoor backdrop (upper and side areas): soft forest shapes, distant trees, falling leaves, and sunset glow visible through the window and around the cabin; emphasize warmth, fairytale softness, and seasonal atmosphere.
- Story text placement (lower-left): {동화본문} rendered as 1–2 short lines in a child-friendly Korean font, aligned neatly inside the illustrated paper panel with comfortable line spacing.
- Decorative page elements: {장식요소} around the story panel, page number, and corners, painted as part of the illustration rather than as separate graphic stickers.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: 어린이 친화적 rounded Korean font such as Pretendard Rounded or Nanum Round, medium weight for the story sentence, smaller weight for header, page number, and tiny prop text.
- Text hierarchy: story body is the most readable text; running header and page number are subtle but legible; prop label is small and charming.
- Palette: {그림스타일} plus specific tones like #E9DDC8 beige, #A7B08A olive, #D8B15A mustard, #F2C6C2 light pink, #FFF6EA warm cream, and #C88A45 honey brown.
- Linework and paint: soft watercolor wash with delicate pencil-like outlines, low-contrast edges, visible handmade paper grain, and slightly uneven brush textures.
- Shadow and page finish: subtle ambient shadow under the table and characters, 8–12px blur feel, very light opacity; outlines stay soft and delicate with a faint hand-painted page-edge vignette.
- Decorative motifs: tiny leaves, acorns, tea steam curls, stitched cloth patterns, and small paper fibers may appear throughout to make the page tactile and storybook-like.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: picture-book illustration view, eye-level composition with a gentle editorial layout; no photographic distortion, balanced page illustration framing.
- Lighting: warm sunset light from the right side and slightly behind the window, with soft fill light inside the cabin; use diffused glow and mild rim light on character outlines.
- Color grade: soft evening pastel grade with honey gold highlights, muted forest greens, creamy paper whites, and warm watercolor bloom around the window.
- Rendering finish: Korean-Japanese picture-book illustration finish, hand-painted watercolor texture, soft pencil contour, matte paper surface, and print-friendly clarity at 1536x1024.

[6. MOOD]
A tender Korean-Japanese picture-book spread feel, like a Maruki-style children’s illustration with the calm warmth of a studio Ghibli storybook page. The page should feel cozy, safe, seasonal, and lovingly published, with enough small details for children to discover during read-aloud time.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Render Korean story text exactly: “{동화본문}”
- Render running header exactly: “{책제목} · {장면소제목}”
- Render page number exactly: “{페이지번호}” and tiny prop text exactly: “{작은소품문구}”
- All Korean text must be clean, fully legible, correctly spaced, and naturally integrated into the illustration.
- Characters must remain cute anthropomorphic animals with rounded proportions, expressive gentle faces, and a wholesome children’s-book tone.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or real-person likeness mashups

args.default: 창가 화분, 나무 선반, 말린 꽃, 찻주전자, 낙엽, 숲 그림자가 어우러진 따뜻한 배경

[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean myth and folktale character illustration poster, vertical editorial art card for social media and blog use.
Traditional fantasy scene combining folk painting motifs with modern subculture illustration, centered on a single iconic character, designed like a fictional museum-night exhibition poster with readable Korean event information.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: {주요 대상} placed as the central hero and occupying about 55–60% of the frame height, with a clear silhouette, expressive pose, and readable costume details.
- Background: {배경} rendered as a layered scenic backdrop with misty depth, waterfall spray, moon glow, mountain silhouettes, wet rocks, drifting petals, and faint folk-pattern clouds.
- Character traits: {대상의 특징} emphasized through visible shape language, flowing motion, luminous accents around the body, and small narrative props that naturally fit the mythic setting.
- Poster typography: place the main exhibition title {전시 제목} near the upper area, the subtitle {부제} beneath it or vertically along one side, and the character label {캐릭터 라벨} close to the character as a compact identification tag.
- Event information: include {일정}, {장소}, and {티켓 정보} as small but legible poster details near the lower third, with {주최 표기} in a modest sponsor/host line.
- Decorative graphics: add {장식 문양} as thin minhwa-inspired line ornaments, small talisman-paper tags, cloud curls, moon-ring marks, or patterned fabric swatches integrated around the typography and scenery.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Hero character zone (middle 60%): {주요 대상} drawn in full figure, facing slightly toward the viewer, with costume folds, hair, jewelry, shoes, sleeve seams, and accessories sharply defined.
- Trait emphasis layer: {대상의 특징} expressed with translucent energy trails, flowing cloth motion, foxfire-like glow, mist ribbons, and soft rim highlights that wrap around the character while preserving the outline.
- Environmental backdrop: {배경} built in depth from foreground mist and grass, midground rock or water detail, and a far background moonlit mountain silhouette with subtle hanji-like paper grain.
- Traditional detail accents: incorporate Korean cultural elements such as hanbok fabric patterns, norigae knot ornaments, minhwa peony or tiger-cloud motifs, gourd-like decorative forms, talisman strips, traditional hairpins, or patterned silk bands where naturally appropriate to the character.
- Editorial poster layer: arrange {전시 제목}, {부제}, {캐릭터 라벨}, {일정}, {장소}, {티켓 정보}, and {주최 표기} as a believable cultural-event poster system, balancing large title lettering with smaller informational text.
- Sponsor/footer area: create a slim bottom information strip with page-poster realism, including tiny divider lines, a small moon icon, ticket note, host credit, and registration-style number such as “FOLK-ART 247”.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Korean poster typography in Pretendard Medium, Noto Sans KR Medium, or a refined serif Hangul title style; title feels 54–76px, subtitle 24–34px, information text 18–24px, all crisp and legible.
- Color palette: indigo, moonlit blue, jade green, warm ivory, muted crimson, aged gold, and pale cyan highlights; use a restrained folk-painting palette with modern saturation control.
- Linework and shading: clean smooth outlines with subtle painterly fill, soft shadow separation, lightly textured brush transitions inspired by minhwa, and polished contemporary illustration rendering.
- Poster finish: include a premium printed-art-card feeling with hanji paper texture, subtle ink bleed at decorative marks, silk-like costume sheen, small highlight speckles in mist, and a soft atmospheric edge fade.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: anime illustration treated like a high-end poster render, composed as if shot on an 85mm portrait lens with shallow depth cues and strong subject isolation.
- Lighting: moonlit key light from upper-left, cool rim light from behind the character, and a soft reflected glow from waterfall mist below.
- Color grade: deep indigo and sapphire shadows with teal mist, silver moon highlights, and small touches of crimson and gold for traditional ornament accents.
- Rendering quality: high-resolution editorial illustration, crisp facial features, detailed hanbok textile patterning, layered atmospheric perspective, and realistic printed poster texture.

[6. MOOD]
{전체 분위기} Korean fantasy editorial — like a modern museum exhibition poster that blends minhwa heritage with a high-end Pixiv subculture illustration finish, enhanced by believable event-poster details and lyrical night scenery.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 렌더링되어야 하는 문구는 “{전시 제목}”, “{부제}”, “{캐릭터 라벨}”, “{일정}”, “{장소}”, “{티켓 정보}”, “{주최 표기}”이며, 사용자가 입력한 문구를 한 글자도 틀리지 않게 표시한다.
- Main subject must remain a single clearly readable character illustration, not a crowded group scene.
- Traditional Korean costume, accessories, typography, and mythic props must look culturally coherent and not generic fantasy.
- Added poster information should feel like a real Korean cultural exhibition poster while staying secondary to the character illustration.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or recognizable real-person likenesses

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean self-introduction PR card, one-page corporate interview handout, information-dense grid layout.
Realistic, print-ready personal branding sheet for job applicants, mixing Korean and English typography in a polished editorial HR profile style, with practical application details, skill metrics, badges, and a date-stamped portfolio-card feeling.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Vertical one-page layout with a structured grid: top identity header 20%, middle keyword and skill showcase 35%, lower experience infographic 30%, side portrait and contact rail 15%.
- {사진 스타일} is placed in a narrow side column or upper corner as a small ID-style portrait, framed neatly with rounded-rectangle crop, thin stroke, and a subtle paper-card shadow.
- Background is off-white / light gray paper tone with fine realistic paper texture, faint registration marks, tiny section labels, and layered card panels that make the sheet feel like a professionally printed recruiting profile.
- Use {이름}, {전공 및 한 줄 소개}, {핵심 키워드}, {경력 및 역량}, {추가 정보}, {디자인 색상} placeholders throughout the layout.
- Add realistic PR-card metadata: small issue-like label “PR CARD No. 01”, date stamp “2026.05 업데이트”, location label “Seoul, KR”, portfolio/contact micro line, and a small QR-style portfolio block as a graphic element.
- The layout should look submitted to a Korean university career center or corporate interview panel: aligned modules, readable hierarchy, printed paper realism, and credible applicant information density.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Top header band: Place {이름} in the largest type, with {전공 및 한 줄 소개} directly beneath in smaller subheadline text. Add small English/Korean micro labels such as “SELF INTRODUCTION”, “지원자 프로필”, “2026 상반기”, and a thin separator line below.
2) Portrait zone: Show {사진 스타일} as a small clean portrait, cropped tightly like a professional profile photo, with neutral background integration, rounded frame, thin navy border, and a caption label “PROFILE PHOTO”.
3) Core keywords zone: Visualize {핵심 키워드} as 3–4 bold keyword blocks, badges, or pill-like labels with tiny line icons beside each word. Add small supporting tags like “핵심 역량”, “업무 강점”, “협업 지수” to make the center feel like a real candidate snapshot.
4) Experience / ability zone: Present {경력 및 역량} and {추가 정보} as compact infographic modules using progress bars, line icons, small charts, checkmarks, and timeline-like rows. Include realistic labels such as “EXPERIENCE”, “SKILL MAP”, “PROJECT SUMMARY”, “ACTIVITY LOG”, and “AWARDS / LICENSE”.
5) Supporting details: Add concise micro-labels, separators, dotted guide lines, tiny page-number text “01 / 01”, portfolio URL placeholder text like “portfolio.kr/kimjiwon”, and a non-functional QR-style square. Use these details to connect sections while preserving a formal corporate portfolio look.
6) Profile / award-card decoration: Add certificate-inspired corner ornaments, thin rule lines, small skill badges, a date stamp, and a compact stats strip such as “분석 92”, “기획 88”, “소통 95”; these must look decorative and personal-branding oriented, not like an official certification.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Use clean sans-serif Korean and English pairing such as Pretendard, Noto Sans KR, or SUIT; name weight 700–800, subheadline 400–500, body 400–600, size hierarchy clearly separated.
- Color palette: Use the exact set from {디자인 색상} with navy as primary, light gray as background or panel base, and mustard as accent; optional near-black text and warm paper-white panels.
- Border/shadow: Thin 1px dividers, rounded cards with 8–12px radius, subtle layered paper shadows of 0px 4px 12px at 12–15% opacity for key panels, and fine mustard accent rules.
- Use strict grid alignment, consistent padding, formal icon style, and editorial spacing so the page remains credible as a printed interview handout.
- Add realistic print details: tiny footer credit line, small crop-mark-like accents, section numbering, light paper grain, and slight ink texture on dark navy text.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Studio portrait look, Canon EOS R5 with 85mm f/1.8 portrait framing for {사진 스타일}, sharp facial detail, neutral depth separation.
- Lighting: Soft studio key light from upper-left at 45° with gentle fill from right, controlled shadow, balanced for a corporate headshot feel.
- Color grade: Cool navy + light gray base with mustard accent, slightly desaturated, clean editorial print finish.
- Rendering: Realistic printed A4-like card surface, crisp typography, subtle paper fibers, accurate Korean text, and believable ink contrast.

[6. MOOD]
Corporate personal branding sheet — modern Korean recruiting portfolio aesthetic, like a polished university career center PR card with editorial magazine clarity, practical HR readability, and a confident applicant profile tone.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 렌더링할 문구 — “김지원”, “경영학 전공, 데이터 분석과 기획에 능숙한 인재”, “데이터 분석, 기획, 커뮤니케이션”, “인턴 1년, 동아리 대표 경험”, “수상 경력, 자격증”.
- Additional Korean microcopy may include: “지원자 프로필”, “핵심 역량”, “업무 강점”, “경험 요약”, “프로젝트”, “활동 기록”, “2026.05 업데이트”, “서울”, “포트폴리오”, “면접용 PR 카드”, “01 / 01”.
- The page must feel like a single cohesive one-page self-introduction card, not a poster or brochure.
- Portrait must be a small formal ID-style photo, not a full-body lifestyle image.
- Keep all infographic labels aligned and readable, with no overlapping text.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean resume ID photo, formal studio portrait, centered upper-body crop for official application use.
A realistic Seoul photo-studio style head-and-shoulders portrait for {사진 용도}, with Korean document-photo proportions, polished grooming, and believable studio retouching.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Subject placement: {인물 정보} centered in a strict vertical Korean ID-photo composition, shoulders and upper chest visible, face occupying about {얼굴 비율} of the frame height.
- Pose and gaze: {얼굴 방향}, direct front-facing posture, eyes level to camera, chin neutral, shoulders square, calm symmetrical alignment.
- Background treatment: {배경색} studio backdrop with soft real studio falloff, very subtle tonal variation around the shoulders, and clean white presentation suitable for document use.
- Framing direction: tight official portrait crop with balanced left-right spacing, a modest margin above the hairline, and the jacket line visible enough to read as formal attire.
- Wardrobe and grooming: {의상}, {헤어스타일}, {귀 노출 정도}, neat Korean grooming with controlled shine, tidy neckline, and natural skin texture.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Subject block: {인물 정보} shown as a realistic Korean face with natural proportions, even skin tone, subtle pore detail, refined jawline, and restrained retouching.
- Hair block: {헤어스타일} neatly shaped with controlled volume, clean hairline, realistic individual hair strands, and a photo-studio groomed finish.
- Clothing block: {의상} rendered crisply with straight lapels, centered shirt collar, properly knotted tie, faint fabric texture, and a subdued professional look.
- Expression block: {표정} with relaxed eyes, closed lips or barely parted lips, gentle confidence, and a formal ID-photo demeanor rather than a casual portrait mood.
- Background block: {배경색} Korean studio white with soft edge falloff, natural separation around dark hair and suit, and a faint believable contact shadow under the chin and jaw.
- Retouch block: {보정 스타일} applied in a standard Korean portrait studio manner: blemishes softened, under-eye tone refined, skin brightened slightly, face line subtly organized, while facial structure and texture remain believable.
- Print-readiness block: resemble a freshly delivered Korean 증명사진 digital file, sharp eyes, clean contour, neutral white balance, and an official-document compatible crop.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: this is a raw ID portrait file, not a profile card or resume layout; do not add name labels, dates, stamps, watermarks, or UI overlays.
- Color palette: clean white #FFFFFF, soft neutral gray #E9E9E9, natural skin tones, black suit #111111, deep navy-black tie accents.
- Studio finish: maintain a professional photo-booth and Korean portrait-studio look with precise grooming, realistic clothing texture, soft facial highlights, and a clean document-photo background.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Canon EOS R5 with an 85mm f/1.8 portrait lens, straight-on studio headshot framing, sharp focus on both eyes.
- Lighting: front key light at camera axis with large softbox, gentle fill from slightly below camera level, soft catchlights in both eyes, low contrast shadow under chin, even illumination across face.
- Color grade: neutral editorial portrait grade with accurate white balance, slightly cool white background, natural skin saturation, restrained contrast, and Korean studio retouch polish.

[6. MOOD]
Professional Korean ID-photo studio portrait — the clean, standardized look of a Seoul document-photo shop, polished enough for {사진 용도} while still looking like a real person photographed in a studio.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean rendered text: 없음. 이미지 안에는 이름, 날짜, 주민등록 양식, 사진관 로고, 워터마크를 넣지 않는다.
- Anatomy/layout invariants: realistic Korean male proportions, exactly one face, both eyes visible, ears naturally shaped, no extra limbs, no lens-warped asymmetry, centered passport-photo framing.
- Document-photo realism: maintain formal Korean 증명사진 proportions, natural skin texture, sharp eyes, neat suit alignment, and a white-background official portrait crop.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or recognizable public-figure likeness

[INPUT]

- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean anniversary caricature illustration, portrait poster for gifting and social sharing.
Lovely, polished caricature with handwritten watercolor touch, designed as a finished printed celebration card that feels personal, warm, and display-worthy.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: {인물 특징} placed slightly above center, occupying about 52% of the vertical frame, with a charming enlarged-head caricature style and recognizable facial cues.
- Scene setup: {상황} at a compact office desk, with the desk edge forming the lower visual anchor and a lived-in celebration atmosphere around the subject.
- Expression/action: {표정 및 행동} clearly readable, with the cake angled toward the viewer so the celebration reads instantly; add small candle light, frosting detail, and a tiny name plaque on the cake.
- Supporting props: {주변 소품} arranged around the desk and background as personal anniversary details: a small bouquet, ribbon, sticky notes, coffee cup, pen cup, desk calendar, framed mini photo, and a few congratulatory cards.
- Outfit treatment: {의상} with one small signature detail added, keeping the look professional and familiar; include soft fabric folds, collar stitching, and a subtle accessory such as a tie pin, brooch, or pocket square.
- Background treatment: soft cream-to-pastel wash with visible watercolor paper grain, a faint office window, bookshelf silhouettes, party bunting, confetti dots, and warm desk-lamp glow.
- Message area: {배경 메시지} placed near the upper background or on a small card element, integrated with a handwritten banner and a date/location label such as “2026.05.01 · 우리 사무실”.
- Add small realistic poster details: tiny illustrator credit text near the bottom reading “illustration for OOO”, a small decorative sticker tag reading “오늘의 주인공”, and a compact caption line reading “함께한 날들을 축하해요”.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Subject block (center 52%): {인물 특징} drawn as a friendly caricature with slightly enlarged head, softened facial proportions, clear likeness, neat linework, lively eyes, natural blush, and carefully shaped hair highlights.
2) Action focus (mid-lower center): {표정 및 행동} with the birthday cake held forward at chest level; show frosting swirls, one or two candles, a small plate shadow, and gentle candle glow that adds warmth to the face.
3) Work context (lower third): {상황} indicated through the office desk surface, monitor glow, keyboard corner, layered documents, calendar page, pen cup, sticky notes, and a warm coffee cup; use compact perspective so the desk supports the story without taking over.
4) Prop arrangement (left/right balance): {주변 소품} placed as small visual cues with simplified hand-illustrated shapes; include slightly skewed papers, a tiny gift box, ribbon curl, flower stem, and a congratulatory card with short Korean text such as “축하해요!”.
5) Wardrobe detail (torso area): {의상} rendered with crisp collar edges, soft watercolor shadows, and a restrained tie or fabric pattern; add one subtle personalized accent such as a pocket square, tie pin, name badge, or tiny enamel pin.
6) Background message layer (upper background): {배경 메시지} set in clean, readable lettering with enough contrast from the pastel wash; make it feel like a greeting card headline surrounded by tiny stars, confetti, tape strips, and a small date label.
7) Celebration card metadata: add two or three tiny printed-card details around the lower or side area, such as “No. 001”, “SPECIAL DAY”, “2026.05”, and “made with love”, kept secondary to the main birthday greeting.
8) Finish layer: thin pen outlines, light watercolor fill, soft paper texture, subtle ink bleed, realistic printed-paper shadowing, and warm separation between subject, cake, desk, and background so the illustration feels like a tangible framed gift print.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: hand-lettered Korean-friendly display style, medium weight, 28–42px feel for the main message; use rounded, legible lettering for Korean captions and small neat sans-serif text for date, credit, and sticker labels.
- Color palette: {색감} with cream #F6F0E8, blush peach #F6C9B8, muted sage #B8C6A5, soft navy #3E4A5A, warm gray #8C847C.
- Decorative treatment: use tape strips, small stars, confetti flecks, ribbon curls, paper labels, and tiny sticker tags in the same pastel palette, with all details feeling hand-painted and gift-card appropriate.
- Border/shadow: thin off-white printed-card border with a soft drop shadow, 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity; watercolor edge bleed kept subtle and natural like a real stationery print.
- Text hierarchy: the exact birthday message should be the clearest text element, with secondary Korean captions, date, and credit smaller and placed as believable card/poster details.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: digital illustration composition with a 50mm portrait framing feel, slightly elevated viewpoint, balanced like a greeting-card editorial illustration.
- Lighting: soft studio light from upper-left at 45°, gentle fill from the right, warm candle accent on the cake, mild paper brightness, and natural soft shadows under desk objects.
- Color grade: warm pastel editorial grade with cream, peach, and muted blue-gray, similar to a refined stationery illustration with realistic paper grain and gentle watercolor layering.
- Rendering finish: clean vector-like line clarity combined with watercolor wash, hand-inked edges, soft granulation, and small real-world print imperfections that make it feel custom-made rather than template-based.

[6. MOOD]
Warm, friendly anniversary caricature with a boutique stationery-card feel, like a polished Korean illustrator’s custom gift portrait capturing a real celebration moment in an office setting.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following string must appear exactly as rendered text in the image: "Happy Birthday OOO"
- Also include short Korean supporting text where appropriate, such as “오늘의 주인공”, “축하해요!”, “함께한 날들을 축하해요”, and a date label like “2026.05.01 · 우리 사무실”.
- Face/body proportions should remain cute and recognizable, not grotesque or overly distorted.
- Keep the office celebration scene visually rich but clearly organized so the subject, cake, and birthday message remain the main focal points.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[INPUT]

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean wedding invitation card with a warm couple illustration, premium vertical layout for print, mobile sharing, and Instagram announcement use.
Formal marriage announcement design with clear event information, name hierarchy, floral Korean stationery styling, realistic paper texture, and small editorial details that make the invitation feel like a finished printed card.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Tall portrait invitation layout: top announcement area occupies about 14% of the frame, central couple illustration about 42%, lower name and event information area about 30%, with polished stationery proportions suitable for 1024x1536.
- Background: warm beige paper texture with visible fine grain, subtle pressed-fiber texture, soft handmade paper edges, and botanical motifs using {배경 모티프} in soft sage green and muted ivory.
- The composition should feel centered, symmetrical, calm, and premium, with refined spacing between headline, illustration, name block, invitation message, and event details.
- Use {신랑 이름}, {신부 이름}, {예식 일시}, {예식 장소}, {커플 의상}, {주요 색감} as editable content anchors throughout the layout.
- Add realistic invitation-card finishing details: faint gold-foil line accents, tiny floral sprigs, small calendar icon, venue pin icon, RSVP/contact microtext, and a subtle photographed-card presentation with soft paper shadow.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top header area: place the large Korean headline “청첩장” centered near the top, using elegant serif display styling with strong contrast against the background. Add a smaller line above or below it such as “WEDDING INVITATION” and a small season/date label “2026 WEDDING DAY” in muted gold.
2. Invitation message: beneath the headline, include a short Korean announcement line: “저희 두 사람이 사랑으로 하나 됩니다” and a smaller supporting line “소중한 분들을 모시고 기쁨을 나누고 싶습니다.”
3. Main illustration area: draw a neat couple portrait in the center, with the couple wearing {커플 의상}, standing close together in a refined, formal wedding-portrait pose; keep facial proportions natural and Korean, with soft expressions, carefully rendered hair, bouquet detail, boutonniere detail, and clean elegant linework.
4. Botanical framing: surround the couple with delicate floral and leaf motifs based on {배경 모티프}, arranged as corner accents, small wreath-like arcs, scattered pressed-flower details, and fine gold botanical strokes that support the couple portrait and stationery feel.
5. Name block: place {신랑 이름} and {신부 이름} beneath the illustration, aligned centrally, with the names slightly larger than the event details and separated by a subtle dot, ampersand, or thin muted-gold divider line.
6. Family and invitation detail line: add a small Korean line below the names such as “양가 부모님의 마음을 담아 초대합니다” and a micro credit-style line “Bride & Groom Illustration / {신랑 이름} · {신부 이름}”.
7. Event details block: render {예식 일시} and {예식 장소} in clean sans-serif Korean text, stacked neatly with clear hierarchy and consistent line spacing for print readability. Add small labels “DATE”, “TIME”, and “VENUE” in muted gold or sage green next to the Korean event information.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Overall layout: top story-brand zone 18%, central product/info zone 58%, bottom CTA + social cue zone 14%, with Instagram Story UI-safe positioning at the top and bottom.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top header area: place a realistic Instagram Story account row first, with a small profile circle, "@our_cafe.kr", "방금 전", and a faint progress-bar feel; place {스토리 목적} as a small supporting label near the top, then set {메인 헤드라인} immediately below in oversized bold Korean sans-serif.
2. Center hero area: feature {메인 비주얼} as the dominant focal point, cropped with editorial product-photo styling so it feels premium and appetizing; include realistic shadows, plate edges, tabletop grain, café receipt detail, and a small handwritten-style sticker reading "오늘의 신메뉴".

5. CTA area: render {CTA 문구} as a bold button at the bottom, with a clear arrow and tap-style visual treatment; add tiny Story UI-inspired actions nearby such as a paper-plane icon, bookmark icon, and "친구에게 공유" in very small text.

[4. STYLE RULES]

- Instagram realism: include a story handle row, location/date chip, hashtags-like text, micro icons, and small social interaction details, but keep them secondary to {메인 헤드라인}, {메인 비주얼}, {핵심 정보}, and {CTA 문구}.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]

- Lighting: soft window light from upper-left at 45°, subtle fill from front-right, gentle shadow falloff, realistic highlights on glaze/cream/packaging, and natural tabletop shadows.
- Color grade: warm beige + caramel + coral with slightly muted saturation, social-media-friendly and polished.
- Material detail: show tactile café-branding surfaces such as matte paper, ceramic gloss, linen napkin texture, kraft sticker, soft cream, pastry crumb detail, condensation, or printed menu-card fibers where appropriate to {메인 비주얼}.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: must appear exactly as written: "새로운 디저트 출시!", "5월 1일부터 한정 판매. 스토리 보고 방문 시 아메리카노 1잔 무료!", "지금 바로 매장 방문하기 →".
- Additional Korean microcopy may appear if legible and secondary: "@our_cafe.kr", "방금 전", "성수동 · 2026.05.01", "오늘의 신메뉴", "한정 판매", "방문 혜택", "5월 이벤트", "NEW ₩7,500", "DM 문의", "#동네카페 #신메뉴 #디저트추천".
- Layout invariants: top headline must remain readable on a single story screen, central visual must not cover the CTA, and all essential text must stay inside Instagram Story-safe zones.

3. Event detail zone: under the headline, create a rounded coupon panel containing {이벤트 내용}, plus realistic Korean details such as "행사기간 2026.05.01–05.31", "운영시간 10:00–21:00", "장소 매장 입구 행사존", and "1인 1회 사용 가능".
4. Store information zone: add a small sponsor/store strip near the bottom with "우리동네 마트", "서울시 중구 샘플로 24", "문의 02-1234-5678", and a tiny QR-code-like square labeled "쿠폰 확인".
5. Poster usage cue: integrate {포스터 용도} as a small footer label or corner tag, paired with realistic print text such as "A4 POP / 계산대 부착용 / VOL.05 EVENT".
6. Style anchoring: reinforce {전체 디자인 컨셉} through color balance, icon style, typography hierarchy, sticker labels, decorative dividers, and lively Korean neighborhood retail signage energy.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use a bold Korean sans-serif such as Pretendard ExtraBold, Noto Sans KR Black, or Gmarket Sans Bold for the headline; use Pretendard Medium or Noto Sans KR Regular for body copy; headline size should visually dominate at 72–120 px equivalent.
- Color palette: emphasize {주요 색상} with strong print-friendly contrast; use saturated red #E53935, yellow #FDD835, black #111111, and white #FFFFFF for readable panels, price tags, and coupon boxes.
- Border/shadow: add thick black keylines around headline blocks, comic-style sale burst outlines, and a subtle 3px–6px drop shadow with 15%–20% opacity to improve legibility on colorful backgrounds.
- Print finish: use crisp vector edges, sharp Korean lettering, slight warm white paper grain, subtle ink texture, tiny registration/crop marks, and realistic A4 indoor-print appearance.
- Decorative content: include practical retail poster elements such as discount badges, arrow callouts, dotted dividers, small item-category pictograms, barcode-style coupon strip, sponsor area, and bottom contact details.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: if product imagery is used, stage it as a front-facing commercial poster composite with 50mm lens perspective, f/5.6 look, minimal distortion, and flat graphic integration.
- Lighting: bright studio-style even illumination, with soft top-left key light and gentle fill from the right so text, paper texture, sticker graphics, and motifs remain high-contrast.
- Color grade: Korean POP poster grade with vivid red-yellow-black emphasis, slight warm white paper tone, saturated retail flyer color, and controlled contrast to preserve readability.
- Realism details: show the poster as a finished A4 printed sheet with subtle paper fibers, very slight corner curl or tape-shadow impression, and dense but organized in-store promotional information.

[6. MOOD]
Korean neighborhood market POP signage — energetic convenience-store flyer energy, cheerful local-event atmosphere, and practical retail-layout realism with bright discount graphics and clear buying cues.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following verbatim Korean strings must appear correctly if rendered: "5월 가정의 달 30% 할인!", "전 메뉴 적용.", "이번 달 한정", "한국 마트 매장 내 A4 POP 포스터".
- Additional Korean poster microcopy may appear clearly: "행사기간 2026.05.01–05.31", "운영시간 10:00–21:00", "장소 매장 입구 행사존", "쿠폰 확인", "문의 02-1234-5678".
- Keep all Korean characters fully legible with correct spacing and no broken jamo.
- Maintain a clear hierarchy: headline largest, event details medium, coupon/store/footer information smallest.
- Decorative graphics, price tags, QR-like elements, and sponsor strips should enrich the poster while leaving all main Korean text readable.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
